attorneys.name: Alexander M. Jadin
attorneys.practice_type: Insurance Appraisals and Litigation Lawyers in Bloomington, MN
attorneys.bio:
"My clients, whether they be individual property owners, businesses, or families, know that I am their advocate and that I will work hard to make sure their voices are heard and that my clients are always cognizant of the economics of their cases. I think that it is important for every client to seriously consider the economic costs and benefits of every dispute. I present their stories to the opposing party, the court, the appraisal panel, and the jury in a way that is both compelling and unassailable."

Throughout his career, Alex has helped secure numerous successful outcomes for his clients in a wide range of legal matters involving insurance policy interpretation and coverage, property damage claims, and construction defects. He also has substantial experience in insurance litigation, including fire cause and origin disputes and product liability litigation, valuation disputes, insurance appraisals, insurance coverage disputes, motion practice, mediation, and trial (appellate). Alex also works with community associations and businesses, handling their corporate governance, and litigation. Alex has handled numerous appeals cases in multiple jurisdictions, leading to new laws and positive results for his clients.

He practices in the following areas:

Insurance Appraisals and Litigation

Insurance Coverage Disputes

Appellate Practice

Construction Defect Litigation

Commercial Litigation

Community Association Law

Estate Planning

General Corporate Representation

In addition to extensive experience in litigation, Alex serves as a counselor for individuals and businesses in estate and business planning for all facets of their needs from asset creation to asset protection, as well as the protection of their estates.

Alex is a member of the Minnesota, Wisconsin, Colorado, and Texas State Bar Associations.

He is admitted to practice in the state courts of Minnesota, Wisconsin, Colorado, and Texas, as well as the U.S. District Court for the District of Minnesota, the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Wisconsin, the U.S. District Court for the District of Colorado, and the United States Court of Appeals for the Eighth District.

Alex obtained his Juris Doctorate from the University of St. Thomas School of Law in 2006, and is a part of the University of St. Thomas mentor program. Alex also received his Bachelor of Arts from the University of St. Thomas in Financial Management and Legal Studies in Business.

Outside of the office, Alex enjoys football, golf, and spending time with his family and three boys.

attorneys.name: Michelle R. Jester
attorneys.practice_type: Banking & Finance Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
There is always something cooking in Michelle's kitchen and her office. And, over the years, Michelle has perfected her recipes and her approach, recognizing that each transaction is unique and calls for a different type of client advocate.

Real estate transactions, oftentimes, require basic ingredients - a mixture of strong business sense, a practical approach and her easy-going nature. Certain transactions, however, require Michelle's special ingredient - her strength, which comes from her innate understanding of the law, and ability to achieve business solutions that make sense and promote her client's interests against the most challenging adversary.

Michelle's practice focuses on all aspects of real estate transactions including sales and acquisitions, development, leasing, and financing. She has special expertise in the representation of lenders in origination of loans, workouts, and foreclosures.

As part of her practice, Michelle litigates issues related to real estate, such as mechanic's liens, property disputes, unlawful detainers, property tax appeals, and title clearance proceedings.

attorneys.practice_type: Banking, Finance & Workout Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Chad A. Johnson is a founding partner of the firm and serves as chair of the Real Estate Practice Group. In this capacity, he serves a broad range of businesses, corporations and limited liability entities, including condominium, townhouse, cooperative and other community associations.

Chad concentrates his business practice in the following areas:

Business organization

General business and corporate representation

Real estate law

Community association formation and maintenance

Applying the knowledge and insight gained as business owner, Chad is uniquely positioned to help his clients effectively address the many challenges of running a successful business. He possesses an uncompromising commitment to his client's success, evidenced by thoughtful counsel and proactive representation.

Chad's services include entity selection and maintenance, contract formation and negotiation, financial and business capitalization, corporate formalities, and buy-sell agreements. His real estate clients in particular benefit from his standing as a MSBA Board Certified Real Property Law Specialist, coupled with extensive experience in all residential and commercial real estate matters, include real estate sales, acquisitions and leasing.

For twelve consecutive years (2001-2012), Chad has been chosen for inclusion in the Minnesota Super Lawyers® list; only five percent of attorneys in Minnesota are chosen each year.

Chad has served on the board of several industry organizations, and also shares his expertise with business leaders and fellow attorneys through continuing education programs and seminars. He is the chief author and editor of the quarterly publication The Authority on Real Estate, and contributing author of the quarterly publication The Authority on Community Associations.

Licensed to practice law in the State and Federal courts in Minnesota, he is a member of the Hennepin County Bar Association, the Real Property Section of the Minnesota State Bar Association, and the American Bar Association. Chad obtained his J.D. from William Mitchell College of Law. He completed his undergraduate studies at St. Olaf College with a B.A. in Economics.

attorneys.name: Jesse A. Johnson
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Chisago City, MN
attorneys.bio:
I grew up locally in Chisago City. I am a graduate of Chisago Lakes Senior High School. I graduated from Hamline School of Law in 1999 and obtained my first legal job as a law clerk for a judge in Hibbing. In 2000 I moved back to Chisago County and started my own practice.

I handle primarily criminal cases, both in adult and in juvenile court. I have taken on cases from traffic tickets all the way to murder and serious felony cases. I take a creative approach to each individual client and their legal situation. I listen to my clients and advise them on what to do to put themselves in the best position to obtain a favorable outcome. Minimizing a client’s exposure to jail or prison is always a top priority. Protecting an individual’s criminal and traffic record is also a top priority. Criminal convictions can have many collateral consequences, and can adversely affect employment opportunities, housing options, insurance rates and more.

Some cases can’t be solved with a plea bargain no matter how creative the plea negotiations are. Sometimes a plea to anything means the loss of a career or a ruined future. Sometimes a person is wrongfully accused, and is truly innocent. These cases need to be litigated. I have obtained countless dismissals in cases where I have challenged the validity of the government’s evidence or methods of gathering evidence.

I have tried countless cases both to judges and to juries with great results for my clients. I have handled more criminal cases and conducted more trials as a defense attorney in Chisago County since 2000 than any other defense attorney. I understand the local culture and the local prosecutors, judges and court staff. Knowing the different players makes a difference in planning the best strategy for the best outcome, whether it is to negotiate a favorable resolution or trial strategy.

I have handled cases throughout the metro counties, and in several rural counties as far away as Lake County in Grand Marias. The majority of my cases are in Chisago, Washington, Anoka, Ramsey, Hennepin, Isanti, Kanabec and Pine Counties. I have forged good working relationships with prosecutors, judges and other defense attorneys throughout the state. If you are facing criminal charges in Minnesota I can help to get you the best result possible.

If you are being investigated for a crime you should have legal representation immediately. Don’t let yourself be intimidated into answering questions by law enforcement without representation. Often a client has already incriminated themselves before they retain an attorney. Don’t let that happen to you. A good defense attorney hired during the investigation stage may more than pay for itself if it results in no criminal charges or reduced charges.

attorneys.name: Lynn A. Johnson
attorneys.firm_name: Lynn A. Johnson Law Office, LLC
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning, Wills, Probate, Trusts Lawyers in Slayton, MN
attorneys.bio:
Lynn A. Johnson earned her Bachelor of Science in Business Administration at Southwest State University in Marshall, Minnesota in 1992. She then went to law school and graduated in 1995 with a J.D. from William Mitchell College of Law. While in law school, she worked as a law clerk for St. Paul Fire & Marine Company in St. Paul and for the Honorable Timothy Connell and David E. Christensen in the summer of 1995.

After passing the bar, she opened an office in her hometown of Slayton, Minnesota in 1996. Since then she has had a general practice law firm. Ms. Johnson also has 10 years of public service as an assistant State Public Defender serving indigent clients in hundreds of criminal defense cases. She's represented individuals charged with everything from DWI to sexual assault. In her private practice she represents many different types of clients including farm cases and real estate, involving very extensive custody cases. She has successfully represented several personal injury cases with positive results. The firm has an enormous network of resources which benefit and/or assist her clients. She has planned numerous estates preparing trusts, wills and probate assets. She also speaks on the the topic of estate planning.

Attorney Johnson is a past President and Vice President of the 13th District Bar Association. She is very active in the community and has taught and coached Mock Trials as well as participated as a Judge. She has served as a board member of the following organizations: Hospice of Murray County for six years; Murray County DAC Board; past Board member for 8 years; President of the Chamber of Commerce and past board member for 8 years; Lake Shetek Regional Clinic Board.

attorneys.name: Samuel V. Johnson
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Chisago City, MN
attorneys.bio:
I grew up in Chisago City, Minnesota, and graduated from Chisago Lakes High School. I later moved to Duluth, where I earned my undergraduate degree from the University of Minnesota Duluth while working as a server and bartender. After that, I relocated to Lowertown–St. Paul to attend William Mitchell College of Law. I now live in St. Paul and share a law office with my brother, Jesse Johnson, serving clients throughout Chisago, Pine, Isanti, Kanabec, Anoka, Washington counties, and most anywhere in the state.

My practice focuses primarily on Family Law, with a particular emphasis on dissolution and divorce. I also regularly handle adoptions, custody matters, guardianship matters, evictions, wills and trusts, civil commitments, and child protection cases. I’m committed to providing straightforward, effective advocacy and helping clients navigate complex legal issues with clarity and confidence.

Outside of work, I enjoy spending time with my wife, Alyssa, and our two English bulldogs, Kevin and Louis. My hobbies include traveling, muskie fishing, being outdoors, snowboarding, and following Twins baseball and Timberwolves basketball.

attorneys.name: Timothy D. Johnson
attorneys.practice_type: Insurance Coverage Lawyers in Bloomington, MN
attorneys.bio:
"Helping people navigate and overcome legal challenges is the best part of being a lawyer. My clients can expect that whether drafting a simple contract or litigating a multimillion-dollar case, I will take the time to understand all of the legal, financial, and business implications of their situation so we can define and develop a clear path to success."

Tim represents both individual and business clients in a wide range of legal matters both in and out of court. Tim has handled numerous cases in state and federal court, before multiple appellate courts, and in administrative court. Tim also represents homeowners and business owners at insurance appraisals. In addition to an extensive litigation practice, Tim counsels clients in real estate transactions such as commercial leases, purchase agreements, and other types of real estate matters. When he is not handling cases, Tim frequently speaks across the country at conferences and events on issues of insurance and construction law.

Tim's primary practice areas:

Insurance Coverage

Insurance Appraisal Hearings

Construction Law

Real Estate Law

Tim is a member of the Hennepin County Bar Association, the Minnesota State Bar Association, the Minnesota Bar Association's Real Property Section, he serves as a volunteer in Mitchell Hamline's Mentor Program, he serves as a volunteer coach for the Thurgood Marshall Moot Court Competition, he serves as a volunteer on the Contractor Association of Minnesota's public policy committee, and he is an adjunct professor at the Mitchell Hamline School of Law.

attorneys.name: Zachary H. Johnson
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Park Rapids, MN
attorneys.bio:
Zack Johnson brings over 20 years of legal expertise to Thomason, Swanson & Zahn, serving clients with a commitment to justice and a deep understanding of the law. Licensed in both Minnesota and New York, Zack has cultivated a diverse and robust practice that spans criminal defense, civil rights, family law, real estate litigation, and probate disputes.

The legendary Manhattan District Attorney Robert M. Morgenthau hired Zack in 2002 to work at the New York County District Attorney's Office, where he honed his skills in prosecuting criminal cases and developed a strong foundation in the complexities of criminal law. Following his tenure in public service, he joined the prestigious firm of Shearman and Sterling LLP, representing corporate clients in high-stakes investigations and legal matters. This experience provided him with unique insights into the intersection of corporate law and individual rights.

In 2009, Zack co-founded Galluzzo and Johnson LLP (now the Law Office of Matthew Galluzzo), where he focused on a private practice encompassing both criminal and civil rights law. This role allowed him to advocate passionately for individuals facing legal challenges, further deepening his dedication to client-centered representation.

For the past seven years, Zack has been practicing in Minnesota's beautiful northern lakes country and has focused his practice on family law, real estate, business and probate litigation, and appeals. His comprehensive understanding of the legal system, coupled with his experience in obtaining favorable outcomes for his clients, makes him a trusted advisor in difficult legal matters, including Orders for Protection (OFP) and Harassment Restraining Orders (HRO).

Zack's approach to law is characterized by his unwavering commitment to his clients, his meticulous attention to detail, and his strategic thinking. He is dedicated to providing compassionate support and effective legal solutions tailored to meet the unique needs of each client.

Outside of the office, Zack is an active member of the Park Rapids community. He has served as the president and membership chair of the Park Rapids Rotary club and serves on the board of the Northern Light Opera Company and the Huntersville Sportsmen's Club. He is an active member of his church where he rotates in on piano duty and teaches Sunday school, and also hosts a local podcast, Northwestern Voices. He is proud to serve the Park Rapids area and is committed to making a positive impact through his work.

Whether you are facing a family law dispute, a real estate issue, or require assistance with a complex litigation matter, Zack Johnson is here to help you navigate your legal challenges with expertise and integrity.

attorneys.name: Christopher R. Jones
attorneys.practice_type: Community Associations Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Chris Jones joined Hellmuth & Johnson in November 2004. Chris is a partner of the firm and member of the Real Estate, Construction and Litigation Practice Groups, where he primarily represents contractors, subcontractors, suppliers, business owners and property owners in a variety of transactional matters and disputes. Chris represents clients in mediations, arbitrations and district court actions regarding mechanic's liens, construction defect disputes and other business and commercial disputes. His practice is primarily concentrated in:

Real estate law and litigation

Construction litigation

Commercial litigation

Chris has a well-established practice assisting homeowners whose homes suffer from water intrusion, water damage and construction deficiencies. Over the past several years, Chris has received significant monetary recoveries on behalf of clients with defective and damaged homes. Those recoveries have helped homeowners get their homes repaired and the ongoing issues resolved. While that process can be very challenging and intimidating, Chris helps guide his clients through the process as quickly, yet aggressively and effectively, as possible to maximize the possible recovery for water intrusion related problems under the circumstances.

Chris also has an active practice representing both buyers and sellers in real estate misrepresentation cases. Chris works with buyers/sellers prosecuting or defending against claims related to alleged misrepresentations made in connection with the sale of real property. On this issue, Chris has authored an article called "An Agent's Guide-Understanding Real Estate Disclosure Laws” which can be downloaded from the link on this page. Chris frequently teaches seminars on these disclosure issues to real estate agents who are frequently the first point of contact when a problem arises.

In addition, Chris also works with a variety of construction industry clients on contract issues, project disputes and general legal matters. Chris takes a problem-solving approach in these matters and tries to determine how to resolve disputes in the quickest and most efficient fashion on behalf of his construction clients. He also has a role in preventing potential future disputes by drafting and reviewing construction contracts, assisting in project documentation, and establishing preliminary dispute resolution procedures.

Chris was named to the 2008-2010 & 2012 Minnesota Rising StarsSM lists, only 2.5% of young attorneys in the state are selected each year. Licensed to practice law in the State and Federal courts of Minnesota as well as the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit, he is a member of the Hennepin County and Minnesota State Bar Associations. Chris also serves as a commissioner on the Planning Commission for the City of Savage and is also a past Board member and President of The Pointe Homeowners Association in Savage, MN. In December 2010, Chris was elected to serve a three year term on the Board of Directors for the National Association of the Remodeling Industry, Minnesota Chapter (NARI-MN).

He obtained his J.D. from the University of North Dakota, graduating with distinction. He also completed his undergraduate studies at the University of North Dakota with a B.S. degree in Criminal Justice Studies.

attorneys.name: Tharika Jor’dan
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Eagan, MN
attorneys.bio:
Tharika Jor’dan serves as an associate attorney in the criminal defense department at Sieben Edmunds Miller. In this capacity, she engages directly with clients, offering consultations, legal advice, and representation throughout their legal challenges.

Before joining Sieben Edmunds Miller, Tharika graduated Magna Cum Laude from Mitchell Hamline School of Law. Recognized by the Minnesota Justice Foundation for public service work, Tharika worked at CRP Law, a private criminal defense firm, during the summer after her 1L year. She also served as a Certified Student Attorney at the Anoka County Public Defender’s Office and volunteered at Minneapolis Adult Education Public School, teaching law through the Minnesota Justice Foundation’s Street Law Program.

Tharika’s experiences include invaluable litigation exposure during her time as a student attorney at the Anoka County Public Defender’s Office, focusing on bail hearings. She also collaborated with a team of attorneys at the Great North Innocence Project during her 3L year, working on complex cases involving wrongful convictions.

In Tharika’s practice, the focus lies on general criminal defense, emphasizing cultural competency and sensitivity to each client’s unique situation. She believes in ensuring clients feel heard and comfortable to advocate for their wishes, guiding them through the legal system with informed decision-making.

Tharika’s commitment to clients has earned recognition, including the Law School Public Service Program Certificate from the Minnesota Justice Foundation and the title of Best Advocate at the Summit Cup from Mitchell Hamline School of Law. Clients appreciate her dedication, understanding, and clarity in explaining legal procedures and laws. They express feeling heard and cared for during interactions with Tharika, illustrating a commitment to their well-being and case outcomes.

Tharika holds a Bachelor of Arts in Gender Women Sexuality Studies with a minor in Social Justice from the University of Minnesota – Twin Cities and a Juris Doctor, Magna Cum Laude, from Mitchell Hamline School of Law. She has been admitted to the Minnesota State Bar Association.

Volunteer involvement includes serving as a Legal Rights Volunteer Teacher at MPD Center for Adult Learning through the Minnesota Justice Foundation and volunteering with Communities United Against Police Brutality.

Recognized by the Minnesota Justice Foundation for public service work, Tharika worked at CRP Law, a private criminal defense firm, during the summer after her 1L year. She also served as a Certified Student Attorney at the Anoka County Public Defender’s Office and volunteered at Minneapolis Adult Education Public School, teaching law through the Minnesota Justice Foundation’s Street Law Program.

Tharika’s experiences include invaluable litigation exposure during her time as a student attorney at the Anoka County Public Defender’s Office, focusing on bail hearings. She also collaborated with a team of attorneys at the Great North Innocence Project during her 3L year, working on complex cases involving wrongful convictions.

In Tharika’s practice, the focus lies on general criminal defense, emphasizing cultural competency and sensitivity to each client’s unique situation. She believes in ensuring clients feel heard and comfortable to advocate for their wishes, guiding them through the legal system with informed decision-making.

Tharika’s commitment to clients has earned recognition, including the Law School Public Service Program Certificate from the Minnesota Justice Foundation and the title of Best Advocate at the Summit Cup from Mitchell Hamline School of Law. Clients appreciate her dedication, understanding, and clarity in explaining legal procedures and laws. They express feeling heard and cared for during interactions with Tharika, illustrating a commitment to their well-being and case outcomes.

Tharika holds a Bachelor of Arts in Gender Women Sexuality Studies with a minor in Social Justice from the University of Minnesota – Twin Cities and a Juris Doctor, Magna Cum Laude, from Mitchell Hamline School of Law. She has been admitted to the Minnesota State Bar Association.

Volunteer involvement includes serving as a Legal Rights Volunteer Teacher at MPD Center for Adult Learning through the Minnesota Justice Foundation and volunteering with Communities United Against Police Brutality.

attorneys.name: Elizabeth L. Juelich
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Minnetonka, MN
attorneys.bio:
Elizabeth Juelich is a partner at Krueger, Juelich & Schmisek, PLLC in Minnetonka, Minnesota.

Elizabeth focuses her practice on family law and estate planning. She understands that her clients' families are their most valuable asset, and she tailors her representation to create a plan for their personal and financial future. Elizabeth values her clients' perspectives, listens to their goals and priorities, and helps them accomplish their objectives through legal and practical advice.

Elizabeth believes clients are more satisfied with their outcome when they are actively engaged in planning and settlement negotiations, and she encourages client participation throughout the process. She educates her clients on the relevant legal precedents and provides a cost-benefit analysis for specific actions. While Elizabeth tries to resolve as many issues as possible through alternative dispute resolution methods such as mediation and informal settlement discussions, she is prepared to litigate if an acceptable agreement can't be reached. Elizabeth also provides legal services under limited-scope representation agreements and through advice-only consultations.

Elizabeth's prior experience in the areas of federal financial compliance, managing multi-million dollar budgets, finance, and strategic planning is the foundation of her passion for analyzing and synthesizing complex financial information and advising business owners, officers, executives, physicians, attorneys, and other high net-worth individuals and their spouses. Her experience in these matters makes her a sought-after author and instructor. Elizabeth presents and has been published in both national and state forums on topics including:

Tax issues in divorce

Spousal maintenance

Discovering hidden income and assets

Dividing employee stock awards and retirement benefits

Executive compensation

Discovery

Case management for complex divorce cases

Child support

Child custody

Qualified domestic relations orders

Post-decree modifications

Estate planning considerations in divorce

Elizabeth is admitted to practice law in Minnesota and is a member of the Minnesota State Bar Association’s Family Law and Estates and Trusts sections, and she served as chair of the MSBA Family Law Section during the 2024-2025 bar year. Elizabeth is also a member of the Hennepin County Bar Association. Her involvement in these sections allows her to keep current on important developments in her practice areas and influence legislative changes to improve the laws that impact her clients.

Elizabeth devotes significant time giving back to the community by providing pro bono estate planning services to first responders through the Wills for Heroes program; coaching and judging mock trial competitions; and serving on the board of Two Rivers Community Land Trust, a nonprofit providing affordable housing for low- and moderate-income individuals and families in Washington County, Minnesota. Elizabeth has been honored for her pro bono work by receiving the North Star Lawyer Award from the Minnesota State Bar Association every year since 2013 in recognition of providing pro bono services exceeding 50 hours annually.

Elizabeth was selected to the Minnesota Super Lawyers Rising Star list each year from 2012 through 2018, a designation received by no more than 2.5% of the attorneys in Minnesota and has been named a Super Lawyer each year since 2019. In 2018, Elizabeth served on the national Rising Stars advisory board, where she represented the central region of the United States. The National Advocates also named Elizabeth as one of the top 40 attorneys in Minnesota under 40 in 2016, 2017, and 2018.

attorneys.practice_type: Business Litigation Lawyers in Saint Paul, MN
attorneys.bio:
Scott Jurchisin is an attorney at Larson • King, LLP. His professional career has been focused on helping individuals. He spent three years at a plaintiff’s civil litigation firm, where he represented individuals who were harmed by medical malpractice. He also clerked for the Honorable Jill Flaskamp Halbrooks at the Minnesota Court of Appeals and at a business litigation firm prior to joining Larson • King, LLP.

Now, Scott's practice includes several types of litigation: business, consumer law, real estate, and banking.

Scott is an active member of the Minnesota State Bar Association’s Mock Trial Advisory Committee—a program he participated in as a high school student—and coaches mock high school and law school mock trial programs. Scott has won numerous awards for his trial skills in mock trial and moot court programs throughout college and law school, including being a quarter finalist in a national mock trial competition in 2016, and winning a national moot court competition and award for best brief in 2015. In law school, he was a CALI award recipient, earned Dean’s List honors, and served on the executive committee of Volume 42 of the Mitchell Hamline Law Review.

attorneys.practice_type: Business & Corporate Law Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
J. Robert Keena is a partner with Hellmuth & Johnson, PLLC and chair of the firm's Litigation Practice, where he assists individuals and businesses of all sizes with a variety of litigation issues, including:

Complex multi-party litigation

Commercial disputes

Construction disputes

Employment law and litigation

Insurance claims

Probate litigation

Robert provides thoughtful counsel and proactive representation to his clients, and aggressively defends their interests in all litigation matters. Robert has extensive commercial litigation experience in matters involving real estate disputes, shareholder disputes, trade secret protection, probate disputes, and large-scale tort actions. His construction practice involves the representation of a significant number of builders faced with contract issues, as well as property owners faced with construction defect claims.

For five consecutive years (2008-2012), Robert has been chosen for inclusion in the Minnesota Super Lawyers® list; only 5% of attorneys in Minnesota are selected each year. He was also named a Rising StarSM for multiple years running. Robert is a frequent speaker and author on a multitude of legal issues including Construction Law and Litigation matters. He has been quoted in Midwest Home magazine, the Star Tribune, and The Builder's Journal, among others, and has appeared on both KSTP-TV and WCCO-TV.

Robert is licensed to practice law in the State of Minnesota, Federal District Court of Minnesota and Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals. He is a member of the Minnesota State Bar Association and the Hennepin County Bar Association.

Robert obtained his J.D. from Golden Gate University School of Law, and graduated with the school's criminal law award for academic excellence. He completed his undergraduate studies at the University of Minnesota, with a B.A. in history.

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Litigation Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
LINDSAY M. KELLER is the managing partner of Keller, Woods & Thompson, P.A. She is an impassioned advocate for her clients. Lindsay’s clients view her as caring, compassionate, and thoroughly knowledgeable about insurance law and the full range of avenues for redress of their injuries. Lindsay’s competitive nature, knowledge of insurance law, work ethic, tenacity, and strategic aggression in a courtroom or negotiation setting has allowed her to successfully close hundreds of cases through settlement, jury trial, arbitration, or appeal.

Aside from her litigation practice, Lindsay was appointed to the governing committee of the Minnesota Automobile Insurance Plan. She is a qualified ADR neutral on the State of Minnesota Roster, and serves as mediator for both civil and family law cases. She also frequently serves as a FINRA financial dispute arbitrator and chairperson, as well as a Minnesota No-fault arbitrator.

Lindsay has been named as a Super Lawyer from 2023 to present, and a Super Lawyers Rising Star from 2015 to 2022. She recently earned a Certificate of Completion for Women and Power, which she attended at the John F. Kennedy School, Harvard University. Lindsay is a past chair of the Civil Litigation Section of the Minnesota State Bar Association and continues to serve on the governing council. She is also the president of the Richard T. Oakes American Inn of Court. Lindsay taught as an adjunct professor at William Mitchell College of Law and the University of St. Thomas Law School, where she developed courses on insurance law.

attorneys.name: Wynne P. Kelly
attorneys.practice_type: Immigration Removal Proceedings Lawyers in St. Paul, MN
attorneys.bio:
Biography

Wynne P. Kelly has an extensive litigation and judicial background in both the public and private sectors. Wynne has worked in large law firms in New York, New York, and Miami, Florida, defending large companies in high stakes litigation. Wynne also served in the Department of Justice for over 16 years, first as a civil assistant United States attorney for the District of Columbia representing the United States government in federal court. Wynne has federal jury and bench trial experience, has argued before the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit numerous times, and has taken and defended dozens of depositions. Wynne remained in the Department of Justice after receiving an appointment by the Attorney General to become an immigration judge. Wynne developed a reputation for his preparedness and fairness in adjudicating the cases before him, resulting in his promotion to Assistant Chief Immigration Judge and, subsequently, to Principal Counsel for Conduct and Professionalism in the Office of the Director. Finally, Wynne was named Senior Counsel to the Associate Attorney General.

Judicial Experience

Wynne began his judicial career in February 2019 when he was appointed as an Immigration Judge at the Arlington, Virginia Immigration Court, while also serving details to the New York, New York Immigration Court and the Houston, Texas, Immigration Court. Wynne heard both detained and non-detained matters and developed a reputation for his preparation and inquisitive nature on the bench, but also his common-sense approach to adjudication.

From January 2023 until January 2025, Wynne served as an Assistant Chief Immigration Judge overseeing the Sterling, Virginia Immigration Court. In this role, he managed court operations, supervised administrative functions, and presided over complex immigration proceedings including deportation, exclusion, removal, and rescission hearings.

Because of Wynne’s skills as an adjudicator and a manager, leadership selected him to serve as a mentor to numerous immigration judges and attorney advisors, as well as to lead trainings for new immigration judges and advanced trainings for experienced adjudicators.

Senior Leadership

From January 2025 through May 2025, Wynne served as Senior Counsel to the Associate Attorney General working within the Sanctuary Cities Enforcement Working Group, a top priority of the Attorney General, analyzing the intersections of federal immigration law and various state laws and policies.

Prior to joining the Office of the Associate Attorney General, from June 2024 through January 2025, Wynne served as Principal Counsel for Conduct and Professionalism in the Office of the Director for EOIR, a Senior Leader (SL) appointment by the Attorney General. In this role, Wynne led a team of attorneys processing, investigating, and analyzing all complaints brought against immigration adjudicators nationwide. Wynne established new standard operating procedures including standardization of the initial triage of all allegations received, as well as designed supplemental training regimens when complaints identified correctable deficiencies. Wynne led numerous internal investigations and coordinated with various components of the Department of Justice depending upon the outcome of those investigations. Wynne also supervised the operations of the Equal Employment Opportunity office and worked closely with the Office of General Counsel and the Justice Management Division on numerous matters. Finally, Wynne served as an expert witness on federal immigration processes and procedures in federal court proceedings in the matter of Securities and Exchange Commission v. Mikhail Kokorich, No. 1:21-cv-01869 (D.D.C.).

Other Public Service

Prior to his judicial appointment, Wynne served as an Assistant United States Attorney for the District of Columbia in the Civil Division from November 2008 through February 2019. Wynne represented the United States in hundreds of civil proceedings before federal district courts and U.S. courts of appeal. He led numerous parallel civil investigations of companies for alleged waste, fraud, and abuse, primarily under the False Claims Act, and secured millions of dollars in settlements, fines, and penalties, for U.S. taxpayers. Further, Wynne served as lead counsel on numerous jury and bench trials, took and defended dozens of depositions, and submitted hundreds of dispositive pleadings. Wynne’s achievements earned widespread recognition including: the Attorney General’s Award for Distinguished Service; U.S. Attorney Special Achievement Awards (7); as well as commendations from, for example, the Judge Advocate General for the U.S. Army, the Acting Director for the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives, and the Department of Transportation.

Education and Professional Development

Wynne holds a Juris Doctor from the Fordham University School of Law, where he served as the Editor-in-Chief for the Fordham International Law Journal and an Associate Editor of the Fordham Moot Court Board. Wynne obtained a Bachelor of Arts with a double major in Government and English from Georgetown University.

Professional Memberships and Community Involvement

Wynne was admitted to the New Jersey Bar in 2006, the New York Bar in 2006, the Florida Bar in 2007, and the U.S. Supreme Court Bar in 2015. Wynne co-founded the Dave Nee Foundation, a 501(c)(3) not-for-profit corporation dedicated to raising awareness of depression and preventing suicide in the legal and law student community.

Awards and Honors

Honors

US Department of Justice, Attorney General Award for Distinguished Service, 2019

US Department of Justice, U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia Special Commendation, 2012 - 2019

Marist School, Young Alumnus of the Year, 2011

attorneys.name: Thomas G. Kennedy
attorneys.practice_type: Investment Management Regulation and Compliance Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Tom is a Partner in Macaluso, LLP’s Investment Management Regulation and Compliance Practice. Tom serves as counselor to institutional investors, issuers, funds, advisers, and broker dealers as well as service providers on regulatory and compliance legal matters including preparations for upcoming SEC rules, review and drafting of investment advisory and other contracts, disclosures, consents and no-action letter requests for various transactions, and advice concerning management and prevention of enforcement liability.

Tom Kennedy is a financial services compliance lawyer with nearly 30 years of experience in the investment management industry. His specific areas of expertise include counseling investment advisory firms (including those who advise private funds (e.g., hedge, private equity, venture capital, and funds of funds), registered investment companies, common and collective funds and separate accounts), broker dealers and banks/trust companies engaged in wealth management and fiduciary activities. He also has experience working with fund administrators, transfer agents and custodians.

Prior to joining Macaluso LLP in October 2024, Tom was a lawyer and compliance consultant serving as a Partner at Sadis & Goldberg LLP in their Regulatory Practice, and as a Managing Director, counsel and consultant with Abide Consulting Group.

Prior to serving as external counsel and consultant, Tom worked in-house as Chief Compliance Officer and held various other compliance and legal roles with growing responsibility for well-known banks, investment advisers and broker dealers including Morgan Stanley, JP Morgan, Citigroup, Arden Asset Management, Bessemer Investment Management and First Manhattan Co. Tom served as a ‘40 Act fund complex CCO for large and small open and closed end fund families, including the Old Westbury Funds, Inc. (Bessemer’s open end mutual fund family), the Arden Sage Funds (a closed end fund complex), and he drove the compliance program aspects of the launch of a series of novel liquid alternative open end mutual funds (which were part of the Arden Investment Series Trust), and First Manhattan’s first semi-transparent Exchange Traded Fund (NYSE: FMCX).

As a result of these roles, Tom has gained expertise in investment advisory, broker dealer and anti-money laundering and sanctions laws and regulations. He also possesses international experience with UK approved advisers, Irish UCITS funds, and other European fund and distribution schemes. Tom’s experience with firms, both large and small, gives him a unique understanding of regulatory needs for his clients in the asset management business.

Tom has significant experience as a liaison with various regulatory bodies including the SEC, FINRA, CFTC, NFA, OCC, Federal Reserve, DOL, FCA and others. Tom has appeared before the SEC, and helped regulators shape new regulations, and he has represented his firm in multiple matters; resolving enforcement matters and implementing remediation plans when necessary. Tom also supplied training to asset management examiners multiple times at the SEC, OCC and Fed’s request.

Tom also serves as a Managing Director, and Head of Institutional Asset Management for AltPilot Group

Via AltPilot, Tom offers institutional investment managers, investment companies, broker dealers and institutional investors, as well as service providers consulting on compliance risk management from designing and implementing compliance programs, to managing a wide range of compliance related functions like compliance program management, regulatory filings, mock exams, testing and assisting with examinations and audits.

Over the course of his career, he has been a sought-out participant and speaker in various industry group functions. Tom holds a Juris Doctor, cum laude, from St. John’s University School of Law, and a BA in Criminal Justice from Iona University. Tom is licensed to practice law in New York.

attorneys.name: David C. Kim
attorneys.practice_type: Agriculture Law & Agribusiness Lawyers in Mankato, MN
attorneys.bio:
Based on his prior experiences as an investment banker, David brings a unique balance between the law and business into his practice, which centers heavily around representing businesses and entrepreneurs in a wide range of areas including manufacturing, engineering, bio-science, financial and agricultural industries. Through his financial and legal career for over twenty years, David has accumulated expertise in corporate and commercial matters and regularly advises clients on $200 million to $500 million transactions each year. David often leads complex transactions across the U.S., as well as growing markets overseas such as Central and South America and Asia.

Practice Focus

David's practice focuses on all transactional aspects in (i) corporate mergers and acquisitions, (ii) sales and acquisitions of business interests and assets, (iii) debt, equity, and mezzanine financing, (iv) LBO transactions, (v) domestic and international joint venture formation and operation, (vi) technology licensing, (vii) IP protection, licensing, and administration, (viii) trademark and copyright registration, prosecution, and enforcement, (ix) regulatory compliance for production and manufacturing, (x) antitrust law compliance for production and distribution, including RPM and minimum price controls, (xi) complex tax planning and dispute resolution, and (xii) domestic and international trade clearance and general contract matters.

REPRESENTATIVE EXPERIENCE

Represented an electric automobile company in the U.S. in conjunction with its joint venture for the production and distribution of electric buses in a $400 million project by negotiating and drafting Shareholders Agreement for the joint venture.

Represented a bio-engineering company in a reverse triangular merger for its acquisition of target stock, regulatory clearance, and minority shareholder claim resolutions by negotiating and drafting the Agreement and Plan of Merger and all related documents and instruments.

Represented a client in a reverse triangular merger for its acquisition of the world's biggest DNA gene cloning and storage services provider.

Represented a client in a $60 million asset acquisition for domestic production assets by negotiating and drafting the Letter of Intent, Memorandum of Understanding, and Asset Purchase Agreement therefor, and performing due diligence, the Hart-Scott-Rodino clearance, WARN Act compliance, permitting process, and post-closing litigations.

Represented a client in an $80 million asset acquisition in conjunction with the competitive bidding process, leading the initial negotiations with the seller and seller's investment bankers and attorneys, drafting the Letter of Intent and performing due diligence in three states in the U.S., and advising client in conjunction with a Section 363 Sale proceeding.

Represented a client in conjunction with $330 million debt financing.

Represented a client in transactions involving Technology Licensing Agreements with various public universities in the U.S., Toll Manufacturing Agreements with custom manufacturers in the U.S. and foreign countries, patent applications, patent prosecutions, and trademark registrations in nine jurisdictions including the U.S., various countries in the E.U. through EPO, China, Japan, Korea, Mexico and Canada.

Represented a client in a joint venture transaction in China for the manufacture and distribution of pharmaceutical products in China.

Represented a client in a joint venture transaction in Korea for the manufacture and distribution of pharmaceutical products in Korea.

Represented a bio-tech client in a share exchange transaction focusing on the business valuation of IP rights of the target company—over $60 million.

Advised a client in developing their dealer agreement and sales representative forms in compliance with state laws and regulations over dealership and sales representative relationship in over twenty states in the U.S.

Represented a majority shareholder client in shareholder dispute involving $30 million equity investment, leading the matter to a favorable settlement and negotiating and drafting Release and Settlement Agreement.

Represented a client in procuring and administering overseas production capacities through Technology Licensing and Manufacturing Agreements, together with advising client for foreign government permitting process and clearing the U.S. export control laws and regulations.

Represented a joint venture formed by U.S. investors for a foreign asset investment in over $20 million, advising on the formation and administration of the joint venture, the formation and registration of its foreign subsidiaries and its U.S. tax reporting compliance.

Represented the major member in a $25 million LLC break-up case, negotiating and drafting the Membership Interest Purchase Agreement, Release and Settlement.

Represented a client in a $1 million AR collection matter in Vietnam.

Represented group of banks and financial organizations in a dispute on the ownership of the source code used to build their financial transaction platforms online.

Represented clients in commodity futures claims over $100 million in conjunction with MF Global bankruptcy.

Represented a European client in conjunction with their business launch in the U.S. by forming a U.S. subsidiary and advising the parent and subsidiary regarding the U.S. Federal and State laws and regulations on production and distribution.

Represented a client in an IRS action challenging the tax exempt status on the client's $9 million IDRB issued to finance production facility.

Represented a client in company restructuring with focus on the Section 108(a) COD income analysis and avoidance.

Represented a client in conjunction with a dispute regarding partnership loss allocation for tax purposes and application of the at-risk rules and substantial economic effect rules.

Represents clients in registering and managing trademark portfolio with over 600 trademarks; work includes trademark application, prosecution with examiners, trademark opposition proceedings, Section 8&15 Acknowledgements and Declarations, Section 8&9 Declarations and Renewals, and trademark Cease and Desist notices and litigations.

Represents clients in drafting, reviewing, and revising contracts in conjunction with their distribution of products in the U.S. and foreign countries.

attorneys.name: Jessica A. Kim
attorneys.practice_type: Family Lawyers in Eagan, MN
attorneys.bio:
"Sometimes people come together. Sometimes they drift apart. We'll help pave the way for your transition."

Jessica is a founding member of Oney & Kim, PLLC, where she compassionately guides clients through both positive and difficult transitions that families face.

Jessica provides strong and compassionate representation to family law clients seeking or going through a divorce, modification or establishment of custody or parenting time, a modification or establishment of child support, or a step-parent adoption. She has successfully assisted non-custodial parents in obtaining increased parenting time and concerned parents in obtaining orders for protection. Jessica has drafted and executed wills, trusts, and powers of attorney for both low-income clientele and those with significant assets.

Jessica has demonstrated a dedication to public service by volunteering over 150 hours of pro bono service assisting pro se litigants at the Hennepin County Family Justice Center and preparing tax returns for low-income individuals through AccountAbility Minnesota.

In addition to her work as an attorney, Jessica has received extensive training in family mediation and uses her prior experience as a Rule 114 qualified mediator to assist clients in negotiating divorce settlements and creating customized custody and parenting time schedules in the best interests of their children.

In her free time, Jessica enjoys an active lifestyle with her husband and their 3 children. Jessica also enjoys a passion for music performance and multi-cultural experiences through international travel.

attorneys.name: Brittany R. King
attorneys.practice_type: Agriculture Law & Agribusiness Lawyers in Mankato, MN
attorneys.bio:
Brittany King-Asamoa, a partner of Gislason & Hunter, focuses her practice on labor and employment law and civil litigation. She enjoys helping companies, agribusiness and human resource professionals navigate the intricacies of employment law. King-Asamoa takes great pride in her work litigating employment claims and counseling employers on employment laws, compliance and best practices. She frequently presents and writes articles on new laws impacting businesses in the areas of employment, business and agriculture.

King-Asamoa received her Juris Doctor, cum laude, from the University of Arkansas School of Law. She received her Master of Business Administration and Bachelor of Science in Human Resources Management degrees from the Minnesota State University, Mankato.

Outside of her legal practice, King-Asamoa joyously spends her time chasing her two young children with her husband.

attorneys.name: John A. Klassen
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Litigation - Employee Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
John is the founder of the Minneapolis employment and civil rights litigation firm of John A. Klassen, P.A. He received law degrees from the University of British Columbia (1992) and Seattle University (1993).

Since 1994, John has practiced exclusively in the areas of employment and civil rights law. He has represented employees and victims of civil rights violations throughout the United States, in the areas of harassment and discrimination law, False Claims Act/Qui Tam claims, whistleblower law, wage and hour disputes, class action claims, employment contract disputes, and sexual abuse. Employees consult with him on a regular basis in regard to their severance agreements and non-competition agreements.

John's cases have received international press coverage, including recent stories by the New York Times, the Washington Post and the International Herald Tribune. His cases have been featured on CNN and Minnesota Public Radio. In 2006 and 2007, John successfully litigated cases against the Minneapolis Fire Department and its fire chief for alleged sexual harassment and retaliation. This series of three related cases included this country's first known reverse sexual orientation discrimination case against the head of a large public agency. Past victories on behalf of victims of workplace discrimination and harassment include million dollar-range results for his clients.

John lives and works in the heart of Minneapolis, Minnesota. He is married and has two children.

attorneys.name: Michelle Kniess
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Inver Grove Heights, MN
attorneys.bio:
Meet the Founder of Mosaic Family Law & Mediation

With nearly 20 years of experience, Michelle leads clients through all kinds of family conflict. From divorce to custody and parenting time disputes, Michelle listens to her clients and advises them along the path to resolution. Michelle understands the interplay between litigation and Alternative Dispute Resolution and can skillfully advise clients in navigating those systems. She has represented numerous clients in Minnesota and Wisconsin courts, through motion hearings and trials. She is a Minnesota Qualified Neutral Mediator and is trained in Parenting Consulting, FENE/SENE and Moderated Settlement Conference. Michelle is a current and prior business owner, has been a member of both large and small law firms, and was a student judicial intern for a state Supreme Court Justice.

Michelle earned her law degree from the University of Wisconsin- Madison, and her business management degree from the University of Wisconsin-La Crosse. She recently earned her Masters Degree in Theological Studies from Bethel University. Her education, skills and experience make her a fierce, yet compassionate advocate.

attorneys.name: Jason Kohlmeyer
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Mankato, MN
attorneys.bio:
Born and raised on the prairie of Western Minnesota, Jason spent his summers on his uncle's farm, which taught him the importance of getting the job done right the first time.

While still a high school student, Jason enlisted in the Army Reserve and went on to serve as an Army Intelligence Analyst after graduation. Then he pursued his education at Concordia College in Moorhead, Minnesota, becoming a High School social studies teacher in White Bear Lake, Minnesota. During this time, he realized his deep-rooted desire to help others resolve their problems, which led him to follow his dream to become a lawyer. In 2000, Jason graduated from Hamline University School of Law in St. Paul, Minnesota.

After gaining valuable experience at the Dakota County Attorney's Office, Jason realized the crucial need for personalized attention and genuine empathy in the legal profession. This understanding motivated him to take up a position in the private sector. After nearly a decade of service with a top-tier boutique trial firm in southern Minnesota, he decided to help clients a little differently and opened his own firm in 2008. Since its inception, Kohlmeyer Hagen has evolved into one of the busiest and largest family and criminal defense firms in southern Minnesota.

Jason has been a prominent speaker at international conferences, sharing his insights on family law issues with the American Bar Association, MN State bar Association, MN Continuing legal Education and the American Association of Justice. Since 2010, he has dedicated his practice exclusively to Family Law, helping clients navigate through challenges related to divorce, spousal support, child custody, and farm and business divorces.

Since 2000, Jason calls Mankato home, where he lives with his wife and children. An avid adventure motorcyclist, Jason has tackled adventures across the Himalayas on a Royal Enfield, through the northern highlands of Vietnam, and the Greek Isles on a Yamaha, as well as the Rockies and the Great Plains. addition to his legal career and motorcycle adventures, Jason has penned his first book titled "The Divorce Survival Guide: Getting Divorced in Minnesota", available in print and Kindle edition on Amazon.com

attorneys.name: Scott E. Korzenowski
attorneys.practice_type: Franchise Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Scott E. Korzenowski is a partner in Dady & Gardner, P.A., who has successfully helped dozens of franchisees and dealers achieve successful resolutions to their disputes with their franchisors and manufacturers, including franchisees in the Nursefinders, Staff Builders, Jamba Juice, Dairy Queen, Pizza Hut and Subway systems. Scott also has helped shape the law to provide additional protections for franchisees and dealers. In Romeo Maintenance & Rental v. U-Haul Co. of Minnesota, Bus. Franchise Guide (CCH) ¶12,259 (Minn. Dist. Ct. Feb. 13, 2002), Scott and John Holland successfully argued that U-Haul's requirement that its dealers maintain dedicated phone lines and install electronic data bases could qualify as franchise fees under the Minnesota Franchise Act. And in Town & Country Equipment, Inc. v. Deere & Company, Inc., 133 F. Supp. 2d 665 (W.D. Tenn. 2000), Scott successfully argued that the implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing required John Deere to act reasonably in deciding whether to approve a dealer's relocation request. Scott also has successfully argued that state dealership laws apply to dealers located in those states despite contrary choice-of-law provisions in the dealership agreements. Cromeens v. AB Volvo, 369 F.3d 376 (7th Cir. 2003); Volvo Construction Equipment North America, Inc. v. CLM Equip. Co., Inc., 386 F.3d 581 (4th Cir. 2004). Scott also has successfully argued that a manufacturer’s decision to re-brand a line of equipment does not provide the manufacturer with good cause to terminate the dealership agreement. Volvo Trademark Holding Aktiebolaget v. AIS Constr. Equip. Corp., 416 F. Supp. 2d 404 (W.D.N.C. 2006); FMS, Inc. v. Volvo Construction Equipment North America, Inc., 2005 WL 843119 (N.D. Ill. 2005).

In addition to his trial experience, which includes several cases before juries and arbitrators, Scott has drafted a successful petition to the United States Supreme Court, and has argued appellate cases before the Minnesota Court of Appeals, Minnesota Supreme Court and the United States Court of Appeals for the Fourth, Seventh and Eighth Circuits.

Scott graduated from the University of Minnesota with a Bachelor of Arts degree in Journalism, and later graduated magna cum laude from the University of Minnesota Law School, where he served as an associate managing editor of the Minnesota Law Review. Following law school, Scott clerked for The Honorable Esther Tomljanovich of the Minnesota Supreme Court. While at the Supreme Court, Scott helped author a chapter for The Minnesota Insurance Law Deskbook, outlining legal strategies for procuring insurance coverage for hazardous waste cleanup.

Scott has fought many successful battles for the "little guy." While with the Minnesota Law Review, Scott authored and published an article entitled, "Valuable in Life, Valuable in Death, Why Not Valuable When Severely Injured" that supported the proposition that Minnesota should recognize loss-of-consortium damages between parents and their severely injured children. Scott wrote the article after helping a local attorney receive a favorable settlement for a client whose young child had been severely injured by a negligent driver for a large linen supplier.

Scott also has first-hand experience with franchisee-franchisor issues, having watched as his father, a former franchisee restaurant owner, struggled with his franchisor over a period of years prior to a successful termination of the relationship in the late 1980s.

A former journalist and radio talk-show host, Scott has extensive writing and speaking experience. Prior to entering law school, Scott was a nationally recognized columnist with the Gannett News Service and later served as a copy editor for the Star-Tribune of Minneapolis and as a morning-drive talk-show host for a major Minneapolis/St. Paul radio station. In his spare time, Scott loves to watch sports and play golf.

attorneys.name: Beverly "B.J." Kranz
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in South St Paul, MN
attorneys.bio:
"I use thorough preparation and detailed planning to execute the best strategy for each client in every case. With an early background in insurance defense followed by long record of diligent and compassionate representation of injured people, I have the skills and experience to examine all facets of each personal injury matter and then formulate the over-all plan of representation. My goal is to enhance monetary recovery for every client, while providing each client with a sense of justice done and enthusiasm for moving forward with their lives."

Over her decades of legal practice, B.J. has represented clients over a broad range of individuals and corporations; B.J. spent the early years of her legal career representing insurance companies in the defense of personal injury and medical malpractice matters. In joining Montpetit Kranz, PLLC, she has converted a comprehensive understanding of insurance company strategies and tactics into a thorough and successful representation of those who have suffered personal injury from a vehicle collision, slip and fall, malpractice or other accident. In addition, together with her law partner, Bill Kranz, she has successfully represented family members bringing wrongful death claims on behalf of a deceased loved one. Bill and B.J.'s combined years of experience, together with their balanced and detailed approach, has resulted in successful representation of clients at both pre-litigation negotiation and arbitration, and at trial. They are dedicated to generating the best possible outcome for each client. Bill and BJ are proud that the firm's representation of clients in both personal injury and wrongful death cases has resulted in several recent pre-trial settlements exceeding a million dollars.

B.J. is a life-long resident of the south metro suburbs. After attending Simley High School in Inver Grove Heights, she obtained her Bachelor of Science degree in paralegal studies from Winona State University, and her law degree from William Mitchell College of Law. During law school, B.J. clerked for the Minnesota State Public Defender's Office and several private practice firms. She also was selected to serve on the William Mitchell Law Review for three consecutive years, as a Writer, Editor, and Executive Editor. Following law school graduation, B.J. clerked for a First Judicial District Court Judge and later clerked for a Minnesota Appellate Court Judge, where she learned courtroom practice and judicial perspective at both the trial and appellate level. Since that time, B.J. has spent most of her time in representing individuals who have suffered personal injury as a result of an auto, work-related or premises accidents--putting forth personalized, effective representation for every client.

When not practicing law, B.J. enjoys reading, traveling, and following the Minnesota Lynx and Minnesota Timberwolves

attorneys.name: Keanu Krech
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Eagan, MN
attorneys.bio:
Keanu Krech began his journey into law with a unique and inspiring background. Initially, he pursued a degree in pastoral ministry and undertook life-changing adventures, such as cycling across the United States to raise funds for food and education programs in Thailand and canoeing down the Mississippi River to raise money to combat sex trafficking. Inspired by Bob Goff’s book “Love Does,” Keanu decided to explore a career in law.

Keanu excelled in law school, where his passion for criminal defense truly took root. As a certified student attorney in the criminal and juvenile defense clinic, he represented clients ranging from juveniles to adults charged with petty misdemeanors, felonies, and everything in between. This hands-on experience, coupled with the mentorship he received, solidified his commitment to becoming a criminal defense attorney. Keanu is dedicated to being a client-centered and reasonable attorney, always prioritizing the best interests of his clients. He believes in understanding their goals and working tirelessly to achieve favorable outcomes.

Joining Sieben Edmunds Miller was a natural fit for Keanu. Recommended by a trusted professor, Keanu found the firm’s personable and humble environment appealing. The open-door mentorship policy and supportive culture at Sieben Edmunds Miller align with his values, making it an ideal place for him to grow as a legal professional. He appreciates the firm’s close-knit, laid-back atmosphere, where attorneys are approachable and patient, fostering a conducive learning environment for a new law clerk.

Keanu’s diverse background includes public speaking, entrepreneurship, and various legal internships. He has worked as a youth pastor, started and sold a window and gutter cleaning company, and gained experience in family law at a nonprofit in Stillwater. His time at a criminal defense firm in Minneapolis provided invaluable insights into sentencing and the importance of being a reasonable attorney. These experiences equip him with a unique perspective and strong people skills, enabling him to approach each case with empathy and dedication.

Keanu is motivated by a deep-seated belief in restorative justice, aiming to treat clients with dignity and respect. He views his role as an advocate not just in legal terms but also in helping clients through difficult times without judgment or shame. His values shape his approach to the justice system, emphasizing humility, compassion, and understanding.

Outside of work, Keanu enjoys spending time with friends, fishing, running, reading, exploring the outdoors, and treasure hunting. Whether hanging out with friends or pursuing his hobbies, Keanu’s diverse interests reflect his dynamic personality and zest for life.

Keanu’s goal is to make a positive impact on the lives of clients and colleagues alike, ensuring that everyone feels supported and understood.

attorneys.name: Eileen Krenner
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Oakdale, MN
attorneys.bio:
Eileen Krenner began her career in Family Law in 2001 while working as a filing clerk in Ramsey County Family Court Administration. Working in Court Administration provided her a knowledge base of court resources and an understanding of the rules and requirements for filing as well as court procedures. While clerking for the child support magistrates and Referee Beddow in Ramsey County Family Court she obtained extensive opportunities to observe multiple hearings and a variety of case types and fact patterns.

While employed as an Assistant County Attorney for the Ramsey County Attorney's office she obtained first-hand experience working on cases while the new child support laws were enacted in 2007. Through this experience she worked on complex child support case as well as appeared in hundreds of hearings in both district court and the expedited process.

After working with a well reputed family law attorney for several years, Eileen opened her own practice, Krenner Law. In private practice she has represented clients in mediation, early neutral evaluations, and litigation actions to modify their divorce decree and other complex arrears of family both financial and social. She has experience working with a variety of different cases and clients from all walks of life.

attorneys.bio:
Since 2003, my legal practice has focused exclusively on Minnesota family law, including divorce; property division (marital and non-marital); spousal maintenance; custody and parenting time; jurisdictional issues, child support; and paternity.

While I still provide direct representation on a limited, case-by-case basis, my work today is focused primarily on serving as a neutral. I regularly act as a mediator, parenting consultant, arbitrator, and moderator of settlement conferences, helping families and professionals resolve disputes efficiently, thoughtfully, and with lasting solutions in mind.

Whether advocating for a client or facilitating resolution as a neutral, my commitment remains the same: to approach every matter with clarity, candor, and a focus on achieving durable, practical outcomes.

attorneys.name: Sherri L. Krueger
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Minnetonka, MN
attorneys.bio:
Sherri L. Krueger is a partner at Krueger, Juelich & Schmisek PLLC in Minnetonka, Minnesota.

Sherri's representation of her clients is family focused and based on practical problem-solving approaches to best position her clients for outcomes aligning with their interests and goals. Sherri is a strong and diligent advocate in negotiation and settlement as well as in court.

Whether the most significant issues facing her clients are related to children, financial interests, or both, Sherri understands the internal emotional and practical struggles facing her clients and their families. With respect and dedication, Sherri guides, coaches, and advises her clients in creating, implementing, and following a course of action to manage each case and to respond to the unique dynamics arising throughout the matter.

Sherri believes that a family is still a family, even when living in two different homes. With this focus, she strives to help her clients achieve an outcome that focuses on the long-term impact, as well as the short-term impact the dispute will have on all family members.

As a Rule 114 Qualified Neutral, Sherri provides mediation services in addition to representing clients in family law disputes. Sherri provides both facilitative and evaluative mediation with a special passion for helping families resolve custody and parenting time disputes. She is also trained to provide private Early Neutral Evaluations in both custody and parenting matters as well as for financial issues, and is trained as a Parenting Consultant.

Sherri offers alternative representation options, including limited-scope representation and advice-only consultations. She understands that guidance and advice is essential to someone experiencing family law issues, and she encourages all parties to obtain information about their legal matters even if they determine to proceed as a self-represented party.

Sherri is actively involved with the Association of Family and Conciliation Courts (AFCC), and previously served on the board for the Minnesota chapter. Sherri volunteers her time to provide legal assistance for the legal self-help center and legal clinics in Scott County, the limited-scope representation program in Hennepin County, and the Ramsey County Volunteer Mediation program. While in law school, Sherri volunteered with Legal Assistance of Dakota County through the Minnesota Justice Foundation (MJF), serving as a student certified attorney in the area of Family Law. She continues to assist the community by volunteering through various legal clinics.

Sherri was selected to the Minnesota Super Lawyers Rising Star list in 2011, 2012, and 2013, a designation given to no more than 2.5% of attorneys in the state. Sherri was selected to the Minnesota Super Lawyers list every year since 2014.

Daniel Kufus represents clients in drafting and execution of estate planning documents. He has experience with Wills, Trusts, and Supplemental/Special Needs Trusts. In addition, Daniel Kufus has represented heirs, devisees, trust beneficiaries, guardians, conservators, trustees, and personal representatives in hundreds of probate matters. Challenging the validity of a will or trust based on diminished capacity and undue influence

Defending wills and trusts against claims of diminished capacity or undue influence

Representing trust beneficiaries

Disputes regarding whether a guardianship/conservatorship should be established

attorneys.practice_type: Workers’ Compensation: Lawyers in Brainerd, MN
attorneys.bio:
Alex Kuhn practices in the areas of workers’ compensation, personal injury, real estate, collections, and civil litigation. Alex especially enjoys working with injured workers, helping them navigate the confusing and often intimidating world of workers’ compensation in order to get the compensation they deserve. He handles accepted claims as well as denied claims and will gladly sit down with an injured worker for a free consultation to help alleviate any concerns they may have. Alex is an advocate for his clients and understands that trust is a fundamental aspect of representing injured workers. That is why Alex makes sure to listen to his clients concerns while also communicating consistently and clearly so that the client feels informed throughout the process.

Alex is currently the President for the Aitkin/Crow Wing County Bar Association, a past President for the Brainerd Kiwanis Club, and member of the Minnesota State Bar Association. Alex is a graduate of Concordia College in Moorhead and William Mitchell College of Law.

Alex grew up in the Brainerd Lakes Area and appreciates the opportunity to be working near his family and friends. Outside of work, Alex enjoys golfing, spending time on the lake and watching the Minnesota Vikings.

attorneys.bio:
John D. Lamey III graduated, cum laude, from William Mitchell College of Law in 2001. Prior to founding Lamey Law Firm, Mr. Lamey clerked for the Honorable Paulette Kane Flynn in Ramsey County, practiced tax law at Pricewaterhouse Coopers LLP, and was in-house counsel for Marquette Financial Companies. Mr. Lamey concentrates his practice on personal and business bankruptcy, secured lending, and general business and corporate law. Mr. Lamey’s passion is helping debtors through the complex bankruptcy code to ensure them a fresh start. Mr. Lamey also represents clients in contested bankruptcies and other litigation in bankruptcy court. Mr. Lamey is a member of the Minnesota State Bar Association, the MSBA Bankruptcy Section (fomer chairman), and was the former Editor-in-Chief of the Bankruptcy Section's Case Update Publication. Mr. Lamey has filed over 4000 bankruptcy petitions in Minnesota and Wisconsin.

attorneys.name: Stephanie S. Lamphere
attorneys.practice_type: Consumer Collections & Creditors’ Remedies – Colecciones de consumidores Lawyers in Plymouth, MN
attorneys.bio:
Stephanie is an attorney focusing in criminal law at Groshek Law P.A. Prior to joining Groshek Law P.A. in 2016, Stephanie worked at the Minnesota House of Representatives as the lead staff member to the Mining and Outdoor Recreation Policy Committee. Her legislative experience gives her a unique perspective to bring to her practice, as she is able to provide her clients with relevant knowledge of newly enacted laws that impact each legal case.

While attending Pepperdine University School of Law in Malibu, California, Stephanie worked as a certified law clerk in the Compton Branch of the Los Angeles District Attorney's Office. In Compton, Stephanie was exposed to a variety of criminal cases and gained valuable experience in state district court. Stephanie also worked as a law clerk at Beach Cowdrey Owen, LLP, a premier insurance defense law firm in southern California, assisting in the civil litigation defense of healthcare facilities. In 2012, Stephanie completed an internship in federal district court with the Honorable Samuel Der-Yeghiayan in the Northern District of Illinois.

In 2013, Stephanie was selected to serve as co-captain of Pepperdine Law School's nationally-ranked moot court competition team. She led the team as an appellate advocate, competing in Washington, D.C., Chicago, Gulfport, San Diego, and Hong Kong, where she secured domestic and international championship titles. Stephanie also served as Note and Comment Editor of the National Association of Administrative Law Judiciary Law Journal. Stephanie graduated from Pepperdine Law in 2014 and was inducted into the National Order of Barristers, an honors society of the top oral advocates of her graduating class. Before Pepperdine Law, Stephanie graduated from Wheaton College in Wheaton, Ill. with honors.

Awards and Honors

Inductee, National Order of Barristers, 2014

attorneys.name: Korine L. Land
attorneys.practice_type: Municipal and Governmental Law Lawyers in Eagan, MN
attorneys.bio:
Kori Land joined LeVander in 1996 as an associate and became a shareholder in 2002. Kori concentrates her practice on municipal and government law, land use, and development. She serves as the City Attorney for the cities of Cottage Grove, Stillwater, South St. Paul, Lilydale and Sunfish Lake and as general counsel to the South Metro Fire Department. As a City Attorney, she has experience in open meeting law, data practices, ordinances, employment law, problem properties, land use, zoning & planning, economic development, residential development, public improvement projects and many other aspects of municipal law.

Kori attended law school at William Mitchell College of Law in St. Paul, Minnesota, where she received her Juris Doctorate with honors. She holds a bachelor’s degree in English and Spanish from Augustana University in Sioux Falls, South Dakota. Kori is admitted to the bar in Minnesota, Wisconsin, and U.S. District Court District of Minnesota. She is a regular speaker at the Minnesota Association of City Attorneys’ conferences as well as at other government organizations, speaking around the state to help guide elected officials and city planners on the ever-changing issues they face. In her spare time, Kori enjoys volunteering her time at Trinity Lutheran Church and Academy in Hudson, WI, on various committees.
