Debbie is a partner at Minnesota's largest and most experienced criminal defense law firm. Before moving into private legal practice, Debbie worked in a City Attorney's Office in Anoka County and later represented thousands of clients charged with criminal offenses in the Ramsey County court system. She has achieved succcessful results in a wide variety of criminal cases, including criminal sexual conduct, DWI, domestic assault, drug possession/sale, fraud/theft, and homicide. Debbie has earned a reputation as an attorney who will vigorously advocate for her clients to ensure that their rights are not violated.

Debbie is a requested speaker on diverse criminal law topics, including property forfeiture, trial strategy and field sobriety testing in DWI cases. She was an adjunct profession at Hamline University within the Legal Studies department for years. Debbie has repeatedly been voted a "Rising Star" by Super Lawyers, an honor held by no more than 2.5% of Minnesota lawyers. She has also been recognized as one of the "Top 100 Trial Lawyers" in the country by the National Trial Lawyers Association and "Top 10 Under 40 Attorney Award" by the National Academy of Criminal Defense Attorneys.

attorneys.name: Gregory A. Lang
attorneys.practice_type: Business & Commercial Law Lawyers in Chanhassen, MN
attorneys.bio:
Greg is recognized for his ability to formulate down to earth, practical solutions for his client's complex problems. He has the ability to explain difficult issues and complicated legal theories in understandable, every day language that his clients can understand. Helping clients achieve their objectives is Greg's primary goal.

Real Estate. Greg is a Real Property Law Specialist. He represents individuals and businesses in residential and commercial real estate settings. He is experienced in all areas of real estate.

Experienced Estate Planner. Greg has substantial experience in planning the estates of his clients. He has worked with all sizes of estates ranging from large, multi-million dollar estates to more modest estates.

Business and Corporate Law. In his business law practice, Greg provides advice as outside general counsel to privately held businesses. He assists his clients in contracts, negotiation, employment issues, mergers, acquisitions and succession planning.

Trial and Arbitration. He is a seasoned trial attorney having litigated significant disputes involving probate, real estate and business matters.

Education and Specialization. J. D. cum laude. Greg earned his law degree, J.D. cum laude, from the Hamline University School of Law in 1977. He pursued his undergraduate education in economics at the University of Minnesota , where he was awarded his Bachelor of Arts degree. Greg is a Real Property Law Specialist, certified by the Minnesota State Bar Association. Minnesota Law & Politics magazine has named Greg a Super Lawyer, a designation reserved for only 5 percent of the total lawyers in the state.

Professional History. Greg was granted a license to practice law in 1977. He was admitted to practice before the Minnesota State Courts and the United States District Court of Minnesota in 1977. Greg is an active member of the Minnesota and Hennepin County Bar Associations. He is a member of the Real Estate Legislative Committee where he reviews and drafts legislation for action by the Minnesota legislature. He has worked as an attorney for the Minnesota Supreme Court and served as the Director of the Supreme Court Judicial Planning Committee. He has also served as counsel to a community foundation as well as general counsel for an estate planning company. Greg has now been engaged in private practice since 1983.

Personal. A Minnesota native, Greg was born in northern Minnesota and raised on the shores of Mille Lacs Lake. He moved to the Twin Cities to complete his education and made his home in the Twin City area. He is married and is the proud father of three children. His children have now grown to adulthood, graduated from college and are successfully making their way in the world. Greg's pet charity is the MS Society for which he is an active fundraiser. An Eagle Scout himself, he still enjoys working with the Boy Scouts. He enjoys traveling, bicycling, reading and the outdoors.

attorneys.name: Jacob Lanthier
attorneys.practice_type: Social Security Disability Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Jacob originally comes from Andover, Minnesota. He went to college at the University of Minnesota where he studied History and Classical Civilizations. Jacob knew he wanted to become an attorney early on. During college he worked for numerous employers including a small law firm in Minneapolis and the Minneapolis office of a U.S. Senator. He graduated with distinction in 2017 after three years. Jacob accepted a position at the University of Minnesota Law School and continued on at the University of Minnesota after graduating with his undergraduate degree.

During Law School, Jacob focused on litigation and gaining practical experience. Jacob interned for a Hennepin County Judge his first summer during law school and served as a research assistant to one of his professors. During his second year, Jacob worked at the Student Legal Services and took classes tailored to litigation. Additionally, Jacob served as a Student Attorney in two of the University of Minnesota Law School's clinics where he assisted low income individuals with family law, unemployment, and tax issues. During his final year in Law School, Jacob served as the managing director for the Law School's Civil Rights/Civil Liberties Moot Court and worked at a small general practice firm and the Minneapolis City Attorney's Office.

Jacob lives in Northeast Minneapolis with his girlfriend and cat. In his free time, he enjoys reading, cooking, and working with his hands.

When serving his clients, John can bring many aspects of the game into play - staying on course, making decisive commitments and weighing risks and rewards to achieve success. As a former business owner, John brings a well-rounded perspective from all sides of business to his clients.

attorneys.name: Jan C. Larson
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Law Lawyers in Buffalo, MN
attorneys.bio:
A Buffalo native, Jan Larson graduated from Buffalo High School, received his degree from the University of Minnesota, and his Juris Doctorate from William Mitchell College of Law. Jan was admitted to practice law in Minnesota State and Federal Courts in 1986 and began his practice of law with a Minneapolis law firm that same year. In 1987 Jan had the opportunity to return to practice in his hometown of Buffalo, and has been with the firm of Johnson, Larson & Peterson, P.A. since that time.

As a Real Property Law Specialist certified by the Minnesota State Bar Association since 1994, Jan has counseled clients through a wide variety of real estate transactions, ranging from complex commercial and residential development projects to assisting clients with the purchase or sale of a home. In the areas of Estate Planning, Jan has been recognized as a Five Star Wealth Manager in Twin Cities Business and Mpls. St. Paul Magazines. He is experienced in counseling clients with a wide range of needs - from drafting complex Wills and Trusts for large estates, to planning for persons with special needs, and planning for young couples and individuals with minor children.

Jan is a member of the Minnesota State Bar Association and the 18th District Bar Association. Community service is important to Jan. He has volunteered his time to serve on the Minnesota Department of Health Newborn Screening Advisory Committee, Elim Care Foundation Board, Buffalo Hospital Ethics Committee, Boy Scouts, and various positions and committees at his church. Jan is married to his wife, Lib, and together they have two adult sons.

attorneys.name: Ben Lavoie
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Ben has been an associate with Lindell & Lavoie, LLP, since 2004, and he law clerked at the office in the two summers prior to that. Since that time, he has become an integral piece in the firm's ongoing success. He has a varied practice, primarily focusing on personal injury and workers' compensation cases, but he loves appellant work and has a special interest in Section 1983 Civil Rights cases.

He has recovered millions of dollars for his clients over that period and has been significantly involved in notable and important cases. In 2012, Ben partnered with his friend and colleague, Grim Howland, to successful resolve a $4 million dollar medical malpractice claim on behalf of his disabled client. That same year, he partnered on a ground breaking workers' compensation civil penalties case with Jim Lindell, successfully arguing at the United States Court of Appeals for the 8th Circuit that the district court erred in granting summary judgment to the defendants and that Plaintiff could prove that the defendants intentionally obstructed her workers' compensation benefits in violation of Minnesota law. See Nunn v. Noodles & Company, and Zurich American Ins. Co., 674 F.3d 910 (8th Cir. 2012). Soon after that decision, Ben and Jim were able to resolve that case for their client, earning her an extraordinary but confidential settlement.

Ben believes that many of the skills he acquired during his years of bartending and teaching English abroad prior to law school have helped immensely in his law practice. He prides himself on making people feel comfortable when explaining to him their problems and concerns, just like he did from behind the bar. Ben is also excellent at distilling complicated legal issues into language and examples that permit his clients to fully understand the strengths and weaknesses of their cases. Ben's clients feel comfortable knowing they have the information they need to make the best decisions for themselves and they have a friend and fine attorney on their side until the end.

Ben has been consistently recognized by his colleagues for his work, successes and devotion to his clients, earning the distinction as one of Minnesota's Rising Stars, by Minnesota Law & Politics magazine 2007, 2008, 2009, 2010 and 2011. This accolade is awarded to just 2.5 percent of attorneys under the age of 40 or who have been practicing less than 10 years. The selection process is peer nominated and reviewed.

Cases:

Motor Scooter Crash - Vespa rider who was knocked off scooter by van while changing lanes proves she suffered a brain injury that changed her life. Result - $1,350,000

Medical Malpractice - Doctor's negligent administration of a routine procedure results in catastrophic injury to a 49 year old woman. Result - $4,000,000 settlement.

Personal Injury - Bicyclist hit by car, sent to collections for car damage, gets the final say on fault. Result - $100,000 settlement.

Slip and Fall - Strip mall's icy sidewalk causes bad fall. Result - $105,000 after Mediation.

Workers' Compensation - Worker's lung condition linked to auto body job. Result: $175,000 plus Medical Benefits left open.

attorneys.name: Timothy D. Lees
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Edina, MN
attorneys.bio:
Timothy Lees earned his undergraduate degree from Gustavus Adolphus College in 1989, and graduated cum laude from William Mitchell College of Law in 1993. Mr. Lees is licensed to practice in the State of Minnesota, U.S. District Court, and the Courts of the Prairie Island Mdewakanton Dakota Community, and the Shakopee Mdewakanton Sioux (Dakota) Community. Mr. Lees is a member of the Minnesota State Bar Association and Ramsey County Bar Association. Since 1994 he has engaged in private practice, and has been named by his peers as a Rising Star and as a Super Lawyer. He has significant successful trial and appellate experience.

Timothy Lees believes that, at its core, the divorce process must be seen as damage control: Minimize the damage to your finances; minimize the damage to your children; and minimize the impact that the divorce will have on your life going forward. Accordingly, settlement should be pursued at the earliest opportunity in the proceedings. This presumes, of course, that both sides are willing to come to the table, make full disclosure, and truly desire settlement. Resolving issues via negotiated agreement allows you to have input and participate in the decisions that will affect you and your family, versus requiring the Court to make these decisions based on a trial where the Court cannot possibly learn everything that is important regarding you and your family. Mr. Lees likes to say that resolving a case through negotiation allows you to divide your property with a scalpel, whereas the Court may resolve it with a meat cleaver. Not all cases need be a war. In fact, most divorce cases are resolved by settlement.

However, Mr. Lees also recognizes that there are cases that cannot be settled, and that litigation and trial are at times necessary. The difficult issues which tend to reach trial include spousal maintenance, child custody, complex property cases, and nonmarital claims. Mr. Lees is very comfortable yet dynamic in the courtroom, and understands that results are garnered by a clean, neat, and cogent presentation of the evidence.

attorneys.name: Robert J. Leighton
attorneys.practice_type: Disability Claims Lawyers in Minnetonka, MN
attorneys.bio:
Rob Leighton is a magna cum laude graduate of the University of Minnesota and a 1991 law school graduate of the University of California at Berkeley, where he served as Moot Court Co-Director. Since graduation from law school he has been admitted to practice in State and Federal Courts in Minnesota. He is a member of the Minnesota and Hennepin County Bar Associations, and also served as past President of the Mower County Bar Association while practicing law in southern Minnesota. He is also an active member of the Minnesota Association for Justice and served on its Board of Governors for 10 years. Mr. Leighton was honored with the MNAJ’s “Excellence Award” for his dedication to the legal profession.

Mr. Leighton has extensive experience in the area of civil litigation and has tried and settled cases involving disability claims, personal injury, wrongful death, product liability, and business disputes. In addition to his litigation practice, Mr. Leighton also represents trade and professional associations before governmental and regulatory bodies.

Mr. Leighton served four terms in the Minnesota House of Representatives, serving as both Assistant Majority Leader and Assistant Minority Leader. He was also appointed a member of the Workers Compensation Advisory Council, which advises the Commissioner of the Minnesota Department of Labor & Industry on necessary changes to Minnesota's workers compensation laws.

Mr. Leighton was raised in Austin, Minnesota and presently lives in Edina with his wife Anna and children. His volunteer activities include youth sports and serving as a member of non-profit community organizations.

attorneys.bio:

Since returning to Minnesota in 1983, he has practiced in the area of workers' compensation law. Initially, he was a defense lawyer for an insurance company and then switched to representing injured workers. He devotes 100 percent of his practice to plaintiffs' workers' compensation cases. Jerry assists clients from all over the state with the help of a very experienced and knowledgeable staff. When injured workers have questions about their rights or benefits, Jerry has answers. Practicing solely in the area of workers' compensation enables Jerry and his staff to keep on top of the many changes in this complex area of law.

attorneys.practice_type: Insurance Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Justice is a veteran litigator and trial lawyer who brings nearly twenty years of respected “big firm” experience with him to the Greenstein Sellers team. With a broad clientele that includes local enterprises and multinational corporations, Justice excels in navigating the intricacies of legal disputes across state and federal jurisdictions. He prides himself on his ability to deliver nuanced, strategic counsel that evolves with his clients' needs. Mr. Lindell's practice covers an extensive range of sectors, including residential and commercial property insurance, consumer goods, medical devices, real estate, and construction. attorneys.name: Jeffrey J. Lindquist
attorneys.practice_type: Workers’ Compensation Lawyers in St. Michael, MN
attorneys.bio:
Jeff has 35 years experience defending clients, large and small, in a wide array of civil litigation matters venued in Minnesota state, federal, and administrative courts. He is a recognized and respected workers’ compensation attorney, and is a chapter author of the Minnesota Workers’ Compensation Desk Book. Jeff has extensive employment law experience covering the full range of employment-related legal services, from consulting on policies and practices, to litigating complex employment disputes, such as wrongful termination and employment discrimination claims. Jeff has also successfully defended clients in broad variety of other civil litigation matters, ranging from personal injury cases to complex commercial disputes. As an experienced appellate lawyer, Jeff serves on the Amicus Committee of the Minnesota Defense Lawyers Association, and has written numerous friend-of-the-court briefs on behalf of that organization.

Outside the office, Jeff volunteers extensively in his home community of St. Michael, including many years of coaching youth sports, working with non-profit groups, and promoting the arts. He is a former Board Member and Board Chair of the St. Michael-Albertville School Board. Jeff loves music, and moonlights as a singer-guitarist in a weekend rock-and-roll band.

Litman & Associates to handle all of their IP needs, including Patent Application drafting, prosecution and appeals; Patent Licensing; Validity and Infringement Opinions; litigation management; and general IP counseling.

Mark A. Litman & Associates have extensive international prosecution experience in a wide range of technologies and can assist in all forms of domestic and international IP filings, including the Patent Cooperation Treaty applications, European patent Applications, Eurasian Patent Application filings, and individual country national filings throughout the world.

Officers and scientists in the companies who are our clients include many individuals who have worked with Mark A. Litman for 5 to 25 years and have come to depend on the individual attention given to them. The majority of new business to our firm comes from client referrals rather then referrals from law firms. There is no better recommendation of our work than this confidence.

attorneys.name: Jeffrey L. Loftness
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce & Family Law Lawyers in Shakopee, MN
attorneys.bio:
I practice exclusively in the areas of family law and criminal defense, with a special focus on high-conflict cases. I have represented clients from a wide range of social, cultural and economic backgrounds, and my assistance has been sought in many complex procedural and jurisdictional issues. I often represent individuals with highly sensitive subject matters, the outcome of which may have an impact on that person’s teaching, childcare or gaming license. I consider professionalism and absolute confidentiality to be critically important with respect to my services.

As someone who was born and raised in Shakopee, I grew up in the Twin Cities area, and currently live with my wife and family in Prior Lake. In my free time outside the office, I enjoy hiking, landscape design, and water gardening.

I received my law degree from Hamline University School of Law and have been in private practice since 1996. While attending Hamline, I served as a writer, published author and Primary Editor of the Hamline Journal of Public Law and Policy.

In the early years of my law practice, I dedicated some of my free time as a volunteer for the Minnesota Valley Humane Society, where I served on the Board of Directors. I have also spent time as a mentor for high school students who are interested in pursuing a career in the legal profession.

I have volunteered as a lecturer for Parents Forever, a parent education course offered in Scott and Carver counties, in which I discussed and answered questions from parents about the laws pertaining to custody, parenting time, child support and the dynamics of raising children as divorced parents.

In addition to being an aggressive advocate, I also serve as a family court neutral, providing Early Neutral Evaluation, mediation and arbitration services to parties going through disputes regarding divorce, custody and parenting time, as well as child support, spousal maintenance, property division, and tax issues, with the objective of helping those individuals to reach a compromised settlement.

Mikkel A. Long has provided high quality criminal defense services in northern Minnesota and Wisconsin since 2002. His practice is exclusively devoted to criminal defense litigation. He has successfully defended people against allegations at all levels of the criminal justice system, including in the most serious felony matters.

Mr. Long began his legal career as a prosecuting attorney. He transitioned to the field of criminal defense when he joined the Indian Legal Assistance Program, and later the Sixth Judicial District Public Defender's Office. He has maintained a private criminal defense practice for over 12 years. Mr. Long prides himself on bringing professional and compassionate representation in all of his cases. He has extensive jury trial experience. He is attentive to the needs of his clients and treats them with dignity and respect.

attorneys.name: Aliza Lopes
attorneys.practice_type: Immigration Appeals Lawyers in St. Paul, MN
attorneys.bio:
Aliza Lopes-Baker, Appellate Attorney

Aliza Lopes-Baker serves as an Immigration Attorney at Emeriti.Law, PLLC, where she leverages her years of experience advising and drafting decisions for Immigration Judges to provide clients with comprehensive appellate and post-proceedings representation, in-depth case consultations, and tailored brief-writing services.

Government Service

Ms. Lopes-Baker brings extensive experience from her tenure as an Attorney Advisor at the U.S. Department of Justice, Executive Office for Immigration Review (EOIR), where she served with distinction from September 2017 to July 2025. In this role, she acted as front-line counsel to Immigration Judges and agency management – providing analysis and guidance on complex legal issues, monitoring changes in immigration law and policy over the course of multiple presidential administrations, creating resources and tools for use in Immigration Court proceedings, and drafting nuanced, well-reasoned judicial opinions on behalf of the Immigration Judges. Ms. Lopes-Baker’s work encompassed issues arising in detained and non-detained proceedings before the Immigration Courts, including but not limited to: applications for asylum, cancellation of removal, and adjustment of status; petitions to remove conditions on residence; waivers of inadmissibility; contested removability; requests for bond redetermination in custody proceedings; requests for relief in reinstated and asylum-only proceedings; and motions to reopen on the basis of ineffective assistance of counsel, lack of notice, previously unavailable evidence, or changed circumstances.

During her time with EOIR, Ms. Lopes-Baker was repeatedly singled out for her sharp, insightful analysis, her skillful writing, and her ability to clearly and effectively convey complicated legal concepts to the Immigration Judges. Due to her aptitude for deftly synthesizing convoluted questions of law, she was entrusted with developing guidance on some of the most complex issues to appear before the Immigration Courts, including questions related to defective notices to appear, the government’s detention authority, the immigration consequences of criminal convictions, choice of law in immigration proceedings, and challenges to evolving agency procedures. These skills earned Ms. Lopes-Baker the distinction of being a sought-after advisor for Immigration Judges faced with novel issues requiring innovative solutions grounded in existing legal authority. Moreover, her incisive editing and proofing skills – coupled with her ability to clearly visualize how to best develop a compelling argument – made Ms. Lopes Baker an in-demand resource for Immigration Judges and attorney advisors seeking review of proposed legal analysis.

Quickly taking on a team lead role, Ms. Lopes-Baker helped coordinate legal support for Immigration Judges across multiple Immigration Courts tasked with adjudicating cases arising in seven different federal circuits. She provided mentorship and training to legal support staff throughout the agency and developed procedures to retain institutional knowledge in the wake of significant employee turnover. Additionally, Ms. Lopes-Baker created tools to improve administrative efficiencies, address assignment backlogs, and facilitate resource and information sharing. She assisted in the creation of the inaugural Cleveland Immigration Court Pro Bono Committee, bringing together Court staff, pro bono stakeholders, and representatives of the Department of Homeland Security to identify obstacles impeding respondent access to pro bono resources and opportunities to improve access to these services. She also served on various agency-wide committees, including EOIR’s Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Accessibility Committee, where she leveraged her background in data analysis, program development, and organizational capacity-building to identify trends in staff attrition and retention recommendations.

In recognition of her unique contributions and leadership, Ms. Lopes-Baker was granted the opportunity to participate in EOIR’s inaugural Leadership, Enrichment, and Advancement Detail. Through this program, she was detailed to EOIR’s Office of the General Counsel, Employee and Labor Relations (“ELR”) Unit, where she provided crucial litigation support in matters before the Merit Systems Protection Board, the Federal Labor Relations Authority, the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, and the federal district courts. She also developed case-tracking tools and standard operating procedures to improve documentation and data retention within the ELR Unit. Ms. Lopes-Baker’s detail was extended upon request of the acting General Counsel pursuant to her exemplary contributions in this role.

Other Professional Experience

Ms. Lopes-Baker’s previous work within the public sector in areas of international law, legal aid, nonprofit capacity-building, and community organizing grounds her detailed knowledge of U.S. immigration law within a broader understanding of the impact of these laws on global and local communities. Ms. Lopes-Baker’s experience includes externing with the INTERPOL Office of Legal Affairs, where she conducted a comparative analysis of extradition and refugee law in the U.S. and abroad, reviewed the legal sufficiency of Red Notices pursuant to international obligations and organizational policy, and provided recommendations to the Assistant Director of Risks and Conflicts based on her findings. In addition, Ms. Lopes-Baker interned with Community Legal Aid of central northeast Ohio, where she assisted in domestic violence and foreclosure proceedings. She also dedicated time as a community organizing fellow in her home city of San Diego, California, developing outreach strategies and trainings related issues impacting local immigrant communities, including access to healthcare and community policing. Over the course of two AmeriCorps tours, Ms. Lopes-Baker contributed her skills to capacity-building projects at mid-sized nonprofit organizations, spanning the gamut of database development and management, program analysis, donor engagement, development of organizational policies and procedures, and staff trainings.

Training and Resource Development

A natural collaborator, Ms. Lopes-Baker’s focus on institutional success through collective achievement informs her approach to developing and sharing tools and resources that are accessible to individuals with differing degrees of professional and legal experience. During her time with EOIR, she created and implemented training modules on complex areas of immigration law for legal staff at all levels, including interns, recent law school graduates, seasoned attorney advisors, and new and experienced Immigration Judges. Her knack for breaking down complex concepts by clearly and linearly delineating individual subcomponents makes Ms. Lopes-Baker particularly adept at demystifying even the most complex areas of immigration law.

Professional Memberships and Education

Ms. Lopes-Baker is admitted to the New York state bar. She holds a Juris Doctor from Case Western Reserve University School of Law, where she graduated magna cum laude in May 2017 with a concentration in international law. There she served as the managing editor of the Canada-U.S. Law Journal/Institute, President of the Lambda Law Students Association, and Senior Editor of the War Crimes Prosecution Watch publication. Based on her efforts and advocacy, she was named a 2016 Squire Patton Boggs Public Policy Fellow and was awarded a 2017 Case Global Service Award. Ms. Lopes-Baker received a Bachelor of Arts from Duke University in May 2011.

Ms. Lopes-Baker is a member of the Ohio Chapter of the American Immigration Lawyers Association.

Current Practice

Having assisted dozens of Immigration Judges adjudicating immigration proceedings across the country, and having drafted hundreds of Immigration Judge decisions crafted to withstand appellate review, Ms. Lopes-Baker has cultivated a wide breadth of knowledge of immigration law as well as best practices for presenting compelling arguments before the Immigration Courts and the Board of Immigration Appeals. In her current role with Emeriti.Law, PLLC, Ms. Lopes-Baker utilizes these unique insights to provide clients with thorough analysis of complex immigration issues, detailed case strategies for navigating convoluted immigration matters, and exceptional brief-writing services setting forth persuasive and legally sound arguments in support of the requested relief.

attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Brainerd, MN
attorneys.bio:
Longtime Brainerd Criminal Defense Attorney Ready to Fight for Your Rights

Committed to helping you avoid jail time or conviction

Facing criminal charges can be a terrifying experience. Being arrested and taken to jail, facing police questioning and the prospect of going before a judge are things most of us have only seen on television and can't imagine going through ourselves. When it happens to you, you need sound legal counsel from a dedicated Minnesota criminal attorney. Even more importantly, you need someone who will speak to you in plain English and tell you exactly what you face and what you need to do about it.

I have practiced criminal law for more than 30 years, first as a prosecutor and for the past 20 years as a defense attorney. Representing people who have been charged with a crime is all I do. I have seen it all and I know what kind of defense you need, whether you are facing serious criminal charges, a traffic violation or the repercussions of a probation violation. I spend my free time, when I have any, chasing aggressive fish. I spend my courtroom time aggressively defending my clients' rights and protecting their freedom.

Crow Wing County, Brainerd and Brainerd Lake DUI attorney offering personal attention

The Law Offices of Dennis M. Lothspeich, P.A. is a great place to start when you find yourself in trouble with the law in the Brainerd Lakes area. I have a well-earned reputation as an experienced and fearless litigator. Unlike some attorneys who will steer you toward a guilty plea, I am known to leave prosecutors few choices besides negotiating a plea or dropping charges against my clients.

You don't want to go to prison. I don't want that either. I guarantee you personal attention and immediate response to your calls. I am BV® DistinguishedTM Peer Review Rated by Martindale-Hubbell®, an indication that I meet high criteria for legal abilities and general ethical standards.

Get the help you need from Minnesota criminal defense Attorney Dennis M. Lothspeich

I accept collect calls from jails and correctional facilities in Crow Wing and nearby counties and can arrange an immediate visit with you onsite. Call me, Attorney Dennis M. Lothspeich, at 218.825.0861 for a free initial consultation, or contact the Law Offices of Dennis M. Lothspeich, P.A. online. I charge a reasonable flat fee, which is set up front. In some cases, my fee can be comfortably spread out into monthly payments during the duration of your case. My office is conveniently located near the Crow Wing County Court House. I am happy to schedule an evening or weekend appointment if needed.

Awards and Honors

BV® Distinguished™ Peer Review Rated by Martindale-Hubbell®

attorneys.name: John Timothy Lund
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in St. Cloud, MN
attorneys.bio:
John Lund is one of St. Cloud's leading family law and business attorneys. As a lifelong resident of St. Cloud, he has effectively helped families and businesses transition through complicated legal matters for over 40 years. He understands that each client's needs are different and caters his approach to fit their specific circumstance. John is respected for his attention to detail and assertive representation throughout the legal process and in litigation if the case cannot be settled out of court. Whether through mediation or litigation, John has extensive experience to help you with your legal issues.

Using Mediation to Settle Family Matters

His experience has contributed to making John a successful mediator where he assists opposing spouses and their lawyers in achieving settlement without depleting their assets to pay for court cases. This approach often provides the best outcome as it minimizes stress on the family and helps make divorce affordable. John seeks problem-solving solutions to help manage and minimize the stress of his family law clients while maximizing the potential for reaching an amicable outcome for the people he serves.

Order of Barristers, 1981

attorneys.name: Jennifer G. Lurken
attorneys.practice_type: Agriculture Law & Agribusiness Lawyers in Mankato, MN
attorneys.bio:
Jennifer's extensive legal expertise provides large and small businesses, agricultural producers, banks and individuals with effective outcomes. As an experienced litigator with an emphasis on bankruptcy, banking, civil litigation and employment law, Jennifer helps clients navigate the complex and confusing process when they are sued or when they need to assert their rights against another.

A seasoned professional in all aspects of bankruptcy and debtor-creditor rights, Jennifer handles complex and sophisticated matters on behalf of clients. Jennifer assists individual and business creditors attempting to collect through the bankruptcy process. Jennifer has served on the panel of Chapter 7 trustees and has acted as a receiver. As a trustee and receiver, Jennifer is the representative for the recovery, preservation, liquidation and distribution of estate and receivership assets and the fiduciary responsible to various parties in interest in a case.

Jennifer strives to understand the needs of each client and to provide counsel in a manner that will help to simultaneously achieve both business and professional objectives.

Outside the office, Jennifer enjoys biking, swimming, cooking and spending time with her husband and two children.

attorneys.name: Thomas J. Lyons
attorneys.practice_type: Consumer Rights Litigation Lawyers in Vadnais Heights, MN
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Tommy Lyons is the founder of the Consumer Justice Center P.A. His goal was to create a law firm dedicated exclusively to consumer rights litigation. Since then, he and the firm have consistently achieved ground-breaking results and are responsible for precedent-setting rulings at the trial and appellate court levels.

As an attorney, Tommy has successfully represented consumers in a variety of legal matters, handling everything from small cases to multi-million-dollar class actions. Tommy focuses his attention on representing consumers against debt collection and repossession businesses, credit reporting agencies, and banking institutions. He has been appointed to serve as class counsel by federal courts all over the country.

Tommy received a B.A. in History and Political Science from Southern Methodist University in Dallas, Texas in 1990. Tommy graduated from the University of Minnesota Law School in 1994. Tommy began practicing alongside his father in 1994 at then opened the Consumer Justice Center P.A. in 1996. Tommy has focused his entire practice on representing the little guy and litigated those cases primarily in the federal court system for nearly 30 years.

Tommy has lectured for continuing legal education programs, law schools, and community groups throughout the country, and has been a regular speaker/contributor and member of the National Association of Consumer Advocates (NACA) and National Consumer Law Center (NCLC) for over 20 years.

Throughout his life, Tommy has diligently and tirelessly fought for justice and equity, standing on the side of people who have been taken advantage of, commercially wronged, abused, or defrauded. He brings that same dedication to his work as an attorney.

During his free time, Tommy enjoys spending time with his wife of 30 years, Sheri, his three children, his extended family, and many friends. Tommy is deeply connected to outdoor sports and recreational activities and his love for travel and adventure.

attorneys.name: Michael J. Macaluso
attorneys.practice_type: Capital Markets Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Michael J. Macaluso is the Managing Partner of the firm. He has a long track record for successfully managing large, innovative, and complex transactions, investments, and projects for some of the world's leading institutions and middle-market companies, including GMAC, Cargill, Wells Fargo, and HSBC. Alternating as a partner with large law firms and as a member of law departments of large corporates, funds, and growth companies, he developed significant experience bridging the management of complex legal engagements as outside counsel and the complexities and needs of the internal legal function consistently delivering legal and strategic solutions to his clients in even the most challenging situations.

As a practice leader and partner with global law firms such as DLA Piper, Morgan Lewis, and Faegre Drinker, where he either chaired or co-chaired these firms' structured finance groups, Mr. Macaluso pioneered the business model at the heart of the firm morphing his practice into an increasingly business advisory platform that served the growing and ever more sophisticated demands of global business. He has successfully completed many billions of dollars in cross-border, in country, transactions, investments, and ventures in many parts of the world, including in the U.S., Greater China, Asia-Pacific generally, parts of the Middle East, and Europe.

For over a decade, Mr. Macaluso was the senior member responsible for legal of the global treasury team of a $120 billion company with activities across three continents. During the financial crisis, he led teams restructuring or working out over $150 billion of liquidity for some of the world's leading institutions.

Mr. Macaluso regularly writes regarding capital markets. Those articles can be found at "The Macaluso Report." He also taught capital markets as an adjunct professor at the University of Minnesota Law School for over a decade. Mr. Macaluso received his JD and MBA from the University of Chicago and his BA from Lehigh University.

attorneys.name: Michael D. Madigan
attorneys.practice_type: Alcohol Beverage Law and Litigation Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Mike Madigan is a founding shareholder of Madigan, Dahl & Harlan, P.A., bringing more than 40 years of experience in administrative, alcohol beverage, antitrust, business, commercial, distributor, dealer, franchise, construction, employment, and environmental law. For over thirty-five (35) years, Mike has been AV-rated by Martindale Hubbell and recognized as a "Super Lawyer" for twenty-one (21) years. Mike has also been selected for inclusion in the Best Lawyers in America in the practice area of Franchise Law. For the last thirty (30) years, he has served as an Arbitrator and Mediator on the Complex Commercial Panel of the American Arbitration Association and served as a Neutral on the Minnesota ADR Neutrals Roster. In addition, Mike has been inducted as a Senior Fellow, Litigation Counsel of America (a trial lawyer honorary society composed of less than one-half of one percent of American lawyers).

Currently, Mike is appointed by the Washington County Commissioners to serve on the Board of Managers, South Washington Watershed District (2011 - present); is Chair (2026) and Treasurer of Minnesota Trout Unlimited (2018 - present); and the Wild Rivers Conservancy (2026). Throughout Mike’s career, he has earned many distinctions, awards and has been recognized for his commitment and leadership which is reflected in his many appointments and board service: appointed by Governor Dayton to the Metropolitan Airports Commission (2011-2019), served eight (8) years on the Woodbury City Council, three (3) years as Chair of the Woodbury Planning Commission, and eleven (11) years on the Board of Minnesota Center for Environmental Advocacy. He is a recipient of the Alumni Student Award of Merit and Editor of William Mitchell Law Review, and a former adjunct Professor at William Mitchell College of Law. Mike is also an instrument rated Private Pilot.

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Elk River, MN
attorneys.bio:
Rhonda founded Rhonda J. Magnussen LLC in 2015, serving individuals and families throughout the Minneapolis–Saint Paul metro area and central Minnesota. With over 35 years of legal experience, Rhonda is known for her dedication, practical guidance, and strong advocacy for her clients. In addition to representing clients in state district courts, she has successfully handled appeals before the Minnesota Court of Appeals.

Rhonda represents clients in a wide range of legal matters, including family law cases involving divorce, custody and parenting time, child support, spousal maintenance, property division, paternity, and grandparents’ rights; as well as probate matters, criminal defense, estate planning, real estate transactions, business law, and other civil matters. Her broad legal background provides valuable perspective to clients addressing complex legal issues and has led many clients to return to her over the years for trusted guidance through different stages of life.

Rhonda works closely with each client to provide clear direction, thoughtful counsel, and a strong voice throughout the legal process.

As a Rule 114 Qualified Neutral, Rhonda also assists parties in resolving disputes through mediation and negotiation whenever possible.

Outside the office, Rhonda enjoys spending time with family and friends, pampering her miniature dachshund, Frankie, attending Pilates and fitness classes, baking, gardening, and traveling.

Malzahn is a partner at Dady & Gardner, P.A., where he represents franchisees and dealers nationwide in all aspects of their relationships with franchisors and manufacturers, from reviewing and negotiating franchise agreements before clients enter into the contractual relationship, to, when necessary, representing franchisees and dealers in various disputes (such as deceptive and fraudulent franchise sales, state and federal franchise registration and disclosure violations, encroachment, non-compete violations, and unlawful terminations) in state and federal court and arbitration. Andrew also represents several franchisee associations, from organization and formation, through tackling and resolving issues and disputes on a system-wide basis.

Andrew is an editor for the American Bar Association's Franchise Law Journal, and he has been named a “Rising Star” by Super Lawyers Magazine and a “Legal Eagle” by Franchise Times every year since 2020.

Andrew is driven to represent and fight for franchisees, dealers, and distributors, who frequently find themselves on the other side of the table from parties with much greater power and resources. Andrew's philosophy is to provide creative, efficient, and effective representation to meet his clients' business objectives.

Andrew will gladly speak to prospective franchisee and dealer clients at no initial charge to determine whether he and his colleagues can be of service.

attorneys.name: Matthew J. Mankey
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Mankey graduated from Benilde-St. Margaret’s High School in 1976. He attended St. John's University where he attained a major in government and history with a minor in philosophy in 1980 but deferred graduation for a year to attend the University of Salzburg, in Austria. He earned a Master's Degree in International Affairs from the American University. During his studies at American University he attended the Instituto de Instruccion de Espanol in Cuernavaca, Mexico in 1983. In 1985 Mr. Mankey completed his Master's program which included a published thesis on the Nicaraguan Revolution. Mr. Mankey has worked as a Congressional Staff person and as a lobbyist on Capitol Hill. He attended William Mitchell College of Law during which time he worked in the family law clinic and in the criminal division of the Hennepin County Attorney's Office drug prosecution team. He graduated from law school with honors in 1992. After graduating from law school Mr. Mankey practiced exclusively in the area of criminal defense. Mr. Mankey has been admitted to the Minnesota State Bar since 1992 and the Federal Bar since 1993. He was accepted onto the Criminal Justice Panel in 1997 and has been appointed by the federal court to dozens of federal criminal cases since that time. In addition to his private practice he served as a contract public defender in Hennepin County in 2004-05 and in Anoka County in 2012. He was chosen to serve as a conciliation court judge in 1997 and has presided part-time since that time. The location of Mankey Law Office has been in its current location in Golden Valley since 1992.

attorneys.name: Julianne Markiewicz
attorneys.firm_name: Markiewicz Law - Now Partner with Meagher & Geer, PLLP
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Julianne Markiewicz is a leading nationwide expert in the areas of matrimonial law, dissolutions involving complex financial issues, custody, and spousal maintenance, as well as divorce, child custody and parenting time, equitable division of property, child support, spousal maintenance, modifications and enforcement, prenuptial agreements, domestic violence, high asset dissolution of marriage, child vaccine disputes, divorce for wealthy individuals, personal injury, and DWI. She is also a recognized specialist in the crafting, negotiation, and drafting of complex prenuptial agreements and all classes of adoptions. A top graduate of Hamline University School of Law, she possesses qualified expertise with decades of courtroom experience. With a deep history forged by her extensive and varied background in civil litigation, she has handled hundreds of cases spanning a myriad of complex issues. The courtroom is Julianne’s backyard.

Recently featured on award-winning Impact Makers Radio, Julianne advised and led listeners through the pitfalls of the emotional divorce process in an information-packed interview entitled “You’re Getting Divorced – Now What?” She is a champion of strategic thinking and decision-making to maximize recovery for divorce litigants with a close eye on costs.

To add to her recent list of accomplishments, Ms. Markiewicz was hand-selected by Remarkable Press’ national search for an exceptional divorce professional to author the litigation chapter in the best-selling divorce book series Stress-Free Divorce: Leading Divorce Professionals Speak. Published by Remarkable Press, this award-winning book hand-picks and places focus on true advocates for the success of divorcing couples in America, while at the same time pledging 100% of the royalties from the retail sales of the book to be donated to Junior Achievement, a nonprofit Corporation focused on leading young people to the exploration of benefits of entrepreneurship.

Julianne is a national leader, practicing law with compassion and integrity. A known fighter and advocate, she is someone that you want to have in your corner in your time of need.

Julianne’s office is centrally located in the small, well-knit community of White Bear Lake. Right around the corner from Julianne’s office is the senior living complex of Pioneer Manor, hosting 42 senior apartment units on a beautiful corner lot. Julianne has become known as the “go-to” for the legal needs of its elderly population. From health care directives to amending complex trust documents, Julianne performs these services of the communities’ elderly constituents on a pro bono basis. This service to the community is a niche for the needs of the elderly. Julianne’s clients stop by when out for a daily stroll in their walkers or just to have a small cup of “warmer” coffee as they go about their daily errands. This is just one of the hallmarks of generosity of Julianne’s practice.

In addition to her successful track record in family and civil courtrooms, Julianne has been a mainstay headliner in the entertainment law industry, providing guidance, negotiation, and detailed strategic drafting of Sponsorship Contracts for major recording stars, including Kenny Chesney, Luke Bryan, Shelby Lynne, and Miranda Lambert. This included implementation of branding and marketing platforms to build sales and increase market share for artists and corporate brands. Sponsors included Cruzan Rum, Absolut Vodka, Crown Imports, Corona and Corona light, Hard Rock International, Hooters Restaurants, Fiji Water and Costa Del Mar sunglasses. Julianne was also involved in the groundbreaking contract negotiations for implementation of brand and marketing for the rising prominence of Skinny Girl Cocktails.

Julianne does not have a standard hourly rate that is published and presented to Clients. Rather, she works on a permanent sliding fee scale, where she determines every individual client’s needs and financial stature. Ranging from pro bono to greatly reduced hourly rates, Julianne strives to meet the legal needs of all—not just those who can afford. Last year, a divorce client passed away, and his brother came to Julianne in need. She probated the Estate for $100 an hour and covered the expenses. Clients in need get served—come hell or high water. Julianne cannot and will not close her door to the downtrodden and hurting.

Businesses in the White Bear Lake area KNOW and TRUST Julianne. The local Starbucks always has a stash of Julianne’s cards right next to the espresso machine. When a Client comes in and is hurting, the motto is “you need Julianne.” From Panera Bread to The Big Bear Car Wash to Freedom Gas Station to Domino’s Pizza to Hugo Nails, local businesses in the community know and trust Julianne and refer all of their friends and business constituents in need to Markiewicz Law.

Julianne serves as the President of the Board at The Shoppes at Banning and Fifth, a prominent business condominium complex located in the heart of the City of White Bear Lake. This non-compensating Board seat presents daily challenges, with everything from zoning and fire safety issues to balancing the budget to meet the needs of this hallmark gathering place in the heart of her community.

Julianne was recently asked to serve on the Ramsey County Conflicts Panel for low-income clients in St. Paul in need of Family Law Services. By providing counsel and comfort to those in need on a pro bono and reduced fee scale, Julianne gives back to the community with her talents and compassionate and learned services.

attorneys.name: N. Georgette Marling
attorneys.practice_type: Immigration Lawyers in Minnetonka, MN
attorneys.bio:
N. Georgette Marling is an attorney at Steven C. Thal, P.A.; she earned her J.D. from the University of Minnesota Law School in 2019 and her Master of Laws in Spain from the Universidad Pontificia Comillas.

Prior to and during law school, Georgette focused on international legal issues, specifically in the fields of environment and human rights. She has a special interest in climate change refugees and corporate responsibility for human rights abuses.

While in law school, Georgette was a legal intern working on asylum applications at The Advocates for Human Rights and at the National Immigrant Justice Center in Chicago. She was a Minnesota Justice Foundation clerk at the Minnesota Center for Environmental Advocacy. Georgette was a student attorney in the Human Rights Litigation and International Advocacy clinic, where she worked on international legal cases with clients from Cambodia, the Philippines, Sri Lanka, and Mexico. She was also a student attorney in the Rural Immigrant Access Clinic where she traveled with other students to rural parts of Minnesota to provide legal advice and social service referrals to immigrants living in those areas. Georgette was a fellow for the University of Minnesota Human Rights Clinic, where she researched human rights issues related to agricultural laws in Colombia. In her final year, Georgette studied at Uppsala University in Sweden, focusing on litigation within the European Union judicial system. She was also a Benjamin B. Ferencz fellow at World Without Genocide, researching climate change legislation.

Since law school, Georgette has narrowed her focus to immigration law. She volunteered at the Immigrant Law Center of Minnesota, working on detained cases. And she is now a member of the American Immigration Lawyers Association and a volunteer attorney and mentor at the Advocates for Human Rights, assisting on asylum applications. She also does remote volunteer work with Lawyers for Good Government, Project Corazon, which assists asylum applicants at the Mexican/Texan border.

Minnesota Justice Foundation – Public Interest in Law Fellowship

attorneys.name: Thomas E. Marshall
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Counseling and Litigation Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Tom Marshall primarily practices in several areas of workplace law, including discrimination matters, disability management issues, the enforcement or challenges to restrictive covenants, trade secrets and related obligations, as well as training and counseling on policies, handbooks and other day to day employment issues. He has helped employers and employees obtain appropriate and effective resolution of disputes including a $2.6 Million federal verdict in favor of an employee who suffered disability discrimination. Tom has represented employers and employees in trials, appeals, mediations, arbitrations, administrative hearings and all other aspects of litigation in Minnesota and other parts of the country. He has tried over 30 jury cases to verdict in state and federal courts.

As an adjunct, he taught trial advocacy at William Mitchell College of Law for eight years. He speaks often about employment matters and litigation techniques.

attorneys.bio:
Alejandra Martinez is an Associate Attorney at Dady & Gardner, where she represents franchisees, dealers, and distributors across the United States in their relationships with franchisors, manufacturers, and suppliers.

Alejandra earned her Juris Doctor in 2019 from Mitchell Hamline School of Law. During her time there, she actively participated in multiple Moot Court and Mock Trial Competitions, demonstrating her dedication to mastering the intricacies of the legal profession.

Since graduating from Mitchell Hamline, Alejandra has refined her advocacy and legal writing skills through a judicial clerkship and her representation of businesses from the pre-litigation stage through trial. Her experience as a litigator helped refine her understanding of the legal landscape, preparing her to navigate complex legal challenges with poise and precision. Alejandra’s background further helped develop the skills necessary to identify the unique nuances and needs of her clients.

Now an integral part of Dady & Gardner, P.A., Alejandra leverages her extensive litigation, trial, and settlement experience to assist clients in all stages of their relationships with franchisors, manufacturers, and suppliers. Alejandra reviews franchise agreements, providing prospective franchisees with comprehensive insights into the opportunities and negotiating terms that align with their best interests.

In her free time, Alejandra enjoys exploring the world through travel, visiting with family and friends, experimenting with culinary delights in the kitchen, and staying active with weightlifting.

attorneys.name: Rodney J. Mason
attorneys.practice_type: Estate & Trust Litigation Lawyers in St. Paul, MN
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Mason practiced law for more than 46 years and has now retired effective June 13, 2023. He no longer provides legal advice or services. He now resides in Portland, Oregon along with his wife of more than 51 years, his two children and their spouses and his four school-aged grandchildren. He looks forward to new involvements and interests, catching up on his personal reading, walking and hiking in the Cascade Mountains, on the beaches of Oregon and Washington, and exploring the great city of Portland. Beyond that, he is excited to spend more time with his family and all three generations. He greatly enjoyed his practice of law and now moves on to the next steps. Opportunity beckons everywhere.

Biography

Mr. Mason is a 1976 graduate of the University of Minnesota Law School which he attended after spending two years in the United States Army, including a shortened stint as an infantryman in Vietnam.

When he retired in 2023, he was licensed to practice law in Minnesota, Wisconsin, and Oregon and before the United States District Court for the District of Minnesota, the United States Circuit Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit, and the United States Supreme Court. He has been a member of the American Bar Association, the Minnesota State Bar Association, the Ramsey County Bar Association, the Wisconsin State Bar Association, and the Oregon State Bar Association.

Mr. Mason's practice for the last twenty plus years centered on litigation relating to family inheritance disputes in the trial courts and appellate courts for the States of Minnesota and Wisconsin and in Federal trial and appellate courts.

Along with his law practice, Mr. Mason was heavily involved in community affairs. He has served as president or other officer of several non-profit corporations, which have provided housing for homeless men, women and children, housing and nursing home services for senior citizens, and mental health services to the community. He has served on blue ribbon task forces for the St. Paul School District, and was a member of the Midway Chamber of Commerce for more than 20 years.

Awards and Honors

Honors

AV Rating (Highest Possible) through Martindale-Hubbell's Peer Review System

attorneys.bio:
With a strong foundation in both real estate law and estate planning, Amy provides sound legal counsel to individuals, families, and business owners across Minnesota.

Planning for the future requires precision—not just in legal strategy, but in language. As a former professional writer and editor turned attorney, Amy brings a sharp eye for detail and a talent for clear, concise communication. Amy’s practice is centered on delivering advice and advocacy tailored to help clients protect their assets, plan for the future, and navigate complex real property matters.

Real Estate Law

Amy focuses her real estate practice to guide clients through every stage of property ownership, development, and investment. Whether developing land, making enhancements to a business portfolio, selling a home, or establishing a personal venture, Amy approaches every challenge with her client’s goals in mind and best interests at heart.

Amy provide hands-on legal support in the following areas:

Residential and commercial real estate transactions

Entity formation and business structuring for real estate ventures

Leases, mortgages, and financing agreements

Zoning, land use, and permitting matters

Partition actions

Lot line adjustments

Title review and registration

Survey review

Seller’s failure to disclose property defects

Landlord representation in residential and commercial evictions

Real estate litigation and contract negotiation

Easement creation and termination

Adverse possession

Other civil disputes involving real property

Estate Planning Law

In her estate planning practice, Amy works closely with individuals and families to create personalized, legally sound plans that provide peace of mind and ensure wishes are clearly documented and enforceable. Amy’s services include:

Wills and trusts for individuals and couples

Health care directives

Powers of attorney

Non-complex asset protection and legacy planning

Business succession planning

Transfer on death deeds

attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Saint Paul, MN
attorneys.bio:
Allison joined Collins, Buckley, Sauntry & Haugh after owning and operating her own successful divorce and family law firm in St. Paul for just shy of 10 years. Allison has a dynamic divorce and family law practice focused on complex child custody and financial matters, and interstate and international child custody and divorce. Allison is a tough lawyer who draws on her advanced degree in psychology as well as her law degree to help clients navigate complicated family circumstances that require excellent legal service. She takes a problem-solving approach to her cases and works closely with each client to develop a strategy that will maximize results. Allison is a compassionate legal advisor as well as an intense and effective advocate. Whether advocating in settlement negotiations or in the courtroom - as your trusted advisor, Allison will have your back.

After growing up in Pennsylvania, attending college in Ohio, and residing in Washington DC for a couple of years, Allison happily adopted Minnesota as her permanent home. She attended graduate school, obtaining a Master's degree in Clinical Psychology before continuing her education at the University of St. Thomas School of Law. Allison enjoys hiking, biking, and kayaking with her husband, Nick, doing yoga, reading, eating Nick's delicious meals, and spending time with her family and friends.

attorneys.name: William J. Mauzy
attorneys.practice_type: White Collar Crimes Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
William J. Mauzy. Fellow, American Board of Criminal Lawyers; Fellow, American College of Trial Lawyers. Having won more than 100 cases in state and federal court, William Mauzy has been selected continuously for 39 years for the book The Best Lawyers in America, he has been a Minnesota “Super Lawyer” for 35 years. Mauzy is certified by the Minnesota State Bar Association as a Criminal Trial Specialist and by the National Board of Trial Advocacy as a Criminal Trial Specialist. Effectively representing individuals and corporations in all criminal matters, he has won acquittals in a wide variety of matters including securities fraud, bank fraud, mail fraud, bid rigging, health care fraud, antitrust, ERISA fraud, mortgage fraud, insurance fraud, environmental crimes and bribery. Mauzy achieved the first acquittal in Minnesota using the battered woman’s syndrome defense in a murder trial, and the first acquittal in the federal district of Minnesota. In one of his many white collar cases, he became the first attorney in Minnesota to try a case against the Office of Independent Counsel. Mauzy’s client, an insurance company CEO, was acquitted of all charges after a lengthy trial in Washington, D.C. Mauzy also won an acquittal for the former Chairman of the Republican Party of Minnesota for alleged illegal corporate campaign contribution, and an acquittal for a highly regarded Twin Cities pediatrician on criminal sexual assault charges. Just recently, he won jury acquittals in a federal fraud trial, a federal insider trading trial, a federal tax evasion case, and a Minnesota State theft by swindle state trial. He was recognized by an award issued in 2023 as an “Icon” of the Minnesota Bar.

Bill is married to retired Hennepin County judge Lucy Wieland, has four children and 10 grandchildren. While he is most proud of his academic and legal accomplishments, he also takes great pride in the fact that he was recently inducted into the Franklin High school Football Hall of Fame. He also enjoys skiing and hiking in Montana.

Mauzy is admitted to practice in the United States District Court, United States Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit, United States Supreme Court and United States Tax Court. He also is admitted to practice in the State of Wisconsin. B.A. 1969, Carleton College; J.D. cum laude, 1973, University of Minnesota.

attorneys.name: Richmond H. McCluer Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Winona, MN
attorneys.bio:
Richmond H. McCluer, Jr. is a native of Winona, Minnesota, and he attended Winona Senior High School, Winona State University and the University of Minnesota Law School. After practicing with a prominent law firm in Minneapolis, he returned to Winona in 1988 and joined the esteemed law firm of Darby, Delano and Price. During his time with the firm, he successfully handled numerous high-profile felony cases, including robbery, narcotics, burglary, assault and criminal sexual conduct. Moreover, he represented injured individuals in accident and negligence cases.

In 1993, he left the firm to work for the Third Judicial District Public Defender’s Office. There, he served as Chief Trial Lawyer and handled serious felony trials in southern Minnesota. In 2003, he joined Price, McCluer and Plachecki, a law firm formed by Michael J. Price and John Paul Plachecki. Richmond was also elected as the president of the Winona County Bar Association in 2004.

McCluer has an impressive record as lead counsel in over 250 jury trials. These trials have covered a wide range of serious criminal offenses, such as homicide, robbery, kidnapping, narcotics, criminal sexual conduct, burglary and assault. His exceptional skills and experience have earned him positive recognition.

Every year, three Minnesota magazines conduct a survey asking around 20,000 Minnesota lawyers to identify exceptional lawyers in specific areas of legal practice. Only 5% of lawyers in Minnesota are chosen for Minnesota Super Lawyers. Richmond McCluer was initially selected in 1996 while serving as Chief Trial Lawyer for the 3rd Judicial District Public Defender’s Office. Since then, he has consistently been recognized on the Super Lawyers list, including every year from 2005 through 2023.

A leading attorney, Mr. Richmond is a Minnesota State Bar Association board-certified criminal law specialist. This prestigious certification program, approved by the State Board of Legal Certification, is administered by the Minnesota State Bar Association. To earn the certified specialist designation, attorneys must undergo a rigorous review process, including an examination in the specialty area, peer review and documented experience. By achieving this specialty certification, Richmond has demonstrated exceptional knowledge, skill and integrity in the field of criminal law. It is an accomplishment that only a small fraction, less than 3%, of all licensed Minnesota attorneys have achieved.

Richmond is rated AV* by the respected Martindale-Hubbell Law Directory. These ratings are developed by obtaining confidential opinions from lawyer adversaries and judges before whom the lawyer has appeared. Ability rating categories are A, B, C and no rating. An “A” rating is the “very high to preeminent” category — the highest rating possible. It signifies that the lawyer has reached the heights of professional excellence, recognized for the highest levels of skill and integrity. The “V” rating is the highest for adherence to ethical standards, reliability and diligence.

From 1988 to 2011, he taught criminal law, federal rules of evidence and Japanese karate at Winona State University. He currently serves as the president of Japan Karate-Do Genbu-Kai of Minnesota, a corporation that runs a full-time Japanese martial arts dojo and programs at Winona State University, St. Mary's University of Minnesota and the Winona Family YMCA. Additionally, he sits on the board of various charitable nonprofit organizations, including the Winona Area Humane Society.

*AV®, AV Preeminent®, Martindale-Hubbell Distinguished and Martindale-Hubbell Notable are certification marks used under license in accordance with the Martindale-Hubbell certification procedures, standards and policies. Martindale-Hubbell® is the facilitator of a peer review rating process. Ratings reflect the anonymous opinions of members of the bar and the judiciary. Martindale-Hubbell® Peer Review RatingTM fall into two categories – legal ability and general ethical standards. AV Preeminent Peer Rated Attorneys are an elite group of attorneys who have been rated highly by their peers as having Very High Ethical Standards and an A grade.

attorneys.name: Ian Feingold McCoy
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Ian McCoy is a Minnesota attorney, born and raised. He brings a unique prospective to the legal field, having worked for years in consumer collections before becoming a lawyer. As an attorney, Ian has practiced both the litigation and collections sides of disputes, obtaining judgments as well as foreclosing on properties and garnishing as necessary to make his clients whole. Ian works tireless in civil litigation, prosecuting cases and finding success for his clients at all steps of the process, from the initial pleadings, to summary judgment, at trial, and in collections afterwards.

Ian has expertise in litigating multiple areas of law. He has spent countless hours in housing court, fighting for the rights of landlords in various disputes, including evictions and rent abatements. Ian also has experience litigating construction matters, representing construction firms against property owners and insurance providers. Ian takes joy in representing clients in civil matters, both as a plaintiff and defense attorney, ensuring his clients’ legal rights are protected in all types of civil claims.

Ian spends his free time hiking and enjoying the beauty of greater Minnesota’s parks with his wife, son, and his two dogs. When stranded at home, he is an avid reader of fiction.

attorneys.name: Thomas E. McEllistrem
attorneys.practice_type: Civil litigation Lawyers in Saint Paul, MN
attorneys.bio:
Tom McEllistrem has a broad-based and dynamic practice, which involves all aspects of civil litigation, including lawsuits and appeals in both state and federal court. Tom also serves as corporate counsel for many business entities, and has become one of Minnesota’s leading authorities on corporate advisory boards. Tom has considerable expertise in corporate law, personal injury (including sexual abuse litigation), probate, corporate and real estate litigation. His practice area is divided equally between plaintiffs and defendants in litigation matters.

Areas of Practice include:

• Representing business entities in formation, transactions and litigation matters

• Representing plaintiffs and defendants in personal injury, business, probate and real estate litigation matters

• Representing both victims and entities in sexual abuse claims

• Briefing and arguing appeals in both state and federal courts

• Creating and chairing advisory boards for new and existing companies

• Application of multi-disciplinary paradigms to create transformational solutions for business entities

Personal Bio

Tom is involved with non-profit and NGOs serving critical needs in both The Democratic Republic of the Congo, Nairobi, Kenya, and Cambodia. He previously served on the fund distribution committee of the St. Paul Area United Way, and subsequently, as a member of the Agency Services Committee for the Greater Twin Cities United Way. He has also served as a volunteer Guardian Ad Litem (GAL) for the Minnesota Pro Bono Challenge for Kids.

attorneys.name: Chad McKenney
attorneys.practice_type: Business Litigation Lawyers in Maple Grove, MN
attorneys.bio:
Mr. McKenney has represented businesses and their owners throughout the life of a business from entity formation through dissolution. He strives to be a trusted partner in the growth of your business while ensuring owners are personally protected from liability. Matters covered are business formation; contract negotiation; confidentiality agreement; shareholder and director issues; employee handbooks; employment issues like non solicitation, discipline and discharge; independent contractor agreements; owner control agreements; buy-sell agreements; purchase agreements; lease issues; documenting annual director and shareholder meetings; loan agreements; personal guarantees; and all areas of business litigation. A significant part of his practice includes working closely with business owners providing guidance and legal advice to help those businesses achieve their goals. Over the years, Mr. McKenney has successfully represented corporate clients in a broad spectrum of cases including contract disputes, shareholder disputes and employment litigation. His strategic approach and meticulous attention to detail have earned him a reputation as a tenacious and effective litigator.

Estate planning issues, including wills, irrevocable and revocable trusts, healthcare directives, powers of attorney, and other matters to carry out the client’s estate planning objectives is another area of law that Mr. McKenney has a strong background in. He meets with individuals and works to ensure their wishes are known, clearly stated and carried out to avoid future conflicts and taxes.

Mr. McKenney is admitted to practice law in all courts in the State of Minnesota, including the United States District Court for Minnesota and the United States Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals. Further, Mr. McKenney is a member of the American Bar Association, Minnesota State Bar Association, Hennepin County Bar Association, and LRIS. Chad is married to Lisa and they have two children. In his spare time, he enjoys cross-country skiing, running and cheering on Minnesota sports teams.

attorneys.name: Brandon McLaughlin
attorneys.practice_type: Workers’ Compensation Lawyers in Sauk Rapids, MN
attorneys.bio:
Brandon received both his undergraduate and his law degree from Hamline University in Saint Paul, Minnesota. After graduating from law school, he worked for an insurance company managing defense of high-exposure and litigated workers' compensation claims. Brandon found his passion for workers' compensation law during his time at the insurance company, but he never enjoyed having to deny injured workers' claims. He wanted to be able to help injured workers whose benefits had been unfairly denied, and provide them with the best representation possible to get the benefits that they deserved.

Early in 2016, Brandon seized the opportunity to represent and advocate for injured workers when he joined Lindberg McLaughlin, P.C. He devotes 100 percent of his practice to plaintiffs' workers' compensation cases. Brandon enjoys and takes pride in being able to explain Minnesota workers' compensation law to injured workers in terms that they can understand, giving them the peace of mind that they deserve.

attorneys.name: Molly M. McMahon
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Molly McMahon is an Associate Attorney at Groshek Law who is deeply committed to criminal defense and to the people she represents. She approaches each case with a thoughtful, strategic mindset and a strong belief that every client deserves to be heard, respected, and vigorously advocated for.

Molly brings a well-rounded perspective to her work, having gained experience in both prosecutorial and judicial settings. She understands how cases are evaluated from multiple angles, which allows her to anticipate challenges and craft effective, client-focused strategies.

She earned her Juris Doctor from Mitchell Hamline School of Law in 2022 and holds a Bachelor of Arts in Criminal Justice from the University of St. Thomas. During law school, Molly worked as a law clerk for the Dakota County Attorney’s Office and volunteered with the Criminal Expungement Self-Help Clinic, where she assisted individuals seeking to clear their records and move forward with their lives. That experience reinforced her belief in the power of the legal system not just to punish, but to create second chances.

Before joining Groshek Law, Molly served as a judicial clerk in Minnesota’s First Judicial District. In that role, she worked closely with the court on a wide range of legal issues, sharpening her analytical skills and gaining meaningful insight into courtroom dynamics and judicial decision-making.

When she’s not in the courtroom, Molly is usually on the ice, on a court, or on a ballfield. And if she’s not competing, she’s busy planning her next trip and deciding which corner of the world to explore next.

attorneys.name: Merlyn L. Meinerts
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Burnsville, MN
attorneys.bio:
Merlyn L. Meinerts provides a unique blend of services to parties involved in marital dissolution proceedings.

Meinerts is equipped to provide effective legal representation in those cases where a party is in need of an advocate or the case involves highly complex matters. When representing a party, Meinerts' approach would likely first include an attempt at a negotiated resolution through settlement discussions or the use of mediation or other forms of Alternative Dispute Resolution. Where settlement efforts are not successful or practical, Meinerts effectively assists his clients in seeking a judicial determination of the matter via a motion or trial.

Meinerts is prepared to assist parties as a neutral third party facilitator, with alternative dispute resolution services ranging from mediation to arbitration. Meinerts' style in mediation involves empowering parties to control their own results in a marital dissolution proceeding. The prospect of a less expensive, less time-consuming and more certain process makes alternative dispute resolution an attractive alternative to litigation.
