attorneys.name: Bacilio Mendez II
attorneys.practice_type: Business/Corporate Law: Lawyers in Walker, MN
attorneys.bio:
Bacilio Mendez II is a Senior Associate practicing out of Breen & Person's Walker and Longville offices in the areas of estate planning, probate, real estate, business/corporate law, and association law. In business/corporate law, he has special interest in business formation, governance, multiple-owner issues, and business succession. Bacilio also enjoys working with clients on their estate plans and helping them tailor a plan to preserve what they have built for the next generation.

Prior to joining Breen & Person, Bacilio was a general litigation attorney at a full-service AmLaw 100 firm. There, he defended global technology, retail, and corporate brands against transportation, premises liability and general liability claims. He also gained valuable insurance defense experience working closely with insurance carrier clients while providing case summary, analysis and valuation memos regarding his case load. A competent civil litigator, he routinely defended organizations in single-plaintiff, class action and B2B litigation arising from data privacy and security incidents, violations of state and federal consumer protection and data privacy laws and breach of contract, among others.

Bacilio is well-versed in settlement negotiations, drafting and defending motions, responding to discovery, and taking and defending party, witness, and expert depositions, while preparing for mediation, arbitration or, if necessary, trial. While generally industry-agnostic, he focused on defending organizations in the manufacturing and distribution, financial services, and retail industry group sectors.

Before his law firm career, Bacilio served as Associate Regional Counsel for the Social Security Administration (SSA) and Special Assistant United States Attorney for the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ), helped found the Blockchain Law for Social Good Center at Golden Gate University (GGU) School of Law, and was the Director of Information and Compliance for a wealth management firm.

attorneys.name: Steven J. Meshbesher
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Unrelenting pursuit of justice for my clients has been the sole focus of my law practice for 35 years. I work hard for my clients and I have created a law firm of diligent lawyers and administrative staff who believe, as do I, that a positive conclusion in a case results from persistence and skill in the handling of every aspect of a file, as well as the ability to maintain effective communication among all parties.

After graduating from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1976 with a major in European Cultural History, I earned my J.D. from the Creighton University School of Law in Omaha, Nebraska, in 1980. I learned how to practice law from one of the best criminal defense lawyers in the country, my uncle, Ron Meshbesher, for over eight years before striking out on my own with partners to start a new criminal defense/personal injury firm. Eight years after that, in 1997, I created Meshbesher & Associates with the goal of continuing and enriching my tradition of successful outcomes combined with good, old-fashioned, attentive service to my clients.

I now have the privilege, through the multi-talented team of associates at Meshbesher & Associates I have gathered together, to expand upon my legacy of personal service and favorable results. Whether it be a personal injury, wrongful death, civil rights or criminal defense case, my colleagues and I are prepared to devote the time, attention and resources to your case that it deserves. We will gladly speak with you to evaluate how we may assist you, your friend or family member during your difficult time.

attorneys.bio:
Steven is a top-rated attorney serving clients across the State of Minnesota for more than ten years. He is an experienced litigator, counselor, and mediator, who finds practical solutions for difficult problems faced by his clients. Steven advocates for clients in probate and civil litigation cases, including related matters such as trust and estate litigation, construction and business disputes, guardianship and conservatorship implementation and actions involving real property. Steven also serves as a mediator in family, probate, and civil disputes.

Steven is a former Judicial Law Clerk to the Honorable Judge Thomas M. Neuville (Rice County - Retired). He is a member of the Board of Trustees for Mitchell Hamline School of Law. Prior to practicing law, Steven served as an assistant to a U.S. Congressman, and later, held various advisory positions for State and Federal candidates and Officeholders. Steven has been recognized as a Rising Star in 2019 and 2020, and a Super Lawyer since 2021.

Steven resides in Woodbury, Minnesota with his wife and three young children.

attorneys.name: Nicole Liguori Micklich
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Nicole Liguori Micklich has earned a reputation for successfully representing franchisees and development agents at every step of the franchise relationship and in litigation with franchisors.

Ms. Micklich’s commitment to her clients and to the field of franchise law leads to enviable results. The outcome of each case depends on the facts and circumstances of each particular case.

Ms. Micklich routinely assists potential franchisees as they review disclosure documents and proposed agreements.

She has successfully represented development agents and franchisees in arbitration and in state and federal courts in cases regarding alleged non-compliance, termination and non-renewal, franchisor refusal to consent to transfer, bad faith, contract and tort claims, and violations of state and federal laws, including disclosure laws. She has also favorably settled numerous cases on behalf of franchisees and development agents involved in such disputes.

Ms. Micklich advises clients regarding the transfer of franchise agreements and has drafted and negotiated the Asset Purchase Agreements and related Agreements, Notes and Resolutions for those transactions. She also frequently drafts and negotiates termination agreements and releases.

Ms. Micklich enjoys extensive involvement in the American Bar Association Forum on Franchising, where she is a member of the Governing Committee. She was a co-chair of the Forum’s 46th Annual Meeting, in Dallas, Texas, November 1-3, 2023. With Mark VanderBroek, Ms. Micklich recently co-authored and presented Annual Developments in Franchise and Distribution Law for the Forum on Franchising. The book provides an overview of franchise cases and developments over its reporting year and the authors provided a comprehensive and entertaining review of the year’s key judicial and legislative developments affecting franchise and distribution during the Forum’s Annual Meeting. She has served on multiple committees of the Forum and was humbled to be the recipient of the 2017 ABA Forum on Franchising Future Leader Award.

Ms. Micklich is honored to be a Fellow of the American Bar Foundation and the Rhode Island Bar Foundation and proudly holds a Martindale-Hubbell AV® PreeminentTM Rating. Ms. Micklich strives to work easily and collegially with franchisor counsel. She was included in the 2024 and 2025 editions of The Best Lawyers in America® for franchise law and was recognized as a Super Lawyer in the field of Franchise/Distribution in 2017, 2018, 2020, 2021, 2022, and 2023, and prior to that time was named to the New England Rising Starts list each year from 2010 through 2016. For more about the Super Lawyer selection process visit https://www.superlawyers.com/about/selection-process/.

Ms. Micklich has taught Franchise Law as an adjunct professor at Quinnipiac University Law School, in Hamden, Connecticut, and is a frequent author and lecturer on franchise law.

During her practice, Ms. Micklich represents property owners, condominium associations, general contractors and subcontractors. She regularly advises clients regarding contracts and corporate plans and policies and drafts Management Agreements, Agreements between Owner and Contractor and General Conditions of Contracts, Design Build Agreements, Subcontracts, and Agreements between Owner and Architect. Ms. Micklich represents commercial landlords and tenants in preparing and negotiating lease agreements and related documents. Ms. Micklich has successfully represented property owners in various design defect claims. The results in any case depend on the facts and circumstances of that particular case.

Ms. Micklich is a trained mediator who completed 40-hours of mediation training in accordance with M.G.L. ch.233 § 23C with MWI, Boston, MA.

Ms. Micklich is admitted in the State and Federal Courts of Rhode Island and Connecticut and the U.S. Court of Appeals, Second Circuit.

Ms. Micklich is a 1999 cum laude graduate of the University of Pittsburgh. She earned her JD from the University of Connecticut School of Law in 2003.

attorneys.name: Jason Migala
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in St. Cloud, MN
attorneys.bio:
Since graduating from the University of St. Thomas Law School, Jason Migala has earned a reputation for being an aggressive defender of people who find themselves on the wrong side of the law. Representing the interests of the criminally accused has been the focus of Jason’s practice since he launched Migala Law Office over thirteen years ago. Jason has represented clients in all types of cases, ranging from simple speeding tickets to homicide.

Jason is known not only for his negotiation skills, but also for taking cases to trial, and winning, if his clients aren’t offered a favorable result. Over the course of hundreds of trials, Jason has won not guilty verdicts in numerous cases, including criminal sexual conduct cases, domestic violence cases, drug cases, even attempted murder cases.

attorneys.bio:
Maya E. Missaghi has been practicing law since 2016 in the areas of elder law, probate, estate planning and guardianship. She most enjoys contested cases where a good argument is in order. Before becoming a lawyer, Maya E. Missaghi worked as a preschool and prekindergarten teacher at a French immersion school. It turns out that this experience prepared her well for handling difficult cases, temper tantrums and tough negotiators, as well as finding ways to play nicely together when possible.

A European transplant, Maya now happily lives in Saint Paul with her husband and two children. She enjoys volunteering through the local bar association (2025-2026 President) and locally in her neighborhood. In her free time, she enjoys reading, hiking, baking and finding sweaters for the family dog.

attorneys.name: Michael E. Molenda
attorneys.firm_name: Dougherty, Molenda, Solfest, Hills & Bauer P.A.
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law and Alternative Dispute Resolution Lawyers in Apple Valley, MN
attorneys.bio:
Mike was born in Milwaukee, Wisconsin in 1950. He grew up in the Milwaukee suburb of Greenfield where he attended high school and participated in swimming, golf, and drama. After high school, Mike attended the University of Wisconsin - La Crosse where he continued to swim and where he met his wife Linda.

Upon graduating from UW-La Crosse, he accepted a position as a physical education teacher at Rosemount Middle School; he also served as head swimming coach for Rosemount High School. He served in both of these roles until 1978 when he left coaching and pursued a law degree from William Mitchell College of Law in St. Paul. Mike graduated from law school, cum laude, in 1982.

Before his retirement in 2017, Mike practiced in the areas of family law, criminal law, and personal injury. He also served as a mediator, parenting time expeditor, parenting consultant and Early Neutral Evaluator in the family law area.

When he is not at work, Mike enjoys golfing and traveling with his wife of Linda. They have a daughter, son-in-law, and two grandsons. Mike is very active in the International Association of Lions Clubs, serving as club president, District Governor for the Lions Clubs in Ramsey, Dakota and Washington Counties in 2010-2011 and as Counsel Chairperson for the Lions Clubs in Minnesota, Manitoba and Northwest Ontario in 2011-2012.

Dennis Monroe is the co-founder of the Minneapolis law firm of Monroe Moxness Berg PA. A pioneer in the retail and franchise finance area, Dennis has developed a broad network of finance contacts and clients. He assists many businesses, from emerging companies to multi-national firms, by providing creative ideas, identifying unique financing sources, and developing the financial tools necessary for their growth and development. He also serves as special counsel to multi-national accounting firms in the areas of corporate finance and tax planning as they relate to multi-unit acquisition.

Dennis focuses his practice on corporate and commercial finance, with additional areas of emphasis in taxation and closely held corporations. His experience includes structuring and negotiating numerous business transactions including mergers and acquisitions, restructures and workouts, divestitures, valuations, joint ventures, commercial lending, and specialty finance transactions, as well as drafting all necessary transactional documentation. Representing lenders, investors, and developers, Dennis has overseen in excess of $4 billion dollars in commercial transactions, ranging from $5,000,000 to $300,000,000.

Dennis has been nationally recognized for his work in corporate and institutional finance and mergers and acquisitions, and he is often consulted regarding the latest acquisition financing techniques. He is a frequent speaker at business conferences, professional organizations, and special finance industry events including the Restaurant Finance and Development Conference. He also frequently speaks at franchisor conferences, law school, and college seminars. Dennis is consistently recognized by Franchise Times magazine as a “Legal Eagle.” He has also been selected to "Who's Who Legal: Franchising" and listed in The Best Lawyers in America® for franchise law.

In addition to speaking, Dennis frequently contributes to franchise finance industry publications, including monthly articles written for the Restaurant Finance Monitor. He is a senior distinguished fellow at the University of St. Thomas School of Law.

attorneys.name: Amanda Montgomery
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in White Bear Lake, MN
attorneys.bio:
Thanks for being here — I’m Amanda Montgomery, owner and attorney of Montgomery Law PLLC. I’d like to share a bit of background about myself as I feel that’s important in starting a successful working relationship.

I believe that I gained powerful customer service knowledge growing up in and working at my family’s restaurant in a suburb of Saint Paul from the time of needing to stand on a bucket to reach the dish sprayer, all the way through completing my undergrad. These invaluable people skills have evolved into my work as an attorney and working with clients from all walks of life. As chef, Anthony Bourdain once stated:

“Service industry work develops the “soft skills” recruiters talk about on LinkedIn — discipline, promptness, the ability to absorb criticism, and most important, how to read people like a book. The work is thankless and fun and messy, and the world would be a kinder place if more people tried it. With all due respect to my former professors, I’ve long believed I gained more knowledge in kitchens, bars, and dining rooms than any college could even hold.”

After obtaining a Bachelor’s Degree in Business Management and a minor in Spanish, I went to law school at William Mitchell (now Mitchell Hamline). I started my own practice in 2012, and have entirely focused on criminal defense work, including expungements. I’ve also handled family law matters that have arisen from criminal case work. I represent clients in all types of cases from petty misdemeanor traffic cases to serious felonies, such as first-degree murder. I am admitted to practice in both Minnesota state and federal courts.

Outside of my own practice, I've collaborated with Earl Gray (Earl Gray Defense), a criminal defense attorney of over 50 years, on many serious felony cases, including federal trial work.

Though I office in White Bear Lake, I have had clients all over Minnesota, from up in Grand Marais, down to Albert Lea.

My personality and demeanor coupled with my ability to communicate and work with prosecutors has achieved favorable results for my clients throughout the years. I have vigorously represented my client’s constitutional rights throughout their cases and will always do the same for you. I am here to listen to your opinions on how you want your case to proceed while also providing the legal advice that you need. Whether you think you are in the wrong or completely innocent, I will work with you to get the best possible results. I’m not afraid to take your case to trial and fight for your freedom. I have been involved in trials with charges of criminal sexual conduct, murder, drugs, assault, child molestation, domestic strangulation, theft, fraud … Whether we are pursuing evidentiary issues, plea negotiation, or jury trial — I will be thoroughly prepared to represent you in your case.

Needing a criminal lawyer can be a very stressful time in your life. Please trust that I am here to listen, be available, guide you through the process — explaining each step of the process — and overall understanding you and your goals. I am committed to being available to answer your questions and giving you honest advice.

attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Saint Cloud, MN
attorneys.bio:
Ross Montgomery grew up in West Fargo, North Dakota and attended Minnesota State University of Moorhead where he played collegiate football. Ross then attended law school at the University of North Dakota. He was elected a member of the Order of the Barristers for his exceptional oral and written advocacy skills, one of nine students recognized for this distinction.

Ross's broad range of experience started at the Fargo Public Defender's office and expanded to writing appellate arguments for a private law firm in Fargo, ND. He then served at the Cook County State Attorney's Office Felony Trial Division in Chicago, Illinois where he represented the State in felony drug cases.

Ross has gained experience from a reputable private firm in St. Cloud, Minnesota, representing individuals in criminal, child protection and family law cases. Ross joined PCG Law in 2020 and practices in the areas of criminal defense, family law, and child protection. Ross enjoys spending his free time with his family and Wife, at the lakes and traveling.

Ross is a member of the Stearns Benton Bar Association, Minnesota Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers and the Minnesota State Bar Association.

Ross has assisted hundreds of clients in obtaining fair and just outcomes to their cases. Ross prides himself in providing effective and caring representation to his clients.

attorneys.name: Terrance W. Moore
attorneys.practice_type: Banking, Finance & Workout Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Terry Moore serves as outside general counsel for closely-held businesses and is an experienced business litigator. Moore is an advisor and problem solver for his clients. He negotiates critical contracts including business acquisitions, financing, mergers, media rights agreements, private offerings, real estate and more routine business documents like leases, sales agreements and employment contracts. Prior to joining Hellmuth & Johnson, Terry was with the Steingart, McGrath & Moore firm for 14 years. He has also served as senior attorney and lead negotiator for National Car Rental and with the Minneapolis law firm of Lommen Nelson Cole & Stageberg, P.A.

Terry Moore advises business clients from a variety of industries, with a concentration in the broadcasting and healthcare industries. His practice taps heavily on his experience in negotiations, the broadcast industry and as an entrepreneur himself. Terry advises companies in a broad range of areas, including contract negotiations, sale and acquisition of businesses, employment matters, real estate, regulatory matters, and many other areas.

In 2012, Terry published his first book, Big Force Negotiations. Mr. Moore is a frequent lecturer and author on a variety of topics, including negotiation tactics, ethics, healthcare marketing boundaries and broadcasting. He was named Attorney of the Year for Minnesota Lawyer in 2006. Mr. Moore was awarded the Minnesota State Bar Association's President's Award in 2003. He has also been named a leading Minnesota healthcare attorney and as a Super Lawyer.

Terry also volunteers his time extensively. He serves on the steering committee for raising funds for Jack Jablonski. Terry is a director of the Minnesota Blades AAA Hockey Club. He is a past chair of both the Minnesota State Bar Association's Civil Litigation Section and the Entertainment Law Section. He has also worked with the Minnesota Conference of Chief Judges and the Minnesota District Judges Association.

Terry obtained his J.D. from the University of Minnesota and his B.S. (Government) from St. John's University. He lives in Edina, Minnesota with his wife, Dr. Anne Moore, and their three children.

attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Mankato, MN
attorneys.bio:
Luis is a criminal defense attorney in southern Minnesota who is dedicated to achieving the best possible outcomes for clients facing criminal charges. He represents individuals throughout Minnesota in cases involving drug possession, DWI and alcohol-related offenses, traffic violations, and other misdemeanor and felony charges.

Before entering private practice, he served as a public defender in Douglas County, Alexandria, Minnesota, where he gained extensive courtroom experience representing clients in a wide range of criminal matters. That role gave him valuable insight into how prosecutors prepare cases, a perspective he now uses to build effective defense strategies for his clients.

Luis currently serves in the Minnesota Army National Guard and previously served in the U.S. Navy, where he deployed on the U.S.S. Kearsarge during the Kosovo conflict in 2001 and later to Kuwait during the 2003 Global War on Terrorism. This experience gives him a unique ability to relate to veterans who are facing criminal charges, as he understands firsthand the pressures and challenges of military life.

Clients who work with him find a dedicated southern Minnesota criminal defense lawyer who combines public defense experience, military discipline, and a client-centered approach to achieve meaningful results.

Chris Moreland is not afraid of any corporate "Goliath." With over 20 years of experience advocating on behalf of injured railroad workers and other victims of corporate misconduct, he adds significant bench strength to Halunen Law's employment team. His national practice includes substantial verdicts for his clients in state and federal courts across the country, as well as a significant appellate practice, including arguments in the Supreme Courts of Minnesota, Nebraska, and Montana.

Chris is empathetic to the needs of clients who face the frightening prospect of confronting a corporate adversary with seemingly unlimited resources. Reminded daily of his clients' courage, Chris is ready for the challenge. He is proud to bring his expertise and tenacity to bear for those he represents.

An active member of the Minneapolis legal community, Chris serves on the Board of Governors for the Minnesota Association for Justice, a group of trial lawyers organized to promote the administration of justice for public good. He speaks frequently at continuing legal education seminars and has written articles on legal process, rights and resolutions.

A cum laude graduate of Hamline University School of Law, Chris was selected several times to the Super Lawyers Rising Star list, representing the top 2.5% of Minnesota Lawyers either 40 years old or younger, or who have been in practice for 10 years or less. In 2018 he was selected to the Minnesota Super Lawyers list.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Chris Moreland is not afraid of any corporate "Goliath." With over 20 years of experience advocating on behalf of injured railroad workers and other victims of corporate misconduct, he adds significant bench strength to Halunen Law's employment team. His national practice includes substantial verdicts for his clients in state and federal courts across the country, as well as a significant appellate practice, including arguments in the Supreme Courts of Minnesota, Nebraska, and Montana.

Chris is empathetic to the needs of clients who face the frightening prospect of confronting a corporate adversary with seemingly unlimited resources. Reminded daily of his clients' courage, Chris is ready for the challenge. He is proud to bring his expertise and tenacity to bear for those he represents.

An active member of the Minneapolis legal community, Chris serves on the Board of Governors for the Minnesota Association for Justice, a group of trial lawyers organized to promote the administration of justice for public good. He speaks frequently at continuing legal education seminars and has written articles on legal process, rights and resolutions.

A cum laude graduate of Hamline University School of Law, Chris was selected several times to the Super Lawyers Rising Star list, representing the top 2.5% of Minnesota Lawyers either 40 years old or younger, or who have been in practice for 10 years or less. In 2018 he was selected to the Minnesota Super Lawyers list.

attorneys.bio: Dennis Moriarty is retired. In 1974 Moriarty was elected Scott County Attorney, where he had the responsibility of not only advising the County on all civil matters, but also the duty to prosecute all criminal cases, from petty misdemeanors to gross misdemeanors and felonies. During his career, Moriarty established himself as a highly respected litigator with immense trial experience in both the civil and criminal realms of law. Dennis was a mentor, teacher and friend to many of the attorneys that have worked for his law firm since 1978 and was integral in building the firm that today is known as a preeminent law firm in Scott County. Dennis retired from the practice of law in 2021.

attorneys.name: Jennifer Mortel
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Oakdale, MN
attorneys.bio:
Jennifer Mortel focuses her practice in the areas of Estate Planning, Wills & Trusts, Probate and Trust Administration. Jennifer endeavors to partner with families to secure their future goals through wills, trusts and other appropriate estate planning. She is a compassionate counselor who helps grieving family members find their way through the probate and trust administration process after the death of a loved one. Jennifer also has extensive experience negotiating top-dollar settlements, as well as handling cases through litigation.

Jennifer was a partner at the law firm of Bowden Cyr Mortel, PLLC from 2009-2013 prior to founding Mortel Law, PLLC and represented clients in the area of estate planning. Jennifer also previously served as Assistant Vice-President and head of the Personal Trust Division at Union Bank & Trust where she was responsible for the administration of all personal trusts, including revocable and irrevocable trusts, testamentary trusts and charitable trusts, as well as probate estates. She is a 2002 honors graduate of William Mitchell College of Law and is admitted to practice law in Minnesota and Wisconsin. Jennifer also served as an Arbitrator for the American Arbitration Association and has been an Adjunct Representation Professor at William Mitchell College of Law.

Jennifer was named a Super Lawyer in 2023, 2022 and 2021, which is an honor received by no more than 5% of the lawyers in Minnesota each year. She was also named a Rising Star by Minnesota Super Lawyers in 2017, 2013, and 2012. (Only 2.5% of all attorneys practicing less than 10 years or under the age of 40 years receive the Rising Star honor)

attorneys.name: Carol R.m. Moss
attorneys.practice_type: Appeals Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Carol R. M. Moss is an attorney with the firm and a member of its Litigation Practice Group. Carol's practice is focused in:

General litigation

Personal injury/medical malpractice

Banking & Finance

After obtaining her juris doctor from Hamline University School of Law, Carol joined Hellmuth & Johnson, PLLC in 2008. At Hamline University, she earned the Presidential Scholarship and was on the Dean's List. She was on the Board of Editors for the Hamline Law Review and authored the case note, You Do Know What You're Doing? Right, Doc? Minnesota Supreme Court Contemplates Negligent Credentialing and Privileging, 30 Hamline L. Rev. 125 (2007).

Carol is licensed to practice law in the following courts:

State of Minnesota;

State of Wisconsin;

State of North Dakota;

U.S District Court for the District of Minnesota; and

U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Wisconsin.

Even before her clients get to the courtroom, Carol advocates strongly on their behalf to ensure that their cases are strong and interests are protected. She works with clients from the initial meeting through the end of trial. Her efforts have been recognized by others in the legal community. Carol was selected as an "Up & Coming Attorney" by Minnesota Lawyer in 2010. This award honors attorneys who have been in practice for ten years or less, and who have distinguished themselves by their professional accomplishments, leadership, and service to the community.

In 2012 Carol was included in the Rising Stars list; only 2.5% of young attorneys are chosen each year.

Carol is a member of the Minnesota State Bar Association, Hennepin County Bar Association, Minnesota Association for Justice, Wisconsin Association for Justice, North Dakota Association for Justice, and the American Association for Justice. She has authored articles for the Minnesota Association for Justice and the Minnesota State Bar Association.

She believes that working in the legal profession is a privilege, and attorneys have a moral responsibility to use their skills for the benefit others and to make society better as a whole. Because of these beliefs, Carol is the Chair of the City of Robbinsdale Human Rights Commission, which helps promote the goals of equal human rights, and she also provides pro bono legal work for victims of domestic violence.

attorneys.name: JaneAnne Murray
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Federal Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
JaneAnne Murray is a skilled advocate with over thirty years of experience representing clients in complex criminal and regulatory matters, both at trial and on appeal. She has defended individuals in many sensitive and high-profile investigations and court proceedings, has tried over thirty jury trials as lead counsel. She has handled major matters involving insider trading, securities fraud, bank fraud, insurance fraud, money laundering, RICO violations, computer and Internet-related crimes, tax offenses, embezzlement, public corruption, bribery, obstruction of justice, espionage, and terrorism.

Ms. Murray brings impressive advocacy and negotiating skills to all stages of a criminal proceeding. On numerous occasions, through meticulous investigation, marshaling of the facts and presentation of mitigating circumstances, she has successfully persuaded prosecutors to refrain from indicting her clients, to dismiss pending charges or to offer very favorable plea bargains. In trial cases, she has creatively and vigorously litigated discovery, suppression, dismissal and evidentiary motions, tirelessly investigated defenses, and won a substantial number of acquittals. At sentencing, she has frequently challenged sentencing guideline calculations with success and, hiring mitigation specialists where appropriate, she has achieved a substantial number of sentences below the applicable sentencing guideline.

Ms. Murray is skilled in written and oral appellate advocacy. She has argued numerous appeals in civil and criminal cases in both state and federal courts, winning several notable reversals. She has also filed habeas motions in many federal district courts.

In addition to her work in criminal cases, Ms. Murray has represented whistleblowers, witnesses and targets before a variety of investigative bodies, including the U.S. Congress, the Department of Justice, the Securities and Exchange Commission, the Internal Revenue Service, the New York Attorney General’s Office and the New York State Tax Department. She has counseled individual and corporate clients with regard to internal corporate investigations. She has also represented lawyers, other professionals and students in disciplinary proceedings.

Previously, Ms. Murray was a litigation counsel at O’Melveny & Myers LLP in New York and a litigation associate at Paul, Weiss, Rifkind, Wharton & Garrison LLP. She was also a trial lawyer with the Federal Defenders’ Office for the Eastern District of New York for five years. In 1999, Ms. Murray spent a year in Cambodia working as a provincial human rights advisor with the United Nations High Commission for Human Rights.

A native of Ireland, Ms. Murray is admitted to practice in the courts of New York State and Minnesota, and the Eastern and Southern Districts of New York, the District of Minnesota, The District of North Dakota, the Second Circuit, the Eighth Circuit and the United States Supreme Court.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
JaneAnne Murray is a skilled advocate with over thirty years of experience representing clients in complex criminal and regulatory matters, both at trial and on appeal. She has defended individuals in many sensitive and high-profile investigations and court proceedings, has tried over thirty jury trials as lead counsel. She has handled major matters involving insider trading, securities fraud, bank fraud, insurance fraud, money laundering, RICO violations, computer and Internet-related crimes, tax offenses, embezzlement, public corruption, bribery, obstruction of justice, espionage, and terrorism.

Ms. Murray brings impressive advocacy and negotiating skills to all stages of a criminal proceeding. On numerous occasions, through meticulous investigation, marshaling of the facts and presentation of mitigating circumstances, she has successfully persuaded prosecutors to refrain from indicting her clients, to dismiss pending charges or to offer very favorable plea bargains. In trial cases, she has creatively and vigorously litigated discovery, suppression, dismissal and evidentiary motions, tirelessly investigated defenses, and won a substantial number of acquittals. At sentencing, she has frequently challenged sentencing guideline calculations with success and, hiring mitigation specialists where appropriate, she has achieved a substantial number of sentences below the applicable sentencing guideline.

Ms. Murray is skilled in written and oral appellate advocacy. She has argued numerous appeals in civil and criminal cases in both state and federal courts, winning several notable reversals. She has also filed habeas motions in many federal district courts.

In addition to her work in criminal cases, Ms. Murray has represented whistleblowers, witnesses and targets before a variety of investigative bodies, including the U.S. Congress, the Department of Justice, the Securities and Exchange Commission, the Internal Revenue Service, the New York Attorney General’s Office and the New York State Tax Department. She has counseled individual and corporate clients with regard to internal corporate investigations. She has also represented lawyers, other professionals and students in disciplinary proceedings.

Previously, Ms. Murray was a litigation counsel at O’Melveny & Myers LLP in New York and a litigation associate at Paul, Weiss, Rifkind, Wharton & Garrison LLP. She was also a trial lawyer with the Federal Defenders’ Office for the Eastern District of New York for five years. In 1999, Ms. Murray spent a year in Cambodia working as a provincial human rights advisor with the United Nations High Commission for Human Rights.

A native of Ireland, Ms. Murray is admitted to practice in the courts of New York State and Minnesota, and the Eastern and Southern Districts of New York, the District of Minnesota, The District of North Dakota, the Second Circuit, the Eighth Circuit and the United States Supreme Court.

Sarah (McEllistrem) Rolig is engaged in the general practice of all aspects of civil litigation with an emphasis on employment law litigation in federal and state courts, including discrimination, harassment, retaliation, vicarious liability, negligence, non-compete agreements, tortious interference with business claims, and contractual disputes. Sarah also handles professional licensing matters including the Board of Nursing, the Board of Social Work, the Office of Professional Responsibility, and others.

Sarah is admitted to practice in the State of Minnesota and is a Qualified Neutral in Civil Alternative Dispute Resolution. She is a member of the Warren E. Burger Inn of Court and the National Employment Lawyers Association. She is an active member of the Minnesota State and is the current Past President of the Ramsey County Bar Association.

Personal Bio

Sarah is active as a volunteer with Ramsey County and Washington County law clinics. Prior to earning her law degree, Ms. McEllistrem was a Buyer for Target Corporation responsible for the development, cost negotiations, and overall financial performance of her category assortments nationwide.

attorneys.name: Susan T. Peterson
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Maple Grove, MN
attorneys.bio:
Susan T. Peterson is a shareholder in the firm of Henningson & Snoxell, Ltd., located in Maple Grove, Minnesota. She is a Chair of the firm's Estate Planning Department which boasts more than 35 years of experience counseling individuals and families. Susan practices principally in the areas of:

Estate planning

Probate, estate and trust administration

Elder law

Susan works closely with individuals and families of all sizes and asset levels to identify and prioritize their goals and implement techniques to carry them out. She builds strong relationships with clients, and in turn, clients have great confidence in her and feel comfortable sharing their most personal information and concerns.

Her practice is heavily concentrated in the following areas:

Drafting wills and trusts, as well as other estate planning documents

Incapacity planning

Family business succession planning

Contested probate administrations

Guardianships and conservatorships

Charitable gifting

Medical assistance planning

Susan also assists multi-generation families with high net worth address complex estate and tax issues. She has helped numerous families and their advisors structure estate plans that accomplish the multiple goals affecting these families. Some of the issues she routinely assists with include:

Minimizing taxes related to the transition of wealth from one generation to the next.

Assuring the effective transition of management of family wealth from one generation to the next.

Addressing the unique needs of a family, such as special needs beneficiaries, divorces, premature deaths, and educational goals.

Addressing philanthropic interests and strategizing to address these interests.

She has been selected for inclusion in Minnesota Super Lawyers® - Rising Star Edition, 2008-2010 and 2012. Susan is admitted to practice in all Minnesota state and federal courts. She is a member of the Hennepin County Bar Association and the Probate and Trust Law and Real Property Law sections of the Minnesota State Bar Association. She is also a member of the National Academy of Elder Law Attorneys and Minnesota Women Lawyers. Susan is a frequent speaker on topics associated with estate planning and estate administration, charitable giving, and elder law, and is the author of several articles.

Born in Iowa City, Iowa, Susan received her B.A. magna cum laude from St. Olaf College, her M.A. summa cum laude in English and American Literature from the University of Nevada, Las Vegas, and her law degree summa cum laude from William Mitchell College of Law. Susan clerked for Chief Justice Russell Anderson of the Minnesota Supreme Court and practiced law both as an associate and as principal of her own law firm before joining Henningson & Snoxell in 2004. She lives in Maple Grove with her family and is the immediate past president of the Rotary Club of Maple Grove.

attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Maple Grove, MN
attorneys.bio:
Susan T. Peterson is a shareholder in the firm of Henningson & Snoxell, Ltd., located in Maple Grove, Minnesota. She is a Chair of the firm's Estate Planning Department which boasts more than 35 years of experience counseling individuals and families. Susan practices principally in the areas of:

Estate planning

Probate, estate and trust administration

Elder law

Susan works closely with individuals and families of all sizes and asset levels to identify and prioritize their goals and implement techniques to carry them out. She builds strong relationships with clients, and in turn, clients have great confidence in her and feel comfortable sharing their most personal information and concerns.

Her practice is heavily concentrated in the following areas:

Drafting wills and trusts, as well as other estate planning documents

Incapacity planning

Family business succession planning

Contested probate administrations

Guardianships and conservatorships

Charitable gifting

Medical assistance planning

Susan also assists multi-generation families with high net worth address complex estate and tax issues. She has helped numerous families and their advisors structure estate plans that accomplish the multiple goals affecting these families. Some of the issues she routinely assists with include:

Minimizing taxes related to the transition of wealth from one generation to the next.

Assuring the effective transition of management of family wealth from one generation to the next.

Addressing the unique needs of a family, such as special needs beneficiaries, divorces, premature deaths, and educational goals.

Addressing philanthropic interests and strategizing to address these interests.

She has been selected for inclusion in Minnesota Super Lawyers® - Rising Star Edition, 2008-2010 and 2012. Susan is admitted to practice in all Minnesota state and federal courts. She is a member of the Hennepin County Bar Association and the Probate and Trust Law and Real Property Law sections of the Minnesota State Bar Association. She is also a member of the National Academy of Elder Law Attorneys and Minnesota Women Lawyers. Susan is a frequent speaker on topics associated with estate planning and estate administration, charitable giving, and elder law, and is the author of several articles.

Born in Iowa City, Iowa, Susan received her B.A. magna cum laude from St. Olaf College, her M.A. summa cum laude in English and American Literature from the University of Nevada, Las Vegas, and her law degree summa cum laude from William Mitchell College of Law. Susan clerked for Chief Justice Russell Anderson of the Minnesota Supreme Court and practiced law both as an associate and as principal of her own law firm before joining Henningson & Snoxell in 2004. She lives in Maple Grove with her family and is the immediate past president of the Rotary Club of Maple Grove.

attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Edina, MN
attorneys.bio:
Minnesota attorney Fred Neff has over 30 years experience practicing law in the Twin Cities

In 1986 Minneapolis lawyer Fred Neff founded Neff Law Firm, P.A to serve people in the Twin Cities of Minneapolis and St. Paul and the surrounding communities with conveniently located offices in Edina and Roseville, Minnesota.

Fred Neff has handled many complex cases in the areas of Civil Litigation, Employment Law , Criminal Law, and Business Law .

Fred Neff lawyer is licensed to practice law in Minnesota, Wisconsin and North Dakota

The founder of Neff Law Firm, P.A., Fred Neff, is a Twin Cities lawyer licensed to practice law in Minnesota, Wisconsin and North Dakota. Attorney Fred Neff is also admitted to practice before the 8th Circuit Court of Appeals and the United States Supreme Court.

Minnesota attorney Fred Neff has served as a prosecutor and private attorney

Minnesota Attorney Fred Neff has worked to provide legal help while serving as an investigator, prosecutor, and private attorney handling both criminal and civil litigation. Minneapolis attorney Fred Neff has handled complicated civil and criminal cases throughout Minnesota and elsewhere.

Lawyer Fred Neff has served on legal panels in Hennepin County

Fred Neff has provided help as a Minneapolis lawyer on the Hennepin County Public Defender's Conflicts Panel , the Hennepin County Juvenile Justice panel and numerous Bar association committees in Hennepin County.

Fred Neff Minneapolis lawyer has worked on complex civil litigation

As a lawyer, Fred Neff has delivered legal assistance to many people, and has handled highly complex litigation in various state and federal jurisdictions. Some of the large law cases in which Minneapolis attorney Fred Neff has been involved in providing legal help were plaintiff's anti-trust, Federal multi-district litigation, wrongful death, employment litigation and discrimination litigation on behalf of individuals and large groups of claimants.

Lawyer Fred Neff has handled State and Federal discrimination claims

Lawyer Fred Neff has rendered legal help to the injured and protected the legal rights of many people subjected to discrimination in and out of the workplace in the twin cities of Minneapolis and St. Paul, and elsewhere. Fred Neff as a lawyer has provided legal help to people who have had state discrimination claims and federal discrimination claims in the twin cities of Minneapolis and St. Paul as well as elsewhere.

Minnesota lawyer Fred Neff has worked to protect peoples' constitutional rights

Minnesota lawyer Fred Neff has also given legal help to people whose constitutional rights were violated and other injured people in need of legal help.

Minnesota Lawyer Fred Neff has been on the Board of Directors of an Insurance Company

Fred Neff has served on the Board of Directors of a prominent Insurance Company.

Fred Neff employment lawyer

Lawyer Fred Neff has extensive experience rendering legal help to hourly wage earners, salaried employees, managers, high level executives and officers. Minneapolis attorney Fred Neff has provided legal help to licensed investment professionals, licensed insurance professionals and bankers. He has helped injured workers with ordinary to very complex claims. Minnesota lawyer Fred Neff has extensive experience as an employment lawyer.

Attorney Fred Neff has helped injured consumers

Fred Neff also has extensive experience as a lawyer providing legal help to injured consumers on investment fraud claims.

Attorney Fred Neff has provided legal help to people and organizations

Attorney Fred Neff has represented many different types of entities including a branch of an international Church, business organizations and numerous members of various unions.

Fred Neff media

From 1989-1991, Minnesota lawyer Fred Neff acted as a co-host on a popular television program Great Puzzles in History covering historical mysteries including unsolved crimes. As the program involved many historically intriguing legal cases and included information and insight into the law and the legal system in general. Two books Great Puzzles of History and Mysterious Persons in History were written by Minneapolis Minnesota lawyer Fred Neff and published by Runestone Press based upon the popular response from the television show.

Awards given to Fred Neff

Fred Neff has received many awards for his accomplishments and community involvement including the City of St. Paul Citizen of the Month Award in 1975, commendations for Distinguished Service from the Sibley County Attorney's office in 1980, the WCCO Good Neighbor Award in 1985, the HLS Justice Award for Lawyers in 1985, the Lamp of Knowledge Award from the T.C.L.G. in 1986, Creative Thinker Award for Lawyers in 1986, Honors Certificate For Authors-Children's Reading Roundtable of Chicago 1988, commendation awards from N.W. Community T.V. 1989, 1990, and 1991, the Presidential Medal of Merit Award in 1990, the Wisdom Award in 1998, and the Ronald Reagan Gold Medal 2004.

Minnesota Lawyer Fred Neff in reference books

Minnesota lawyer Fred Neff has had his biography in reference books including Who's Who in America, Who's Who in The World, Who's Who in American Law, Who's Who In The Midwest, Who's Who in Finance and Business, and Who's Who in Society.

Fred Neff featured in Twin Cities Luxury and Fashion

Twin Cities Luxury and Fashion published an article in July 2007 issue on Minnesota lawyer Fred Neff that stated:

"His achievements are numerous from receiving a commendation from the Sibley County Attorney's office, St. Paul Citizen of the Month Award, WCCO Good Neighbor Award and the Presidential Medal of Merit, to writing 19 books, to getting the Creative Thinker Award for Lawyers. He's even acted as a co-host on a TV show called, "Great Puzzles in History" where he gave insight into the legal system.

The range of cases he handles, which includes everything from discrimination to wrongful death claims to fraudulent business practices, keeps him studying he says, but also keeps him fresh and enthused. It explains the sparkle and the humor but also the aura of curiosity that drives him and causes others to lean forward into the conversation as much as he does."

attorneys.name: Blake R. Nelson
attorneys.practice_type: Banking, Finance & Workout Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Blake Nelson is a partner with the firm and chair of the Construction Law Group, and also serves on the firm's Board of Governors. He primarily represents privately-held businesses of all types, with a concentration in meeting the unique needs of those in the construction industry.

Blake's practice includes counsel and representation in the following primary areas:

Construction law and litigation

Real estate law and litigation

General corporate representation

Creditor's remedies

Blake's background brings unique experience to his construction law practice. He grew up working at his family-owned lumber yard in his teens and early twenties, learning about the construction industry from the inside out. His first-hand experience working in the construction industry gives him a unique perspective when counseling his clients.

One of Blake's particular areas of expertise is the perfection and enforcement of mechanic's liens. He is widely regarded as an authority in that area, and has written numerous articles and taught many seminars about enforcement of mechanic's liens and creditor remedies for businesses in the construction industry. He also has extensive experience helping construction clients with contract disputes and bond claim enforcement.

Blake is also the chief author and editor of the quarterly publication The Authority on Construction Law and the author of Construction Liens: A National Review and Template for a Uniform Lien Act, published in the William Mitchell College Law Review. Blake routinely writes for other construction industry publications and trade journals, and is a frequent lecturer on construction law and creditor issues.

Blake is also a Minnesota State Bar Association (MSBA) Board Certified Real Property Law Specialist, a designation held by a select few Minnesota attorneys. He represents many commercial real estate investors, owners and developers and provides counsel regarding their purchase, sale and leasing transactions. He also has extensive experience in handling and structuring tax deferred real estates exchanges under Section 1031 of the Internal Revenue Code (26 U.S.C. § 1031).

An experienced business counselor, Blake also serves in a general counsel capacity for his clients, guiding them in formulating creative strategies to maximize opportunity and minimize risk. As such, his services encompass a wide range of transactional matters including:

Buy/sell agreements

Business sale and purchase agreements

Joint venture agreements

Independent contractor and sales representative agreements

Shareholder/partnership agreements

For his entire career, Blake has counseled and assisted creditors in recovering accounts receivable, having represented both businesses and collection agencies. With a specific concentration on clients in the construction industry, Blake routinely recovers funds and negotiates favorable settlements in connection with construction projects. Absent mechanic's lien rights, collection in these cases can be more difficult, but clients rely upon Blake's years of experience in this area to create favorable results. Blake assists clients in every phase of creditor remedies, from reviewing and improving contracts and credit applications to obtaining and collecting judgments against debtors.

Outside of his successful law practice, Blake also serves in other areas of the community and has been honored numerous times over the years.

Blake serves on the Board of Directors for Minnesota Bank and Trust in Edina, Minnesota, the only new bank to successfully open in Minnesota in 2008. Kate Kelly, president and CEO of Minnesota Bank & Trust, called Nelson an "outside of the box thinker" who helped the new bank get on its feet and build a market presence.

In 2009, Blake was honored as one of the Minneapolis/St. Paul Business Journal's "40 Under Forty" top business leaders.

Blake has repeatedly been chosen for inclusion in the Minnesota Super Lawyers® list, only 5% of attorneys in the state of Minnesota are selected each year.

Blake is also AV® Peer Review Rated – the highest possible peer review rating from Martindale-Hubbell™. An AV Rating shows that a lawyer has reached the height of professional excellence, has usually practiced law for many years, and is recognized for the highest levels of skill and integrity.

The first letter rates the lawyer's ability, with A being the highest possible ranking and indicating that the lawyer's abilities are "Very High to Preeminent."

The second letter rates the lawyer's general ethical standards, and denotes adherence to professional standards of conduct and ethics, reliability, diligence and other criteria relevant to the discharge of professional responsibilities. "AV" rating indicates that the lawyer's ethical rating is "Very High."

Together, the "AV" rating is the highest possible and Blake is proud to have achieved that rating in 2005 in only his tenth year of practice.

Blake served for six years on the Hennepin County Fourth District Ethics Committee as a member and investigator.

Blake obtained his J.D. magna cum laude from William Mitchell College of Law and graduated cum laude from Gustavus Adolphus College with Bachelor of Arts degrees in English and Political Science. He is licensed to practice law in the State and Federal courts in Minnesota and is a member of the Hennepin County and Minnesota State Bar Associations.

Blake offers a free 30 minute initial consultation to potential new clients and is happy to discuss new matters by phone or in person.

With a specific concentration on clients in the construction industry, Blake routinely recovers funds and negotiates favorable settlements in connection with construction projects. Absent mechanic's lien rights, collection in these cases can be more difficult, but clients rely upon Blake's years of experience in this area to create favorable results. Blake assists clients in every phase of creditor remedies, from reviewing and improving contracts and credit applications to obtaining and collecting judgments against debtors.

Outside of his successful law practice, Blake also serves in other areas of the community and has been honored numerous times over the years.

Blake serves on the Board of Directors for Minnesota Bank and Trust in Edina, Minnesota, the only new bank to successfully open in Minnesota in 2008. Kate Kelly, president and CEO of Minnesota Bank & Trust, called Nelson an "outside of the box thinker" who helped the new bank get on its feet and build a market presence.

In 2009, Blake was honored as one of the Minneapolis/St. Paul Business Journal's "40 Under Forty" top business leaders.

Blake has repeatedly been chosen for inclusion in the Minnesota Super Lawyers® list, only 5% of attorneys in the state of Minnesota are selected each year.

Blake is also AV® Peer Review Rated – the highest possible peer review rating from Martindale-Hubbell™. An AV Rating shows that a lawyer has reached the height of professional excellence, has usually practiced law for many years, and is recognized for the highest levels of skill and integrity.

The first letter rates the lawyer's ability, with A being the highest possible ranking and indicating that the lawyer's abilities are "Very High to Preeminent."

The second letter rates the lawyer's general ethical standards, and denotes adherence to professional standards of conduct and ethics, reliability, diligence and other criteria relevant to the discharge of professional responsibilities. "AV" rating indicates that the lawyer's ethical rating is "Very High."

Together, the "AV" rating is the highest possible and Blake is proud to have achieved that rating in 2005 in only his tenth year of practice.

Blake served for six years on the Hennepin County Fourth District Ethics Committee as a member and investigator.

Blake obtained his J.D. magna cum laude from William Mitchell College of Law and graduated cum laude from Gustavus Adolphus College with Bachelor of Arts degrees in English and Political Science. He is licensed to practice law in the State and Federal courts in Minnesota and is a member of the Hennepin County and Minnesota State Bar Associations.

Blake offers a free 30 minute initial consultation to potential new clients and is happy to discuss new matters by phone or in person.

attorneys.practice_type: Family law Lawyers in Saint Paul, MN
attorneys.bio:
Evan is associate attorney practicing in the areas of family law, employment law, and business law. He approaches his practice with compassion, a friendly demeanor, and an eye for details, all the while vigorously advocating for his clients’ rights. Evan has a passion for helping folks traverse the legal landscape, which can be overwhelming and full of complicated and contentious disputes, and is committed to finding the right solution for each unique circumstance.

Prior to joining Collins, Buckley, Sauntry & Haugh, Evan was a judicial law clerk in Hennepin County Family Court for several years, where he worked exclusively for Family Court Presiding Judge Theresa Couri. During his clerkship, Evan worked on divorces, custody and parenting time disputes, as well as domestic abuse and harassment matters, from which he gained invaluable experience resolving cases that involved significant conflict and intricate financial situations. In law school, Evan served as a moot court student instructor, where he began developing his abilities in litigation and advocacy.

Evan grew up in St. Paul and loved it so much that he never left the Twin Cities area. Outside of his practice, Evan enjoys spending time with his family and friends, hopelessly rooting on Minnesota sports teams, and playing pickup basketball and recreational softball with his buddies.

attorneys.name: Eric L. Newmark
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Minnetonka, MN
attorneys.bio:
An attorney with nearly 30 years of trial experience, Eric L. Newmark is the founding partner of the Newmark Law Office LLC in Minnetonka, Minnesota. Eric defends clients in all types of criminal charges, including drug crimes, violent crimes, white collar crimes, driving offenses, DUI/DWIs and many other felonies and misdemeanors. Eric represents individuals charged with crimes in both State and Federal court and is licensed in Minnesota and Wisconsin. Eric also has represented clients in federal courts in Wisconsin, North and South Dakota, and Wisconsin, as well as state court in South Dakota and Montana.

Certified as a Criminal Law Specialist by the Minnesota State Bar Association, Eric has earned acquittals and dismissals in nearly every type of criminal case from 1st Degree Murder to driving offenses. Eric is often hired by trucking and insurance companies to represent their drivers in vehicular homicide cases and has been retained by other attorneys as an expert witness in the area of criminal law.

A "lawyer's lawyer" and a problem solver, Eric is respected for his professionalism and integrity, and admired for his aggressive, pragmatic and creative approach to representing clients.

In addition to his criminal practice, Eric also represents Judges, attorneys, doctors, nurses, real estate agents and other professionals in investigations before licensing and disciplinary boards.

Eric has presented at national criminal defense seminars on drug interdiction, and locally on jury selection and the interplay between immigration and criminal law, jury selection, and ethics, among other subjects. Eric has appeared on numerous media outlets including MSNBC, KARE, KSTP, FOX9, and has offered analysis for the Star Tribune, the Los Angeles Times, and the Baltimore Sun, among other outlets.

Eric was selected as a Rising Star in 1999, just three years after becoming a practicing attorney and has been recognized as a super lawyer for 25 consecutive years.

attorneys.name: Kathleen M. Newman
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
November 2014- Read Kathy Newman's article published in Expert Beacon, "Navigating prenuptial agreements for same-sex couples getting married

"My clients need an advocate and that's why they hire me. I'm a good negotiator, but I'm not a pushover and my opposing counsel knows that. I know the system and how it works and I know most of the players. I can tell my clients if what they want is realistic, and if so, how they can go about getting it."

With extensive experience in all aspects of marital dissolutions, Kathleen M. Picotte Newman has represented many complex and ongoing matters in the personal, financial and business interests of her clients. You will likely first notice her quiet demeanor and listening skills as she discerns the critical issues of a case. Then she will quickly drill down with practiced interviewing skills to the facts, timelines and your goals for resolution.

Focusing her practice on clients whose business and financial interests require sophisticated counsel for discovery, negotiations and potential court representation, Kathleen is adept at legal strategies that keep your case moving forward toward a reasonable and appropriate conclusion. Until then, she will assertively pursue your interests even for issues that evolve after your divorce. Her experience includes business and asset valuation issues, custody, prenuptial agreements and maintenance disputes, and hidden or non-marital property matters.

When children are involved, Kathleen sets herself apart through her strong advocacy of custody, support and parenting agreements that meet long-term needs. Although she rarely represents children directly, her counsel to clients always keeps a child's interests in the mix of negotiations.

Kathleen is Board-Certified as a Family Law Trial Advocate by the National Board of Trial Advocacy. But she is also a skilled mediator, approved for inclusion in the Minnesota ADR Statewide Neutrals Roster in all categories of Family Neutrals.

Minnesota Law & Politics has consistently listed Kathleen as a Super Lawyer and named her among the Top 40 Super Lawyers for Family Law. She was also named among the Top 100 Women Super Lawyers by Minneapolis-St. Paul Magazine. Since 1993, Kathleen has been named every year to the Best Lawyers in America (Family Law). She is also a Fellow in the prestigious American Academy of Matrimonial Lawyers.

In the midst of developing her successful legal practice, Kathleen was trained at the internationally renowned Hudson Institute of Santa Barbara as a certified Life Coach. She focuses her coaching practice on professional development for attorneys.

When children are involved, Kathleen sets herself apart through her strong advocacy of custody, support and parenting agreements that meet long-term needs. Although she rarely represents children directly, her counsel to clients always keeps a child's interests in the mix of negotiations.

Kathleen is Board-Certified as a Family Law Trial Advocate by the National Board of Trial Advocacy. But she is also a skilled mediator, approved for inclusion in the Minnesota ADR Statewide Neutrals Roster in all categories of Family Neutrals.

Minnesota Law & Politics has consistently listed Kathleen as a Super Lawyer and named her among the Top 40 Super Lawyers for Family Law. She was also named among the Top 100 Women Super Lawyers by Minneapolis-St. Paul Magazine. Since 1993, Kathleen has been named every year to the Best Lawyers in America (Family Law). She is also a Fellow in the prestigious American Academy of Matrimonial Lawyers.

In the midst of developing her successful legal practice, Kathleen was trained at the internationally renowned Hudson Institute of Santa Barbara as a certified Life Coach. She focuses her coaching practice on professional development for attorneys.

attorneys.name: Benjamin J. Nicolet
attorneys.practice_type: Personal injury Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Meet Attorney Ben Nicolet

Benjamin Nicolet joined Nicolet Law Accident & Injury Lawyer as an attorney in 2017. Prior to joining the firm, Ben spent summers during law school clerking at the office. Ben handles personal injury cases across Minnesota and Wisconsin. Ben is admitted to practice law in the state courts of Minnesota and Wisconsin; as well as the federal courts of the District of Minnesota and Western District of Wisconsin.

A Strong Background In Legal Studies And Civil Advocacy

Benjamin graduated cum laude from the University of Minnesota Law School in May 2017. While attending law school, Ben was actively involved in the school's bankruptcy clinic program, where he represented low-income individuals from the Twin Cities in bankruptcy filings and proceedings. Ben also competed in Minnesota Law's Maynard Pirsig Moot Court program and upon graduation, Ben received the law school's Civil Litigation Concentration certificate. Ben is a member of the American Bankruptcy Institute and has co-authored articles for the institute's journal on multiple occasions.

Dedicated To Learning At A Local And Global Level

Benjamin graduated from the University of Wisconsin - Eau Claire in 2013. Between graduating from UW - Eau Claire and beginning law school, Ben spent a year living and teaching English in Kharkiv, Ukraine. During that time, he began learning the Russian language and he continues to study it.

In his free time, Benjamin enjoys spending time with his wife Vilena, bicycling, traveling, and playing chess.

"Clients generally come to us when they feel like their lives have been turned upside down; whether it's from a car accident that has caused them injuries or relentless creditors harassing them day and night. In chaos, there must be calculation. My goal is to be a steady hand for our clients that guides them to financial freedom or recovery."

attorneys.name: Brian N. Niemczyk
attorneys.practice_type: Appeals Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Brian Niemczyk joined Hellmuth & Johnson in 2012. He is a 2006 graduate of Hamline University School of Law, and spent several years before law school working as an intern at the United States Attorney's Office in Minneapolis. Mr. Niemczyk practices primarily with the firm's litigation group and focuses on employment law, commercial litigation, and real estate litigation.

During law school, Mr. Niemczyk was a two-year staff member of the Hamline Law Review, serving as symposium editor during his final year. In 2005, Mr. Niemczyk published an article in the Hamline Law Review entitled, "Baker v. Nelson Revisited: Is Same-Sex Marriage Coming to Minnesota?" 28 Hamline L. Rev. 425 (2005). Mr. Niemczyk was also an active volunteer in the Minnesota Justice Foundation, serving as a volunteer in the Public Defender's Office for the First Judicial District.

Mr. Niemczyk represents a wide variety of businesses and individuals involved in a wide range of real estate and commercial disputes. These commonly include disagreements over real estate and asset purchase agreements, leases, mortgages, mechanic's liens, and condominium disclosure statements. In addition, Mr. Niemczyk represents numerous individuals and small businesses in connection with employment disputes, including illegal retaliation and discrimination claims and disagreements concerning employment contracts and non-compete agreements. Mr. Niemczyk works to provide pragmatic solutions to his clients, whether it be through litigation, negotiation, or other forms of alternative dispute resolution.

Mr. Niemczyk is originally from Little Canada, Minnesota. He currently resides in Maple Grove with his wife, Emily and two children.

attorneys.name: Andrea B. Niesen
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Law Lawyers in Rochester, MN
attorneys.bio:
Andrea B. Niesen is a civil litigation attorney with experience in all areas of employment law, disability matters, professional licensing and contracts, workers' compensation, and construction defect claims. Andrea is a qualified neutral as recognized by the Minnesota Supreme Court, able to assist with mediations related to employment disputes. She is admitted to practice in both state and federal court systems in Minnesota and Wisconsin.

Andrea has been a dedicated member of the Rochester legal community, starting at Bird, Jacobsen & Stevens in 2004, and then transitioning her legal practice to Klampe, Delehanty & Pasternak, LLC in 2016 and became a partner to form Klampe, Delehanty, Pasternak & Niesen, LLC in 2019. Andrea grew up in central Wisconsin. She received a business management degree from the University of Wisconsin-Stout in 2000 and her law degree from Marquette University Law School in 2003. Upon completing her law degree, Andrea started her legal practice at a well-respected law firm in Milwaukee, handling employment and workers' compensation cases.

For over 15 years, she has volunteered with Make-A-Wish Foundation of Minnesota, as both a former executive board member and a local wish granter. In 2018, she was appointed to the executive board for the People's Food Co-Op, and she is currently the board secretary. She also serves on the executive board for Family Services Rochester, a nonprofit organization with the mission to support and enhance the dignity and quality of life for individuals and families in our community. Andrea was named Attorney of the Year for 2017 - a prestigious honor awarded to a select group of attorneys each year.

attorneys.name: Karina Norberg
attorneys.practice_type: Workers’ Compensation Lawyers in St. Paul, MN
attorneys.bio:
Karina Norberg is an associate attorney at the Law Office of Joshua Borken and handles workers' compensation cases on behalf of Minnesota workers who have been injured on the job or have contracted an occupational disease and are seeking their rightful benefits. Karina has a genuine commitment to secure for her clients the maximum amount of compensation possible to cover their medical bills, replace lost wages, and other expenses related to work accidents.

Karina has served as a judicial law clerk at the Fourth Judicial District in Hennepin County and worked at two other prominent Minneapolis law firms for more than 2 years. During that time, she gained invaluable litigation skills which she now applies to her workers' compensation practice.

Karina obtained her first Juris Doctor degree from San Marcos University in Lima, Peru. In 2008, Karina was awarded a full scholarship by the Ford Foundation to pursue her master's degree in Public Affairs at the University of Texas at Austin. Karina then moved to Minnesota where she obtained her second Juris Doctor degree from Mitchell Hamline School of Law.

Karina is licensed to practice law in Minnesota and in Peru. Holding both licenses give Karina unparalleled skills to provide legal representation services in both English and Spanish. Karina can fluently communicate and explain complex information to her Spanish-speaking clients.

Karina is a member of the Minnesota State Bar and the Minnesota Hispanic Bar Association.

Karina Norberg es abogada en la Oficina Legal del Licenciado Joshua Borken y representa a trabajadores en sus demandas de compensación por accidentes de trabajo o enfermedad ocupacional en el estado de Minnesota. Karina está muy comprometida en lograr que sus clientes obtengan el máximo monto de compensación para cubrir sus gastos médicos, salarios perdidos, y otros gastos asociados con los accidentes de trabajo.

Karina ha sido asistente judicial en el 4to Distrito Judicial del Condado de Hennepin y ha trabajado en dos importantes firmas de abogados de Minneapolis por más de 2 años. Durante ese tiempo, Karina ha ganado una importante experiencia en litigación, la cual ahora aplica en defensa de los trabajadores.

Karina se graduó como abogada en la Universidad Nacional Mayor de San Marcos en Lima, Perú. En 2008, Karina obtuvo una beca para realizar una maestría en la Universidad de Texas en Austin. Para poder ejercer como abogada en los Estados Unidos, Karina estudió Derecho en la Escuela de Leyes Mitchell Hamline de San Pablo en Minnesota.

Karina esta habilitada para ejercer como abogada en Minnesota y en Perú. Por esa razón, Karina puede ofrecer servicios legales en inglés y español. Karina tiene un dominio del español que le permite communicarse con sus clientes sin ninguna dificultad.

Karina es miembro de la Barra del Estado de Minnesota y de la Asociación de Abogados Hispanos de Minnesota.

sections.content:

Roz has over 40 years of experience as a family law attorney, and she understands the family law system. She is a strong legal advocate for her clients in marriage dissolutions, post-decree matters, paternity proceedings, child custody and parenting time disputes, child and spousal support issues, same-sex partnership and property agreements and dissolutions, antenuptial and postnuptial agreements, and family-law-related appeals. Roz is supportive of alternative dispute resolution options for her clients, but she also has the skills to successfully litigate cases that need court involvement. Roz is an honors graduate of Augsburg College and the University of Minnesota Law School. In her time away from the office, Roz enjoys travel, attending sporting events, reading, golf and time with her family and friends.

attorneys.name: André A.S. Novack
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Rochester, MN
attorneys.bio:
André A.S. Novack is a partner at Klampe Law Firm and best known for representing clients in personal injury cases. With millions of dollars won for injury victims, his assertive yet ethical approach to advocacy consistently has delivered results case after case.

Each case presents unique challenges, and André works closely with clients through every phase—from free consultation to trial. Although he thrives in litigation and the courtroom, he makes every effort to maximize results without the need for lawsuits. He represents injury clients on a contingency-fee basis, meaning they can focus on healing and never need to worry about paying attorney fees out of pocket, while allowing André to work diligently on their case.

In 2024, Martindale-Hubbell honored André with a rating of AV-Preeminent, its highest possible distinction awarded for professional skill and ethical standards, achieved by only about 10% of lawyers. In 2023, he was also named to the list of Super Lawyers – Rising Stars, a distinction reserved for just 2.5% of Minnesota attorneys. His past pro bono work has also earned him multiple North Star Lawyer recognitions, underscoring his commitment to accessible justice.

Through his time at William Mitchell College of Law, his commitment to justice became clear. He represented a low-income client against a prominent Twin Cities firm at the Minnesota Court of Appeals as a certified student attorney, and he built skills in moot courts, mock jury and bench trials, and an externship with Hennepin County Judge Susan B. Robiner. Winning his law school’s client counseling competition cemented his passion for client advocacy.

Born and raised in the Twin Cities, André relocated to Rochester in 2016 with his wife. Before joining Klampe Law Firm in 2017, he worked for legal aid and honed his skills on large-scale litigations for premier law firms in Minneapolis. As a partner at Klampe Law Firm, André is honored to represent clients from all backgrounds, committed to achieving optimal outcomes and upholding their rights.

Outside the courtroom, André enjoys family time with his wife and two young children. He also shares his home with a number of beloved four-legged furballs. An outdoors enthusiast and theatergoer, André tries to balance his dedication to his clients with a love for nature, physical activity, and the arts.

attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Saint Paul, MN
attorneys.bio:
Practice Experience

Sonja is an attorney and focuses her practice exclusively on family law, including but not limited to divorce, custody matters, paternity, child support, spousal maintenance, non-marital tracing and property division, prenuptial agreement drafting and review, as well as interstate and appellate work. Sonja takes great pride in helping individuals through the most difficult of family matters, zealously and empathetically advocating for their rights. The quality of Sonja’s work has resulted in her receipt of a “Superb” rating through Avvo.com and being named a Super Lawyer, a selection based off of an evaluation of 12 indicators including peer recognition and professional achievement in legal practice.

Prior to beginning her practice in 2012, Sonja secured a judicial clerkship in Hennepin County Family Court. There, she worked on high asset divorce cases with complex financial matters, as well as high conflict custody disputes. Sonja learned firsthand how judicial officers decide cases and what makes a family law attorney effective inside and outside of the courtroom. Sonja knows that every family is different. Her experience, knowledge of the court system, and reasoned approach to these matters helps her clients achieve their unique goals.
