Eric was born and raised in Central Minnesota. Eric's primary areas of practice are general litigation, workers compensation, insurance defense, personal injury litigation, and motor vehicle law. Eric's goal is to achieve successful results for his clients in a cost-effective and time-efficient manner.

Eric graduated from St. John's University Magna Cum Laude before receiving his J.D. from the University of Missouri. Eric was named a Minnesota Rising Star, an award limited to 2.5 percent of lawyers in the state, in 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022 and 2023. Eric was named a Minnesota Super Lawyer in 2025.

Eric has worked with insurance companies, self-insureds, third-party administrators, contractors, agricultural cooperatives, large businesses, small business owners, and individuals, among others. Eric has argued in front of the Minnesota Court of Appeals and the U.S. District Court for the District of Minnesota.

Eric has represented clients in/at the Minnesota District Courts, the Minnesota Court of Appeals, the Office of Administrative Hearings (workers compensation and OSHA matters), the Minnesota Department of Labor and Industry, the American Arbitration Association, the U.S. District Court for the District of Minnesota, and the United States Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit.

Outside of the office, Eric enjoys fishing (both ice fishing and soft water fishing), golfing, biking and traveling. However, spending time with his wife and children is his favorite past time.

attorneys.bio:
Jill Oleisky graduated from the William Mitchell College of Law in 1997. She has been representing clients charged with criminal offenses for over 22 years. Jill has represented clients on a multitude of cases, including DWI, assault, drug offenses, theft, fraud and criminal sexual misconduct. She has had numerous court and jury trials in Minnesota. She enjoys advocating for her clients and ensuring for them the best results.

Jill has contracted as a substitute Hennepin County Public Defender since 2014 representing clients charged with misdemeanor and gross misdemeanor offenses

Jill has been involved with many Minnesota bar associations. She is a past chair of the Minnesota State Bar Association Criminal Division, past co-chair of the Hennepin County Bar Association Criminal Section, and 2018-2019 president of the Minnesota Society for Criminal Justice. She is slated to be the 2020-2021 President of the Amdahl Inn of Court.

Jill is the coordinator for the weekly reading program - Everybody Wins Reading Program which pairs up adults to work with second graders in North Minneapolis on their reading skills. Jill has been the coordinator of this program since 2010.

attorneys.name: Robert E Oleisky
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal defense Lawyers in Minnetonka, MN
attorneys.bio:
Bob Oleisky has spent his entire legal career practicing criminal defense and advocating for his clients. He has represented clients over the last 28 years on every type of criminal charge ranging from DWI, assaults, thefts and even murder. He has been named a Minnesota “Super Lawyer” for 20 straight years.

Bob graduated from Hamline Law School in 1992 and founded his own law firm representing individuals accused of criminal offenses. In 1997, his sister, Jill Oleisky, joined him and they formed the law firm of Oleisky & Oleisky, P.A.

Bob has tried jury and court trials across the state of Minnesota. He has obtained dismissals of charges in misdemeanor and felony cases. He practices criminal defense in both state and federal court.

Bob is a member of Minnesota Society for Criminal Justice, the MN State Bar Association and has spoken at many Continuing Legal Education seminars over the years.

attorneys.name: Trevor S. Oliver
attorneys.practice_type: Administrative Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Trevor Oliver is an associate attorney at Burns and Hansen, focusing on real estate litigation, probate law, estate planning, municipal law, civil litigation, and transactional matters.

Trevor has over a decade of experience in addressing property owner disputes, including rent escrow, evictions, illegal activity provision, and violations of local and state ordinances. Trevor has experience interacting with municipal officials on behalf of clients to resolve issues with local ordinance compliance, licensing, and permitting. Trevor has handled cases involving land ownership, boundary disputes, zoning compliance, variances, and permitting. Trevor also assists clients with their probate matters by drafting wills, health care directives, powers of attorney, and transfer on death deeds. In addition, Trevor advocates for clients in probate disputes involving real property, personal property, and monetary assets. Trevor represents clients in civil litigation cases involving disputes between business owners, breaches of contract, specific performance, and debt collection. In transactional matters, Trevor drafts purchase agreements, employment agreements, leases, and business formation documents.

Trevor is a thoughtful, thorough, and meticulous advocate on behalf of his clients. He articulates himself clearly, both in the courtroom and in his pleadings. Trevor takes a big-picture view of the case, bringing to bear his experience in a variety of areas to position his client for the best result possible in their case.

Trevor attended the University of Chicago, where he received his Bachelor's degree in Political Science. Trevor received his law degree from the University of Minnesota, where he participated in the prosecution clinic as a certified student attorney.

After law school, Trevor served for four years in active duty with the United States Army as a Judge Advocate General (JAG). As a JAG officer, Trevor was a legal assistance attorney in preparing wills and answering legal questions for deploying soldiers and their families as the US military mobilized in the immediate period after 9/11. Later in his career as a JAG officer, Trevor served as trial defense counsel and then senior trial defense counsel, representing soldiers in military justice proceedings.

After finishing military service, Trevor worked in private practice for eight years at a law firm, concentrating on municipal law, labor law, and civil litigation. Before joining Burns and Hansen, Trevor worked for the Minnesota legislature as a majority party research consultant for the commerce committee, energy policy committee, and labor and regulated industries committee.

In 2011, Trevor was appointed by the Mayor of St. Paul, Chris Coleman, to serve on the Planning Commission, a post he held for ten years.

In his spare time, Trevor enjoys spending time with his family and friends, competing in recreational softball, and being a fan of the Minnesota Twins. Trevor has also coached youth baseball and soccer teams in the Twin Cities east metro.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Named "Rising Star" by Minnesota Law & Politics Magazine, 2009

attorneys.name: Edward C. Olson
attorneys.practice_type: Social Security Disability Lawyers in Chaska, MN
attorneys.bio:
I was born and raised in Minnesota. I am married with a young daughter. I began practicing law with my father, Rodney, in 1991. Since 1995, I have been developing my own practice representing individuals claiming Social Security Disability Insurance benefits and Supplemental Security Income.

Getting to know Ed Olson...

I became a lawyer because... it allows me to help people who have really had some bad breaks and who really deserve some help.

What I like most about the law is... it is a lot like solving a puzzle. When all the pieces fit together, a beautiful picture emerges.

When you need an attorney... it is important to find an attorney you can be comfortable with. A legal proceeding is sometimes a very long and arduous process and it is important that your lawyer is someone you can trust not only with legal matters but with the personal information related to any law suit.

In addition, it is important the attorney you choose have experience in the area of law relevant to your problem. Like doctors, attorneys have areas of expertise and it is important that your attorney have experience successfully dealing with your legal problem.

My most rewarding case involved...a young man who had been involved in several automobile accidents. After a prolonged dispute, he was finally awarded the Social Security benefits to which he was entitled. The award of benefits allowed him to keep his home and afford his children's education.

My most disappointing case involved... an elderly gentleman who was improperly denied Social Security disability benefits. He came to me long after he started his claim for benefits. By the time I became involved, his claim was is such disarray, that my best efforts were not successful. If this gentleman had come to me earlier, I feel I would have been able to help him secure his benefits.

I began solo practice because... I like to manage my cases myself. I know exactly what is going on with each of my clients and their cases.

What makes Edward C. Olson different from other lawyers? I really listen to my clients.

My friends describe me as... someone with a good sense of humor.

My opponents describe me as... persistent.

If I had to attempt another profession, I would try... coaching athletics. I think I could do a good job teaching and inspiring people to achieve team success.

Two people I really admire are... my mother and father. As the father of a young daughter myself, I admire the fact that my parents were able to raise four children and maintain their sanity.

My favorite quote is... "If you can't laugh at yourself make fun of other people."

My favorite book is... "The Choirboys" by Joseph Wambaugh. The funniest book I have ever read.

My favorite sports team is... the Minnesota Golden Gophers.

My favorite music is... classic rock and roll.

My favorite movie is... Goodfellas.

A sound or noise I love is... the sound of my daughter's laughter.

Outside of my family, my most treasured belonging is... my dog, Liz.

When not at work, I enjoy... golfing, playing cards and chasing after my young daughter.

My favorite lawyer joke is... it was so cold out yesterday, I saw two lawyers with their hands in their OWN pockets.

attorneys.name: Heather Olson
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Buffalo, MN
attorneys.bio:
Criminal Law And Family Law Attorney Heather Olson

As a respected criminal defense and family law attorney, Heather Olson is a head above the rest when it comes to interpersonal skills with clients and her command of criminal and family law. Not only does she know the law and fight for what’s right for her clients, she manages each assessment with compassion and sensitivity.

When clients come into Heather’s office, they do not feel as though they are being judged. Heather treats people as equals and individuals. While still maintaining her professionalism, she has a knack for making clients feel as though they have just spoken to a friend. Clients feel reassured that Heather is taking her top-notch knowledge of the law and applying it with close attention to detail to each case in order to achieve the best possible outcome.

Whether facing criminal charges or conviction, or distress caused by personal family crises, many people caught up in the justice system are intimidated, uncertain how to protect their rights, and fearful for their future and their freedoms.

Heather is strategic, tenacious, and forward thinking in her tactics for each case. Clients find her to be an approachable, genuinely caring family law attorney with passion and diligence in protecting her client’s rights.

Criminal Defense Attorney Committed To Fighting For Your Rights

Heather has extensive experience prosecuting cases at the Wright County Prosecution Attorney’s Office; she has been a part-time Public Defender and is now a private attorney. Her ability to creatively approach each case and see the inherently unique qualities sets her apart. She has significant courtroom experience and the ability to negotiate effectively and persuasively in high-stress situations. She knows how the legal system works and crafts her cases to overcome potential challenges, positioning her clients in the best light.

“Strategy is key to how I approach my cases. By working from a big picture perspective, I am able to make the process of dealing with the legal system less awkward and humiliating for my clients, and am able to more flexibly negotiate with prosecutors and find solutions that are in the best interests of my clients.”

Family Law Attorney With Accountability From The Beginning

When you work with Heather, she will be honest with you about your options. You will know what to expect at every stage. If there are issues such as chemical dependency or mental health problems, Heather’s trusted network of professionals can help. Seeking help up front and addressing issues from the beginning leave a client’s credibility intact. She has effectively helped clients achieve more positive outcomes as a result of an accountability-based approach.

Minimize Consequences And The Impact On Your Reputation

Most criminal convictions carry some sort of “collateral consequences” or “civil sanctions” and can be devastating to a person’s ability to move on with their lives after they have been convicted of a crime. For families going through difficult transitions like divorce, child custody or spousal maintenance, the physical and emotional effects of separating assets and connections can have lasting effects. Heather is committed to ensuring her clients move on with their lives without significant scarring from what is often a mistake or poor decision. There may be ways to negotiate your case to avoid additional negative repercussions.

Chart a Path Through Your Difficulties. Contact us for a free, confidential consultation today: 763-682–4009. Expect a response within 24 hours or less. If you cannot travel to our office, we can come to you. We also offer flexible payment plans.

Olson has been proudly recognized by the Minnesota State Bar Association for providing 50 hours or more of pro bono legal services per year as a 2015 North Star Lawyer. By donating her time, Heather’s tireless efforts have helped numerous people who wouldn’t have been able to afford legal counsel.

Awards and Honors

Honors

North Star Lawyer, Minnesota State Bar Association, 2015 - Present

attorneys.practice_type: Family Lawyers in Eagan, MN
attorneys.bio:
Julie Oney is a founding member of Oney and Kim Family Law where she is dedicated to helping individuals and families navigate the complexities of family legal matters with empathy and expertise. With a strong commitment to preserving the well-being of her clients and their loved ones, Julie has earned a reputation as a trusted advocate in the field of family law.

Julie understands the emotional challenges that often accompany family legal matters. She approaches each case with compassion and a focus on the unique needs and goals of her clients. Her personalized legal strategies are designed to ease the stress of family transitions and protect her clients' rights and interests.

While highly experienced in the courtroom, Julie recognizes that litigation is not always the best approach. Julie is skilled in alternative dispute resolution methods, including mediation and evaluations. She strives to find amicable solutions whenever possible, saving her clients time, money, and emotional turmoil.

Julie is married with two young children and two cats. In her free time, Julie enjoys camping, gardening, and cooking.

attorneys.name: Kimball Orwoll
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Rochester, MN
attorneys.bio:
Kimball G. Orwoll, now serving in an of counsel capacity at Klampe Law Firm, is a Rochester native with over 44 years of experience practicing family law in the Olmsted County and Southeast Minnesota area. He was admitted to practice in 1980 and was a solo practitioner for over 34 years focused on family law, in addition to representing clients guardianship/conservatorship matters, child protection cases and estate planning. He is a graduate of St. Olaf College and Mitchell Hamline School of Law.

He has taken particular interest in advocating for the best interest of children, and served as a Guardian Ad Litem, as well as having extensive experience serving as legal counsel for Guardians Ad Litem. He was a member of Olmsted County’s Children’s Justice Initiative Team, a joint venture of the Minnesota Supreme Court and the Minnesota Department of Human Services focused on improving the processing of cases and outcomes for children in child protection cases.

He is a strong supporter of alternative dispute resolution (ADR), which provides both parties with the opportunity to achieve positive outcomes through cooperation and respect, while avoiding the financial and emotional burdens that often result from litigation. He has served as an Early Neutral Evaluator and has represented many clients through mediation, arbitration, Social and Financial Early Neutral Evaluations (SENE/FENE), and other forms of ADR.

He is the eldest child of two very active and community minded parents. His father served as legal counsel for a well-known medical institution here in Rochester. He credits his parents’ guidance for setting the standard by which he has treated and interacted with clients. Kim and his wife, of over 46 years, also a Rochester native, place great emphasis on family and are extremely proud of their adult daughter, son-in-law, and first grandchild. His personal interests extend in many directions, including the pursuit of outdoor activities to the unique experience he has had for over 50 years presenting licensed professional fireworks displays.

sections.content:
Kimball G. Orwoll, now serving in an of counsel capacity at Klampe Law Firm, is a Rochester native with over 44 years of experience practicing family law in the Olmsted County and Southeast Minnesota area. He was admitted to practice in 1980 and was a solo practitioner for over 34 years focused on family law, in addition to representing clients guardianship/conservatorship matters, child protection cases and estate planning. He is a graduate of St. Olaf College and Mitchell Hamline School of Law.

He has taken particular interest in advocating for the best interest of children, and served as a Guardian Ad Litem, as well as having extensive experience serving as legal counsel for Guardians Ad Litem. He was a member of Olmsted County’s Children’s Justice Initiative Team, a joint venture of the Minnesota Supreme Court and the Minnesota Department of Human Services focused on improving the processing of cases and outcomes for children in child protection cases.

He is a strong supporter of alternative dispute resolution (ADR), which provides both parties with the opportunity to achieve positive outcomes through cooperation and respect, while avoiding the financial and emotional burdens that often result from litigation. He has served as an Early Neutral Evaluator and has represented many clients through mediation, arbitration, Social and Financial Early Neutral Evaluations (SENE/FENE), and other forms of ADR.

He is the eldest child of two very active and community minded parents. His father served as legal counsel for a well-known medical institution here in Rochester. He credits his parents’ guidance for setting the standard by which he has treated and interacted with clients. Kim and his wife, of over 46 years, also a Rochester native, place great emphasis on family and are extremely proud of their adult daughter, son-in-law, and first grandchild. His personal interests extend in many directions, including the pursuit of outdoor activities to the unique experience he has had for over 50 years presenting licensed professional fireworks displays.

attorneys.name: Collin Ostroot
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Buffalo, MN
attorneys.bio:
Family Law And Criminal Defense Attorney Collin Ostroot Is At Your Service

Collin Ostroot helps to clear the confusion around complex legal issues and provide clear context for his clients with every case. Always striving for your ideal outcome, Collin is a family law and criminal defense attorney who treats every situation as unique and will help you find the best solutions for all of your legal needs.

One of Collin’s biggest strengths is his ability to deeply analyze the details of your case and understand the full scope of your legal situation. He truly recognizes that the whole is not always equal to the sum of its parts, and will help you work through each component of your case on a minute level, while showing you how each element can affect the bigger picture.

Clients who work with Collin praise his sharp attention to detail, ability to develop long-term strategies that work to his client’s benefit, as well as how he is able to negotiate in the midst of tense situations. His cool-under-pressure demeanor is a great asset, as it helps his clients remain calm during stressful courtroom appearances.

The Practical Knowledge You Need

After first earning a bachelor’s degree in political science (with minors in philosophy and American studies), cum laude, from St. Paul’s Macalester College, Collin earned his law degree from William Mitchell College of Law in St. Paul, Minnesota. He began working with Olson Law as a law clerk during his time at William Mitchell.

Through intensive practical training, Collin began developing his courtroom skills while he was still in law school. Along with working as a law clerk for our firm while in school, he served as a Judicial Extern for Hon. Douglas Meslow, the Assistant Chief Judge of the Tenth District, in Anoka County. Collin was also selected to participate in William Mitchell’s Criminal Law Residency program. One of only ten students selected, he was placed with the Tenth Judicial District Public Defender’s Office and represented clients in court as a Certified Student Attorney in Anoka and Sherburne Counties. His extensive pro bono work was recognized by William Mitchell at commencement.

Our firm recognized the valuable skills that Collin brought to the table as our law clerk – especially his ability to critically analyze legal issues, his eagerness to practice in the areas of criminal defense and family law, and his commitment to the clients for whom he worked – and we brought him on as an Associate Attorney as soon as he passed the bar exam.

Rooted In The Community

A lifelong hockey player, Collin played two years of Junior A hockey in Burlington, Vermont, for the Green Mountain Glades. Although he played nationally, his hockey career began locally: as an Elk River High School graduate, he captained the Elks to two Minnesota State High School Hockey Tournaments.

Collin lives in Albertville with his wife, two daughters, and son where they enjoy cooking, reading, and spending time as a family. They also love to catch an occasional hockey game when they can.

A Family Law and Criminal Defense Attorney That Fights For You

When you’re working through a difficult legal situation, Collin is here for you. To learn more about how he can help you better navigate your family law or criminal defense case, set up a free, confidential consultation by calling 763-682-4009 today.

attorneys.name: Eric M. Palmer
attorneys.practice_type: Truck Accidents Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Eric Palmer is a seasoned trial lawyer. In a world where many personal injury lawyers shy away from the courtroom, Eric is known for his eagerness to take cases to verdict when necessary. His reputation for securing significant jury verdicts has established him as one of the premier personal injury litigators in Minnesota.

Eric focuses his practice on truck collisions and catastrophic injury. He has represented families that have lost loved ones in fatal collisions and also people that have endured life-altering injuries. No matter the circumstances, Eric strives to tell each the impactful story of each client in a sincere and compelling way.

In 2023, Eric was recognized as Attorney of the Year by Minnesota Lawyer, the largest legal publication in the state. He was also named Trial Lawyer of the Year by the Minnesota Association for Justice, Minnesota’s largest collective of plaintiff’s attorneys. These honors arrived after Eric secured multiple significant jury verdicts for his clients, including the largest personal injury verdict in Sherburne County history.

Through his compassionate engagement, Eric understands the injuries and their impact on each client’s life. He often pays home visits and walks collision scenes to fully immerse himself in the situation. He also regularly leads technology-driven collision reconstruction and vehicle inspections to assure a complete understanding of the collision specifics. This level of understanding is part of how Eric tells the personal story of each client.

Trial Lawyer of the Year, Minnesota Association for Justice, 2023

Jeff uses a variety of tools to resolve client matters and his experience as an entrepreneur gives him unique insight into the legal process and allows him to provide legal solutions that make business sense.

attorneys.bio:
Wyatt Partridge is an attorney in Foley & Mansfield's Minneapolis office. He practices in the Commercial Finance and Transactions and Commercial Litigation groups, with a focus on real estate and financing transactions and disputes. Wyatt works with banks, lending insututions, insurance companies and private businesses.

Wyatt works with clients on a variety of matters involving real estate and finance issues - including mortage priority and reformation, title disputes and secured transactions. He also advises businesses on matters involving leasing, landlord/tenant issues and buy/sell agreements, drafting and negotiating contracts - and when necessary, litigating contract disputes. Since joining the firm, Wyatt has litigated nearly 100 cases to successful resolution.

After law school, Wyatt served as a judicial clerk to the Honorable Terri J. Stoneburner at the Minnesota Court of Appeals, where he worked with appellate judges creating bench memos and draft opinions. While earning his J.D. from William Mitchell College of Law, he was an editor of the Law Review and co-director of the school's mentoring program. Wyatt's William Mitchell Law Review article, Reviving Mutuality: Restricting the Application of Defensive Collateral Estoppel - State v. Lemmer, was presented at the annual Cases You Need to Know Symposium.

In his free time, Wyatt is a volunteer tennis coach for the Minneapolis InnerCity Tennis program.

attorneys.name: Carole A. Pasternak
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Rochester, MN
attorneys.bio:
Carole is a partner at Klampe Law Firm and has been with the firm since 1999. Her practice focus is family law, a dynamic field involving all aspects of divorce, custody, child support, parenting time, step parent adoption, and domestic abuse. She is Rule 114 neutral providing family mediation services.

While attending law school, Carole was Associate Editor of the Seton Hall University School of Law Constitutional Law Journal and authored "Victims Once Again: The New Jersey Supreme Court's Unwillingness to Provide all Marital Tort Victims the Right to a Jury Trial". She was selected to be a research assistant to Professor Jack M. Sabatino, Deputy Presiding Judge for Administration, New Jersey Superior Court Appellate Division.

During law school, Carole worked with the State Division of Mental Health and Guardianship Advocacy involving the rights of children in juvenile psychiatric civil commitments. She interned for The Honorable Donald W. de Cordova as an assistant law clerk and clerked for Honorable Herbert S. Glickman; both positions focused exclusively on family law matters. Carole was active in the Center for Social Justice at Seton Hall and represented underprivileged clients in family law matters as a student attorney through a mentorship program. She also served as a mediator in the special civil part of the district court handling landlord/tenant issues and other conciliation court matters.

attorneys.name: Derek A. Patrin
attorneys.practice_type: Traffic Violations Lawyers in Andover, MN
attorneys.bio:
Derek A. Patrin has spent more than two decades focused exclusively on DWI defense, helping thousands of people navigate one of the most stressful moments of their lives. Along the way, he’s earned honors such as being named one of Minnesota’s Attorneys of the Year and being recognized repeatedly as a Super Lawyer—but what he’s most proud of is the impact his work has on real people and families.

Derek graduated cum laude from the University of Minnesota Law School in 1998 and started his career at a large downtown Minneapolis firm representing corporations and insurance companies. It didn’t take long for him to realize that defending big companies wasn’t where his heart was. He wanted to stand up for individuals—everyday people who suddenly find themselves facing a system that feels stacked against them.

He shifted his career toward DWI defense in 2001 and never looked back. His work quickly gained attention: he handled hundreds of cases early on, was named a Rising Star by Minnesota Law & Politics, and his win in the Court of Appeals in Jones v. Commissioner of Public Safety was featured on the front page of Minnesota Lawyer.

But for Derek, the real reward is helping good people get through a difficult situation with their dignity, livelihood, and future intact.

“I never planned to be a criminal defense attorney, but as soon as I started doing this work, I realized it was exactly where I was meant to be. I get to help people who feel overwhelmed and outmatched, and there’s nothing more meaningful to me than making a real difference in someone’s life. Many clients have become good friends. That’s the part they don’t tell you in law school.”

Derek is known for being honest, down-to-earth, and deeply committed to protecting his clients’ rights. He believes the DWI system has become too harsh—especially for people who made a mistake but aren’t habitual offenders—and he sees his role as leveling the playing field when the state pushes too far.

With decades of focused experience, courtroom-tested skill, and a genuine commitment to the people he represents, Derek brings both heart and expertise to every case.

attorneys.bio:
As of July, 2022, Kim has ended his nearly 43 year tenure as an attorney licensed to practice law in Minnesota, all of which was spent in private practice in St. Cloud. He will continue to be affiliated w/the law firm by providing mediation, arbitration and related ADR services (pre-suit and in litigation) throughout the state of Minnesota (online sessions and in-person sessions). His contact phone number and email address through PCG Law is unchanged.

The ADR services (facilitative and adjudicative) which Kim will continue to offer include the subject matters of serious injury and wrongful death claims, business and employment litigation, commercial and real estate-related litigation, discrimination, harassment and defamation claims, family law disputes (including marriage dissolutions, family disputes related to estates, trusts, inheritances and related family legal conflict) and various additional matters involving legal conflict within the jurisdiction of the state and federal courts of Minnesota.*

Mediations, arbitrations and other hybrid ADR services provided by Kim will continue to be scheduled through PCG Law staff and/or this website.

Kim has been listed as a qualified neutral on the Minnesota Supreme Court's civil facilitative/hybrid and civil adjudicative/evaluative roster since 1994 and on the family adjudicative, evaluative and facilitative/hybrid rosters since 1998. In retiring his license to practice law, he is not eligible to remain on those rosters. However, he will continue to serve as a facilitative and adjudicative neutral (as determined by counsel and her/his clients in each matter).

attorneys.name: Ignacio Antonio del Carmen SANZ PEREZ
attorneys.practice_type: Immigration Law Lawyers in Minnetonka, MN
attorneys.bio:
Ignacio is an immigration attorney with broad experience in employment, family, and humanitarian cases, working at Steven C. Thai, P.A. since 2018. He is a member of the American Immigration Lawyers Association (AILA), the Attorney Bar Association (ABA), and Minnesota Bar Association (MSBA), and he is admitted to practice in New York and before immigration courts and federal agencies throughout the United States for immigration law matters. His office is located in Minnetonka, Minnesota. Ignacio is fluent in Spanish and English, as he was born and raised in Santiago, Chile.

Ignacio holds a bachelor and JD degree from Pontificia Universidad Catolica de Chile (2015) and a LLM degree from University of St. Thomas Law School (2017). He interned with The Advocates for Human Rights in Minnesota and the Center for Democracy and Development in Chile. As an immigrant himself, he understands the complexities and challenges of navigating the U.S. immigration system.

Having immigrated as a student himself, Ignacio has broad experience with F-1 visa students trying to change status to H-IB visas for professional workers or O-1 visas for individuals of extraordinary ability with the goal of finally obtaining a greencard and citizenship. Ignacio has also worked on extraordinary ability petitions and national interest waivers for many renowned individuals including musicians, actresses, singers, athletes, and engineers. Ignacio also has extensive experience representing individuals in removal and custody cases before the immigration courts, including asylum, cancellation, and all types of waivers.

Before working at Steven C. Thal, Ignacio worked for a few years in several non-profit organizations working with immigrants, including law clinics, The Advocates for Human Rights, and International Amnesty.

Shane Perry is a trial attorney with extensive, broad experience representing clients before trial courts, appellate courts and other tribunals (e.g. tribal court, licensing boards, office of administrative hearings). He has represented physicians, surgeons, and other healthcare professionals before licensing boards as well as negotiated terms of healthcare professionals' severance from professional partnerships. He has represented clients in tribal court, administrative proceedings, among others. attorneys.name: Shawn M. Perry
attorneys.practice_type: Business Litigation Lawyers in Wayzata, MN
attorneys.bio:
Shawn Perry's practice focuses on commercial litigation, including complex commercial litigation and class actions. He also represents individuals and businesses in a variety of pre-litigation and non-litigation matters with the goal of helping individuals and companies avoid disputes with thoughtful and carefully drafted contracts and to resolve disputes through negotiations without having to resort to lawsuits. When it is necessary to resolve disputes in court or arbitration, Shawn has the experience, skills and resources necessary to vigorously represent businesses and individuals and is regularly pitted against litigation boutique law firms and some of the largest law firms in the nation. Shawn also counsels businesses and individuals in corporate and personal matters to plan and prevent lawsuits in the first place.

Since the early 1990s Shawn has been lead counsel, co-lead counsel, liaison/local counsel in several class action cases, including antitrust, ERISA, securities, contract and employment actions.

Shawn is AV rated by Martindale Hubbell and has been practicing since 1987. Prior to becoming an attorney, he acted as a legal assistant from 1977 through 1987.

attorneys.name: Vincent A. Petersen
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Lawyers in Excelsior, MN
attorneys.bio:
A leader in workers’ compensation litigation, attorney Vincent A. Petersen serves injured workers of Minnesota from the Noack Law Office in Excelsior. He has successfully defended thousands of people for over two decades in the legal profession with great results against insurance companies.

Mr. Petersen graduated magna cum laude with his Bachelor of Arts degree from Gustavus Adolphus College in Saint Peter, Minnesota. He then secured his Juris Doctor from the University of Minnesota Law School in Minneapolis. He was admitted to practice in Minnesota in 2000.

He began representing insurance firms as a defense attorney early in his career. His familiarity with defense tactics as well as judges and opposing counsel enables him to secure fantastic results for his clients.

Mr. Petersen is aware that an injury can cause pain, lost income, uncertainty, as well as mental and financial stress that severely alters his client’s lives. He never assumes that the insurance company is paying all benefits that the employee is entitled to, but instead meticulously scrutinizes any and all partially accepted and/or denied claims in an effort to secure the best outcome.

In his spare time Mr. Petersen is an avid outdoorsman who enjoys spending quality time with his family.

attorneys.name: Charles Peterson
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Lawyers in Buffalo, MN
attorneys.bio:
Charles (Charlie) Peterson is an Attorney with Johnson, Larson & Peterson, P.A., practicing primarily in the areas of civil litigation, real property law, and estate planning.

Charlie has been a resident of Wright County since 1994 when his family moved from Camp Lejeune in Jacksonville, North Carolina, after his father's completion of active duty in the U.S. Marine Corps. Charlie relishes his steeped family history within Wright County. His great-great-grandfathers homesteaded family farms north of Waverly, in Marysville Township, in the 1870's, which his father and uncle co-own to this day.

Charlie joined the firm in 2023. He graduated from Buffalo High School in 2010, and went on to graduate from St. John's University, Collegeville, Minnesota in 2014, where he won back-to-back National Championships in Rugby. He then graduated from MitchellHamline College of Law in 2017. Charlie resides in Waverly, Minnesota with his two daughters, and enjoys everything outdoors.

attorneys.name: John T. Peterson
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Lawyers in Buffalo, MN
attorneys.bio:
John T. Peterson has been, with the exception of the first three years of his life, a lifelong resident of Wright County. The Peterson family itself has deep roots in Wright County, with John M. Peterson and Erick Kelstrum (John's great-grandfather's on both his father's and mother's sides) having homesteaded family farms north of Waverly, in Marysville Township, in the 1870's. John co-owns the Peterson farm today with his younger brother, Wallace H. Peterson, Jr.

The Peterson family has a steeped history of public service in Wright County, with John's great-uncle, Oscar J. Peterson serving as Wright County Treasurer from 1926-1936; and John's great-uncle Earnest J. Anderson serving as Wright County Auditor from 1918 to 1940. John also has two siblings, a sister-in-law and other relatives employed by Wright County at the Wright County Government Center and serving in various capacities.

John joined the firm in 1992. He graduated from St. John's University, Collegeville, Minnesota in 1985, and William Mitchell College of Law in 1988, being admitted to the Minnesota State and Federal Bars in that same year. Upon receiving his juris doctorate, he entered active duty as a Judge Advocate in the U.S. Marine Corps, serving on active duty until June 1992. Upon completion of active service, John continued his service in the U.S. Marine Corps Reserve where he presently holds the rank of Lieutenant Colonel. During the summer of 2008, John was recalled to active duty in support of Operation Iraqi Freedom and served with 3rd Marine Air Wing in Al Asad, Iraq, where he was deployed until February of 2009.

John's areas of practice are concentrated in real estate, estate planning, elder law, business/corporate/partnership law and civil litigation, with an emphasis on real estate related causes of action. He has represented numerous clients in resolving all types of issues from rectifying title issues, to successfully negotiating purchase agreements for the sale/purchase of properties ranging from the tens of thousands to millions of dollars in value. His probate practice has involved representation of clients from the smallest estates to estates in excess of ten million dollars. John's insightful, no nonsense approach to identifying the issues and reaching a timely, well balanced resolution, have impressed both clients and the courts.

He is also a member of the Minnesota State Bar Association and is Certified as a Specialist in Real Property Law. He has received Martindale-Hubbell's highest peer review rating for the last ten plus years based upon his high level of legal ability and ethical standards. His personal affiliations include membership in the Waverly Knights of Columbus, Waverly American Legion and Parish Council, St. Mary's Catholic Church, Waverly, MN.

For hobbies, John enjoys hunting, running, hiking, downhill skiing, snowshoeing, and raising poultry on his farm in Marysville Township north of Waverly, and engaging in numerous other outdoor activities with his wife, Tammy, children and grandchildren.

attorneys.name: Susan T. Peterson
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Maple Grove, MN
attorneys.bio:
Susan T. Peterson is a shareholder in the firm of Henningson & Snoxell, Ltd., located in Maple Grove, Minnesota. She is a Chair of the firm's Estate Planning Department which boasts more than 35 years of experience counseling individuals and families. Susan practices principally in the areas of:

Estate planning

Probate, estate and trust administration

Elder law

Susan works closely with individuals and families of all sizes and asset levels to identify and prioritize their goals and implement techniques to carry them out. She builds strong relationships with clients, and in turn, clients have great confidence in her and feel comfortable sharing their most personal information and concerns.

Her practice is heavily concentrated in the following areas:

Drafting wills and trusts, as well as other estate planning documents

Incapacity planning

Family business succession planning

Contested probate administrations

Guardianships and conservatorships

Charitable gifting

Medical assistance planning

Susan also assists multi-generation families with high net worth address complex estate and tax issues. She has helped numerous families and their advisors structure estate plans that accomplish the multiple goals affecting these families. Some of the issues she routinely assists with include:

Minimizing taxes related to the transition of wealth from one generation to the next.

Assuring the effective transition of management of family wealth from one generation to the next.

Addressing the unique needs of a family, such as special needs beneficiaries, divorces, premature deaths, and educational goals.

Addressing philanthropic interests and strategizing to address these interests.

She has been selected for inclusion in Minnesota Super Lawyers® - Rising Star Edition, 2008-2010 and 2012. Susan is admitted to practice in all Minnesota state and federal courts. She is a member of the Hennepin County Bar Association and the Probate and Trust Law and Real Property Law sections of the Minnesota State Bar Association. She is also a member of the National Academy of Elder Law Attorneys and Minnesota Women Lawyers. Susan is a frequent speaker on topics associated with estate planning and estate administration, charitable giving, and elder law, and is the author of several articles.

Born in Iowa City, Iowa, Susan received her B.A. magna cum laude from St. Olaf College, her M.A. summa cum laude in English and American Literature from the University of Nevada, Las Vegas, and her law degree summa cum laude from William Mitchell College of Law. Susan clerked for Chief Justice Russell Anderson of the Minnesota Supreme Court and practiced law both as an associate and as principal of her own law firm before joining Henningson & Snoxell in 2004. She lives in Maple Grove with her family and is the immediate past president of the Rotary Club of Maple Grove.

Susan works closely with individuals and families of all sizes and asset levels to identify and prioritize their goals and implement techniques to carry them out. She builds strong relationships with clients, and in turn, clients have great confidence in her and feel comfortable sharing their most personal information and concerns.

Her practice is heavily concentrated in the following areas:

Drafting wills and trusts, as well as other estate planning documents

Incapacity planning

Family business succession planning

Contested probate administrations

Guardianships and conservatorships

Charitable gifting

Medical assistance planning

Susan also assists multi-generation families with high net worth address complex estate and tax issues. She has helped numerous families and their advisors structure estate plans that accomplish the multiple goals affecting these families. Some of the issues she routinely assists with include:

Minimizing taxes related to the transition of wealth from one generation to the next.

Assuring the effective transition of management of family wealth from one generation to the next.

Addressing the unique needs of a family, such as special needs beneficiaries, divorces, premature deaths, and educational goals.

Addressing philanthropic interests and strategizing to address these interests.

She has been selected for inclusion in Minnesota Super Lawyers® - Rising Star Edition, 2008-2010 and 2012. Susan is admitted to practice in all Minnesota state and federal courts. She is a member of the Hennepin County Bar Association and the Probate and Trust Law and Real Property Law sections of the Minnesota State Bar Association. She is also a member of the National Academy of Elder Law Attorneys and Minnesota Women Lawyers. Susan is a frequent speaker on topics associated with estate planning and estate administration, charitable giving, and elder law, and is the author of several articles.

Susan clerked for Chief Justice Russell Anderson of the Minnesota Supreme Court and practiced law both as an associate and as principal of her own law firm before joining Henningson & Snoxell in 2004. She lives in Maple Grove with her family and is the immediate past president of the Rotary Club of Maple Grove.

Bruce has lived in Rochester for most of his life. He graduated from Lourdes High School in 1978 before attending Macalester College in St. Paul, Minnesota. He graduated from Macalester with honors in 1982 and went on to attend Hamline Law School, where he earned his degree in 1988.

His twenty- five years plus of practice has given Bruce broad legal experience. Bruce is an active martial artist. He practices and is currently the chief instructor at Aikido of Rochester, Minnesota in the martial art of Aikido, a Japanese martial art similar to Judo and Jujitsu.

attorneys.name: J.P. Plachecki
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Winona, MN
attorneys.bio:
J.P. Plachecki, a native of Winona, attended Cotter High School. He was named best actor in 1978 and served as the three-year varsity football defensive captain, helping Cotter achieve a record of six straight defensive shutouts. He earned his B.A. from St. Mary's University of Minnesota, graduating cum laude. He then pursued his J.D. at Hamline University Law School, where he made the dean's list.

Continuing his education, he obtained an LLM from Boston University School of Law. Afterward, he worked as a Special Assistant Attorney General for the Massachusetts Department of Revenue. In 1994, he returned to his hometown and joined the law firm of Darby, Delano & Price. His practice primarily focuses on representing accused individuals in criminal matters across the Midwest.

J.P. Plachecki achieved a significant victory in State v. Burbach, a landmark Minnesota Supreme Court decision. You can watch him arguing the case at the Minnesota Supreme Court. He has consistently been recognized by the Minnesota Super Lawyers, earning his spot on the list every year from 2005 to 2023. Minnesota Law & Politics named him one of the Top 40 Criminal Defense Attorneys in the state in both 2007 and 2008. Minnesota Law & Politics also featured him in an article called "The Winona Boys" in their April/May 2008 issue.

Plachecki has extensive experience trying criminal cases throughout Minnesota and even worked alongside George Parnham, a frequent legal commentator on CNN and counsel to Andrea Yates, on a Minnesota case. For a decade, he partnered with Douglas Walser Thomson, Minnesota's most renowned criminal defense attorney, trying cases in the Midwest. Additionally, he served as an adjunct faculty member at Winona State University.

attorneys.name: Nancy T. Polomis
attorneys.practice_type: Collections, Creditor Remedies & Bankruptcy Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Nancy Polomis is a partner with the firm and chair of the Real Estate Development Practice. Her clients include builders, developers, banks, condominium and townhouse associations, and individuals and entities involved in real estate transactions.

Nancy's practice is focused on:

Real estate development

Community association law

Residential real estate transactions

Lender-based collections

Nancy brings an in-depth understanding of the real estate market, coupled with the unique perspective of a former mortgage banking professional, to work for her clients who benefit from her decidedly direct and proactive counsel.

Nancy's services include:

Real estate purchases

Sales

Financing

Land acquisition

Negotiation of commercial leases

Formation and maintenance of community associations

Representing numerous community associations, she brings considerable experience and insight to all stages of association development-and all association matters-including entity formation, the creation and interpretation of covenants and bylaws, and collections.

Her ongoing representation of established associations enables her to anticipate potential issues when new associations are formed, and she works accordingly with builders in the initial development process to help ensure that documents are crafted with future needs in mind.

Nancy's approach to her practice mirrors that of the entire firm-exceeding clients' expectations. She is a valued resource to her clients, providing clear, concise information and explaining complex legal theories and concepts in everyday language. She taps into her years of experience with associations to assist an association with situations that are “new" to that association, but which Nancy no doubt has addressed in the past.

Nancy works to establish a rapport with her clients from the very first encounter. She offers a prompt response to clients' needs and clear direction on a recommended course of action. Nancy modifies the firm's “standard procedures" to accommodate the client's needs, whether that entails more frequent status reports, different modes of communication or simply providing multiple copies of correspondence to the client. She is friendly with her client contacts, but firm with her adversaries, and always keeps her eye on the ultimate goal-acting in the best interests of the client. Clients even contact Nancy for guidance in areas they know she doesn't regularly practice in—knowing that she likely can direct them to the appropriate resources to get the quick answers the client needs.

Licensed to practice law in the State courts in Minnesota, Nancy is a member of the Real Property Section of the Hennepin County and Minnesota State Bar Associations, and a member the American Bar Association. She is active in the Professional Women in Building Council of the Builders Association of the Twin Cities (BATC), and is a member of the BATC Core Committee. Nancy is also active in CAI-MN, the local chapter of the Community Associations Institute, and is a member of the Board of Directors of CAI-MN. Nancy is a frequent speaker for continuing education seminars and is a regular resource for and contributor to several print and online publications.

Nancy joined Hellmuth & Johnson in 1999. She obtained her J.D. from William Mitchell College of Law, graduating cum laude. She completed her undergraduate studies at the College of Saint Benedict with a Bachelor of Arts degree in English and Business Administration.

attorneys.name: Jack L. Prescott
attorneys.practice_type: Bankruptcy Lawyers in New Brighton, MN
attorneys.bio:
Jack Prescott has passed and with him passes an era of bankruptcy practice. Jack started a bankruptcy practice in the 60's when consumer bankruptcy was in the back waters of the law. Magistrates oversaw bankruptcy proceedings, and bankruptcy clients faced a strong stigma associated with the process. Medical collections, subprime auto lenders, utility companies, legal loan sharks in the form of small retail credit financer's, and even some real loan sharks were the creditors. Representation was costly and hard to find. Jack helped that dynamic change dramatically. With his clear understanding of bankruptcy law and its process Jack created a practice were clients in financial need could find good quality representation at a reasonable cost.

Jack loved people and the greatest joy in his practice was the interaction he had with clients and the people he met in the process. He treated all of the people he dealt with respect, be they clients, attorneys, creditors, judges or trustees. When you were dealing with Jack, Jack was your friend and confidant no matter the situation. Above all he was a people person and had a personality that would unintentionally but perceptively take over the room. His humanity, kindness, quick wit, deprecating manner and empathy will be deeply missed. He always had a quick smile, a joke, a wink, and some odd old saying he would throw out to alleviate a client's tension, the trustee's unease or the creditor's enmity. As generations of Minnesotans heard from Jack "this is all we do and we do it well." We will miss you Jack.

You can read more about Jack Prescott's life and memorable slogan by clicking here to read the article on the Star Tribune.

attorneys.name: Jill M. Presseller
attorneys.practice_type: Probate and Trust Administration Lawyers in St. Michael, MN
attorneys.bio:
Jill takes pride in providing the highest quality legal services to every client. In her many years of practice, she has found that no two cases are exactly alike, and gives each file the individualized attention it deserves.

She provides legal representation to individuals dealing with probate and trust administration, including complicated tax issues and family disputes. She represents clients faced with establishing and maintaining guardianships and conservatorships for loved ones. She prepares estate plans that help clients achieve their goals and carry out their intentions, including Wills, Trusts, Financial Powers of Attorney, Health Care Directives, business succession planning, and pre and post nuptial agreements. She enjoys advising individuals, closely-held businesses, associations, and financial institutions in complicated corporate, real estate and commercial lending transactions, and drafting legal agreements tailored to meet each client's specific needs. For example, she has been involved with establishment, conversion and amendments of numerous Common Interest Communities, Planned Communities, Condominiums and Homeowners' Associations, including Master Associations. The breadth and depth of her legal practice provides a unique perspective, supporting a holistic approach to meeting all of her clients' legal needs.

Jill practices primarily in the areas of probate, trust administration, guardianships and conservatorships, estate planning, commercial lending, real estate, corporate and business.

When she is not working, Jill enjoys cross-country skiing and biking, volunteering at her children's schools and Scouting activities and spending time on the South Shore of Lake Superior with her family.

attorneys.name: Michael James Price
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Winona, MN
attorneys.bio:
Michael James Price was born in Kidderminster, England. He moved to the United States with his parents in the same year. He obtained his undergraduate and law degrees from the University of Minnesota.

After working as a claims examiner for the United States Veterans Administration, he became an Assistant Winona County Attorney. In 1974, he joined the prestigious law firm of McMahon, Darby, Price and Brooks. Throughout his illustrious career, he has passionately advocated for the people of southeastern Minnesota in criminal, personal injury and general legal matters.

He, along with attorney Douglas Thomson, handled the high-profile State vs. Howard homicide case in Minnesota. Starting in 1976, he taught civil and criminal law courses at Winona State University for more than 10 years. He has been involved in various community organizations, such as the Gamehaven Council – Boy Scouts of America, the Winona Volunteer Services, the United Way of the Greater Winona Area, Watkins United Methodist Home and the American Cancer Society – Winona County Chapter/, serving as a board member, officer and adviser.

attorneys.bio:
Joe represents clients across the spectrum of complex financial disputes, including shareholder conflicts, business contracts, civil fraud, regulatory interpretation, and more. He approaches every matter with thoroughness, creativity, and a focus on understanding the facts that shape his clients’ goals. From there, he develops legal strategies aligned with the client’s objectives and resources, ensuring that any investment in litigation is guided by a clear cost-benefit analysis. He vigorously pursues the best outcomes for his clients while providing them candid assessment of both the strengths and weaknesses of their situation.

In the past Joe has worked on matters involving business valuation, co-owner disputes, supply agreements, securities and other types of fraud, pharmaceutical pricing, civil RICO and money laundering allegations, federal and state Medicaid regulations, the False Claims Act, termination of employment, catastrophic injury, estate disputes, and trade dress litigation. He has managed all phases of litigation from initial investigation through appeal.

Outside the office, Joe’s hobbies include distance running, strategy games, reading, disc golf, and spending time with his six children.

sections.content:

He approaches every matter with thoroughness, creativity, and a focus on understanding the facts that shape his clients’ goals. From there, he develops legal strategies aligned with the client’s objectives and resources, ensuring that any investment in litigation is guided by a clear cost-benefit analysis. He vigorously pursues the best outcomes for his clients while providing them candid assessment of both the strengths and weaknesses of their situation.

In the past Joe has worked on matters involving business valuation, co-owner disputes, supply agreements, securities and other types of fraud, pharmaceutical pricing, civil RICO and money laundering allegations, federal and state Medicaid regulations, the False Claims Act, termination of employment, catastrophic injury, estate disputes, and trade dress litigation. He has managed all phases of litigation from initial investigation through appeal.

Outside the office, Joe’s hobbies include distance running, strategy games, reading, disc golf, and spending time with his six children.

attorneys.name: Michael Rajkowski
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation: Personal Injury, Wrongful Death, and Contract disputes Lawyers in St. Cloud, MN
attorneys.bio:
Mike was born in St. Cloud, MN. He is a graduate of St. John's University and William Mitchell College of Law. He has over 34 years of legal experience, including 31 of those years being in the St. Cloud area. Mike brings a broad range of legal experience, including personal injury, trust and estate, eminent domain, business and employment matters. Mike also has past experience in Family and Criminal Law. He's argued numerous cases in the Minnesota Court of Appeals and was successful in two Minnesota Supreme Court cases; Northern States Power Co v. Aleckson, et al. and Great River Energy v. Swedzinski, et al.

In the area of personal injury and wrongful death, Mr. Rajkowski is committed to obtaining the best results for injured people and grieving families. He has obtained numerous 6 figure trial verdicts and settlements for his clients. He is a strong advocate for his clients and will help them through difficult times after an accident occurs. In the area of estates and trusts, Mike will assist clients in making sure their final wishes are known and followed. He will also try to keep your estate out of the courts by planning ahead, and hopefully avoiding having your estate tied up in court for months or longer. Mike is also a strong advocate for individuals who after the death of a loved one find themselves involved in a probate litigation. He will be your advocate and will work for you to obtain the best possible result and the wishes of the deceased loved ones are met.

In the area of condemnation/eminent domain, Mike has been a strong advocate for landowners' rights. He has represented landowners in a variety of local and state eminent domain proceedings. He has had significant involvement in cases against the CapX2020 Project, which involved public utilities erecting multiple 345kv lines throughout Minnesota. This involved hundreds of landowners.

Mike is a current board member of the St. Joseph Preserve. Mike is a past board member and president of the Tri-County Humane Society and New Beginnings. Mike was also an adjunct Professor at the St. Cloud Technical and Community College. He also chaired the St. Cloud Chamber of Commerce's Business Development Council. Mike and his wife Patrice have three beautiful daughters. He also enjoys spending time reading, cooking, doing crossword puzzles, traveling, and golfing.

attorneys.name: Mark E. Rath
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Law Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Mark Rath is an attorney with the firm and member of the Litigation practice group. Mark concentrates his practice in the following areas:

Property and casualty insurance defense

Municipal defense litigation

Business and commercial disputes

Employment law and civil rights

Mark primarily handles municipal liability claims, automobile accident claims, and various civil litigation matters. His litigation experience includes a diverse practice in the areas of civil rights, claims against municipalities and their employees, and real estate matters involving zoning and land use issues.

Mark makes being prepared at every turn a top priority with every case. He has had numerous favorable outcomes for his clients over the years and keeps his clients informed through each step in the process. Mark's diverse practice experience provides unique perspectives to the cases he handles, with a problem solving approach. His practice is focused on the successful resolution of all litigation matters, with an emphasis on defending claims and disputes on behalf of his individual and business clients.

He is licensed to practice law in the state courts of Minnesota and Michigan. He is also admitted to practice in the United States District Courts for the Eastern and Western Districts of Michigan, the U.S. Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals, and the Tribal Court for the Saginaw Chippewa Indian Tribe. Mark is a member of the Hennepin and Ramsey County Bar Associations as well as the Minnesota Defense Lawyers Association.

He earned his J.D. cum laude from the Thomas M. Cooley Law School, where he served on the Law Review Board of Editors. He completed his undergraduate studies at the University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign, obtaining a B.S. in psychology and speech communications.

Benjamin L. Reitan began his legal career in San Diego, California. Mr. Reitan practiced at a civil litigation firm which specialized in business and general civil litigation. While at the firm Mr. Reitan worked on many complex cases including gasoline pricing disputes against major oil companies and multi-national personal and business disputes.

Additionally, Mr. Reitan worked with small businesses drafting corporate documents such as By-Laws, Buy-Sell Agreements, and other corporate papers. While in San Diego Mr. Reitan also clerked for a successful plaintiffs’ personal injury law firm.

In 2005 Mr. Reitan returned to Minnesota to join Reitan Law Office. Mr. Reitan handles Personal Injury actions, Workers’ Compensation claims, and Social Security appeals on a contingent fee basis. Mr. Reitan also continues to practice in the areas he specialized in while working in Southern California, including Business Litigation, Business Formation, and General Civil Litigation.

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Chaska, MN
attorneys.bio:
Jacob Reitan joined Reitan Law Office in 2014. Jacob completed his undergraduate degree at Northwestern University in 2004, where he graduated magna cum laude with a degree in political science and communication studies. After Northwestern, Jacob received a Presidential Scholarship to attend Harvard Divinity School where he received a Masters in Theological Studies. Jacob went to law school at the University of Minnesota where he graduated magna cum laude. While in law school, Jacob clerked for the Carver County Attorney and the Hennepin County Attorney.

Prior to starting his legal career, Jacob worked as an advocate for the gay, lesbian, bisexual and transgender community. As a part of this work, Jacob founded the Equality Ride and the Right to Serve Campaign. In 2006, Jacob was invited by the White House to be with President Obama when he signed the repeal of the “Don’t Ask, Don’t Tell” law. In 2012, Governor Dayton named Jacob to the Governor’s Task Force on the Prevention of School Bullying. For his advocacy Jacob has been awarded the Brian Coyle Leadership Award from the Human Rights Campaign, and he has been named one of the people of the year by Advocate Magazine and Lavender Magazine.

At Reitan Law Office, Jacob joins his brother and his father fighting for the rights of the injured and disabled.

attorneys.name: Anthony A. Remick
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Edina, MN
attorneys.bio:
Anthony has experience with insurance law and litigation. During law school, Anthony clerked at an insurance defense and subrogation firm, specializing in claims of property damage related to fires and fire suppression systems. After law school, he served as a law clerk to the Honorable Judge M. Jaqueline Regis in Hennepin County District Court. He then continued to work in the areas of insurance defense, subrogation, insurance coverage, and insurance claims investigations.

Anthony joined Smith Jadin Johnson LLP in 2020 where uses his experience and knowledge to help property owners recover the proper value of their insurance claims following a loss. Anthony also works on construction defect issues and provides opinions regarding insurance coverage.

“I have seen the insurance claims process from the perspective of the insurer and the insured. I understand the process, motives, and goals of each side of an insurance claim. Therefore, I work amicably with insurers to fight for fair payment property owners deserve after a loss. If discussion cannot get a reasonable outcome for my clients, I am willing and able to engage in the process of appraisal or litigation to enforce my clients’ rights under the policy and at law.”

attorneys.name: Anna M. Restovich
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Rochester, MN
attorneys.bio:
Anna was born and raised in Rochester, Minnesota. She attended St. John’s Grade School, Lourdes High School, and graduated from Mayo High School in 1994. She earned her Bachelor of Arts Degree from the University of Notre Dame, Indiana, 1999, majoring in both English and Theology. She graduated from the University of Minnesota Law School in 2002.

Following graduation in 2002, Anna had the honor and privilege of joining her father, George F. Restovich, in his solo legal practice in Rochester, Minnesota, which he started in 1992. Anna is now the co-owner of Restovich Braun & Associates.

Anna has been actively involved in the Rochester community, including in her parish, the Co-Cathedral of St. John the Evangelist and Rochester Catholic Schools, and has served on several boards and committees.

Anna has diverse litigation experience in the areas of family law (divorce/custody/third-party custody, spousal maintenance, child support, adoption), civil litigation (representing religious and educational institutions), estate planning/probate, personal injury, and criminal defense (serious felonies including criminal sexual conduct, drug offenses, assault/domestic abuse, DUI). Anna is a Rule 114 Qualified Neutral and conducts civil as well as family mediations. She has successfully tried a number of criminal and civil cases throughout her legal career.

attorneys.name: Michael J. Restovich
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Rochester, MN
attorneys.bio:
Michael Restovich is a native of Rochester, Minnesota. He attended St. John the Evangelist Elementary School, Willow Creek Junior High School, and ultimately graduated from Rochester Mayo High School in 1997. Although he received and accepted a full athletic scholarship from the University of Notre Dame, Michael chose to forgo college after being drafted in the second round of the 1997 Major League Baseball amateur draft by his hometown Minnesota Twins.

Michael played 15 seasons of professional baseball, making it to the Major Leagues with the Minnesota Twins, Colorado Rockies, Pittsburgh Pirates, Chicago Cubs, and Washington Nationals organizations. In 2008, he had the unique opportunity to play one season in Japan as a member of the Fukuoka SoftBank Hawks of the Nippon Professional Baseball League. In 2012, Michael retired from professional baseball to pursue his other childhood dream of becoming a lawyer like his father.

Michael earned his Bachelor of Arts Degree from Maryville University in St. Louis, Missouri, in 2014, majoring in English. He graduated from Mitchell Hamline School of Law in 2018. Throughout his time in law school, Michael had the privilege of working with his sister and brother-in-law as a law clerk at the firm his late father established. Today, he is honored and proud to join them as an attorney at the firm.

attorneys.bio:
Robert W. ("Bill") Reutiman, Jr. is a solo practitioner in Wayzata, MN, 14 miles west of Minneapolis. A Phi Beta Kappa, magna cum laude graduate of the University of Minnesota, and the University of Minnesota Law School, he practiced for four years as a captain, United States Army Judge Advocate General's Corps. Thereafter he has practiced privately. He has a "people practice" that includes real estate and estate planning. He also has a major area of concentration in collection. After decades of collecting delinquent student loans he now concentrates on the collection of commercial accounts representing such clients as Ambassador Press, Inc. and Unishippers.

Bill has chaired the Spring Park, MN Planning Commission and is an administrative hearing officer for the Cities of Hopkins and Minnetonka, MN. His biography has been consistently listed since 1990 in Marquis Who's Who in American Law and since 1996 in Marquis Who's Who in America. His office is always receptive to new clients.

Bill prides himself on one-on-one service. This includes the prompt return of phone calls, periodic file updates and, if necessary, visiting clients at their residences to provide tailored estate planning services. His office is always receptive to new clients.

attorneys.name: Jerome S. Rice
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Edina, MN
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Rice is a well-known, respected trial lawyer who has offered professional and caring service to clients since 1964. Mr. Rice carefully monitors his caseload so that he is able to dedicate the time and energy needed to provide each client with top-quality, personal representation. His clients are treated with respect and are kept advised at every step of their case, and over the years, we have developed warm friendships and often stay in touch with our clients long after their case has been resolved.

When appropriate, Mr. Rice also affiliates other experienced lawyers to conduct research, assist with depositions, and second chair at trial. When you engage our firm to represent you, you can feel confident that we have the resources and experience to provide you with superior legal representation, as well as a compassionate shoulder to lean on and a caring hand to guide you through the legal process.

Honors and Awards:

Recipient of AV Preeminent Rating from Martindale-Hubbell .

Obtained the largest civil rights verdict in Minnesota in Dick v. Watonwan County Social Services, et al.

Successfully represented the Committee to Save the Roseau County Seat in state and federal district courts and the court of appeals.

Successfully represented Marlin Torgeson in a shareholder control dispute for control of Casino Magic Corporation. (Holmes v. Torgeson).

Over the years, Mr. Rice has successfully represented many clients throughout the upper Midwest in state and federal courts, in executive terminations, shareholder disputes, professional malpractice, business breakups, securities cases, agribusiness, banking, insurance disputes, fraud, defamation, and many other diverse cases.

Mr. Rice has obtained several multi-million dollar personal injury and wrongful death settlements on behalf of his clients.

Honors

Named "Super Lawyer", Minnesota Law & Politics Magazine

Preeminent "AV" Rated (the Top Ranking for Attorneys) by Martindale-Hubbell

attorneys.name: David J. Risk
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Dave Risk has earned a reputation for excellence as a criminal defense attorney through his aggressive representation of thousands of clients over the past seventeen years. Dave has represented people charged with all types of crimes ranging from misdemeanor driving offenses to multiple counts of first-degree murder.

Dave began his career as a public defender in Ramsey County after graduating seventh in his law school class. After only two years he began teaching classes to other defense attorneys on the best practices in DWI defense as well as other criminal defense topics.

In 2005 Dave joined a large and successful private criminal defense law firm where he initially focused much of his work on DWI and Implied Consent cases. Dave became a Partner at Halberg Criminal Defense in early 2013. Since that time he has spent more of his time defending high profile Criminal Sexual Conduct cases and helping other clients whose cases have brought significant media attention against them. Dave is particularly skilled at finding novel legal issues and successfully litigating those issues through powerful cross-examination skills. As a result his peers named him a “SuperLawyer” or “Rising Star” ten different times among the many awards he has earned.

attorneys.name: Daniel Roach
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Daniel Roach is an associate attorney in Burns and Hansen's civil law department. Daniel's practice focuses on civil litigation, housing, real estate, and business disputes.

Daniel has experience representing clients through all aspects of litigation, from commencing or responding to a lawsuit through trial. He also has experience assisting businesses and individuals draft, negotiate, or understand a variety of contracts and other agreements.

He emphasizes a client-centered approach throughout every stage and strives to accomplish the client's goals whether through aggressive representation, settlement and negotiations, or straightforward legal advice. Daniel is dedicated to providing honest and concise legal advice and crafting solutions that meet the individual needs of client's and their case.

Prior to joining Burns and Hansen, Daniel served as a judicial law clerk in the 10th Judicial District. During this time, he gained experience in a variety of areas of law and honed his skills in research, legal writing, and analysis. His unique perspective on the judicial decision-making process is an asset to clients in determining the best, most cost-effective approach to litigation.

Daniel graduated from the University of Minnesota Law School in 2016 with a concentration in Environmental and Energy Law. He has a degree in Philosophy from the University of Wisconsin - Madison.

Daniel volunteers through LegalCORPS Small Business Landlord Clinic, for which he was previously awarded Special Project of the Year. He is also a Certified Information Privacy Professional/United States (CIPP/US) through The International Association of Privacy Professionals.

In his spare time, Daniel enjoys attending live music events, backpacking, fostering rescue animals, and coping with being a fan of the Minnesota Timberwolves.

attorneys.bio:
Natalie is licensed to practice in both Florida and Minnesota, where she advises clients in the areas of estates and trusts, tax, business succession planning, tax minimization, and wealth preservation. She provides highly personalized and sophisticated legal counsel, driven by a passion for excellence and integrity. Across her practice areas, she uses both cutting-edge and well-tested techniques and strategies to achieve each client’s unique objectives.

Natalie has clients in both Florida and Minnesota, and often counsels Minnesotans on successfully changing their state of residence to Florida, an area of practice casually referred to as “Snowbird Law.” She frequently travels to Tampa, Florida to meet with clients and colleagues. Natalie grew up in Palm Harbor, Florida, but has spent much of her adult life as a resident of Edina, MN.

Natalie is a board member of the Twin Cities Estate Planning Council and participates in her local Rotary Club. She is also a member of the Tampa Chamber of Commerce and Leadership Tampa Alumni group.
