content: Young, et al. v. ECTG Limited, (D. Minn. 2015). Lead counsel for plaintiff lenders in breach of promissory note litigation. Summary judgment granted in favor of clients for entire amount of requested monetary relief.

Joan M. Christenson, et al. v. SII Investments, Inc and Paul A. Schmidt, FINRA Dispute Resolution, 2015. Lead counsel for Respondents in successful defense against unsuitability and fraud claims. Following grant of partial motion to dismiss and arbitration hearing, panel awarded less than 6% of Claimants’ requested monetary relief.

Private AAA Arbitration (2014). Lead counsel for Registered Investment Advisor firm defending against claims of fraud, unsuitable financial planning advice and breach of contract. Following arbitration hearing, all claims dismissed with prejudice.
Du v. U.S. Bancorp Investments, Inc., FINRA Dispute Resolution, 2012. Lead counsel for Respondent. Following the hearing, the FINRA arbitration panel dismissed all claims with prejudice.
Gentile Nissan v. Nissan North America, Inc., Wis. Div. Hearing and Appeals, 2010. Counsel for Respondent Nissan in dealer termination; after trial, judgment for Nissan.
Zimbrick Honda v. American Honda Motor Co., Inc., Wis. Div. Hearing and Appeals, 2010. Counsel for Respondent Honda in add-point case; after trial, judgment for Honda.

United States ex rel. Barber v. Paychex, Inc., et al., (S.D. Fla. 2010). Represented defendant Ceridian Corporation in False Claims Act claim. Motion to dismiss granted; case dismissed with prejudice.
Coleman v. Franken, Minnesota District Court, 2009. Represented candidate in 2008 U.S. Senate election contest proceedings.

Krieg v. Ameriprise Financial Services, Inc., FINRA Dispute Resolution, 2007, Iowa District Court, Iowa Court of Appeals and Iowa Supreme Court 2008-2009. Lead counsel for respondent. Following the hearing, the FINRA arbitration panel dismissed all claims with prejudice. Claimant/plaintiff filed subsequent motions to vacate and reconsider, and appeals, all of which were decided in favor of respondent.

Rockwell v. SII Investments, Inc., NASD Dispute Resolution, 2006. Lead counsel for respondents, a broker-dealer and financial advisor. Following hearing, the NASD arbitration panel dismissed all claims with prejudice and ordered claimant to pay all forum fees.
R.L. Imports v. Subaru of America, Inc., D. Minn., 2005. Counsel for defendant in add-point protest. Following trial, favorable settlement allowing establishment of new dealer.
Kohler v. Commissioner of Internal Revenue, United States Tax Court, 2003. Represented Petitioner in a case regarding estate tax valuation of closely held stock. Petitioner prevailed.

attorneys.name: Taylor A. Rolf
attorneys.practice_type: Assisted Reproductive Technology Law Lawyers in Champlin, MN
attorneys.bio:
Taylor is the owner and managing partner at Steven H. Snyder & Associates with a primary focus in Assisted Reproductive Technology Law, providing support and assistance to surrogates, donors, and intended parents in their family-building journeys. Taylor graduated cum laude from William Mitchell College of Law in 2016 and was admitted to practice law in the State of Minnesota in 2017. Ms. Rolf has extensive experience in the area of Assisted Reproductive Technology having provided in-depth assistance to hundreds of intended parents relating to parentage establishment proceedings, gestational carrier contracts, and medical insurance coverage analysis associated with third-party family building. Ms. Rolf also practices in other family law areas such as gestational carrier reviews, donor agreements, stepparent/second parent adoption.

In addition to guiding intended parents and surrogates alike as they embark on this complex journey, Taylor works closely with other professionals involved in third-party reproduction both within the U.S. as well as internationally. This allows Taylor to have a unique understanding and perspective as it relates to all aspects of assisted reproductive technology including legal, medical, psychological, and financial both domestically and internationally.

In her spare time when she is not assisting parents in their family building journey she can be found chasing her three young boys, Harrison, Hayden, and Hayes, around with her husband, Cory.

attorneys.name: Steven E. Rolsch
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Rochester, MN
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Steven Rolsch brings over 40 years of legal experience to the table when meeting clients. Growing up in nearby Zumbro Falls, he decided he wanted to become a lawyer after staying up to watch Perry Mason with his parents. He looks back now and likes what he sees. "I love how he helped people, his thoughtfulness and empathy. He was also a solo guy, but he had Della Street.

While the television show often revolved around murder cases and courtroom drama, Steve provides a wide range of services to his clients quickly and cost-effectively. He could have specialized in one area of law, but instead, he grew his law practice organically, helping clients with divorce, DUI, personal injury, and wrongful death, as well as business and real estate matters.

"My job is to figure out what we can do to reduce the pain," he explains. "That's the key factor." It may involve resolving a difficult custody dispute, reducing a license revocation, or helping injury victims and their families.

His long career has led to many fond professional memories, none better than helping a father get custody of his daughters back when mothers usually got full custody during a divorce. The mother had some mental health issues and could not provide a safe and nurturing environment, yet it still took a full trial to get the girls safe with their dad. Not only has he stayed in contact with the father and daughters, but he has since represented the children who are now adults.

While Perry Mason had Della Street, Steve also has a team who helps get the work done. "I've got three really great staffers, Shana Schaefer, Erika LaPlante and Christopher Eisner. They really help me a lot with the clients and the clients like them. They are enthusiastic, and they care. When the client sees that we care, it makes it easier for them. They appreciate the fact that we treat them with empathy and respect."

A longtime resident of Rochester, Steve has enjoyed watching and being a part of the city as it grows and changes. He no longer coaches youth sports or plays on any city league teams, but he remains engaged with the community and speaks with pride about the growing city he and his wife call home.

Once clients from Rochester and the surrounding area work with Rolsch Law Offices, they come back whenever the need arises, knowing that Steve's experience and versatility give them the best chance to solve their legal problems.

attorneys.name: Christopher P. Rosengren
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Lawyers in North Mankato, MN
attorneys.bio:
Prior to becoming a lawyer, Chris served eight years in the U.S. Army as a paratrooper and Russian translator for Military Intelligence. He continued in government service as a prosecuting attorney; a position for which he made hundreds of court appearances. It is this extensive courtroom experience that Chris brings to Rosengren Law Office, LLC.

Prior to founding Rosengren Law Office, LLC, Chris spent eight years as a Workers' Compensation Attorney for Wal-Mart Stores, Inc. He worked exclusively on Wal-Mart's Minnesota workers' compensation claims for its stores throughout the state. He has personally appeared hundreds of times before Judges and Hearing Officers at the Minnesota Department of Labor and Industry (DOLI) and the Office of Hearings and Appeals (OHA).

Chris's work for Wal-Mart provided him a tremendous amount of trial experience and a unique insight into how multi-billion dollar companies defend Workers' Compensation claims. He now uses that experience and insight to help his clients recover the absolute maximum amount of benefits to which they are entitled under Minnesota's Workers' Compensation laws.

Chris was recognized in 2004 as the first recipient of the Fifth Judicial District's Pro Bono Attorney of the Year Award, honoring his work providing legal assistance to the indigent. He is an active member of the St. Peter Catholic Church.

attorneys.name: Joseph Rossman
attorneys.practice_type: Creditors’ Rights Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Joseph Rossman is an attorney who has focused his practice on Creditors' Rights, Bankruptcy and Real Estate law.

Joseph has substantial experience recovering monies owed to creditors and resolving their debt collection issues utilizing both pre-judgment and post-judgment legal collections mechanisms. He also is well versed in the Fair Debt Collections Practices Act (FDCPA) and advising clients how to ensure internal compliance within their businesses. Prior to joining Greenstein Sellers, Joseph worked at a national law firm that specialized in representing lenders, servicers, and landlords in foreclosure(s), bankruptcies, evictions, replevins, eminent domain, and real property litigation. He has represented clients in quiet title, declaratory actions, proceedings subsequent, and eminent domain actions, ensuring their lien interests remain fully protected. He has also represented lenders in processing of actions to obtain possession of automobiles, manufactured housing, heavy equipment, and other collateral. His landlord-tenant practice has included representing clients on matters ranging from drafting leases to bringing eviction actions. Representation has included advocacy in both State and Federal court.

Away from the office, Joseph enjoys playing basketball and softball, watching his favorite professional sports teams, and spending time with his wife, two children and dog.

attorneys.name: Aaron John Roy
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Aaron graduated from the University of Colorado at Colorado Springs with a degree in Political Science and Economics. Knowing what he wanted to do with the degree, he returned to his home state of Minnesota and immediately went to law school at the University of St. Thomas.

After his first year of law school, Aaron knew he wanted to practice criminal defense and spent the summer working as a certified student attorney with the Anoka County Public Defender, representing clients at bail hearings. He later was a student in the Criminal and Juvenile Defense Clinic at St. Thomas where he and other student attorneys represented clients in a variety of criminal and juvenile delinquency cases from start to finish.

After his second year of school, Aaron began working as a law clerk at Groshek Law. He continued clerking with us his entire third year of school and even after graduation as he studied to take the bar examination. He has since graduated, passed the bar, and is a licensed attorney, diligently representing clients. He has spent nearly all of his legal career at Groshek Law and has internalized the core values we practice.

We keep our overhead low and use cutting edge technology to provide legal services to our clients in a timely, efficient and cost effective manner. We take pride in listening to a client's problems, concerns and goals in order to best serve that client's interests. We are committed to promptly returning phone calls and regularly reporting to clients on cases. We use "big firm" experience to offer sophisticated yet practical advice and options to our clients, and we strive to solve legal problems quickly and sensibly.

The firm advises and represents clients primarily in the areas of business and banking law, commercial litigation and appeals, commercial law, consumer law, business and consumer bankruptcy, and financial restructuring and workouts. Our practice areas page provides a brief description of each practice area.

attorneys.practice_type: Business & Corporate Law Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Sequoia L. Rutan is an associate attorney with a practice in business formation, real estate, mergers and acquisitions, and commercial and business litigation.

Sequoia is committed to delivering exceptional client service by developing strategic solutions that provide substantial value and advance client goals. She works to gain a deep understanding of a client’s goals, business, and values to deliver the best possible outcome. Leveraging her strong organization skills and analytical mindset, Sequoia advises clients on complex legal matters, such as governance structure, litigation strategy, commercial transactions, and general contract matters. Sequoia’s ultimate goal is to ensure that clients feel a sense of satisfaction and success from working together.

After receiving her undergraduate degree in Political Science and International Studies from Macalester College, Sequoia received her J.D. from the University of Wisconsin Law School, where she served as the Senior Managing Editor of the Wisconsin International Law Journal. After law school, Sequoia served as a law clerk for the Honorable Sara R. Grewing in the Second Judicial District of Minnesota.

Sequoia and her husband live in Saint Paul, MN. A native New Yorker, Sequoia enjoys spending her free time searching for the perfect bagel. She also enjoys trying new bakeries, baking, and reading.

attorneys.name: Stephanie Sadoon
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Stephanie Sadoon earned her Bachelor’s degree in Political Science from the University of Iowa, with a minor in Arabic Studies. After graduating, she worked in Iowa City as an outreach mental health counselor, where she gained valuable expereince supporting indiviuals facing complex personal and social challenges. With a strong passion for helping others, Stephanie pursued a career in law to further advocate for others and support indivisduals navigating difficult situations.

Stephanie attended and earned her Juris Doctorate from the University of South Dakota Knudson School of Law. During law school, she served as a facaulty research assistant for USD Dean of Students where she was able to hone in on her legal research skills. Stephanie was also a member of USD’s Trial and Advoacy team, served on serveral student boards on campus, and participated in the Midwest Innocence project clinic.

After graduating from law school, Stephanie moved to Colorado to work as a law clerk, while studing for and taking the bar exam. Although she enjoyed her time in Colorado, she ultimatly decided to return to the midwest to be closer to family and pursue licensure as an attorney in Minnesota. Stephanie worked as an accoaite attorney in downtown Minneapolis, assisting clients with complex litigiation matters. Once she was ready to focus on her area of specialty, she joined Groshek Law as a criminal defense attorney.

attorneys.name: Aaron D. Sampsel
attorneys.practice_type: Legal Ethics and Professional Responsibility Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Aaron D. Sampsel is the Managing Attorney and a Shareholder with the firm of Christensen Sampsel PLLC. He routinely represents lawyers, law firms, and judges related professional responsibility and legal ethics issues in Minnesota. Aaron also manages the firm's associate attorneys on business litigation, corporate transactions, consumer law, real estate, and intellectual property matters.

After earning an undergraduate degree, Aaron earned his Juris Doctor from Mitchell Hamline School of Law in 2016. While in law school, he earned a CALI Award and was on the dean’s list. He was also a staff member and editor of the Mitchell Hamline Law Review. Since graduating from law school, he has given numerous CLEs on legal ethics and professional responsibility. He has also taught as an Adjunct Professor of Law at his alma mater.

Aaron is admitted to practice law in the State of Minnesota, the United States District Court for the District of Minnesota, the United States Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit, and the United States Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit. He has also appeared in trademark matters before the United States Patent and Trademark Office Trademark Trial and Appeal Board. Before his career as an attorney, he worked in the consumer deposit compliance and retail banking industry.

Aaron is an active participant in the local legal community as a member of the Minnesota State Bar Association and he sits on the MSBA's Professional Regulation Committee. He is also a member of the Association of Professional Responsibility Lawyers and the American Bar Association's Center for Professional Responsibility.

Bill Sand attended college at Hamline University where he served as captain of the men’s baseball team. He then attended law school at the University of San Diego where he was awarded the Honorable Louis M. Welsh Endowed Scholarship. This award is given to the person that best “exemplifies the highest ethical standards and believes in the humanity of the law” and who demonstrates a “passionate desire to fulfill a lifelong dream of becoming a trial lawyer.” While in law school Bill spent time with the public defenders office, worked for a civil litigation firm, and also wrote published articles based on various state agencies.

After law school Bill entered the field of Child Advocacy Law and has since helped obtain millions of dollars in services for children. He has continued this trend by focusing his practice primarily in the area of Personal Injury Law as well as handling cases involving School Abuse, Injury, and Discrimination. Bill has experienced uncommon success with an abnormally high success rate at all stages of litigation - from jury verdicts to judicial rulings in favor of his clients.

Outside of the law Bill enjoys playing music, hiking, and spending time with family. He is involved with the Special Olympics, has volunteered at care centers for the elderly, and founded a number of youth baseball camps.

attorneys.name: Jill M. Sauber
attorneys.practice_type: Elder Law Lawyers in Eden Prairie, MN
attorneys.bio:
I love what I do! My entire professional career has focused on death, dying, and pre-planning. I started out my professional career as a licensed mortician. It is not all as macabre as you may think! I find peace in helping my clients and their family prepare for the "inevitable"​ (death and taxes), and make life's transitions easier.

I help clients navigate estate planning, as they focus on asset growth, to long-term care planning, where the focus shifts to asset preservation and care. After a death occurs, I help resolve contested Will or Trust issues (litigation), counsel on Medical Assistance claims, and guide families through the probate process.

I obtained my law degree from the University of St. Thomas School of Law and earned Bachelor of Science degrees from the University of Minnesota in Biology, Physiology, and Mortuary Science. My background and experience as a licensed mortician provides me with a unique perspective in both estate planning and elder law.

I enjoy a broad-based Estate and Elder Law practice, with emphasis on long-term care planning, asset protection, government benefits, estate planning, estate administration (probate), trusts, litigation, and mortuary law.

I am Certified as an Elder Law Attorney (CELA®) by the National Elder Law Foundation (NELF).

I enjoy the diversity of my practice which involves both planning and litigation-related issues. As a result, I have experience working with a broad spectrum of clientele, both business and personal. Litigating matters to conclusion brings perspective in planning for my clients’ long-term care needs, and provides insight to ensuring that my clients’ wishes are carried out in their final estate planning documents. My litigation experience includes successfully litigating long-term care insurance disputes, probate and trust disputes, and financial exploitation cases.

I am a member of the National Academy of Elder Law Attorneys (NAELA), past president of the NAELA Minnesota Chapter, a current member of the NAELA Foundation Board of Trustees, and active member of the American Bar Association (ABA) Senior Lawyers Division (SLD).

I am a Commissioner on the American Bar Association Commission on Law and Aging (COLA).

I am also a volunteer for the Minnesota State Bar Association (MSBA) Wills for Heroes Program, a volunteer with Minnesota Assistance Council for Veterans (MAC-V), a Dementia Champion through the ACT on Alzheimer’s Initiative, and am an active member of the Elder Law Section of the Minnesota State Bar Association.

I enjoy a broad-based Estate and Elder Law practice, with emphasis on long-term care planning, asset protection, government benefits, estate planning, estate administration (probate), trusts, litigation, and mortuary law.

I am Certified as an Elder Law Attorney (CELA®) by the National Elder Law Foundation (NELF).

I enjoy the diversity of my practice which involves both planning and litigation-related issues. As a result, I have experience working with a broad spectrum of clientele, both business and personal. Litigating matters to conclusion brings perspective in planning for my clients’ long-term care needs, and provides insight to ensuring that my clients’ wishes are carried out in their final estate planning documents. My litigation experience includes successfully litigating long-term care insurance disputes, probate and trust disputes, and financial exploitation cases.

I am a member of the National Academy of Elder Law Attorneys (NAELA), past president of the NAELA Minnesota Chapter, a current member of the NAELA Foundation Board of Trustees, and active member of the American Bar Association (ABA) Senior Lawyers Division (SLD).

I am a Commissioner on the American Bar Association Commission on Law and Aging (COLA).

I am also a volunteer for the Minnesota State Bar Association (MSBA) Wills for Heroes Program, a volunteer with Minnesota Assistance Council for Veterans (MAC-V), a Dementia Champion through the ACT on Alzheimer’s Initiative, and am an active member of the Elder Law Section of the Minnesota State Bar Association.

attorneys.bio:
A knowledgeable advocate with over 30 years of experience, Brenda M. Sauro is founding partner at Sauro & Alton, PLLC. She represents those in Minnesota and Wisconsin in legal cases related to construction law, first party property insurance claim disputes, real estate fraud and non disclosure, mediation, litigation, arbitrations, appraisals and appeals. A talented advocate for the rights of businesses, associations, single family owners, and commercial property owners , she has successfully litigated thousands of claims involving defective construction or underpayment of property insurance disputes with financial recoveries for the firm's clients in excess of $64,000,000. Ms. Sauro also serves as an arbitrator.

Ms. Sauro graduated cum laude with a Juris Doctor from William Mitchell College of Law in 1991 after earning a Bachelor of Arts and graduating with honors from the University of Wyoming in 1988. Currently, she is an active member of the Minnesota State Bar Association including the organization’s Solo/Small Firm Section where she serves on the council.

Originally admitted to practice in Colorado and before the U.S. District Court for the District of Colorado, Ms. Sauro is now admitted to practice in Minnesota, Wisconsin, Arizona (inactive) and before the U.S. District Court for the District of Minnesota and the District of Wisconsin. She regularly writes and lectures for organizations such as the American Bar Association, the Minnesota Bar Association, the Ramsey County Bar Association, and the National Association of Public Insurance Adjusters.

Recent notable cases showcasing the strategic success of her representation include an industrial fire loss resulting in a $26,000,000 appraisal award, a tornado loss resulting in a $654,000 increase in payment to her client, a defense verdict for a wrongly accused seller of a property, a partner theft case resulting in a half million dollar theft award and a jury verdict for a resort for wind damage in excess of $600,000. In arbitration, Ms. Sauro has obtained six figure and recission awards for her clients. Whether in arbitration or trial, she is prepared to take a case to appraisal, arbitration or trial when necessary to fairly compensate or defend her clients.

attorneys.name: Matthew J. Schaap
attorneys.firm_name: Dougherty, Molenda, Solfest, Hills & Bauer P.A.
attorneys.practice_type: Appeals Lawyers in Apple Valley, MN
attorneys.bio:
Matthew Schaap is a shareholder with the firm. He regularly assists clients with a variety of personal and business litigation matters.

Matthew began his legal career as a Judicial Law Clerk to Elizabeth Hayden, a Minnesota District Court Judge. As a Law Clerk, he played an active supporting role in the process of judicial decision-making. He provided judges with the legal research, writing and analysis that they used to decide the legal questions and issues before them. As a Law Clerk, Matthew also assisted in numerous jury trials in both the criminal and civil context. This practical experience gave him first-hand exposure to winning trial techniques as he observed highly-effective trial lawyers both in the courtroom and also in chambers.

Matthew joined Dougherty Molenda in 2004 after completing his judicial clerkship. At Dougherty Molenda, Matthew focuses on litigation and trial practice. Matthew's primary goal in any litigation is to serve as a zealous advocate for his clients by thoroughly researching all issues (both legal and technical) that are important to presenting the case in court. However, Matthew also focuses on helping clients to understand the legal process so that they can actively participate in the case and make informed decisions about its resolution. To accomplish this goal, Matthew has developed a variety of practical guides to assist clients in understanding critical aspects of the legal process, such as discovery. Like all litigation attorneys at Dougherty Molenda, Matthew provides his clients with early case analysis designed to 1) evaluate the risks of litigation and 2) develop successful trial strategies that maximize the likelihood of favorable trial or settlement outcomes.

At times, litigation involves an appeal to a higher court. During law school, Matthew's appellate brief was selected by the Legal Writing Department faculty as the "Best Appellate Brief in the First Year Law School Class." As an attorney, Matthew has continued his commitment to excellence in legal writing: He has authored or co-written numerous appellate briefs that led to affirmance of favorable outcomes for clients. Matthew has also presented oral arguments in appeals before the Minnesota Court of Appeals and the Federal Circuit Court of Appeals (Washington, D.C.), receiving favorable decisions of affirmance from both courts.

In addition to his civil jury trial and appellate experience, Matthew has successfully represented the firm's clients at numerous mediations, arbitrations, court trials and motion hearings. He has been recognized in Minnesota Law and Politics as a top young attorney and was named to the Minnesota Rising Stars® List from 2007 to 2016.

Jeffrey Schiek, concentrates his practice in employment law, representing professionals facing employment-related misconduct allegations. Mr. Schiek represents victims of workplace abuse and harassment. Mr. Schiek has helped develop brochures and articles for workshops nationwide on the topics of criminal law and procedure diversity in education, the community and the workplace, and on the topics of the prevention of workplace violence and harassment.

attorneys.name: Patti Adams Schinzing
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Saint Paul, MN
attorneys.bio:
Patti Adams Schinzing, formerly known as Patti A. Adams, is the founding shareholder of the firm. The law is a second career for Patti where she has extensive experience in Human Resources, Employee Benefits and Long Term Disability Insurance. Patti currently practices in the areas of family law, estate planning, probate, and small business matters.

Patti’s goal is to assist client in achieving their desired results in a less adversarial manner, ever mindful that in many cases a relationship continues beyond the point when litigation has been completed. So if it is a family law dispute or a problem within your small business Patti strives to provide professional services with a dignified respectful approach, and as a result has enjoyed a high level of client satisfaction and referrals.

Patti was born and resided as a child in Moorhead Minnesota. Graduated from Fargo Shanley High School in 1983. Patti did her undergraduate study at the University of North Dakota receiving a Bachelor of Science and Social Work in December of 1996. At that time Patti relocated to the Twin Cities area and was employed at New York Life Insurance and Ecolab Inc. During that same time Patti attended William Mitchell College of Law. Upon graduation, she passed the bar exam and was admitted into practice in the Bar in the fall of 1995. Upon admittance to the Bar, Patti went into private practice, where she remains today at Adams Schinzing P.A.

Patti is married to Mike Schinzing, also an Attorney and a retired United States Naval Office, as a result of her marriage, she has become very familiar with issues surrounding military marriage, divorce and military pension. Patti and Mike have one son. Patti, along with her family is very active in the St. Paul community where she serves on the board of directors for their local youth hockey program, Johnson Como Hockey Association.

attorneys.name: Daniel S. Schleck
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Dan Schleck practices in the areas of Transactional Law, Debtor/Creditor Law, Municipal Law, Banking and Finance, Environmental Law, and Real Estate Law-including municipal and land use law and eminent domain proceedings. Voted one the Best Lawyers in America (2001) in the Best Lawyers Consumer Guide, Dan has vast experience in structuring complex transactions and financing packages for contaminated and uncontaminated property development. He has been extremely successful in securing public grant funds for clients that choose to redevelop contaminated property. His expertise on these projects, along with his experience as the former city attorney for Mendota Heights, Minnesota, allows Dan to add value when negotiating Development Agreements with municipalities. Dan's technical experience, along with a hands-on background of cleaning up contaminated sites, allows him to provide a unique perspective on client’s issues in this area.

Dan hasn't always been a lawyer

Prior to entering the practice of law, Mr. Schleck was an engineer with Waste Management, Inc. of Oakbrook, Illinois. While at Waste Management, his work focused on hazardous waste site remediation, reuse of previously polluted properties and general strategic corporate environmental compliance. Mr. Schleck was admitted to the bar in 1995 after graduating from Chicago Kent College of Law with honors in that same year. Since that time, Mr. Schleck has practiced in the area of real estate development and secured transactions, with a focus on environmental due diligence and redevelopment of Brownfield properties. Mr. Schleck is a licensed professional engineer in Wisconsin; he is also a certified hazardous materials manager, a certified environmental specialist and is a speaker at many continuing education classes and seminars.

attorneys.name: Lauri Ann Schmid
attorneys.practice_type: Bankruptcy (Chapter 7 and 13) Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Lauri Schmid is a graduate of Concordia College (Bachelor of Arts in General Business) and Hamline University School of Law, both of St. Paul.

Lauri has been involved in the legal industry since 1986, when she began her career as an office manager/receptionist with a law firm in Edina, Minnesota. In 1987, she took on the role of legal assistant. She continued to work with one of the attorneys, Michael Mollerus, through 1997.

In 1997, she earned her law degree from Hamline University School of Law in St. Paul, Minnesota. She began work as an attorney with the firm of Mollerus & Haug, Ltd. At that time, her name was Lauri Haug, and she became a firm partner in November of 1997 and continued as a full partner until June of 2003. In July of 2003, Lauri capitalized on her experience and expertise and started her own firm, L.A. Haug & Associates, Ltd. In July 2008, she changed her last name to Schmid and began the law firm of Schmid & O’Brien, Ltd.

In 2010, Lauri formed the new Schmid Law Firm, Ltd in order to offer a singular level of service and commitment to her clients.

Lauri keeps her legal knowledge current by attending seminars that cover the latest changes and trends in the laws. She is actively involved in the Minnesota State Bar Association’s Bankruptcy Section (2016-17 Secretary of the Section; 2017-2018 Vice Chair of the Section; and 2018-2019 Chair of the Section) and she also is the past chair of the Consumer Debtor Attorney Subcommittee.

Lauri currently resides in Savage, Minnesota, with her husband, Mike. Her hobbies and areas of interest include travel, reading, sports and riding motorcycles.

attorneys.name: Cathryn Schmidt
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Saint Paul, MN
attorneys.bio:
Practice Experience

Cathryn Schmidt is an experienced and highly regarded family law attorney who draws on more than 25 years of legal experience when representing her clients in family law matters. She represents her clients in all matters with respect to family law including custody, parenting time, asset valuation and division, spousal maintenance, and orders for protection. Cathryn has been named "Super Lawyer" by Minnesota Law and Politics and has been recognized for her excellence in family law by selection to the American Academy of Matrimonial Lawyers, Minnesota Chapter. She has also attained the highest rating possible from Martindale Hubbell for both her legal ability and ethical standards as rated by her colleagues and judges. While she is well-versed in settlement negotiation and mediation (she is a qualified mediator), Cathryn is also an experienced trial attorney and has successfully litigated scores of contested family law matters, both at the trial court level and at the Court of Appeals. She recently argued a case to the Minnesota Supreme Court.

Before joining Collins, Buckley, Sauntry & Haugh, Cathryn was a partner at Swaden Law Offices, in Edina where she spent 14 years devoting her practice exclusively to family law. Her prior experience includes clerking for the Honorable Gordon W. Shumaker and the Honorable John S. Connolly in Ramsey County District Court. Ms. Schmidt assisted Judge Shumaker (now retired from the Minnesota Court of Appeals) in the determination of complex litigation matters, including Minnesota's landmark silicone breast implant insurance coverage declaratory judgment action. Following her clerkships, she developed a reputation as an excellent trial court advocate as a Ramsey County Public Defender while also maintaining a private practice devoted primarily to family law.

Cathryn is a long-standing member of the Warren E. Burger Inn of Court, a membership of attorneys and judges that promotes excellence in advocacy and civility in Minnesota's court system. She volunteers as a mentor at the University of St. Thomas School of Law.

Honors

“Rising Star” by Minnesota Law and Politics

attorneys.name: Ryan M. Schmisek
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Minnetonka, MN
attorneys.bio:
Ryan Schmisek is a partner at Krueger, Juelich & Schmisek, PLLC in Minnetonka, Minnesota.

Ryan focuses his practice on all areas of divorce and family law. He is experienced in the division of marital property and debts, child custody, parenting time, child support, the negotiation and preparation of divorce settlement agreements, estate planning, premarital agreements, and adoption.

Ryan has represented numerous military members, federal employees, including foreign service officers, and their spouses, and therefore has a unique knowledge of issues affecting these individuals, including division of retired pay, survivor benefits, and other issues specifically affecting these individuals. He has considerable experience with child custody matters interstate and international issues. While he understands that a negotiated settlement in family law cases is preferable, he also has extensive experience in bringing matters to trial.

Ryan spent more than a decade practicing law at a prestigious family law firm in the Virginia suburbs of Washington, DC. Since returning to Minnesota, Ryan has worked for a small family law firm in the western Twin Cities suburbs and a large firm in Minneapolis. He has written appellate briefs for the Minnesota Court of Appeals, the Virginia Court of Appeals, the Virginia Supreme Court, the United States Court of Appeals for the 4th Circuit, and the United States Supreme Court.

Ryan was recognized by SuperLawyers® Rising Stars list for many years and has been was included on the SuperLawyers® list for 2016 - 2021. He has also been designated by Martindale Hubbell Peer Review Ratings as "AV Preeminent®," the highest possible designation reflecting legal skills and ethics.

Ryan is member of the Minnesota State Bar, Virginia State Bar, Minnesota State Bar Association, Hennepin County Bar Association Family Law Section, Dakota County Bar Association Family Law Section, and Virginia Attorneys Abroad.

attorneys.bio:
Brian has thirty (30) years combined professional experience practicing before the United States Patent and Trademark Office and advising businesses and individuals on the importance of protecting their intellectual property rights. He utilizes his extensive background in law and technology along with sound business advice to provide counseling on a wide variety of legal and business related issues concerning the protection of intellectual property and other technological endeavors.

Brian's practice involves all aspects of US and international intellectual property law, including the preparation and prosecution of patent, trademark and copyright applications, reexaminations, oppositions, and matters involving validity, due diligence and infringement investigations, including litigation. He also represents large and small businesses in all forms of technology licensing transactions, and negotiates and drafts licensing agreements, as well as general business, distribution and technology transfer agreements pertaining to the protection of intellectual property rights.

Brian draws upon his extensive experience in computer law and electrical engineering to represent technology-driven companies focusing on applications of computer technology, software, and e-commerce related advances. Other representative areas of Brian's expertise include, without limitation, irrigation fittings and assemblies, fluid flow monitoring systems, hydraulics, elastomeric seals and sealing applications, robotics, plastic and rubber assemblies and components, soil, drainage and erosion control technology, and dairy processing and food handling machinery.

Brian received his Bachelor of Science degree in Electrical Engineering in 1981 from the University of Minnesota . Thereafter, he was employed by Honeywell, Inc., Defense Division, as an electrical engineer, where he was awarded for his special achievements in connection with his robotics work in the area of conformal coating applications. Brian enrolled at Hamline University School of Law in 1984, and earned his Juris Doctor (J.D.) degree in 1987.

In advance of graduating from law school, Brian was admitted to practice before the United States Patent and Trademark Office, and began working for the law firm of Schroeder & Siegfried, P.A. as a patent agent in 1986. Upon receiving his law degree, Brian joined the firm as an associate attorney in 1987, and is now the managing partner of Schroeder & Siegfried, P.A.

attorneys.name: Anthony M. Schrier
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Edina, MN
attorneys.bio:
Anthony is an associate attorney at Hill Crabb, LLC who focuses exclusively on family law matters. Prior to obtaining his law degree from Mitchell Hamline School of Law in 2020, Anthony worked as a paralegal in a variety of practices of law, including personal injury and toxic tort/mass litigation. As an attorney, he has experience representing clients in all areas of family law, including divorce, child custody, parenting time, child support, spousal maintenance, orders for protection, harassment restraining orders, and third-party custody matters.

Anthony graduated in 2020 from Mitchell Hamline School of Law St. Paul, MN. While attending Mitchell Hamline, Anthony served as a certified student attorney and served as his cohort's representative on the Student Bar Association. Additionally, he was an active member in the Diversity and Inclusion Committee and Social Committee. Prior to law school, Anthony received his Bachelor of Arts degree in Legal Studies at Hamline University in St. Paul, MN and obtained an ABA approved paralegal certificate.

Anthony also serves as a board member for the Family Law League, a local non-profit organization focused on professional development and promoting collegiality among family law professionals. Additionally, Anthony serves on the Public Relations Committee of the Association of Family and Conciliation Courts – Minnesota Chapter, an interdisciplinary and diverse association of professionals dedicated to improving the lives of all children and families through the resolution of family conflict. In his free time, Anthony enjoys playing guitar and spending time with his wife and children.

attorneys.name: Jacqueline M. Schuh
attorneys.practice_type: Business Law and Litigation Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Jacqueline M. Schuh practices at Engelmeier & Umanah, P.A. law firm's office located in St. Cloud, Minnesota. She has practiced in outstate Minnesota for over twenty years. Ms. Schuh's practice focuses on creating and advising small and large businesses, healthcare law and litigation, estates, trusts, probates, employment law and related litigation, including appeals. She advises and assists individuals, families, businesses and farms with developing and implementing estate, business, and succession plans with the goal of preserving assets and minimizing or avoiding estate taxes and probates. Ms. Schuh also advises individual and corporate Personal Representatives, Trustees, and Health Care Agents.

Jackie also served as a Judge Advocate General ("JAG" military lawyer) for more than twenty years in both the Army and Air National Guard, and retired at the rank of LtCol.

Jackie too, taught for over eighteen years as Adjunct Faculty in Communication Studies, Political Science, and Criminal Justice at her alma mater, St. Cloud State University. She completed her Juris Doctor at Mitchell Hamline School of Law.

Finally, Ms. Schuh has served on local boards and committees, including Goodwill Easter Seals, Stearns-Benton Bar Association, and the Central Minnesota Estate Planning Council.

attorneys.bio:
Leo F. Schumacher is always looking for his next great adventure, whether it's hiking the Pacific Northwest, climbing the mountains of Ecuador, or discovering the next great Americana/folk band. Maybe that's why he enjoys his commercial real estate practice so much. For those who would argue that commercial real estate can't be all that exciting, Leo firmly disagrees. Coming to work means jumping into a new challenge every day, from assisting clients with the acquisition and development of real estate to negotiation of leases. If his work didn't give him the adrenaline rush he craves, he'd hit the trail with Rainy, his beloved basset hound.

In addition to being a certified Real Property Law Specialist by the Minnesota State Bar Association, Leo has been rated by Martindale-Hubbell® as AV Preeminent. Leo also has extensive experience in advising closely held business in a broad range of issues, including business structuring, mergers, and acquisitions.

attorneys.practice_type: Agriculture Law & Agribusiness Lawyers in New Ulm, MN
attorneys.bio:
Dan has a focused expertise as a business attorney. He began his career with a large Minneapolis-based law firm, representing financial institutions, cooperatives and other businesses in the areas of mergers and acquisitions, private placements, bankruptcy and creditors' remedies, secured transactions, business formation, corporate governance and commercial litigation.

Dan later left the city for the opportunity and privilege to work as corporate counsel for his family's local agribusiness. He represented the company in connection with real estate and asset acquisitions, contract negotiation and drafting, local and state permitting, regulatory audits and internal compliance.

Drawing on his broad and diverse experience, Dan understands and appreciates the risks and choices businesses face during the course of a transaction or lawsuit. He is just as comfortable in the board room as he is in the court room protecting and advancing his clients' interests.

Dan received a Bachelor of Arts degree, magna cum laude, from the University of St. Thomas in 2005 and a Juris Doctor degree, magna cum laude, from the University of Minnesota Law School in 2008. Dan was named a Minnesota Super Lawyers Rising Star in 2015 and 2016.

attorneys.practice_type: Business Litigation Lawyers in Oakdale, MN
attorneys.bio:
Brandon is a Board-Certified Civil Trial Law Specialist by the Minnesota State Bar Association, a Board-Certified Civil Trial Advocate and Family Trial Law Advocate by the National Board of Trial Advocacy and has received recognition from peers and clients alike for his thorough, zealous, and ethical representation. Whether it be resolution at jury trial, court trial, arbitration, mediation, or pre-suit negotiation, Brandon has the experience and legal knowledge to effectively advocate for his clients.

Brandon earned an undergraduate degree cum laude in finance and economics from Michigan Technological University in 2006 while on a full hockey scholarship and earned his Juris Doctor, cum laude and in the top ten students in his class, from the William Mitchell College of Law in 2011. Admitted to practice in Minnesota, Iowa, Wisconsin, Arizona and Massachusetts.

Prior to entering law school in 2008, Brandon played professional hockey in the American Hockey League and East Coast Hockey League while employed as a clerk for the Schwartz Law Firm, a job that he kept until his graduation.

attorneys.name: Rozlyn B. Scott
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Buffalo, MN
attorneys.bio:
Rozlyn Scott is an Attorney and Partner at Johnson, Larson & Peterson P.A., practicing primarily in the areas of family law, guardianships and conservatorships, probate, estate planning, and landlord-tenant law. She is passionate and committed to helping families work through difficult times, and truly appreciates the value of having an attentive and zealous advocate on her client’s side. She has experience handling an array of family law issues, including divorce, paternity, child custody, parenting time, child support, spousal maintenance, and post-divorce issues. Rozlyn also practices in the areas of estate planning, guardianships, probate law, and landlord-tenant law.

Rozlyn values being at a firm that has such close-knit ties to the town of Buffalo and its surrounding communities. She provides pro bono legal assistance through the Central Minnesota Legal Services Wright County Legal Advice clinic in the area of family law and is a member of the Minnesota Bar Association.

Prior to joining Johnson, Larson & Peterson, Rozlyn served as a Staff Attorney for the Minnesota Judicial Branch at the Statewide Self-Help Center where she assisted self-represented litigants with an array of legal issues, including family law, orders for protection, criminal law, child protection, civil law, and landlord/tenant issues. Prior to her work in Self-Help, Rozlyn spent almost 3 years clerking for the Honorable Joy D. Bartscher in Ramsey County District Court where she gained meaningful experience in the areas of family, juvenile, and criminal law.

Rozlyn received her Juris Doctorate Degree from William Mitchell College of Law in 2015, and her Bachelor's Degree from the University of Minnesota, Duluth. In her free time, Rozlyn enjoys traveling, camping, cooking, and spending summers on the lake with family and friends.

attorneys.practice_type: Banking Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Jacob is a seasoned litigator who represents plaintiffs and defendants of all sizes, from sole proprietors to Fortune 500 companies, in complex commercial litigation matters before state and federal courts, and in high-risk, bet-the-company situations.

Jacob has significant experience resolving issues affecting manufacturers, service providers, and financial institutions, including unfair competition and antitrust, products liability, warranty claims, supply-chain relationships and management, and dealer/distributor/sales representative relationships.

Prior to becoming a founding partner at Greenstein Sellers, Jacob spent twelve years in large corporate law firms where he developed and perfected his legal skills. Since joining, he has focused on turning out "big firm work product," but without all the "bells and whistles" and price tag.

For many of his clients Jacob serves as outside general counsel. In that capacity, Jacob serves, not just as lawyer, but as strategic advisor, as well. Jacob's clients rely on him for the kind of unfiltered advice they might not otherwise get, even from their own management. He regularly counsels CEOs and boards of directors on a wide variety of business matters, helping them to see their businesses "from 50,000 feet up."

attorneys.name: Mary L. Senkbeil
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Counseling Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Over the last couple of decades, Mary has primarily provided advice to employers on a wide variety of employment issues. After working for small and rather large firms representing employers in all facets of counseling and litigation, she moved in house. Mary joined (and eventually led) the employment law and risk management departments for Regis Corp., a Fortune 1000 company with locations in all 50 states, all Canadian provinces and Puerto Rico. She understands the necessity of being a trusted legal advisor to achieve business objectives while avoiding litigation.

Now, Mary works on both sides of the aisle. On the one hand, she counsels employers on a wide variety of employment issues including avoiding discrimination and harassment and creating a respectful workplace. She also advises on leave issues, including sick and safe time laws, disability and other leave laws, wage and hour compliance (FLSA and state), wage payment laws, reductions in force, disability law and accommodation, background checks, the National Employment Relations Act as it applies to non-unionized work places, whistleblowing, drug and alcohol testing, and drafting, enforcing and defending non-compete, non-disclosure, arbitration and compensation agreements. She also helps businesses stay current and compliant with the ever-changing world of employment law and reviews and revises policies and handbooks.

On employee side, Mary assists employees and executives in addressing workplace concerns through thoughtful and effective communication or an adversarial approach. She assists with requests for accommodation and leave, disability benefits, employment contracts, including non-competition, non-solicitation and confidentiality agreements, severance negotiations and executive contracts, as well as matters involving nonpayment or underpayment of wages.

In her free time, Mary enjoys hiking, travelling, photography, cooking for and with others, gardening and, especially, baseball.

George Serdar is a graduate of the University of Minnesota and a graduate of the William Mitchell College of Law, with honors. George has been involved in business litigation on a full-time basis since 1981. He has concentrated on representing business owners and companies in a wide variety of disputes including mergers and acquisitions, non-competition disputes, breakups of professional organization and small company shareholder disputes.

George emphasizes developing a strategy with his clients at the beginning of a dispute so that the entire process moves toward a reasonable business solution with effective cost management.

As a certified mediator, George also provides services to attorneys and law firms around the State for dispute resolution when the parties are voluntarily engaged in mediation or have been ordered to mediation by a Court. His mediation practice focuses on business disputes, non-competition and non-solicitation disputes between individuals and companies, and real estate development disputes.

attorneys.name: Debra Lynn Shapiro
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning, Wills, and Trusts Lawyers in Oakdale, MN
attorneys.bio:
Debbie Shapiro is an estate planning attorney whose career blends years of legal practice with decades of higher education teaching and training. Her path reflects a deep commitment to service, adaptability, and client-centered advocacy. After beginning her career in law, she stepped away to care for her children, later reimagining her professional life in higher education, where she served as a law professor, director of student support, educational consultant, and national trainer.

Returning to full-time legal practice with renewed purpose, Debbie now blends her legal expertise with an educator's skill set which includes active listening, clear communication, and compassionate guidance. She brings unique insight into estate planning, shaped in part by her own family's experience with a contentious estate dispute. That personal history underscores the necessity of precision and ethical diligence when preparing end-of-life documents, and it continues to fuel her passion for teaching Professional Responsibility as an adjunct professor.

In addition to her legal work, Debbie has designed and delivered hundreds of professional development trainings nationally and internationally. Her teaching portfolio includes Professional Responsibility, Legal Research and Writing, and bar exam preparation. Her teaching has sharpened her analytical and writing skills while enhancing her ability to explain complex ideas with clarity.

Debbie's strengths are grounded in years of legal practice, raising a family, and supporting students and clients through important decisions. Whether guiding clients through estate planning or mentoring aspiring attorneys, she approaches her work with integrity, compassion, and an unwavering commitment to helping others navigate challenges with skill and confidence.

attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
ANDREW P. SHERWOOD is a senior trial attorney at Keller, Woods & Thompson, P.A. Andy grew up in St. Paul where he graduated from St. Paul Central High School before attending Purdue University and the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

After graduating from William Mitchell College of Law, Andy worked as an associate attorney at Palmer, Cody & O'Dea representing claimants in no-fault arbitration litigation. From 2003 to 2021, Andy was a Staff Attorney for the Progressive Minneapolis House Counsel Office. As a house counsel attorney, Andy handled and tried personal injury cases involving complex medical issues, including traumatic brain injury, spine surgery, and injection therapy management of chronic pain.

With over 18 years of insurance house counsel experience, including 2 years managing the Minneapolis Progressive House Counsel Office, and over 14 years of jury trial experience, Andy is skilled in providing insightful and effective personal injury litigation and settlement strategies and producing successful jury trial results. Andy also understands the importance of empathy and civility during the understandably stressful civil litigation process.

When he's not in the office or courtroom, Andy enjoys vacationing with his wife Michelle and their two children, watching his son's St. Paul Blackhawk soccer matches, his daughter's STAR swim meets, and following Golden Gopher basketball and football.

Mr. Sieben’s practice is limited to representing personal injury clients. John Sieben has spent his entire legal career representing personal injury clients in both district court and in the workers’ compensation system. He has successfully represented thousands of clients since 1986 through favorable settlements, trial results and appellate decisions. He combines old-fashioned litigation tactics with modern alternative dispute resolution methods to produce good results. He has been honored on three separate occasions as a “Rising Star” in the Minnesota Journal of Law and Politics.

attorneys.name: Kevin Sieben
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Eagan, MN
attorneys.bio:
Kevin Sieben is an award-winning criminal defense lawyer in Minnesota, dedicated to defending those accused of crimes throughout the state. As a third-generation attorney from Hastings, Minnesota, Kevin’s legal career is shaped by a commitment to justice and helping clients navigate the complexities of the legal system.

A graduate of St. John’s University and William Mitchell College of Law, Kevin’s early career included work in Washington, D.C., for Congressman Bill Luther and managing legislative campaigns. However, Kevin quickly found his passion in criminal defense. From securing a not-guilty verdict in a jury trial within his first six months of practice to defending clients facing serious felony charges, Kevin’s practice has consistently focused on delivering successful outcomes for his clients.

Kevin has earned numerous prestigious awards throughout his career, highlighting both his dedication to his clients and his skill in criminal defense. He has been named a Top Lawyer in Minnesota (Criminal Defense: Non White-Collar) by Minnesota Monthly, recognized on the Super Lawyer list from Thomson Reuters, and listed in Best Lawyers. These accolades are a testament to his unwavering commitment to achieving the best results for his clients.

In addition to his success in the courtroom, Kevin’s leadership in the legal community is widely respected. He served as President of the Minnesota Society for Criminal Justice in 2021/2022, an exclusive, invitation-only organization of 50 elite attorneys. In 2020, Minnesota Lawyer named him Attorney of the Year for his work in expunging criminal records for individuals impacted by the pandemic, further demonstrating his commitment to helping his clients move forward with their lives.

Kevin’s approach to criminal defense is rooted in his belief that every person deserves a strong advocate, whether they have been falsely accused or are seeking to minimize the impact of a mistake. He is known for his hands-on, client-focused approach, ensuring that each case is handled with care and precision. Kevin emphasizes communication and personal connection, taking the time to understand the unique circumstances of each client to tailor the best defense strategy. Whether it’s fighting for an acquittal at trial or negotiating the best possible outcome, Kevin’s focus remains on protecting his clients’ rights and freedoms.

Kevin Sieben comes from a distinguished family with deep roots in law, politics, and public service. His father, Bill Sieben, is a prominent personal injury attorney, and his mother, Joyce, is active in the Hastings Public Schools Foundation. Kevin’s uncles, Harry and Mike Sieben, served in the Minnesota House of Representatives, with Harry also holding the rank of Major General in the Minnesota National Guard. His cousin, Senator Katie Sieben, continues the family’s political legacy. Kevin’s grandfather, Harry Sieben, was appointed U.S. Marshal by President John F. Kennedy, and his great-grandfather and great-great-grandfather both served as mayors of Hastings. His great-uncle, James Sieben, was a decorated World War II hero and Adjutant General of the Minnesota National Guard.

Kevin Sieben is available to represent clients across Minnesota, including those in Minneapolis and surrounding areas, and offers defense in all types of criminal cases.

“Nothing is more important than protecting our liberties, and I have dedicated my life to doing that.”

His father, Bill Sieben, is a prominent personal injury attorney, and his mother, Joyce, is active in the Hastings Public Schools Foundation. Kennedy, and his great-grandfather and great-great-grandfather both served as mayors of Hastings. attorneys.name: Roy A. Sjoberg
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Woodbury, MN
attorneys.bio:
Roy A. Sjoberg opened the doors of Sjoberg Legal Services, Ltd. on October 15, 1982. Prior to practicing law, he worked as a health and life insurance agent, and it was in doing this that he learned the great value of persistence and perseverance. Bolstered by these qualities, he worked earnestly to build his law firm. Over time, he built a team of exceptional staff and fellow attorneys. Today, Sjoberg & Tebelius, P.A. is a thriving practice, respected by both clients and the community.

Roy is very proud of the vast experience represented among the attorneys of Sjoberg & Tebelius, P.A.. His particular area of expertise is estate and business planning. He believes this is a very personal field, and as such works to create a close relationship with each of his clients. He is humbled each time a prospective client places their trust in him, permitting him to develop a deep understanding of their values and aspirations.

Recognized by his peers for his exceptional interpersonal skills, Roy has a unique ability to address complicated issues with practical, yet sophisticated, planning solutions. His clients often come to him with blended family circumstances and are unable to work through an estate planning solution on their own. His approach permits clients to talk openly about their thoughts, concerns, and fears without causing emotional crises in their relationships.

For his clients who are business owners and seeking his guidance for the successful continuation of their businesses, he develops customized solutions to pave the way for a smooth transition into their company's future.

Outside of work, Roy is most passionate about making a difference in social and civic concerns, particularly when he observes those in power and influence taking advantage of those who are under-represented. For example, as an elected public official for St. Croix County, he aims to keep groundwater safe for small farm residents against the abuses of absentee-owner mega-farms.

Rotary International introduced Roy to the community leaders of Hudson, Wisconsin, his home for the last 25 years. Through the organization, he has led mission trips to Nicaragua, hosted foreign exchange students, served as Club President 2001-02, and served as District Governor 2008-09.

Roy and his wife enjoy traveling together, and spend much of their summers camping and biking. Roy has a background in music education, and in addition to singing in choirs, he enjoys attending concerts, particularly the Minnesota Opera. He also spends his time writing, reading, and playing cribbage with his wife.

In looking forward in his life and career, Roy knows one thing is certain: "I will never give up my positive attitude that I can and I must do my best to make a difference in the world. That passion is at the very core of my beliefs."

attorneys.name: Stephanie Skoro
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Eagan, MN
attorneys.bio:
Stephanie Skoro is a dedicated criminal defense attorney at Sieben Edmunds Miller, known for her compassionate approach and unwavering commitment to justice. She combines a strong legal background with firsthand courtroom experience, offering strategic and empathetic representation to clients facing serious criminal charges and child protection matters across Minnesota.

Skilled Criminal Defense Lawyer with Proven Trial Success

Stephanie has successfully defended clients in complex jury trials, securing acquittals in cases involving:

Intentional Homicide

First-Degree Criminal Sexual Conduct

Domestic Assault

Second-Degree Assault

Threats of Violence

Her experience includes litigating high-stakes felony cases and presenting persuasive arguments before both trial courts and the Minnesota Court of Appeals. Stephanie’s background as a former prosecutor gives her unique insight into how the state builds its cases, an advantage she now uses to vigorously defend the rights of the accused.

Stephanie believes in treating each client with dignity and respect, taking the time to clearly explain the legal process and empower individuals to make informed decisions. She prioritizes clear communication and client trust, ensuring every person she represents feels heard and supported throughout their case.

Minnesota CHIPS Defense Attorney and Child Protection Advocate

In addition to her criminal defense practice, Stephanie is a respected CHIPS defense attorney in Minnesota, representing parents and guardians in child protection matters, termination of parental rights (TPR) hearings, and emergency protective care (EPC) proceedings. She defends against CHIPS petitions and emergency removal orders and works tirelessly to pursue family reunification where appropriate.

Stephanie also has extensive experience in:

Indian Child Welfare Act (ICWA) cases

Foster placement hearings

Reestablishment of parental rights

Voluntary foster care agreements

Appeals in child protection matters

Her ability to navigate these sensitive, high-emotion cases with professionalism and empathy makes her a trusted advocate for families across Minnesota. Whether defending against allegations of child maltreatment or safeguarding parental rights during difficult investigations, Stephanie brings strength, clarity, and compassion to every case.

A Background Rooted in Advocacy and Service

Stephanie earned her J.D. from Mitchell Hamline School of Law, where she honed her legal skills and commitment to client advocacy. She holds a Bachelor’s degree in Political Science from the College of St. Benedict and St. John’s University, where her passion for justice was sparked during her involvement in undergraduate mock trial competitions. She also received an art scholarship and studied fine arts, with an emphasis in ceramics, an experience that shaped her creativity and connection to people.

After law school, Stephanie began her career as a criminal prosecutor, handling serious felony jury trials and numerous child protection cases. She later transitioned to criminal defense to advocate directly for individuals whose rights and freedom were at stake.

Community Involvement and Personal Interests

Stephanie volunteers with Project Access, a program supporting adults with disabilities. This community engagement reflects her deep commitment to equity and cultural understanding – values that inform her legal practice daily.

Outside of work, she enjoys spending time with her family and her miniature dachshund. You can often find her cheering for the Minnesota Twins, relaxing at a ballgame, or enjoying a quiet moment with loved ones.

Facing Criminal Charges or Child Protection Issues in Minnesota?

Whether you’re seeking an experienced criminal defense lawyer in Minnesota or need help from a CHIPS attorney to fight for your parental rights, Stephanie Skoro is here to provide knowledgeable, compassionate representation. She proudly serves clients throughout the Twin Cities and greater Minnesota.

attorneys.name: Anthony T. Smith
attorneys.practice_type: Community Association Law Lawyers in Bloomington, MN
attorneys.bio:
Anthony ("Tony") T. Smith has been representing property owners for most of his career. Tony's practice focuses on the diverse legal needs of common interest communities. He regularly advises condominium and townhome associations on all aspects of operation, management, governance, and litigation, including:

Governing document preparation, amendment, and interpretation;

Rule enforcement;

Compliance with applicable state and federal laws (MCIOA, Minnesota Nonprofit Corporations Act, Fair Housing Act, Minnesota Human Rights Act, etc.);

Homeowner dispute resolution;

Collections;

Contract review and negotiation;

Insurance claim disputes and litigation; and

Contractor disputes and construction defect litigation.

A skilled communicator, problem solver, negotiator, and trial lawyer, Tony has represented clients in cases before Minnesota's state and federal courts, state and federal appellate courts, and the Minnesota Supreme Court.

Tony is a frequent lecturer on issues pertaining to common interest communities and insurance disputes. He regularly presents educational seminars for CAI-Minnesota, CIC-Midwest, Minnesota Continuing Legal Education, and the National Business Institute. Additionally, he serves on CAI-Minnesota's Board of Directors.

Tony volunteers his time and experience as legal counsel for Rein In Sarcoma, a nonprofit organization dedicated to educating the public and medical community about sarcomas, supporting sarcoma patients and their loved ones, and funding research directed toward developing new treatments and finding a cure for sarcoma cancers.

Well respected by his peers, Tony has repeatedly been named to Minnesota's list of "Rising Stars" and "Super Lawyers."

attorneys.bio:
With nearly 20 years of experience, Jeffrey D. Smith is a distinguished attorney known for his adept representation of a wide spectrum of clients, from individuals to businesses of all sizes. Armed with an MBA and a wealth of business experience, Jeff excels at integrating legal risk assessments into clients' overall business strategies, delivering pragmatic solutions and insightful guidance that drive success.

Jeff's journey to Greenstein Sellers was marked by a tenure at a prestigious corporate law firm, where he mastered the art of representing parties in complex bankruptcy and commercial finance transactions. His expertise spans advising purchasers, sellers, boards of directors, borrowers, and secured creditors on both ordinary-course and distressed-asset finance and sale transactions. Jeff is highly skilled in structuring, documenting, and enforcing secured financing arrangements that align with clients' objectives.

attorneys.practice_type: Business & Commercial Law Lawyers in Maple Grove, MN
attorneys.bio:
Jim is a founding partner and chair of the Business Law department of the law firm of Henningson & Snoxell, Ltd., located in Maple Grove, Minnesota. Jim practices primarily in the areas of:

Business and corporate law

Privately held companies

Nonprofit organizations

Mergers and acquisitions

Strategic and succession planning

Licensing and regulatory matters

Trademark and copyright law

Employment law

Estate planning

Jim works closely with the firm's business and corporate clients providing advice on business and corporate law issues, advising nonprofit organizations about their special legal concerns, and working to prevent and resolve employment law problems. He also helps clients protect their intellectual property rights, represents them in licensing and regulatory matters, and provides advice on business succession. Jim also assists business clients with their personal estate planning needs, as well as real estate law issues.

He has received an AV® Preeminent Peer Review Rating in the distinguished legal directory, Martindale-Hubbell®,* and has been selected for inclusion in Minnesota Super Lawyers®, 2001, 2002, 2004, 2006, 2008-2012 Editions.

Among other publications, Jim is the author of the Minnesota Mechanic's Lien Practice Manual, which was published by Butterworth Legal Publishers in 1987 as a reference book for real estate attorneys in the Minnesota, and two chapters in Minnesota Business Law Deskbook 2 – The Ongoing Business Deskbook that will be published by Minnesota Continuing Legal Education in the fall of 2012. He is admitted to represent clients before all Minnesota state courts, the U.S. Supreme Court, the Minnesota Supreme Court, the Federal District Court for Minnesota, the Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals, and the U.S. Tax Court. Jim is a member of the American, Minnesota and Ramsey County bar associations, American Association for Justice (formerly the American Trial Lawyers Association), and Minnesota Association for Justice (formerly the Minnesota Trial Lawyers Association).

Like the other attorneys at Henningson & Snoxell, Jim is active in the communities we serve and his home neighborhood. He currently serves as a director of the TwinWest Chamber Foundation, North Hennepin Community College Foundation, Brooklyn Community Business Association, St. Anthony Park Properties, LLC, St. Anthony Park Booster Club, and Henningson & Snoxell, Ltd. In recent years, Jim also served both the TwinWest Chamber Foundation and the North Hennepin Community College Foundation as chairperson of their respective boards of directors, and his church as a director and chairperson of its board of trustees.

Jim received his B.A., cum laude, from Carleton College and his J.D., cum laude, from the University of Minnesota Law School. When away from the office, Jim enjoys hiking, leading a Destination Imagination team at his neighborhood’s elementary school, gardening, youth soccer coaching, and a variety of activities with his family. Jim has also been an adult Cub Scout leader and an age group coordinator and team manager for the Blackhawks of St. Paul Soccer Club.

*AV® Preeminent™ is a certification mark of Reed Elsevier Properties Inc., used in accordance with the Martindale-Hubbell certification procedures, standards and policies.

attorneys.name: Steven Henry Snyder
attorneys.practice_type: Assisted Reproductive Technology (Fertility) Law Lawyers in Champlin, MN
attorneys.bio:
Steven H. Snyder, Esq., is Of Counsel at Steven H. Snyder & Associates, where he previously served as the founding owner for over 20 years. Mr. Snyder attended law school at the University of Minnesota, graduating cum laude in 1982. Mr. Snyder successfully litigated the first contested Minnesota surrogacy case in 2006 in which he won sole custody of the child for a single father; this case has been affirmed by the Minnesota Court of Appeals. Mr. Snyder is a member of the American Bar Association (Real Property, Probate and Trust Law, Law Practice Management, and Family Law sections), Past Chair of the Assisted Reproductive Technology Committee of the ABA Family Law Section, a member of the Minnesota State Bar Association (Family Law, Real Property, Probate and Trust Law sections), Past Chair of the Family Law Section, Hennepin County Bar Association, and Wisconsin State Bar Association, and a Fellow of the American Bar Foundation. Mr. Snyder also serves as a member of the national advisory committee of RESOLVE: The National Fertility Association, past chair of the legal advisory group for the Path2Parenthood (national non-profit organizations for education, support, and advocacy on behalf of infertile persons), and is a professional member of the American Society of Reproductive Medicine (national organization of fertility physicians) and its Legal Professionals Group. Mr. Snyder is a frequent national and international speaker on assisted reproductive technology topics and from 2009-2010 was an adjunct professor of assisted reproductive technology law at the Hamline University Law School and at William Mitchell College of Law from 2009 to the present.

Loren Solfest is a managing shareholder and Vice-President of Dougherty, Molenda, Solfest, Hills & Bauer P.A. He heads the firms banking, business and commercial law and civil and commercial litigation practice groups and he has been practicing transactional and litigation law since 1986. He practices in the areas of banking, commercial litigation, business and real estate law. He has successfully represented clients in a wide variety of transactions and cases in state and federal courts, at both the district and appellate court levels.

Loren is certified as a Real Property Specialist by the Minnesota State Bar Association, is also a qualified neutral under Rule 114 of the Minnesota General Rules of Practice, and he has served as a mediator and arbitrator in numerous cases since 1997. Loren is licensed to practice law in the States of Minnesota and Wisconsin. He is also admitted to practice in the United States Court of Appeals, Eighth Circuit; the United States District Court, District of Minnesota; and the United States District Court, Western District of Wisconsin. Loren has been repeatedly named to the Super Lawyers list and AV Peer Review Rated.

When he is not at work, Loren enjoys family and church activities, participating in various sports, coaching his children's sports teams and following the Fighting Irish.
