attorneys.name: Russell Spence
attorneys.practice_type: Business & Corporate Law Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Mick Spence is a partner with Hellmuth & Johnson, PLLC representing entertainment, intellectual property and business clients through the firm's Business Services Group. He assists individuals and entities of all sizes, with a wide variety of business and litigation issues, including:

Copyright, Trademark, Patent, Trade Secrets & Right of Publicity/Privacy

Asset acquisitions, licensing and protection

Complex, multi-party litigation, including class-actions

Commercial disputes of all varieties

Estate counsel & Probate litigation

Mick provides thoughtful counsel, proactive advice and zealous representation to his clients, while aggressively defending their rights and interests in all business or litigation matters. Combining his passions for creativity, commerce, advocacy and success, Mick has established a reputation as the go-to attorney for both creative talents and entrepreneurial businesses.

Mick’s extensive litigation experience involves entertainment assets, businesses, talent and their careers. His commercial litigation experience includes shareholder & partnership disputes, infringement actions, class-actions, trade secret protection, fraud, unfair competition and even estate or probate disputes.

Mick has been chosen by his peers as a Minnesota Super Lawyer®; with only 5% of Minnesota attorneys earning this recognition. Prior to that, he was selected as a Rising Star for multiple years running. Mick has taught college courses in Copyright, Music Publishing and Contract Law. He also frequently speaks and writes regarding business and legal issues, including the evolving entertainment industry and litigation developments.

Mick is licensed to practice law in Minnesota’s Federal and State Courts. He has also been admitted and represented clients in the Courts of New York, Florida, Texas and Utah. He is a member of the National Academy of Recording Arts & Sciences (the Grammy® Organization), the Association of Media & Entertainment Counsel, the Forum of Entertainment and Sports Industries of the ABA and the Art & Entertainment Section of the MSBA, serving as its Chairperson. He was also twice elected as President of the Minnesota Music Academy, where he produced the Minnesota Music Awards. Minneapolis Mayor R.T. Rybak also appointed him to serve and advise on the Minneapolis Arts Commission.

Mick received a business degree from the Entrepreneur Program at the University of Southern California in Los Angeles. He left the sun, sand & smog behind, returning to his home state of Minnesota, to earn his J.D. from William Mitchell College of Law.

attorneys.name: Jon R. Steckler
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial and Business Law Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Jon's practice is focused on commercial and business law and related litigation and appeals. Serving as general corporate counsel for companies in various industries, Jon regularly advises clients on a broad range of issues facing businesses on a day-to-day basis.

Jon advises on complex commercial contracts, franchise agreements, distribution contracts, construction contracts, non-compete agreements, commercial leases, and asset and stock purchase agreements. In addition to representing clients in general commercial, corporate and operational matters, Jon represents clients in state and federal courts, administrative hearings and in alternative dispute resolution in jurisdictions nationwide. Assessment and management of risk for clients on wide-ranging operational and strategic issues, timely issue spotting and front-end problem solving are among Jon's core strengths.

Jon received his undergraduate degree in Political Science from South Dakota State University, and his J.D. from the University of South Dakota School of Law, where he served as the Managing Editor of the South Dakota Law Review and earned Dean's List honors. After law school, Jon served as a judicial clerk at the Minnesota Court of Appeals. Early in his legal career, Jon served as a prosecuting attorney for several suburban municipalities.

Jon has provided pro bono legal services through Volunteer Lawyers Network and LegalCORPS and has served as pro bono general counsel for a non-profit no-kill animal shelter and adoption agency for over 16 years.

Jon has been selected to the Minnesota Super Lawyer’s list since 2022 and has been recognized by America's Top 100 Bet-the-Company Litigators. Jon and his wife live in Golden Valley with their daughter and their Chihuahua, Jeffrey. In his spare time, Jon enjoys running, biking, swimming, hiking, and golfing, and has volunteered as an instructor for the Loppet Foundation Trail Kids Mountain Bike Program.

attorneys.name: John J. Steffenhagen
attorneys.practice_type: Appeals Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
John J. Steffenhagen is a partner with the firm, where he has a broad-based litigation and counseling practice honed over 20 years of experience helping clients succeed in both the courtroom and boardroom. John's practice is concentrated in the following areas:

Employment law and litigation

Commercial litigation

Municipal law

John represents corporations, other business entities and individuals in litigation ranging from employment disputes to complex multi-party litigation involving real property, commercial and environmental matters. In addition to being a seasoned litigator, clients regard him as a trusted counselor on a wide variety of day-to-day employment matters affecting their business operations.

He also has extensive experience in the municipal law arena-from challenges on behalf of entities or homeowners facing eminent domain or addressing adverse zoning determinations, to assisting municipalities with internal matters including annexation, detachment and incorporation. For example, he served as lead trial counsel for the City of Columbus incorporation-one of the few, if not only Minnesota cases in which a township simultaneously won legal status as a city, while defeating annexation of an entire commercial district to a far larger, neighboring city.

Licensed to practice law in the state and federal courts of Minnesota, John is a member of the American and Minnesota State Bar Associations. He is dedicated to a wide variety of civic and charitable causes, including serving on the Board of Directors of the St. Louis Park Emergency Program (STEP), a community based not-for-profit agency providing crisis services to residents in need.

John obtained his J.D. from Georgetown University Law Center in Washington, DC and his B.A. from St. John's University in Collegeville, Minnesota.

attorneys.name: Mark V. Steffenson
attorneys.practice_type: Business & Commercial Law Lawyers in Maple Grove, MN
attorneys.bio:
Mark is a shareholder in the law firm of Henningson & Snoxell, Ltd., located in Maple Grove, Minnesota. He concentrates his practice representing clients in business and commercial litigation. Minnesota Law & Politics magazine has repeatedly named Mark a Super Lawyer, a designation reserved for only 5 percent of the total lawyers in the state. He has also received an AV® Preeminent Peer Review Rating in the distinguished legal directory, Martindale-Hubbell®.*

Mark has devoted his entire career to representing clients in civil litigation trying dozens of cases in state and federal courts. He also resolves disputes using arbitration and mediation.

His approach to representing clients is based on years of experience as a commercial litigator, as well as a professional who understands business. From the outset of the relationship, Mark is committed to carefully listening to his clients to thoroughly understand the problems they face and their desired outcome. At that point he will evaluate the problem to provide his client with a fair and accurate assessment as to where the case is headed relative to the ultimate cost, the realistic chance of recovery, and determine the actual value of the case to the client.

Mark's practice includes representing businesses and nonprofit organizations in the following areas:

Contract disputes. For more than 20 years, Mark has diligently represented the interests of his clients in contract disputes, whether large or small. Most often such disputes are related to contract terms, interpretation, or breach of contract.

Employment and ERISA litigation. In the area of employment law, Mark counsels his business clients in the downsizing process and their legal obligations under federal and state law, such as the WARN Act. He has represented businesses ranging from small employers to the world's largest media conglomerate in all of their Minnesota employment and ERISA matters. Mark has successfully represented business clients with regard to employment contracts, harassment matters, trade secrets, defending and enforcing non-competes, as well as in ERISA litigation.

Insurance coverage disputes. Mark's business clients seek his counsel to review commercial liability policies, determine if there is coverage for a claim, and to take appropriate action to recover. He has successfully recovered insurance awards related to:

Fire

Theft and embezzlement

Property damage

Employee misconduct in areas such as harassment and motor vehicle accidents

Life insurance awards related to issues for failure to disclose information on the insurance application

Shareholder and partnership disputes. Mark works with closely held entities and partnerships to assist them in resolving internal disputes or management problems. He has represented both minority and majority shareholders in disputes in a variety of industries, such as CNC manufacturers, personal services, telecommunications and ammunition manufacturers.

Third Party Administrators (TPAs). Mark has many years of experience representing TPAs involving disputes regarding administration of plan claims, both welfare and pension based.

Trust and estates litigation. Mark represents clients relative to the disposition of assets from a trust or an estate, as well as the interpretation of the Will or other controlling document.

Appellate law. During the course of his career, Mark has represented clients on appeal to the Minnesota Court of Appeals, the Minnesota Supreme Court, as well as the federal appellate system. Highlights of his appellate representation include:

Employment related appeals

ERISA

Nursing home responsible party

Consumer fraud on behalf of students of the Minnesota School of Business

Mark is admitted to practice in all Minnesota state courts, as well the U.S. District Court of Minnesota, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 8th Circuit, and the U.S. Supreme Court. He is a member of the Minnesota Trial Lawyers Association and the Federal, Minnesota State and Hennepin County Bar Associations.

Mark is a member of the Maple Grove City Council and was elected Mayor of the City in 2001. He also serves on the Board of Directors of the North Minneapolis Convention Bureau, is President of the North Metro Mayors Association, a member of the Regional Council of Mayors and the Municipal Legislative Commission, and serves on the Board of Directors of Community Action for Suburban Hennepin (CASH). Mark is also active in the North Hennepin Chamber of Commerce, Hennepin County Sheriff's Community Advisory Committee, and the Steering Committee for the Maple Grove D.A.R.E. House Project.

Born in Robbinsdale, Minnesota, Mark received his law degree, cum laude, from the University of Minnesota Law School, and his B.A., cum laude, from St. Olaf College. Following law school, Mark clerked for the Honorable Chief Magistrate Judge J. Earl Cudd and the Honorable Magistrate Judge Floyd Bodine. He joined Henningson & Snoxell, Ltd. in 1996.

*AV® Preeminent™ is a certification mark of Reed Elsevier Properties Inc., used in accordance with the Martindale-Hubbell certification procedures, standards and policies.

attorneys.name: Daniel J. Steinhagen
attorneys.practice_type: Probate Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Dan Steinhagen has been a probate and elder law attorney for over 36 years. He has helped hundreds of clients with estate plans and estate administrations. When possible, he helps clients avoid probate entirely. In addition, Dan is recognized as one of the Minnesota's most experienced guardianship and conservatorship attorneys, having handled over 1000 cases. He is often called upon to present lectures and seminars to attorneys, guardians, conservators, and social workers. His probate and elder law experience includes:

Drafting over 1000 Wills, Trusts, Powers of Attorney, and Healthcare Directives

Assisting clients with over 600 estate adminstration proceedings

Establishing over 1000 guardianships and conservatorships

Counseling clients on avoiding probate and minimizing estate taxes

Preparing Transfer of Death Deeds

In recognition of his experience in the areas of probate and elder law, Dan was designated by his peers as a "Super Lawyer", chosen as Hennepin County Bar Association Probate and Elder Law Section Chair, twice elected President of the Minnesota Association of Guardianship and Conservatorship, and selected to serve on the MSBA Elder Law Section Governing Council. Dan is also a Martindale-Hubbell AV rated attorney.

attorneys.name: Benjamin C. Stellplug
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Ben is a detail-oriented and pragmatic attorney whose practice focuses on commercial litigation, construction defect, banking, creditor remedies, and real estate matters. He represents financial institutions, contractors and construction companies, established businesses, and individuals in a wide range of civil litigation and transactional matters in both state and federal courts. Prior to joining the firm, Ben spent the first years of his career focused on litigating products liability and catastrophic injury cases in federal and state courts around the country, gaining extensive experience in every phase of the litigation process. Ben was personally involved in some of the largest medical device and pharmaceutical cases in the country’s history prior to joining the firm. Most recently, Ben worked in-house at a Silicon Valley-based startup company focused on supporting Fortune-50 companies on employment matters. As such, Ben brings a diverse and valuable set of skills to the Greenstein Sellers team.

Ben takes a strategic and hands-on approach to resolving disputes, offering thoughtful counsel throughout the litigation process while also advising clients on broader business and operational concerns. He is committed to the relentless pursuit of the best possible outcome for all of his clients. Due to his diverse and pointed experience, Ben is able to provide practical advice before litigation arises, as well as expertise at every stage of the process if and when litigation does ensue.

As a lifelong Minnesotan, Ben is an active member of the local Twin Cities community and enjoys spending quality time with his wife and growing family.

attorneys.name: Francis E. Stephens
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury -- Plaintiff Lawyers in Duluth, MN
attorneys.bio:
I have been practicing law for over 25 years exclusively in personal injury litigation. I have successfully represented hundreds of personal injury clients in a wide variety of personal injury claims. My experience includes work on cases ranging from serious motor vehicle accidents to cases involving wrongful death, brain injury, spinal injuries, burns, limb loss, and toxic exposure.

I have successfully tried jury cases to verdict in state district court and worked on appeals, having argued my clients' cases both in the Minnesota Court of Appeals and the Minnesota Supreme Court. I am admitted to practice in both Minnesota State Court and Federal District Court.

I was nominated by my legal peers as a Rising Star of Minnesota in Minnesota Law & Politics magazine. I am an active member of the Minnesota State Bar Association and work as a certified arbitrator for the American Arbitration Association resolving insurance disputes for auto accident claims. I have also served as President of the John E. Simonett Chapter of the American Inns of Court, an organization of judges and lawyers whose purpose is to foster excellence in ethics, civility, and advocacy skills in the legal profession.

I am a 1993 honors graduate of William Mitchell College of Law in St. Paul, Minnesota. I was an honors graduate from the University of Minnesota, Duluth, with undergraduate degrees in English, French, and political science. I also studied internationally at Appleby College in Toronto, Ontario, and at the Université Paul Valéry in Montpellier, France.

I enjoy spending time with my children hiking and exploring the outdoors. I also enjoy running trails on the north shore of Lake Superior with my dog Wyatt and competing in half-marathons. I consider myself an amateur photographer and love live music.

attorneys.name: Kathy Stephens
attorneys.practice_type: Agribusiness Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Kathy is an experienced litigation and commercial attorney who joined Rock Hutchinson as a Senior Attorney in 2019. Kathy focuses her practice on complex commercial and contract litigation for a wide variety of corporate clients, including hospitals, financial institutions, and food and beverage companies. Kathy also provides a broad range of corporate counseling and transactional services to clients in the food and agribusiness industries.

Kathy and her family relocated to Minneapolis from San Antonio, Texas, where she formerly served as the Original Proceedings Staff Attorney to the Fourth Court of Appeals. Her role at the Court involved responsibility for complex legal research, drafting opinions for Justices, and management of the docket of majority, concurring and dissenting opinions through to publication. Prior to her role at the Fourth Court, Kathy's private practice included briefing appeals before several Texas intermediate Courts of Appeal, the Texas Supreme Court, the United States Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit and the United States Supreme Court. Kathy continues to apply her appellate experience to assist clients through the appellate process in Minnesota.

Kathy began her legal career in 2004 as a Briefing Attorney to the Honorable Justice Phylis J. Speedlin, an Associate Appellate Justice at the Fourth Court of Appeals in Texas. After completing this one-year position, Kathy went on to become an associate and then shareholder at Clemens & Spencer, P.C. where her litigation practice included representation of attorneys and other professionals in malpractice and fiduciary litigation, commercial and corporate litigation, personal injury and products liability matters, and contract and policy review for corporate clients. Kathy has handled litigation matters up to and including trial and appeal, arbitration cases, mediations, administrative law matters and grievances before professional review and licensing boards.

Contact Kathy by e-mailing her at kstephens@rockhutchinson.com or by calling her at 612-573-3688.

attorneys.practice_type: Trust and Estate Litigation Lawyers in Woodbury, MN
attorneys.bio:
As a senior attorney at Messick Law, PLLC, in Saint Paul, Minnesota, Patricia Jean Stotzheim offers legal advice to individuals and families in matters involving trusts, estates and dispute resolution. Her practice areas include trust and estate litigation, probate and trust administration, alternative dispute resolution and wills. She works closely with clients to handle complicated legal and family dynamics, offering practical guidance tailored to their long-term goals.

Ms. Stotzheim represents beneficiaries, fiduciaries, and other interested parties in contested trust and probate cases. She also helps clients with the orderly administration of estates and trusts, helping them understand their responsibilities and comply with the law. Additionally, she serves as a mediator, facilitating productive discussions and negotiated resolutions in estate-related conflicts. Her approach emphasizes clarity, preparation and thoughtful advocacy, whether in litigation or collaborative settings.

Ms. Stotzheim completed her undergraduate studies at Hamline University School of Liberal Arts. After an impressive career coaching collegiate gymnastics, she then went on to attend the Hamline University School of Law, where she developed her legal principles and earned her Juris Doctor, graduating cum laude in 2006, an achievement that reflects her commitment to the study of law. She studied dispute resolution at Hamline’s Dispute Resolution Institute (DRI) and attended DRI courses offered in France, Budapest, and Israel.

An active member in the legal community, Ms. Stotzheim holds several leadership roles within professional organizations. She serves as a council member of the Minnesota State Bar Association for the Probate and Trust section, is a member of the section’s legislative committee, and was previously co-chair of the section’s Continuing Legal Education Committee. Since 2010, she has been a member of the Minnesota Women Lawyers. She formerly served as Continuing Legal Education co-chair for the Ramsey County Bar Association. As a proud Hamline Piper, she also frequently provides her time and energy to Hamline gymnastics and the athletic department.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
As a senior attorney at Messick Law, PLLC, in Saint Paul, Minnesota, Patricia Jean Stotzheim offers legal advice to individuals and families in matters involving trusts, estates and dispute resolution. Her practice areas include trust and estate litigation, probate and trust administration, alternative dispute resolution and wills. She works closely with clients to handle complicated legal and family dynamics, offering practical guidance tailored to their long-term goals.

Ms. Stotzheim represents beneficiaries, fiduciaries, and other interested parties in contested trust and probate cases. She also helps clients with the orderly administration of estates and trusts, helping them understand their responsibilities and comply with the law. Additionally, she serves as a mediator, facilitating productive discussions and negotiated resolutions in estate-related conflicts. Her approach emphasizes clarity, preparation and thoughtful advocacy, whether in litigation or collaborative settings.

Ms. Stotzheim completed her undergraduate studies at Hamline University School of Liberal Arts. After an impressive career coaching collegiate gymnastics, she then went on to attend the Hamline University School of Law, where she developed her legal principles and earned her Juris Doctor, graduating cum laude in 2006, an achievement that reflects her commitment to the study of law. She studied dispute resolution at Hamline’s Dispute Resolution Institute (DRI) and attended DRI courses offered in France, Budapest, and Israel.

An active member in the legal community, Ms. Stotzheim holds several leadership roles within professional organizations. She serves as a council member of the Minnesota State Bar Association for the Probate and Trust section, is a member of the section’s legislative committee, and was previously co-chair of the section’s Continuing Legal Education Committee. Since 2010, she has been a member of the Minnesota Women Lawyers. She formerly served as Continuing Legal Education co-chair for the Ramsey County Bar Association. As a proud Hamline Piper, she also frequently provides her time and energy to Hamline gymnastics and the athletic department.

attorneys.name: Michael R. Strom
attorneys.practice_type: Mesothelioma and Asbestos-Related Cancers Lawyers in Eagan, MN
attorneys.bio:
Mike Strom is the Treasurer and former President and Managing Partner of Sieben Polk, and has been a trial lawyer with the firm since 1985. He has obtained several recoveries for his clients in excess of one million dollars. He has represented Plaintiffs in Minnesota’s four largest recoveries in asbestos personal injury claims. His eight million dollar verdict on behalf of a Koch Refinery employee in 2001 stands as the largest asbestos verdict in Minnesota history. In March of 2008, he obtained a 4.6 million dollar damage award on behalf of an NSP pipefitter. In 2014, he was part of the trial team that obtained a $4.5 million award on behalf of a Taconite Harbor laborer. In addition to toxic torts, Mr. Strom focuses his practice in the area of complex products liability, premises liability, and general personal injury. He has been a partner and shareholder of the firm for many years.

Mr. Strom’s accomplishments have led to his being named Plaintiff’s Product Liability “Lawyer of the Year” for 2020 by “Best Lawyers.” He has similarly been honored as a “Super Lawyer” by Minnesota Law & Politics, Twin Cities Business Monthly, and Mpls St. Paul Magazine since 2004. Mr. Strom has been voted a “Top 100” Super Lawyer six times, placing him in the top one percent of Minnesota attorneys as ranked by his peers. He has also been repeatedly recognized as one of Minnesota’s “Top 40” Plaintiff personal injury attorneys by Minnesota Super Lawyers. For many years, he has also been selected as one of the “Best Lawyers in America.” He has further obtained an AV attorney ranking in Martindale Hubbell, the highest ranking available from that publication. Finally, Mr. Strom received a perfect 5.0 peer rating from lawyers.com.

In addition to his extensive trial practice, Mr. Strom heads the firm’s appellate department, and recently defeated asbestos product manufacturer John Crane’s appeal of a $3,689,193.00 judgment in Newinski v. John Crane, Inc., WL 1752011 (Minn. Ct. App. June 23, 2009), rev. denied, (Minn. Sept. 16, 2009). Mr. Strom had previously tried the case to a Ramsey County jury in March of 2008. The jury returned a verdict for $4,611,492.00, and had determined that Crane was responsible for 55%. Mr. Strom successfully argued in post-trial motions that Crane was jointly and severally liable for 80% of the verdict under Minnesota law, raising Crane’s liability from $2,536,320.60 to $3,689,193.00, an increase of $1,152,872.40 for his clients.

Another aspect of Mr. Strom’s support of asbestos victims is his service as a member of the claimants’ committee of the Western Asbestos Settlement trust, which administers claims of individuals suffering diseases caused by exposure to asbestos by various entities including MacArthur Corporation, one of the most prevalent former asbestos contractors in Minnesota.

Mr. Strom also argued successfully on behalf of the Plaintiff in the Minnesota Supreme Court’s landmark decision of Gray v. Badger Mining Co., 676 N.W. 2d 268 (Minn. 2004). The decision overruled a Court of Appeals decision that would have deprived injured workers from recovering damages against manufacturers of defective products if the worker’s employer knew of the product’s dangers.

Mr. Strom recently served on the Products Liability subcommittee assigned to assist the District Court Judges Association in drafting Minnesota’s newest civil jury instruction guide, the purpose of which is to assist trial courts and practitioners in properly advising jurors of the law applicable to the case before them. He had previously served on the General Law subcommittee for the previous edition of the guide.

In addition to presenting continuing legal educational programs to fellow attorneys, Mr. Strom served from 2001 to 2009 as an adjunct professor at the William Mitchell College of Law teaching first year law students legal research, writing, and analysis. He has also contributed materials to publications of the Minnesota Association for Justice, and served for many years on the prestigious Amicus Committee.

Mr. Strom is frequently asked by other attorneys to serve as a case arbitrator, and is a certified neutral of the American Arbitration Association. He further serves as an arbitrator of asbestos claims for the Eagle-Picher Industries Personal Injury Settlement Trust, and routinely serves as a case evaluator for other attorneys through the MAJ case evaluation service.

Mr. Strom is an honors graduate of the University of Minnesota Law School, and completed his undergraduate training at Carleton College, where he was elected a member of Phi Beta Kappa and graduated Magna Cum Laude. He has been a member of the Minnesota State Bar since October of 1985, and is currently licensed to practice before the Supreme Court of the United States, the Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals, the United States District Court for the District of Minnesota, and Minnesota’s state court system. He has also been admitted to practice pro hac vice to litigate cases in the state and federal courts in Ohio, and also Wisconsin.

In addition to serving as a Master and membership committee co-chair of the Warren E. Burger Inn of Court for many years, Mr. Strom is a member of the Minnesota State Bar Association, the Minnesota Association for Justice, and the American Association for Justice.

Mike Strom is a lifelong Minnesotan, and lives with his wife Pamela and two children in Minneapolis.

sections.title: Representative Cases
content: 2018—Part of trial team obtaining a multi-million dollar verdict on behalf of former NSP employee, recently upheld on appeal

2014 – Obtained $4,516,250.00 verdict with Patrick DeBlase of DeBlase, Brown, Eyerly on behalf of accountant who contracted mesothelioma as a result of asbestos exposure at taconite plant. Client worked for just four months at the plant, working as a laborer to earn college money in 1957. Client recalled cutting, mixing, and handling pipe covering and asbestos muds. Partner Chad Alexander also served on trial team

2014 – Mr. Strom and partner Chad Alexander recovered over $635,000 on behalf of mesothelioma victim who had worked as a mechanic at service station from 1961-77. Client's chief exposure was to asbestos-containing friction materials

2014 – Recovered over $1.4 million for Butler Taconite millwright and pump mechanic suffering from mesothelioma. Defense unsuccessfully argued that client’s secondary diagnosis of pancreatic cancer should limit or preclude recovery

2013 - Obtained over $2.5 million in settlement for farmer who had earlier been exposed to asbestos while working as a union pipefitter. The client contracted mesothelioma, an asbestos-related cancer of the lining of the lung. The case settled shortly before trial following the trial court's denial of Defendants' motions for summary judgment.

2012 - Secured over $2 million for airline mechanic, who had contracted mesothelioma as a result of on the job asbestos exposure. Plaintiff identified asbestos used within aircraft engines manufactured by several different defendants, as well as asbestos used within the airframe and standard airline maintenance materials.

2011 - Recovered over $1 million dollars for retired railroad worker who contracted mesothelioma as a result of exposure to asbestos early in his career during steam locomotive overhauls. The Plaintiff was also exposed to asbestos during the original construction of a taconite plant on Minnesota's Iron Range.

2011 - Negotiated multi-defendant settlement in excess of $1.8 million on behalf of nursery and greenhouse owner/operator suffering from mesothelioma. The Plaintiff was exposed to asbestos from a variety of materials used on the job, including asbestos boiler insulation, gaskets, transit sheets, and agricultural grade vermiculite.

2011 - Recovered settlements totaling over $1.16 million for commercial estimator suffering from mesothelioma. Plaintiff's only known asbestos exposure occurred when he would visit construction sites to take measurements for industrial steel railings, stairways, and walkways fabricated by his employer.

2010 - Wrongful death suit on behalf of office worker, whose only known asbestos exposure occurred when she was in high school. Her father operated a rural school bus line and replaced bus brakes. Plaintiff was exposed to asbestos visiting her father after school at the bus maintenance garage located next door to family home, and contracted mesothelioma just before her fiftieth birthday. Claim ultimately settled for just over $1 million.

2009 - Obtained over $1.05 million in wrongful death suit brought on behalf of brazier in aeronautics industry. Plaintiff contracted mesothelioma as a result of asbestos released from transite panels that he routinely abraded in performing his duties.
$4.6 million jury award in March 2008 for NSP worker in case against gasket manufacturer, affirmed by Minnesota appellate courts on appeal.
Seven figure aggregate settlement in 2007 for outside delivery man exposed to asbestos in various industrial plants.
$625,000.00 settlement in 2006 for wrongful death of thirteen-year-old boy killed during roll over of unstable modified golf car. Case prosecuted by attorneys Michael S. Polk and Michael R. Strom.
$1.65 Million jury verdict in 2003 for refrigeration worker exposed to asbestos in case tried by Mr. Strom and his partner Scott Hertogs.
$8.05 Million jury verdict in 2001 for pipe fitter exposed to asbestos at refinery.
$1.35 Million settlement on behalf of a burn victim in a service station explosion in Columbus, Ohio.
Several total settlements in asbestos product liability cases in excess of one million dollars.

As a result, Minnesota essentially retains joint and several liability in asbestos cases)

Doten v. ACandS, Inc., et al., 1997 WL 118248 (Minn. Ct. App. Mar. 18, 1997); Court of Appeals affirmed $1.5 Million verdict against in asbestos personal injury case, including $ 500,000.00 punitive damage award against Owens Corning Fiberglas.

Swanson v. Timesavers, et al., 1997 WL 104917 (Minn. Ct. App. March 11, 1997); Court of Appeals affirmed $766,000.00 verdict in favor of employee who lost two fingers in an industrial sander. Court rejected assertions that employee assumed the risk, that no manufacturing defect existed in the sander, and that co-employee was not grossly negligent.
Dodge v. Jose's American Grill, 1995 WL 25209 (Minn. Ct. App. Jan. 24, 1995); Court of Appeals rejected

Board of Regents of the University of Minnesota v. Ind. School Dist. 622 v. Keene Corp., 511 N.W. 2d 728 (Minn. 1994); Minnesota Supreme Court affirmed $820,750.00 compensatory damages verdict against asbestos manufacturer for cost of removing asbestos fireproofing from Tartan high school in Oakdale, Minnesota. Court rejected manufacturer's claim that was entitled to comparative fault finding against other settled entities not at trial.

Keene Corp. v. Cass, 908 F. 2d 293 (8th Cir. 1990); court rejected civil rights action filed against court and plaintiff's counsel for enforcing orders compelling discovery against corporation despite it's claims of privilege.
2010 – Represented Plaintiffs in two companion cases arising out of asbestos exposure at a Minnesota refinery during the 1960s and 70s. Both cases culminated in settlements in excess of $1 million.

attorneys.bio:
I believe the best results begin with a collaborative attorney-client relationship, and are realized through hard work and perseverance. That is why I take a hands-on approach to my clients' cases from the start, and fight until their goals are achieved. My focus at Meshbesher & Associates is plaintiff's-side personal injury and civil rights cases. I have extensive experience in these areas from pre-claim investigation, through settlement negotiations, litigation and trial. I attribute my track record of success to dedicated and personalized attention to each case I handle.

I earned my bachelor's degree from Miami University in Oxford, Ohio, where I double majored in economics and philosophy. I then came home to Minnesota in 2006 and attended the University of Minnesota Law School, graduating in 2009. During law school, I was a staff member and editor with the Minnesota Journal of International Law. I am admitted to practice with the Minnesota State Bar, the Federal District Court in Minnesota and the Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals.

Since joining Meshbesher & Associates in 2012, I have handled hundreds of personal injury and civil rights cases - ranging from small but important claims involving temporary injuries, to wrongful death and major civil rights cases, some of which have gained national media and government attention. I am more than happy to speak with you directly about your potential case today.

attorneys.name: Paul T. Sullivan
attorneys.practice_type: Antitrust/Competition Lawyers in Boston, MN
attorneys.bio:
Paul T. Sullivan is the Managing Partner of the Boston office of The Chartwell Law Offices, LLP. Paul handles a variety of complex litigation matters with an emphasis in insurance coverage. While with another firm, he represented a major property insurer in the multi-billion dollar coverage and subrogation litigation related to the destruction of the World Trade Center on September 11, 2001. Paul was involved from start to finish, nearly 100 hearing days, in the appraisal of the property and time element losses associated with the destruction of the World Trade Center. Given the high stakes, the appraisal process dealt with nearly every conceivable construction and property insurance coverage issue. For a description of the World Trade Center appraisal process, See "Appraising the 9/11 Damages to the World Trade Center," Dispute Resolution Journal, August/October 2007 issue.

Upon settlement of the World Trade Center insurance coverage litigation, Paul became involved in the negotiation of damages issues in the multi-billion subrogation action related to the losses sustained on September 11, 2001. The litigation recently settled for $1.2 billion, reportedly the largest subrogation recovery ever obtained. Based on these experiences, Paul has developed considerable expertise in the analysis and presentation of complex damages issues.

In addition to his first party coverage experience, Paul has also successfully represented insurers in third party coverage litigation, including environmental and contractor claims, and extra-contractual claims, including defense of allegations of bad faith.

Paul also has significant experience in antitrust and class action cases and has represented clients in a number of antitrust recovery actions.

Prior to entering private practice, Paul served for five years as an assistant prosecuting attorney. In that position, he was responsible for the prosecution of serious felonies, including homicides, and tried over 20 cases to juries.

Paul started his legal career at a litigation firm that specialized in defense work, including general and products liability.

Upon settlement of the World Trade Center insurance coverage litigation, Paul became involved in the negotiation of damages issues in the multi-billion subrogation action related to the losses sustained on September 11, 2001. The litigation recently settled for $1.2 billion, reportedly the largest subrogation recovery ever obtained. Based on these experiences, Paul has developed considerable expertise in the analysis and presentation of complex damages issues.

In addition to his first party coverage experience, Paul has also successfully represented insurers in third party coverage litigation, including environmental and contractor claims, and extra-contractual claims, including defense of allegations of bad faith.

Paul also has significant experience in antitrust and class action cases and has represented clients in a number of antitrust recovery actions.

Prior to entering private practice, Paul served for five years as an assistant prosecuting attorney. In that position, he was responsible for the prosecution of serious felonies, including homicides, and tried over 20 cases to juries.

Paul started his legal career at a litigation firm that specialized in defense work, including general and products liability.

attorneys.name: Ryan P. Supple
attorneys.practice_type: Business Law Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Ryan Supple is a seasoned attorney with extensive litigation experience across a variety of practice areas. Ryan currently focuses his practice on construction law, business law, consumer law, and real estate. Ryan also advises clients on matters related to municipal law, entity formation, and cannabis law.

While Ryan is ready to fight for clients in litigation, he is also keenly aware of the burden and expense that protracted litigation can impose. In this regard, Ryan also has experience successfully negotiating settlements to avoid costly litigation and ensure client recoveries.

Before joining Christensen Law Office PLLC, Ryan clerked for a Minnesota district court judge and worked for several law firms in the Twin Cities, representing individuals, businesses, and municipalities in a variety of matters. Ryan has appeared frequently in Minnesota and Wisconsin courts, administrative hearings, and argued cases before the Minnesota Court of Appeals. Ryan has also represented clients before various state and federal government agencies.

During law school, Ryan worked for a city attorney's office and worked for a government relations practice lobbying in the Minnesota legislature. Before law school, Ryan worked as a legislative aide in the Wisconsin State Senate where he became intimately familiar with the legislative process and government operations.

In his free time, Ryan enjoys spending time with his wife and kids; doing outdoor activities such as hiking, biking, kayaking, skating, and skiing; and he also loves going to see live music.

attorneys.name: Matthew D. Swanson
attorneys.practice_type: Homeowners Associations Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Matt is a Partner and a seasoned attorney with over a decade of experience in complex litigation. His practice focuses on bankruptcy law, real estate law, creditor remedies, construction law, and general business law. Matt represents a broad range of clients, including individuals, businesses of all sizes, homeowner associations, and bankruptcy trustees. Prior to joining Greenstein Sellers, Matt was a partner at a boutique law firm focused on the specialized representation of homeowner associations and Chapter 7 panel trustees. Through this work, Matt gained critical experience navigating various areas of law, allowing him to provide his clients with a well-rounded legal perspective.

Matt has successfully litigated complex legal issues in the United States Federal Bankruptcy Courts, and won appeals in front of the U.S. District Court, 8th Circuit Bankruptcy Appellate Panel and 8th Circuit Court of Appeals. Having managed cases from filing through appeal, Matt is able to counsel clients through the complex reality of the legal process. Matt takes pride in providing clients with an honest assessment of their legal claims and creative options to successfully resolve whatever challenge they are facing.

When Matt is not at work, he enjoys spending time with his wife and four kids. Matt considers himself an avid outdoorsman and tries to hunt and fish as much as possible. Matt is also an engaged and dedicated member of his local church, serving his community in many capacities.

attorneys.bio:
As a dedicated Family Law Associate Attorney, Kala brings a compassionate and client-focused approach to the practice of law. With a commitment to helping individuals navigate the complexities of family legal matters, Kala strives to provide effective and personalized solutions tailored to the unique needs of each client. Understanding the emotional and financial challenges associated with family law issues, Kala approaches each case with empathy and a commitment to finding solutions that promote the well-being of all involved parties. attorneys.name: Jodi L. Tagessen
attorneys.practice_type: Land Use & Development Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Jodi specializes in providing comprehensive legal solutions to complex commercial real estate transaction questions. Clients come to her when they need help navigating intricate title issues, structuring real estate transactions, and ensuring seamless closings. With more than 20 years of experience across the commercial real estate lifecycle, Jodi brings particular expertise to retail properties and self-storage facilities. She also has experience working with complex organizations to close transactions such as state and local government, charter school and church governing bodies.

At Monroe Moxness Berg, Jodi collaborates with internal teams on real estate components of mergers and acquisitions, conducts thorough title review, and manages complex real estate transactions from due diligence through closing.

Jodi takes pride in her practical, client-first approach to legal challenges. She believes in identifying efficient solutions that move transactions forward while protecting her clients’ interests. Her experience spanning title insurance, construction disbursing, construction project management, and corporate legal counsel gives her a multifaceted perspective on commercial real estate matters. This allows her to offer clients valuable insights into potential risks and opportunities while guiding them through complex transactions.

Prior to joining MMB, Jodi served as Director of Legal at KO Storage, where she spearheaded over $200M in self-storage facility acquisitions while developing standardized due diligence and closing processes. Her implementation of AI-assisted workflows increased efficiency while maintaining confidentiality and quality output. Jodi’s deep understanding of title issues, regulatory compliance, and risk management contributed significantly to the company’s rapid portfolio expansion.

attorneys.name: Andrew M. Tatge
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law & Divorce Lawyers in Mankato, MN
attorneys.bio:
Andrew is a partner and chair of the firm's Family Law & Divorce Practice Group and is also a member of the firm's Estate Planning Practice Group. Andrew represents business owners, farmers, and other individuals throughout southern Minnesota and the Twin Cities in a wide range of family law matters. Andrew is also regularly consulted on family law-related issues necessary for protection of businesses and for estate planning purposes.

Andrew enjoys solving complex and difficult issues and guiding his clients through what for many is the most emotional and difficult time of their lives. He has represented numerous farmers, business owners, and professionals (or their spouses) in complex and high net worth divorce and other family law matters throughout Minnesota. In addition to representing his clients, Andrew is a frequent lecturer on complex family law issues to both local and national audiences.

Clients seeking to protect businesses and assets from divorce before a divorce is ever even contemplated as well as divorcing parties with significant assets or a business appreciate Andrew's experience representing businesses and business owners and his knowledge of farm, real estate, and business valuation, accounting, and finance principles.

Andrew also represents unmarried individuals in custody and parenting time matters as well as those entering into cohabitation agreements to protect assets and income.

Divorcing parents and unmarried parents involved in disputes concerning their children appreciate Andrew's analytical and logical approach to resolving child custody and parenting time issues.

No matter what kind of case Andrew is handling, he understands and appreciates clients' concerns about the cost of legal services and utilizes his experienced administrative staff, paralegals, and other attorneys in the firm to ensure that financial resources are used efficiently and appropriately, and that the right person is doing the job.

Andrew provides a full range of personal legal services for his and the firm's Minnesota clients, including:

Litigation Matters:

Divorce

Paternity (issues arising between never-married parents)

Child custody, parenting time and modifications

Child Support and modifications

Spousal Maintenance and modifications

Property Division (including farms, businesses, professionals, and high net worth cases)

High net worth and complex divorce cases, including cases involving complex tax, valuation, and discovery issues

Mediation, Social Early Neutral Evaluations, Financial Early Neutral Evaluations, and other Alternative Dispute Resolution procedures

Post-Divorce or Paternity matters, including modification of court orders and contempt of court matters

Orders for protection and harassment restraining orders

Grandparent and third-party visitation issues

Interstate child custody jurisdiction and enforcement

Family law appeals

Transactional Matters:

Antenuptial ("Pre-nuptial") Agreements

Post-Nuptial Agreements

Cohabitation Agreements

Qualified Domestic Relations Orders

Estate planning focused on protecting assets and income from divorce of the parties or their intended beneficiaries

Business planning focused on protecting assets and income from divorce of business owners, "divorce proofing" businesses, and minimizing or eliminating other effects of divorce and family dynamics on businesses

He strives to understand each situation and then develops a customized course of action that best resolves each client's concerns and issues. Mark's knack for building client relationships is well known within the firm, and he is proud of his dedication to considerate and thoughtful interactions with each individual client. His goal is that the firm's clients always leave completely satisfied with the work he has done.

attorneys.bio:
I have been practicing immigration law since 1982 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. I am a 1982 graduate cum laude of the University of Minnesota Law School. Prior to law school I spent two years in the Peace Corps in Ecuador, South America. I received a Bachelor of Elected Studies Degree from the University of Minnesota College of Liberal Arts in 1977. I am a past Chair of the Immigration Section of the Minnesota State Bar Association. I have served as a past Chair of the Minnesota/Dakotas American Immigration Lawyers Association (AILA) Chapter and has previously served as Vice Chair and Secretary/Treasurer. I have served on the AILA Essential Workers Committee, AILA Immigration Works Committee, AILA InfoNet Committee, and have chaired the Technology Seminar Committee and the Legislative Ways and Means Committee. I am an AILA mentor on St. Paul DHS District Office procedures, and have served as an AILA mentor on immigration issues to Congressional offices. I edited articles for AILA's publication, Immigration Law Today as part of the editorial advisory board.

I am a member of the American Immigration Lawyers Association, Minnesota State Bar Association, American Association for Justice, Minnesota Advocates for Human Rights and various other professional and civic groups. I hold an "A-V" rating from Martindale-Hubbell and am listed in their Directory of Preeminent Lawyers. Minneapolis-St. Paul Magazine and Twin Cities Business Monthly have recognized me as a "Super Lawyer" in immigration law. I have received the AILA National Presidential Commendation for "creative and tireless advocacy" on behalf of immigrants. I am a Trustee Emeritus of the Board of Trustees of the American Immigration Law Foundation. I have spoken and written for various immigration law seminars.

attorneys.name: Timothy Theisen
attorneys.practice_type: Bankruptcy Lawyers in Anoka, MN
attorneys.bio:
Tim Theisen has been a sole practitioner with his main office in Anoka, concentrating in consumer debtor work with a dash of family law, since 1992. He has offices throughout the metro area for your convenience.

The family law made up the majority of his practice in the 1990s. He was the newsletter editor of R-KIDS of Minnesota, a noncustodial parent's grassroots lobbying group, from 1997-2007

His practice is currently 90% consumer bankruptcy and 10% family law. He has lectured before other attorneys several times on issues concerning the intersection of family law and bankruptcy, as well as second mortgage lien stripping. Tim is a member of the National Association of Consumer Bankruptcy Attorneys, the Minnesota State Bar Association, including Bankruptcy Law Section and Family Section, the Anoka County Bar Association, and the Hennepin County Bar Association.

Tim has been married since 1998, has three kids, collects rock n' roll pinball machines, captains two 4.5 tennis teams, and enjoys bicycling and waterskiing.

Thole was also a past President of the Washington County Bar Association.

attorneys.name: Delacy Thomas
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Delacy Jarvis Thomas is a seasoned attorney with a passion for immigration law. Before beginning her legal career, Delacy spent 21 years as a chemist at 3M, where she honed her analytical and problem-solving skills. Inspired by her commitment to advocacy and justice, she transitioned to law, earning her Juris Doctor and joining Jarvis-Fleming Law Ltd., a dedicated boutique firm. Today, she helps clients navigate the complexities of immigration law with expertise and compassion.

Delacy’s personal connection to immigration law stems from her family’s journey as immigrants from Antigua and Barbuda to the United States. Her deep understanding of the immigrant experience drives her to provide thoughtful, thorough representation to clients facing life-changing legal challenges.

Memberships & Expertise

- Member, Minnesota State Bar Association

- Member, American Immigration Lawyers Association (AILA)

- Wide-ranging experience in areas such as adjustment of status, asylum, removal defense, U.S. citizenship, and consular processing.

- Skilled at working with U.S. consulates worldwide to facilitate immigrant visa cases for individuals seeking to live in the United States.

When she’s not advocating for her clients, Delacy enjoys traveling, exploring current events, spending time with her family, and delving into genealogy to uncover the rich stories of her ancestors.

Delacy holds a Juris Doctor (JD), Master of Business Administration (MBA), and a Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry. Her unique background as a scientist-turned-lawyer brings a meticulous, detail-oriented approach to her practice, ensuring her clients receive the highest level of service.

attorneys.name: Kirk C. Thompson
attorneys.firm_name: Kirk C. Thompson Law Office, P.A.
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
kirk.thompson@cpqlaw.com

Kirk C. Thompson has represented the interests of employees, insurers and other parties in Minnesota workers' compensation cases since his admission to practice in 1984. Kirk handles all varieties of compensation cases, including occupational disease claims.

Kirk has edited and published a Minnesota workers' compensation case law update and is a frequent speaker at continuing legal education seminars. He is a trained mediator, and conducts mediations of worker's compensation claims.

In the case of Reider v. Anoka-Hennepin School District No. 11, 728 N.W. 2d 246 ( Minn. 2007), Kirk's appeal of unfavorable lower court rulings resulted in the Minnesota Supreme Court's reversal in his client's favor. The Reider decision established the absolute right of a party to a neutral medical exam in workers' compensation cases, overruling prior cases which held that a party's request for a neutral medical exam was left to the discretion of the compensation judge. A neutral medical examination can provide valuable and decisive evidence in workers' compensation claims.

Awards and Honors

Honors

AV rated by Martindale Hubbell

attorneys.name: Mark K. Thompson
attorneys.practice_type: Business Dispute Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Mark K. Thompson has been practicing business law and litigation since 1999. His business litigation experience is broad and in addition he has extensive appellate experience in civil and criminal matters. Mark founded his law firm, MKT Law, PLC, in 2012. At MKT Law, PLC, Mark is focused on representing small and medium-sized businesses in litigation. The types of businesses MKT Law, PLC represents include those ran by professionals (law firms, lawyers, architects, doctors, engineers, professors) in the construction industry (general contractors and sub-contractors performing structural, finishing, installing, surfacing, excavating, etc.) real estate (developers, agents, brokers) financial services (brokers, agents, bankers), health care providers, wholesalers and the service industry (retail, auto repair, restaurants and bars). Mark has represented individuals involved with these business at all levels from CEO, other officers/directors, management, representatives, independent contractors and employees.

Some recent lawsuits MKT Law, PLC has been counsel on have involved claims of breach of contract, fraud, misrepresentation, fraudulent transfers, shareholder disputes, tortious interference with contract and economic advantage, defamation, to name a few. Mark also provides non-litigation/transactional services to businesses in a number of areas, including business formation, sales and acquisitions, start-up advice, contract drafting and negotiations, commercial leasing and collections, buy-sell agreements and other corporate governance matters.

Mark is a proactive, creative and strategic litigator. In 2005, 2006, 2007 & 2008, he was named a "Rising Star" by Minnesota Law & Politics, Twin Cities Business Monthly and Mpls. St. Paul Magazine. Mark has extensive experience in complex (and not so complex) commercial cases before state and federal courts and in arbitrations. He is adept in handling your case from start through trial and up on appeal is necessary. He is also extremely skilled in settlement negotiations and client advisement and counseling. Recently, Mark was victorious in convincing the Minnesota Court of Appeals to fully reverse a trial court award of about $500,000.00 in a farm property lease dispute involving an option-to-purchase.

Prior to forming MKT Law, PLC, Mark was a business litigation attorney at a leading law firm in Saint Paul, Minnesota, where he was responsible for representing a broad range of clients with shareholder disputes, contract claims, trade secret/intellectual property misappropriations, employment disputes, construction claims, enforcing creditors’ rights/remedies, as well as numerous other areas of law.

Mark also has been an Adjunct Professor at the University of Minnesota School of Law since 2007. He teaches advanced appellate advocacy for the school’s Civil Rights Moot Court, instructing law students on how to properly research and draft appellate briefs and prepare for and deliver effective oral arguments. In this role, Mark also coaches third-year law students in an annual national moot court competition.

Mark was a member of the US District Court—District of Minnesota’s Attorney Advisory Committee, advising the court on its implementation of electronic filing. He has been published in the Hamline Law Review: Has Isaacs v. American Iron & Steel Altered the Pleading, Policy And Purpose Supporting Shareholder Dispute Claims Under Section 302A.467, 28 Hamline L. Rev. 479 (2005). Mark regularly speaks at continuing legal education seminars on ethics, debt collection techniques and emerging developments in the law.

attorneys.name: Paul A. Thompson
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
PAUL A. THOMPSON is the founding partner of Keller, Woods & Thompson, P.A. law firm, a boutique personal injury firm dedicated to helping individuals and families who have been hurt in accidents. While he has concentrated his practice on civil litigation and has experience representing a wide variety of personal injury accident cases, including victims of car accidents, slip, and falls, wrongful deaths, dog bites, medical malpractice, dram shop/drunk driving, boating accidents among others, Paul has also developed a vast amount of experience in the business world. Particularly, he has an understanding about representation of orthopaedic, dental and chiropractic clinics with an emphasis on clinic start-up and development as well as business consultation services such as buy-sell agreements, partnership agreements, IC/employment contracts, insurance billing issues/practices, lease issues, etc. Paul really does have a unique legal background as not just a personal injury lawyer, but as an attorney who is tailor-made for helping those who have been injured in accidents.

Paul combines his vast experience with effective and compassionate client communication and representation to successfully translate the client's case into a successful courtroom strategy. He takes the time to truly understand the client's needs. As a result, he has earned the trust and respect of his clients for always keeping their best interests in mind, and the doctors who refer to Paul for his honesty, integrity and dedication to their patients.

While trying a case to a jury is not always the best option for each victim of an accident, this personal injury lawyer knows that his clients deserve to have their case built for trial to maximize their recovery. Paul has significant experience in resolving claims by means of negotiated settlement or other alternative processes. By constantly striving to provide the highest quality of legal representation to the people who hires him, Paul keeps the success of his clients his ultimate goal. This approach has resulted in just compensation for personal injury victims and clients who have confidence in making referrals.

Paul graduated from Augsburg College with summa cum laude honors in 1985. While working and raising a family, he obtained his juris doctorate from the University of Minnesota Law School in 1988. Since founding the law firm of Woods & Thompson, P.A. (now Keller, Woods & Thompson, P.A.) in 1997, Paul has represented thousands of injured victims who have valued his dedication, experience and steadfast loyalty, but he also finds time to continue to serve our local chiropractic and medical community with educational seminars and counseling.

Paul is licensed and admitted to both the Minnesota and Wisconsin Bar and member of the following:

Minnesota State Bar Association

Minnesota Association of Justice

Minnesota Federal District Court

Wisconsin State Bar Association

Wisconsin Association for Justice

American Association for Justice

United States Court of Federal Claims

United States Supreme Court Bar

attorneys.name: Randy V. Thompson
attorneys.practice_type: Business & Commercial Law Lawyers in Minnetonka, MN
attorneys.bio:
Randy Thompson was born on August 27, 1951 and is a summa cum laude graduate of the University of Minnesota in 1975 and a magna cum laude graduate of William Mitchell College of law in 1980.

Mr. Thompson has litigated cases throughout the United States. He is admitted to practice and has argued before the United States Supreme Court and the Minnesota Supreme Court. Mr. Thompson is also admitted to practice before the Fourth, Seventh, and Eighth Federal Circuit Courts of Appeal, the Federal District Courts of Minnesota and the Eastern District of Michigan, and various Tribal Courts. Mr. Thompson has arbitrated numerous commercial and no-fault insurance cases. He has been a frequent lecturer at continuing Legal Education Seminars.

Mr. Thompson has extensive civil litigation experience, and has both tried and settled multi-million dollar cases. He has practiced extensively in the areas of commercial litigation and Indian law. He represents the Minnesota Service Station Association, and is a nationally recognized expert in the area of petroleum litigation. His work for service station dealers has included both litigation against major oil companies as well as representation in the sale of business and real estate interests, petroleum contamination and real estate condemnation.

Mr. Thompson has also practiced extensively in the franchise area, representing groups of franchisees in litigation in various states. Additionally, he has practiced regularly in the area of employment law, representing both employers and employees in a wide variety of cases. His landmark case established the public policy exception to employment at will in the State of Minnesota.

In the area of Indian law, Mr. Thompson has represented the rights and interests of both Indians and non-Indians in disputes with tribal governments, and has represented tribal officials in internal tribal disputes.

attorneys.name: Peter Timmons
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Eagan, MN
attorneys.bio:
Peter J. Timmons is of counsel with Sieben Edmunds Miller PLLC. He is an experienced lawyer in the areas of Criminal and DWI defense.

He is a former shareholder in the law firm of Moss & Barnett, where he began to develop his criminal and DWI practice. Peter also has broad experience in civil litigation and personal injury litigation – experience that can be vitally important in criminal and DWI defense cases.

Mr. Timmons has over 35 years of experience in representing numerous clients on felony, drug, DWI and traffic charges, along with related license revocation and automobile forfeiture cases. Peter has defended criminal, DWI, and forfeiture cases all over the State of Minnesota and is also an experienced appellate lawyer in DWI and license revocation appeals. In fact, Peter has been civilian defense counsel for a Marine in a general court-martial for a felony offense in the United States Marine Corps.

Beginning in 1998, Minnesota Law and Politics Magazine named Peter Timmons as one of the “Super Lawyers of Criminal Defense.” Since that time, Peter Timmons has been named a “Super Lawyer” repeatedly. Peter also enjoys an “AV” rating in Martindale-Hubbell, the long-standing lawyer directory of American lawyers – the highest rating that can be given to a lawyer by his or her peers.

Peter is tenacious and persistent in pursuing the interests of his clients prosecuted with crimes. Peter believes that everyone deserves the best defense they can obtain and he strives to achieve that in each and every case, regardless of the charge involved.

Awards and Honors

Honors

One of the “Super Lawyers" of Criminal Defense, Minnesota Law and Politics Magazine

AV Rating from Martindale-Hubbell (highest peer-review rating)

attorneys.name: Kirk Tisher
attorneys.practice_type: Business Law Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Kirk Tisher is a Senior Associate in Burns and Hansen's civil practice group, focusing on real estate, corporate and litigation matter. Kirk's practice focuses on helping small and medium size business owners with their various legal needs.

Kirk has successfully represented clients in district courts throughout the state of Minnesota, the Minnesota Court of Appeals, and the federal District of Minnesota. Kirk also represent clients who must address their disputes through an arbitration process. Additionally, he has drafted and negotiated contracts of all types, including real estate purchase agreements and business sale agreements.

To best represent his clients, Kirk seeks to understand their goals, and make sure his representation is tailored to accomplish them in a cost-effective matter. He provides his clients with clear and concise guidance that allows them to understand how to navigate what can be a difficult and complicated process.

Prior to joining Burns & Hansen, P.A., Kirk served as a judicial law clerk for the Honorable Walter Kaminsky in Minnesota's Tenth Judicial District. Kirk diligently represents his clients in both litigation and transactional matters. Kirk graduated from the University of Minnesota Law School in 2015. He has a degree in Geological Engineering from the South Dakota School of Mines and Technology.

In his spare time, Kirk enjoys spending time with family and friends, reading, exercising, and woodworking.

attorneys.bio:
Attorney Jessica D. Triebe was raised in Peoria, IL and later moved to the Chicago area to attend Benedictine University as an undergraduate. She earned a B.A. in International Studies from Benedictine, which included a semester studying abroad in France to complete her French Language minor. After graduation, Jessica worked for two years as a paralegal in a Chicago metro area bankruptcy and foreclosure law firm. She then decided to pursue her legal degree and spent one year at Gonzaga School of Law in Washington State before transferring to and graduating from DePaul College of Law. During her law school career, Jessica was an active participant in school volunteer organizations. She interned at the Washington State Department of Social and Human Services in the Adult Protective Services division pursuing elder abuse violations and at the Cook County Public Guardian's Office in the Adult Guardianship division maintaining guardianship estates. She also volunteered at the Domestic Violence Project in Chicago as a Supervising Attorney responsible for dozens of law students aiding individuals in obtaining Orders or Protection. Outside of the law, Jessica enjoys spending time with family and friends, riding horses, watching foreign films, and traveling.

In recent years, with support of Midwest Disability, she has worked with several pro bono clients on Social Security Disability overpayment cases.

Jessica has remained focused on using her legal knowledge and skill to help those that are disabled, elderly, or abused. This focus and motivation keep her firmly committed to Midwest Disability's clients in their pursuit of much-needed benefits.

attorneys.bio:
Vadim Trifel graduated from the University of Minnesota with a double major in Political Science and Sociology of Law, Crime and Deviance. In 2005, Mr. Trifel attended William Mitchell College of Law on a Merit Scholarship. In 2006, he studied abroad in Malta where he was Certified Arbitrator and Mediator by the Frank G. Evans Center in International Mediation and Arbitration. As a Student Certified Attorney, Mr. Trifel gained extensive courtroom experience. During his third year of law school, he argued and won a constitutional case before the Minnesota Court of Appeals. Mr. Trifel won verdicts on behalf of tenants who were living in uninhabitable conditions. He also successfully handled and argued cases on behalf of the City of St. Louis Park Prosecutor’s Office. In addition to his courtroom work, he traveled to New Orleans to legally assist victims of Hurricane Katrina, taught high school students constitutional law and performed investigative work for the disabled. In 2008, he was awarded three scholarship awards for leadership, community involvement and litigation.

As an attorney, Mr. Trifel represents both individuals and businesses in insurance coverage and contract disputes. He handles a wide variety of cases ranging from smaller disputes to complex litigation involving production of hundreds of thousands of documents and numerous witnesses. Mr. Trifel regularly appears before the State and Federal benches. He is admitted to practice in the State of Minnesota and before the United States District Court, District of Minnesota. He is a member of the Minnesota State Bar Association and the Hennepin County Bar Association.

In addition to his courtroom work, he traveled to New Orleans to legally assist victims of Hurricane Katrina, taught high school students constitutional law and performed investigative work for the disabled. In 2008, he was awarded three scholarship awards for leadership, community involvement and litigation.

As an attorney, Mr. Trifel represents both individuals and businesses in insurance coverage and contract disputes. He handles a wide variety of cases ranging from smaller disputes to complex litigation involving production of hundreds of thousands of documents and numerous witnesses. Mr. Trifel regularly appears before the State and Federal benches. He is admitted to practice in the State of Minnesota and before the United States District Court, District of Minnesota. He is a member of the Minnesota State Bar Association and the Hennepin County Bar Association.

Ivory is a founding member of Engelmeier & Umanah’s Trust, Estates and Business practice group where he focuses on helping families and business owners to develop and implement plans for their families and assets so that their assets are available for their families when they need them. He is also admitted to practice in Wisconsin, the US District Court for the District of Minnesota, and the US Tax Court. He holds a Bachelor of Science degree from Kutztown University of Pennsylvania and an MBA from St. Joseph’s University, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.

attorneys.name: Todd R. Vollmers
attorneys.practice_type: Capital Markets Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Todd R. Vollmers has extensive international and business experience both in government and in the private sector. Todd previously served as Senior Advisor to the Assistant Secretary for Enforcement & Compliance within the International Trade Administration at the U.S. Department of Commerce in Washington, D. C., which involved a variety of assignments in an advisory and/ or policy capacity concerning administration of the laws regulating unfairly traded imports into the United States.

Prior to that, Todd also worked as an attorney in the Office of General Counsel at the U.S. Department of Commerce, where he managed legal issues related to U.S. government advocacy on behalf of U.S. companies with foreign governments, and foreign trade obligations arising under the World Trade Organization (WTO) and North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) (before the USMCA entered into force in July 2020).

In the private sector Todd practiced law as an international transactional attorney with a law firm in Minneapolis, handling a variety of business matters in Asia and Latin America, and as General Counsel for a private equity firm with offices in Minneapolis and Shanghai. He holds a Certificate in Chinese Business Law from Fudan University Law School, Shanghai, a Master of International Policy and Practice degree focusing on International Trade and Economics from The George Washington University, Washington, D.C., a Juris Doctor from the University of Minnesota Law School, and a Bachelor of Arts in Political Science from the University of Minnesota. Before attending college, Todd served as a Spanish translator in the U.S. Army, Military Intelligence Branch.

attorneys.bio:
In his career as a civil trial lawyer Greg has tried over 30 jury/bench trials, handled hundreds of arbitrations, and resolved even more cases through mediation. A creative and inquisitive mind combined with a naturally competitive spirt propelled Greg to be named a Super Lawyer by his peers in the legal community after only his third year in practice. Greg has continued to maintain the Super Lawyer recognition over the course of his career. In 2006 Greg gained membership into the Million Dollar Advocates Forum and in 2020 into the Multi-Million Dollar Advocates Forum.

Greg was admitted to the Minnesota State Bar Association and the United States District Court of Minnesota in 1999. He obtained his law degree from William Mitchell College of Law, now Mitchell-Hamline School of Law, and received his undergraduate degree from the University of St. Thomas.

Since being admitted to the bar Greg has been an active member in the following legal associations:

• American Association of Justice

• Minnesota Association of Justice

• Minnesota Bar Association

• Ramsey County Bar Association

In addition to practicing law Greg has been a member of the St. Paul Curling Club for over thirty years and in 2012 co-authored a historical book about the St. Paul Curling Club entitled 100 Roaring Years on Selby Avenue, The St. Paul Curling Club.

Additionally, Greg is a volunteer Coach for a high school Mock Trial team and organizer of intramural high school curling clubs.

Greg also serves on the Boards of Directors for the St. Thomas Academy Alumni Association, St. Paul Curling Club and St. Paul Curling Foundation (Board Member 2009-201 and Finance Committee 2020).

attorneys.name: Daniel E Warner
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Law Lawyers in Inver Grove Heights, MN
attorneys.bio:
Warner Law Office, P.A. was founded in 1987 by Daniel E. Warner. Mr. Warner is an attorney licensed to practice law in all state and federal courts in the district of Minnesota, as well as before the United States Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals and the United States Supreme Court. Mr. Warner is a cum laude graduate of William Mitchell College of Law (1983), where he obtained the distinction of taking first place in its moot court competition. He has tried numerous jury and court trials on behalf of individuals in the field of employment law and has argued cases before the Minnesota Supreme Court, the United States Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals, and the Minnesota Court of Appeals. Mr. Warner has also tried labor arbitrations, unemployment compensation cases and has handled claims before the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC), the Minnesota Department of Human Rights, and the Minnesota Department of Labor and Industry. He is a member of the National Employment Lawyers Association and the Minnesota State and Dakota County Bar Associations. Mr. Warner is also certified by the Minnesota State Bar Association as a Labor and Employment Law Specialist.

Volunteer Activities

Mr. Warner was the President of the South St. Paul/Inver Grove Heights Rotary Club in 2015-16 and is on the Board of Directors of Neighbors, Inc., a food shelf in South St. Paul. Additionally, Mr. Warner volunteers his time with the federal court Pro Se Project, which provides free legal assistance to certain unrepresented employees in federal court proceedings upon the request of the court. Mr. Warner also has served as a mock trial judge in the Minnesota state high school mock trial competition. Mr. Warner formerly served on the Board of Directors of Civil Society for over 15 years, a Minnesota non-profit corporation which rescues and restores international human trafficking victims. He formerly served on the Metropolitan Council Minority Advisory Committee, the Board of Directors of Blackberry TownOffice Association, was formerly President of Shannon Town Homes Homeowner's Association, and was a former board member and officer of the Minnesota Valley Exchange Club.
