attorneys.name: Mike Weiner
attorneys.practice_type: Auto Accident Lawyers in Brooklyn Park, MN
attorneys.bio:
Did your car accident injury, personal injury, dog attack or the death of a loved one turn your life upside down? Are you wondering how you will recover your health, your emotional strength, and your finances? If you were injured because of another’s negligence, you have Mike Weiner, Scott L. Anderson, and the law on your side.

Mike Weiner associates with Scott L. Anderson on Auto Accident, Personal Injury and Dog Attack Cases. Scott and Mike have worked tirelessly and zealously for clients for over 75+ years combined. Our goal is to help to return your life to normal as soon as possible by being compassionate and securing swift and the highest possible compensation.

Mike Weiner’s Experience Is Backed By Results

Mike Weiner believes the only way to measure a law firm’s success is by the lawyer’s results for their clients. Mike’s trial and settlement results are second to none, garnering some of the most significant settlements and jury awards in the Twin Cities and Minnesota.

A partial list of Mr. Weiner’s significant personal injury and railroad/FELA claims results includes:

$4 million settlement for an amputation

$2.5 million for wrongful death

$2 million for back and head injuries

$2.1 million verdict for Post Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) from a train crash

$1.2 million verdict for the wrongful death of a child

Hundreds of other seven- and six-figure settlements for deaths, spinal and brain injuries, amputations and other life-changing injuries.

Numerous landmark court decisions upholding the right to sue tobacco companies and other corporations for wrongdoing, striking down immunity for governmental defendants, and protecting the rights of injured railroaders.

Mike has more than four decades of professional legal experience. He has taught products liability as an adjunct professor at Mitchell Hamline for over 25 years and has spoken at several Continuing Legal Education seminars.

Mike Is A Seasoned Attorney For People Injured By Negligence

Did your car accident injury or the death of a loved one turn your life upside down? Are you wondering how you will recover your health, your emotional strength and your finances? If you were injured on a road, highway or interstate freeway because of another driver’s negligence or misconduct behind the wheel, you have the law on your side.

Mike Weiner has been honored to be selected for inclusion by both Best Lawyers© from 2006 to present and Superlawyers© from 2000 to 2010 and 2016 to present. He has more than 40 years of handling car crash cases, dog attacks, motorcycle crashes, truck accidents and personal injury cases.

Let Mike focus on the legal details of your car accident claim to take the stress and worry off of you. He builds the strongest case possible to win in court — before we sit down to negotiate a full and fair settlement.

Mike understands the complexities involved in serious injury and wrongful death cases. That’s why he is dedicated to thoroughly examining the details of each incident to determine the viability of a negligence claim.

Mr. Weiner assists his clients in collecting and organizing essential evidence to strengthen their cases, such as securing police reports, medical records, witness statements and other proof of negligence and resulting harm.

Recognizing the emotional toll of losing a loved one, or caring for a loved one, Mike strives to provide compassionate and effective support to secure swift compensation.

With over 40 years of experience in handling these cases, Mike is astute and skilled at accurately assessing a case’s value and pursuing the highest possible compensation, considering both economic and non-economic damages.

If you’re looking for the personalized attention of a local firm combined with the experience of a high-caliber litigator, don’t hesitate to contact Mike Weiner.

A Small Firm Atmosphere With Extensive Trial Experience In Accident Cases

For over four decades of legal experience, I have provided strategic legal representation to clients dealing with the aftermath of car crashes and other serious accidents.

I understand that a car crash and other serious accidents can be a traumatic experience, often resulting in severe injuries and overwhelming medical bills. This is why I am dedicated to helping my clients seek personal injury compensation, covering expenses such as lost wages, emotional distress, property damage, medical costs and more.

With the help of our long-term association and dedicated paralegals, who have all worked together with us for decades, we aim to secure the maximum possible compensation for our clients so they can face the future with security and optimism.

While our clients will find us friendly, helpful and exceptionally understanding of their circumstances, we are known as relentless advocates whose extensive courtroom experience demands respect and yields positive results.

Negotiating with insurance companies is often necessary to obtain fair compensation. Mike brings extensive experience to these discussions, focusing on protecting his clients’ rights and interests.

You Need Representation Immediately After An Accident.

The aftermath of an accident involves substantial paperwork, including police reports, insurance forms and potentially legal documents. To ensure clients’ peace of mind, Mike handles the entire legal process, meeting deadlines and filing requirements.

If a case goes to court, Mike has extensive trial experience and is committed to representing and protecting his clients’ rights and interests every step of the way.

If you’re looking for the personalized attention of a local firm combined with the experience of a high-caliber litigator, don’t hesitate to contact Mike.

You might be surprised to discover the full extent of compensation you’re eligible to receive after an injury. Insurance companies are rarely eager to offer more than necessary, which is why having a knowledgeable and experienced lawyer on your side is essential.

Mike understands that cost can be a concern when you’re injured and potentially losing income. However, it costs nothing to call or meet for a free initial consultation to discuss your situation and explore your best options for moving forward.

sections.content:
Did your car accident injury, personal injury, dog attack or the death of a loved one turn your life upside down? Are you wondering how you will recover your health, your emotional strength, and your finances? If you were injured because of another’s negligence, you have Mike Weiner, Scott L. Anderson, and the law on your side.

Mike Weiner associates with Scott L. Anderson on Auto Accident, Personal Injury and Dog Attack Cases. Scott and Mike have worked tirelessly and zealously for clients for over 75+ years combined. Our goal is to help to return your life to normal as soon as possible by being compassionate and securing swift and the highest possible compensation.

Mike Weiner’s Experience Is Backed By Results

Mike Weiner believes the only way to measure a law firm’s success is by the lawyer’s results for their clients. Mike’s trial and settlement results are second to none, garnering some of the most significant settlements and jury awards in the Twin Cities and Minnesota.

A partial list of Mr. Weiner’s significant personal injury and railroad/FELA claims results includes:

$4 million settlement for an amputation

$2.5 million for wrongful death

$2 million for back and head injuries

$2.1 million verdict for Post Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) from a train crash

$1.2 million verdict for the wrongful death of a child

Hundreds of other seven- and six-figure settlements for deaths, spinal and brain injuries, amputations and other life-changing injuries.

Numerous landmark court decisions upholding the right to sue tobacco companies and other corporations for wrongdoing, striking down immunity for governmental defendants, and protecting the rights of injured railroaders.

Mike has more than four decades of professional legal experience. He has taught products liability as an adjunct professor at Mitchell Hamline for over 25 years and has spoken at several Continuing Legal Education seminars.

Mike Is A Seasoned Attorney For People Injured By Negligence

Did your car accident injury or the death of a loved one turn your life upside down? Are you wondering how you will recover your health, your emotional strength and your finances? If you were injured on a road, highway or interstate freeway because of another driver’s negligence or misconduct behind the wheel, you have the law on your side.

Mike Weiner has been honored to be selected for inclusion by both Best Lawyers© from 2006 to present and Superlawyers© from 2000 to 2010 and 2016 to present. He has more than 40 years of handling car crash cases, dog attacks, motorcycle crashes, truck accidents and personal injury cases.

Let Mike focus on the legal details of your car accident claim to take the stress and worry off of you. He builds the strongest case possible to win in court — before we sit down to negotiate a full and fair settlement.

Mike understands the complexities involved in serious injury and wrongful death cases. That’s why he is dedicated to thoroughly examining the details of each incident to determine the viability of a negligence claim.

Mr. Weiner assists his clients in collecting and organizing essential evidence to strengthen their cases, such as securing police reports, medical records, witness statements and other proof of negligence and resulting harm.

Recognizing the emotional toll of losing a loved one, or caring for a loved one, Mike strives to provide compassionate and effective support to secure swift compensation.

With over 40 years of experience in handling these cases, Mike is astute and skilled at accurately assessing a case’s value and pursuing the highest possible compensation, considering both economic and non-economic damages.

If you’re looking for the personalized attention of a local firm combined with the experience of a high-caliber litigator, don’t hesitate to contact Mike Weiner.

A Small Firm Atmosphere With Extensive Trial Experience In Accident Cases

For over four decades of legal experience, I have provided strategic legal representation to clients dealing with the aftermath of car crashes and other serious accidents.

I understand that a car crash and other serious accidents can be a traumatic experience, often resulting in severe injuries and overwhelming medical bills. This is why I am dedicated to helping my clients seek personal injury compensation, covering expenses such as lost wages, emotional distress, property damage, medical costs and more.

With the help of our long-term association and dedicated paralegals, who have all worked together with us for decades, we aim to secure the maximum possible compensation for our clients so they can face the future with security and optimism.

While our clients will find us friendly, helpful and exceptionally understanding of their circumstances, we are known as relentless advocates whose extensive courtroom experience demands respect and yields positive results.

Negotiating with insurance companies is often necessary to obtain fair compensation. Mike brings extensive experience to these discussions, focusing on protecting his clients’ rights and interests.

You Need Representation Immediately After An Accident.

The aftermath of an accident involves substantial paperwork, including police reports, insurance forms and potentially legal documents. To ensure clients’ peace of mind, Mike handles the entire legal process, meeting deadlines and filing requirements.

If a case goes to court, Mike has extensive trial experience and is committed to representing and protecting his clients’ rights and interests every step of the way.

If you’re looking for the personalized attention of a local firm combined with the experience of a high-caliber litigator, don’t hesitate to contact Mike.

You might be surprised to discover the full extent of compensation you’re eligible to receive after an injury. Insurance companies are rarely eager to offer more than necessary, which is why having a knowledgeable and experienced lawyer on your side is essential.

Mike understands that cost can be a concern when you’re injured and potentially losing income. However, it costs nothing to call or meet for a free initial consultation to discuss your situation and explore your best options for moving forward.

attorneys.bio:
Patricia is the Chair of the firm's Commercial Real Estate Department. She has more than 25 years experience representing clients locally and nationally in complex commercial real estate acquisitions and sales, as well as real estate development, leasing and finance projects. Patricia provides full-service representation to clients from inception of a transaction through closing. Her due diligence reviews include title, survey, land use, permitting and environmental matters.

Patricia's experience in sophisticated leasing includes representing both landlords and tenants in the negotiation of ground leases, build-to-suit leases, leases for space in office building and condominium complexes and leases in shopping centers and developments governed by extensive public and private restrictions, covenants and easements. Additionally, Patricia counsels her clients in traditional bank financing as well as complex structured financing, sale-leaseback transactions, leasehold financing and financing for multi-unit, multi-state packages.

attorneys.name: Alaina Wenning
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Edina, MN
attorneys.bio:
Alaina is an associate attorney with Hill Crabb Law Firm and practices in the area of Family Law.

Prior to joining Hill Crabb Law Firm, Alaina worked as a judicial law clerk for two judges in the Fourth Judicial District’s Hennepin County Family Court. Through her clerkships, Alaina gained valuable court perspectives and learned first-hand how to apply complex decision-making processes to family law cases in order to resolve conflict.

Alaina displays a commitment to helping families navigate the judicial system and assists clients in reaching resolutions with creative solutions that best meet their family’s needs.

In addition to her proficiency in general Family Law matters, Alaina Wenning also brings expertise in the areas of step-parent adoption and estate planning.

Her work in step-parent adoption showcases her ability to navigate the complexities of blending families legally and emotionally, ensuring that the process is handled with sensitivity and legal acumen. This expertise underscores her commitment to family dynamics and the well-being of children within these new family structures.

Alaina's knowledge in wills, estates, and trusts further complements her skill set. She is adept at guiding clients through the intricacies of estate planning, ensuring their assets are managed and transferred according to their wishes. Her work in this area often involves creating comprehensive plans that include wills, trusts, and other estate planning instruments. This expertise is particularly valuable for families looking to secure their financial future and provide for their loved ones.

In her free time, Alaina enjoys playing with her dog, Poppy, spending time with her husband and children, and traveling to see her family members and friends that live out of state.

attorneys.name: William J. Wetering
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Worthington, MN
attorneys.bio:
Practice Information:

Bill Wetering has practiced primarily in the areas of family law, criminal defense, personal injury, insurance defense, civil litigation and business litigation since joining the firm in 1987. Bill is an experienced litigator and has the ability to zealously represent his client’s interests and advocate on his or her behalf. Bill was admitted to practice before the South Dakota Supreme Court in 1986 and the Minnesota Supreme Court in 1987.

Personal Information:

Bill Wetering was born in 1959, in Sioux Falls, South Dakota. He graduated from South Dakota State University with a B.S. in 1983 and he attended the University of South Dakota School of Law, where he received his J.D. in 1986. He is a member of the the State Bar of South Dakota, the Minnesota State Bar Association, the American Bar Association, the American Association for Justice, the South Dakota Trial Lawyers Association and the Minnesota Trial Lawyers Association. Bill and his wife Betsy live in Worthington, Minnesota and are members of St. Mary’s Catholic Church in Worthington. He is a member of Worthington Noon Kiwanis and serves as a Board Member of both the Adrian State Bank and the Worthington Regional Economic Development Corporation.

attorneys.name: Kevin J. Wetherille
attorneys.practice_type: General Practice Lawyers in Shakopee, MN
attorneys.bio:
Kevin began working with Jaspers, Moriarty & Walburg during law school as a Law Clerk. After spending over 2 years clerking with Jaspers, Moriarty & Walburg, the firm hired Kevin as an associate following his admission to the bar in 2003. Kevin was named a shareholder in Jaspers, Moriarty & Walburg in 2007. Kevin became the firm CEO/Managing Partner in 2014. Currently, Kevin resides in Shakopee, Minnesota with his wife and their three children.

A significant portion of Kevin's practice is devoted to litigation in the areas of Civil Litigation, Probate Law, Family Law as well as more transactional areas of practice such as Estate Planning and Real Estate. Kevin has represented clients in settlement negotiations, alternative dispute resolution, trial, and appeals. Kevin’s ability to craft creative solutions based upon the facts of each case sets him apart from many other attorneys.

Kevin has also been appointed by local district court judges as a receiver, neutral personal representative in probate cases, guardian ad litem for litigants in family law cases and currently serves as the Scott County Veterans Treatment Court defense counsel.

attorneys.name: Merryn L. Wier
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Saint Paul, MN
attorneys.bio:
Practice Experience

Merryn Wier is an Associate Attorney at CBS&H, where she practices in the areas of employment law, family law, and civil litigation. She is dedicated to helping clients navigate complex legal issues with clarity and confidence, combining strong analytical skills with a practical, client-centered approach.

Personal Bio

Before joining CBSH, Merryn gained experience in employment litigation, where she developed skills in legal research, writing, and case strategy. She has worked on matters involving discrimination, retaliation, and wage disputes, as well as family law cases involving divorce, custody, post-decree issues, and both orders for protection and harassment restraining orders. Merryn approaches each case with attention to detail and a commitment to achieving fair and effective resolutions for her clients.

While earning her J.D. from the University of St. Thomas School of Law, Merryn served as President of Delta Theta Phi and as a 3L Class Representative. She also worked as a Research Assistant to Professor David Grenardo, contributing to award-winning scholarship on civility in the legal profession and collaborating on international research examining racism in sports. In addition to her academic work, Merryn served as a mentor to newer law students through the Tourek-Marvin Peer Mentor Program.

Outside of her practice, Merryn enjoys volunteering in the legal community, golfing, skiing, and exploring the Twin Cities restaurant scene. She strives to make the legal process accessible and less intimidating for clients, ensuring they feel supported and informed every step of the way.

attorneys.name: Trent R. Wilcox
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Park Rapids, MN
attorneys.bio:
Trent R. Wilcox practices in the areas of Family Law, Guardianship, Personal Injury, Employment Disputes and General Civil Litigation. He is admitted to practice in the state courts of Minnesota, along with the Arizona state and federal courts.

As an extension of his family law practice, Trent worked closely in the past with the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children to return abducted children to the custodial parent; he assisted parents from Honduras, Great Britain, Lebanon, Mexico and other countries in cases brought under The Hague Convention of Oct. 25, 1980 on the Civil Aspects of International Child Abduction. He is committed to protecting children who have been wrongfully abducted from their home countries. He received the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children Award of Merit in recognition and appreciation for outstanding commitment to the protection of children and knowledge of the Hague Convention and international child abduction issues.

Trent was originally admitted to practice law in Arizona in 1995 and returned to northern Minnesota to continue his legal practice in 2012. In his spare time, his interests include fishing, motorcycling and snowmobiling. In addition, he still plays golf regularly, although certainly not to the level he formerly did while playing professionally.

attorneys.name: Ann M. Wilczynski
attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of Ann M. Wilczynski, PLLC
attorneys.practice_type: Wills, Trusts, Estate Planning and Probate Lawyers in St. Louis Park, MN
attorneys.bio:
I believe that estate planning should be as convenient, affordable and painless as possible. Let's face it: does anyone enjoy writing their will or trust, or dealing with the other issues that arise when discussing this topic? I can't make this process fun, but I can make it easier for you.

How do I do that? First, in most instances I will complete your work for a fixed fee, which I will tell you before we begin. Generally speaking, I charge a married couple $1000 for an estate plan for both spouses, and I charge a single person $500 for an estate plan for him or her. In other words, I generally don't charge clients on an hourly basis, but if that is necessary, I will tell you that before we begin and give you an estimate of the total fee for the work I would recommend doing for you. Second, I offer free initial consultations, so that we can get to know each other and discuss what services I could offer you. I can meet with you at a time and location convenient for both of us; I am happy to make housecalls. Third, I use technology to enhance, but not replace, the "human element" that is important when practicing law in this area. After all, wills, trusts, and other estate planning documents or services are really all about a person's most private thoughts, information, and feelings. Finally, while I have practiced this type of law for a number of years, I try to take advantage of every opportunity to stay up to date on changes in the law in this area.

attorneys.bio:
Andrew Willaert is a true counselor to his clients. He believes that strong representation is the product of good listening. He helps his clients understand their options and make informed decisions. Among these clients are privately owned businesses, agriculture producers, and individuals, for whom he provides advice and services in the areas of business organization, purchases and sales, succession and estate planning, real estate, and probate.

attorneys.bio:
James Williamson started Williamson Family Law, PLLC, in September 2020, having practiced family law exclusively since 2004. James represents clients in a wide variety of family law matters including complex business valuation, property division and cash flow analysis relating to spousal maintenance and child support, as well as parenting time and custody matters.

James believes in a compassionate, sensible and cost-effective approach to family law. To attain client focused results, James regularly participates in mediation and other alternative dispute resolution methods. If litigation is necessary, James uses his extensive experience to guide the client through the court system and to advocate for his client's interests.

James is a veteran of the United States Air Force, where he learned discipline and the value of teamwork. Subsequent to his military service, James earned a Bachelors of Science in computer science, magna cum laude, at the University of North Dakota. He worked for a number of years as an IT Professional in charge of overall network design and administration, which taught him analytical thinking, and creative, efficient problem-solving, both of which have served him well in his legal career. James obtained his Juris Doctor from William Mitchell College of Law in 2003.

attorneys.name: David L. Wilson
attorneys.practice_type: Immigration Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
David L. Wilson is the Managing Attorney of Wilson Law Group. David is licensed to practice in the State of Minnesota, U.S. District Court of Minnesota, U.S. District of Colorado, the Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals, the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals, and the US Supreme Court. David attended the University of St. Thomas and graduated cum laude in 1993. He then graduated from the William Mitchell College of Law with cum laude honors in 1997.

David is a member of the American Immigration Lawyers Association (AILA) and the Federal Bar Association. He is a Past Chair of the Minnesota / Dakotas Chapter of AILA. David has also served as the AILA Liasion for the Executive Office for Immigration Review. David has also served as an adjunct professor at Hamline University School of Law where he co-taught immigration law. He also served an adjunct law professor for the William Mitchell College of Law, teaching Writing Research Advocacy and Presentation, Appellate Advocacy, and the William Mitchell College of Law’s Immigration Law Clinic.

David is a frequent guest speaker on many legal topics in Minnesota and nationally, and provides pro bono services to victims of domestic abuse and children in need. The Children's Law Center of Minnesota recognized David for his pro bono work on behalf of immigrant children in foster care in 2012. David was also awarded the 360 Communities Caring Award for his pro bono work with the Lewis House Domestic Abuse Shelters in February 2013. In 2016, Minnesota Lawyer awarded David for one of its Minnesota Attorneys of the Year. David also won the Minnesota Justice Foundation private attorney public service attorney in 2016.

David litigates cases before the federal government, federal court system, Minnesota courts, and Minnesota agencies. He is the attorney of record in multiple published decisions as well as several unpublished federal and Minnesota Court of Appeal decisions.

attorneys.name: Peter J. Wollan
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Burnsville, MN
attorneys.bio:
Peter understands that divorce, custody, and child support matters come with a lot of emotions and a lot of questions. He takes the time to get to know you and your family's unique situation to craft an individualized approach to your case with your goals in mind. Peter believes that most matters can be resolved through alternative dispute resolution including mediation and early neutral evaluation. While he strives to resolve cases amicably when possible, he is well prepared to advocate on your behalf in court if necessary to achieve your goals.

Prior to joining Meinerts Law Office, Peter worked for the largest family law litigation firm in the nation. This experience exposed him to training and practices throughout the country in oftentimes high conflict cases. During law school, he spent time working for a small southwest metro law firm practicing general litigation with an emphasis on family law.

Before beginning his legal career, Peter spent nearly a decade in banking working for both large and small banks conducting anti-money laundering investigations and mortgage fraud investigations. He also has a previous background in law enforcement and criminal justice. This experience means that he can handle both complex financial cases where one party has attempted to conceal marital funds, as well as custody matters involving criminal charges, orders for protection, and sexual abuse allegations.

Peter lives in Shakopee and is active in his children's school and the local soccer association among other community pursuits. In his free time, he enjoys golfing, bicycling, reading, and travel.

attorneys.name: Ryan R. Wood
attorneys.practice_type: Immigration Removal Proceedings Lawyers in St. Paul, MN
attorneys.bio:
Former Judge Ryan R. Wood is a seasoned legal professional with more than 20 years of experience spanning military service, federal prosecution, immigration enforcement, and the judiciary. As a former Assistant Chief Immigration Judge for the Executive Office for Immigration Review (EOIR), Ryan has built a distinguished career marked by leadership, strategic thinking, and a deep commitment to the fair application of immigration law.

Judicial Experience

From March 2019 until his retirement in February 2025, Ryan served as an Assistant Chief Immigration Judge, where he oversaw immigration courts in Fort Snelling, Cleveland, Detroit, and Kansas City. In this role, he managed court operations, supervised administrative functions, and presided over complex immigration proceedings including deportation, exclusion, removal, rescission, and bond hearings.

Ryan began his judicial career in April 2017 when he was appointed as an Immigration Judge at the Fort Snelling Immigration Court. During his time on the bench, he developed a reputation for his thorough preparation, analytical approach, and clear communication of complex legal concepts. His expertise in immigration law made him a valued trainer for new judges on specialized topics including criminal immigration issues, evidence, asylum, and mental competency proceedings.

Throughout his judicial tenure, Ryan demonstrated remarkable success in managing significant court growth and caseload increases. Under his leadership, the Fort Snelling and Cleveland Immigration Courts achieved substantial increases in case completions while maintaining high standards of judicial process and fairness. He was recognized for his strategic docket management skills, including the implementation of innovative approaches that increased court efficiency without compromising due process.

Federal Prosecution and Legal Service

Prior to his judicial appointment, Ryan served as a Special Assistant United States Attorney for the District of Minnesota from November 2014 to April 2017. Assigned to the Major Crimes and Priority Prosecutions section, he represented the United States in federal court and before the 8th Circuit Court of Appeals. His prosecution portfolio included cases involving identity theft, passport fraud, illegal reentry, tax fraud, child exploitation, intellectual property crimes, and armed bank robbery. In this role, he secured more than thirty-five felony convictions, including two successful jury trials. Ryan was also responsible for training more than one hundred federal law enforcement officers on Fourth Amendment protections.

Ryan's expertise in immigration law was further developed during his service as Assistant Chief Counsel for U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement from October 2009 to March 2014. While representing the Department of Homeland Security in immigration proceedings, he was designated as a National Security Attorney with Top Secret security clearance. His accomplishments in this role included successfully negotiating and coordinating a high-profile national security removal to Iran, for which he received a Special Achievement Award in 2012. Ryan also served as a trial attorney for worksite enforcement actions related to I-9 audits and investigations.

His federal service also included a position as an Embedded Attorney with Homeland Security Investigations, where he provided legal guidance and litigation support on complex criminal cases involving border searches, forfeitures, narcotics, wiretaps, human trafficking, child exploitation, cybercrimes, worksite enforcement actions, and commercial fraud.

Military Service

Ryan's legal career began in the U.S. Army Judge Advocate General's Corps, where he served in various capacities from 2005 to 2009. As a Trial Defense Counsel with the U.S. Army Trial Defense Service, he represented soldiers facing court-martial proceedings and administrative hearings, including a twelve-month deployment to Iraq where he defended soldiers facing criminal charges across Iraq, Kuwait, and Afghanistan. For his exceptional service in a combat zone, he was awarded the Bronze Star Medal and the U.S. Army Commendation Medal.

Before his defense work, Ryan served as a Senior Trial Counsel and Trial Counsel for the U.S. Army 4th Infantry Division, prosecuting criminal cases before military juries, military judges, and administrative boards. As Senior Trial Counsel, he led the training of new Trial Counsel and provided Fourth Amendment training for federal law enforcement officers. He was also appointed as a Military Magistrate by the Fourth U.S. Army Judicial Circuit, where he conducted pre-trial confinement hearings and issued search authorizations and arrest warrants.

During his military service, Ryan also worked as Soldiers' Counsel for the U.S. Army 7th Infantry Division, representing injured soldiers in administrative proceedings related to fitness and disability determinations. His remarkable success rate in contested cases led to his selection as one of only two JAG attorneys Army-wide to attend a conference on redesigning the Army's disability system.

Education and Professional Development

Ryan holds a Juris Doctor from Hamline University School of Law, where he served as an editor for the Hamline Law Review. He subsequently earned a Master of Business Administration from Hamline University School of Business, complementing his legal expertise with advanced business acumen that proved valuable in his court management roles. His undergraduate education includes a Bachelor of Arts in Political Science with a minor in Management from Hamline University College of Liberal Arts.

Ryan's commitment to ongoing professional development has been evident throughout his career. While serving as Assistant Chief Immigration Judge, he delivered hundreds of hours of formal instruction across all EOIR components. He also served on various committees and special assignments, including the Immigration Judge Hiring Committee, EOIR Training Committee, and the Pro Bono Steering Committee (Director's Award recipient), and led efforts for the OCIJ Case Flow Management Action Plan (Special Commendation recipient).

Leadership and Management

Ryan's leadership approach combines analytical rigor with interpersonal effectiveness. During his tenure as Assistant Chief Immigration Judge, he successfully managed significant caseload growth while improving court efficiency.

His management philosophy emphasizes data analysis, strategic resource allocation, and clear communication with both internal and external stakeholders. Ryan has been recognized for his ability to distill complex information into clear, understandable terms—a skill that has made him effective in training, stakeholder engagement, and court administration.

Professional Memberships and Community Involvement

Ryan was admitted to the Minnesota Bar in October 2004 and has maintained active involvement in the legal community throughout his career. He served as a local union representative for the National Association of Immigration Judges during his time as an Immigration Judge.

Beyond his legal work, Ryan has demonstrated a commitment to community service as a volunteer with Team Rubicon Disaster Response, where he serves as a level 1 sawyer. As of May 2024, he also serves as a board member for MicroGrants, a nonprofit organization.

Current Focus

Following his retirement from the bench in February 2025, Ryan brings his wealth of experience and expertise to private practice, where he focuses on immigration law consultation and complex case strategy. Drawing on his judicial perspective and comprehensive understanding of the immigration system, he offers unique insights to clients navigating complicated immigration matters.

Ryan's approach to client service reflects the same values that guided his judicial career: thorough preparation, clear communication, and an unwavering commitment to the fair application of immigration law. His experience on both sides of the immigration system—as a government attorney and as a judge—gives him a comprehensive understanding of immigration proceedings that few practitioners can match.

Licensed to practice in Minnesota, Ryan brings a strategic, solution-oriented approach to his work, helping clients understand the complexities of immigration law and navigate pathways toward successful outcomes.

Awards and Honors

Honors

US Department of Justice, Executive Office for Immigration Review Special Commendation, 2024

US Department of Justice, Executive Office for Immigration Review Director’s Award, 2023

US Department of Homeland Security Special Achievement Award, 2012

US Army Bronze Star medal, 2009

US Army Commendation medal (2), 2007 & 2009

attorneys.name: Elizabeth Lee Young
attorneys.practice_type: Affirmative Immigration Applications Lawyers in St. Paul, MN
attorneys.bio:
Professional Biography

Elizabeth L. Young is a seasoned legal professional with over 20 years of experience spanning service in federal immigration courts, university law schools, and community organizations, establishing her as a recognized expert in immigration law practice, education, and policy development. Elizabeth’s leadership extends beyond the courtroom through her extensive professional service, mentorship of legal professionals, and commitment to the fair application of immigration law.

Judicial Experience

From January 2024 to January 2025, Elizabeth served as Regional Deputy Chief Immigration Judge, serving the Western Region of the United States. This position required selection by an independent governmental board as a member of the Senior Executive Service, a group of key leaders within the government that “possess well-honed executive skills and share a broad perspective on government and a public service commitment that is grounded in the Constitution.” In this position, Elizabeth supervised Assistant Chief Immigration Judges across the western United States while providing critical legal guidance and developing nationwide policy initiatives to enhance court operations.

Prior to this executive role, Elizabeth served as Assistant Chief Immigration Judge in San Francisco from July 2021 to January 2024, supervising over 100 Immigration Court personnel including judges, attorney advisors, court administrators, and staff supervisors. In this capacity, she addressed comprehensive personnel matters while assessing court health and developing strategic plans for case management across regular and specialized dockets.

Elizabeth’s judicial career began as an Immigration Judge in September 2016 where she maintained non-detained adult and juvenile dockets, conducting master and merits hearings while issuing both oral and written decisions. She served as backup for detained dockets and acted as a mentor for incoming and sitting Immigration Judges throughout her tenure.

Elizabeth began her career as an Attorney Advisor at the San Francisco Court. This pivotal time in her career gave her valuable judicial system experience where she worked “behind the scenes” researching and drafting orders and bench memoranda as well as analyzing changes to immigration law.

Academic Experience

Prior to entering the judiciary, Elizabeth’s academic career spans nearly a decade of distinguished service in legal education, with particular expertise in immigration law and clinical instruction. At the University of Arkansas School of Law, she progressed from Assistant Professor of Law (2008-2011) to Associate Professor of Law (2011-2016), being awarded tenure in 2016. There, she founded the first Immigration Law Clinic in the University of Arkansas system. This groundbreaking initiative included developing course proposals, community partnerships, comprehensive syllabi, and original course materials while maintaining subject matter expertise in public immigration awareness.

Her teaching responsibilities encompassed fully subscribed Immigration Law I seminars and skills-based coursework, while simultaneously supervising student attorneys in live client representation before U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services, the Executive Office for Immigration Review, and the Board of Immigration Appeals. Throughout her academic tenure, she maintained an independent caseload, ensuring her practical expertise remained current.

Young also served as Visiting Professor of Clinical Law and Interim Director of the Immigration Clinic at The George Washington University Law School from 2007-2008, where she taught Immigration Clinic Seminars and supervised student attorneys in trial level cases before the Executive Office for Immigration Review as well as complex appellate matters reaching the Fourth Circuit Court of Appeals.

Education and Professional Development

Elizabeth holds a Juris Doctor from The George Washington University Law School, having graduated with honors. She served as a member of The George Washington International Law Review, and subsequently the Executive Editor of The Guide to International Legal Research. While at GW, Elizabeth was introduced to immigration law through the Immigration Law Clinic, where she would eventually go on to receive the Richard C. Lewis, Jr. Memorial Award for Clinical Excellence. She further attended the International Human Rights Law Programme at Oxford University, providing her with global legal perspectives that would inform her later immigration law expertise.

Elizabeth is a firm believer in continuous learning and professional development. Her academic career required continuous professional development in clinical legal education methodologies, curriculum development, and pedagogical approaches to experiential learning. She continued this trajectory as an Immigration Judge through mentorship of new Immigration Judges, Attorney Advisors, and conducting learning seminars for new judicial law clerks at the San Francisco Immigration Court. As one of approximately 40 Assistant Chief Immigration Judges, Elizabeth participated in nation-wide training for new attorneys, judges, and staff of the court. As Regional Deputy Chief Immigration Judge, she directed nationwide training programs for both new and experienced Immigration Judges, covering fundamental and advanced immigration law.

Leadership and Management

Elizabeth’s leadership capabilities are evident in her progression to a Senior Executive Service role within the federal judiciary. Her management portfolio included comprehensive human resources oversight, involving allocation and planning of human and fiscal resources while evaluating program effectiveness and ensuring compliance with Departmental fair employment initiatives on a national scale.

Elizabeth demonstrated exceptional collaborative leadership by participating in and leading inter- and intra-agency working groups focused on developing national court policy and implementing regulatory, statutory, administrative, and litigation initiatives. During her tenure as Assistant Chief Immigration Judge, she served on specialized national committees addressing judge and attorney training, Immigration Court Practice Manual updates, judicial recruitment and hiring processes, and pro bono legal service practices.

In academia, Elizabeth exhibited entrepreneurial leadership by founding Arkansas's first immigration law clinic, requiring strategic vision, community engagement, and institutional navigation. Her administrative service included leadership roles on faculty appointments committees and graduate legal studies committees, demonstrating her commitment to institutional governance and academic excellence.

Professional Memberships and Community Involvement

Elizabeth was admitted to the Virginia Bar in October 2004, joining the California and Arkansas Bars in 2009. Prior to joining the judiciary, Elizabeth maintained active engagement with professional organizations that advance legal education and immigration law practice. She served on the Central States Law Schools Association Board from 2009-2014 and held leadership positions within the Arkansas Bar Association International Law and Immigration Section, including Chair-Elect from 2011-2012. Her professional affiliations included membership in the American Bar Association, American Immigration Lawyers Association, and AALS Clinical Legal Education Association.

Her community involvement reflects a deep commitment to literacy, education, and immigrant services. She served as a Board Member of the Ozark Literacy Council from 2011-2016 and participated in the One Book One Community Planning Committee at the University of Arkansas. She further serviced as Board Member from 2002-2012 with Catholic Charities Immigration Services as a Board Member from 2009-2012, and in an advisory role with the Hispanic Women's Organization of Arkansas from 2010-2016.

More recently, Elizabeth has engaged in local educational leadership, serving on the Donlon Elementary School Site Council for Strategic Planning from 2020-2022.

Awards and Recognition

Young's exceptional contributions to law, education, and public service have earned her prestigious recognition throughout her career. She received the Executive Office for Immigration Review Director's Award in 2022, acknowledging her outstanding service within the federal immigration court system. The Arkansas Times recognized her as Visionary Arkansan of 2013, while the Northwest Arkansas Business Journal honored her with the Fast 15 Award in 2009.

Her academic excellence was recognized early in her career with the Richard C. Lewis, Jr. Memorial Award for Clinical Excellence from The George Washington University Law School in 2004. Her commitment to public service was acknowledged during her undergraduate years with the Ferris C. Baker Sociology Award in public service from Hendrix College in 1999.

Awards and Honors

Honors

US Department of Justice, Executive Office for Immigration Review Director's Award, 2023

Arkansas Times, Arkansas Visionary Award, 2013

Northwest Arkansas Business Journal, Fast 15 Award, 2009

Chosen to represent Hamline in Washington, D.C., as a part of the Washington Semester Program, she had the opportunity to work at Holland & Knight, LLP, and the privilege of meeting the United States Supreme Court justices.

As a top student in her Lawyering course in her first year of law school, Rachel was named a Summer Fellow. She clerked for a Minnesota District Court Judge of the Third Judicial District. She continued her law school training abroad in London, England.

Rachel graduated cum laude a semester early from Mitchell Hamline School of Law in 2018. She served as an associate editor for Mitchell Hamline Law Review and was on the Dean's Honor Roll.

Since joining Dady & Gardner, Rachel has represented clients in all stages of their relationships with their franchisors and suppliers. As a franchisee attorney, Rachel regularly reviews hundreds of franchise agreements to help prospective franchisees understand the pros and cons of the opportunity and negotiate the terms of their franchise agreements to their benefit. Rachel also advises new and existing franchisee associations.

Rachel enjoys spending time with her three daughters and husband, walking her dog, and playing the piano. Rachel is also a children's book author.

attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Christina Zauhar has practiced exclusively in the area of criminal defense since her graduation from law school. Christina is a strong believer in an individual's right to a trial and the importance of the State's burden to prove a criminal defendant guilty beyond a reasonable doubt. From misdemeanors to felonies, Christina will ensure that her client's constitutional rights are protected and that the State will be held accountable. Christina is a contributing author to Minnesota's DWI Deskbook, which is utilized by judges, prosecutors, and defense attorneys across the state as a comprehensive reference guide to Minnesota DWI laws. Christina's extensive knowledge of DWI laws is illustrated through her innumerable negotiations of DWI charges to reduced charges, and even acquittal in trial.

Outside of work Marcus is an avid sports fan and enjoys golfing, running, and spending time with his family.

attorneys.name: Rodney M. Zerbe
attorneys.practice_type: Insurance Litigation Lawyers in Minneapolis, MN
attorneys.bio:
Rodney M. Zerbe is a counsel with Crowell & Moring's New York City office. Rodney has litigated a broad range of complex commercial litigation matters, with a concentration in the defense of insurance brokers and reinsurance intermediaries on professional malpractice claims.

Rodney has twenty-five years of large law firm experience, during which he has successfully defended insurance brokers and intermediaries on errors and omissions claims involving placement of commercial general liability, directors and officers liability, property and casualty, marine protection and indemnity, builders’ risk, business interruption and loss portfolio transfer insurance, and facultative and treaty reinsurance placements. Rodney has also litigated numerous complex commercial disputes, including defense of federal securities fraud, RICO and shareholder derivative actions, breach of fiduciary duty and shareholder disputes involving closely-held corporations, unfair trade practices claims, restrictive covenant and non-compete litigation, claims for breaches of commercial representation and warranty agreements, defense of loan servicers on claims relating to collateralized debt offerings, accountants' malpractice liability, partnership disputes, foreign sovereign distressed debt recovery litigation, and other contractual and commercial disputes.

Rodney has handled appellate arguments before the United States Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit and the Appellate Division of the New York State Supreme Court and has conducted arbitrations of commercial disputes in proceedings before the American Arbitration Association, ARIAS and the ICC.

attorneys.name: Dean M. Zimmerli
attorneys.practice_type: Agriculture Law & Agribusiness Lawyers in New Ulm, MN
attorneys.bio:
Dean Zimmerli, a partner of Gislason and Hunter, grew up on a Southern Minnesota farm. He understands and appreciates the work farmers do to maintain their business and feed and fuel the country. Much of the work he does relates to the agriculture industry. His practice includes civil litigation related to agriculture law and agribusiness, business and corporate law, real estate, environmental law and land use, finance and banking, commercial disputes and general litigation.

Zimmerli's broad experience in civil litigation beyond collection and enforcement actions allows him to provide comprehensive representation to banks and other creditors through the entirety of a lending relationship with a borrower. He regularly represents banks and other creditors in bankruptcy and state courts to enforce the creditor's rights, recover collateral and maximize recovery on troubled loans.

He has developed expertise and a unique perspective in drainage and water law, by representing project proponents, concerned landowners and drainage authorities. Zimmerli represents clients throughout the drainage project process from preparing petitions, to advocating at drainage authority meetings and hearings and litigating drainage appeals. Serving as an advisor to landowners or other stakeholders with concerns over potential projects, he represents clients from all points of view on drainage projects.

Beyond drainage, he helps clients with various regulatory and environmental concerns related to water and agriculture, including disputes between landowners concerning water, flooding, crop loss and more.

Zimmerli is a skilled appellate attorney who has briefed or argued numerous cases before the Minnesota Court of Appeals and other appellate courts. He enjoys the intellectual challenge that appellate work entails and is able to pare down complex cases to their essential parts in order to provide concise and persuasive analysis to appellate judges. He provides advocacy and attention to detail on cases managed from inception and cases where clients have sought new representation on appeal.

Outside of work, he enjoys spending time with his wife, Chelsey and their rescue dog. As a family they camp, hike, fish and tackle remodeling projects on their Victorian-era home. In the fall and spring he continues to help with his family's farm.
